(A.) ― -b2- A^abaratohu AlEaqorabu (tropical:) The scorpion stung him with the extremity of its tail. A^aborN (M, Msb, K) and A_ibaArN and A_ibaArapN , (M, K,) He fecundated a palm-tree [by means of the spadix of the male tree, which is bruised, or brayed, and sprinkled upon the spadix of the female; or by inserting a stalk of a raceme of the male tree into the spathe of the female, after shaking off the pollen of the former upon the spadix of the female (see A^aloqaHa )]; (T, S, A, Msb;) as also ↓ A^b~r , (S, A,) inf. n. taA^obiyrN : (S:) or the latter has an intensive and frequentative signification [meaning the doing so much, or frequently, or to many palmtrees]: (Msb:) and the former (S, M, A, K) and ↓ latter, (M, A, K,) he dressed, or put into a good or right or proper state, a palm-tree, (S, M, A, K,) and seed-produce, (M, K,) or any thing, as, for instance, a snare for catching game. (A Hn, M.) You say also, A^ubirati Aln~axolapu , and ↓ A^ub~irat , and wubirat , The palm-tree was fecundated. (Aboo- 'Amr Ibn-El-'Alà, L.) -A3- A^abira , aor. , He, (a man, TA,) or it, was, or became, in a good or right or proper state. (T, K.)

definition: A dog that has had a needle given him, to eat, in bread: (S:) and, with p , applied to a sheep or goat ( $Ap ) that has eaten a needle in its fodder, and in whose inside it has stuck fast;
sourceDefinition: A dog that has had a needle given him, to eat, in bread: (S:) and, with p , applied to a sheep or goat ( $Ap ) that has eaten a needle in its fodder, and in whose inside it has stuck fast; in consequence of which the animal eats nothing, or, if it eat, the eating does it no good. (TA.) It is said in a trad., Almuw^ominu kaA@lokalobi AlmaA^obuwri The believer is like the dog that has had a needle given to him, to eat, in bread. (S.) [Accord. to Ibr D, the meaning is, that he is generous and incautious, so that he is easily deceived.] -A2- Also, (T, S, A,) and ↓ muw^ab~arN , (S,) A palm-tree fecundated: (T, S, A:) and the same, and seed-produce, dressed, or put into a good or right or proper state. (T, TA.) The former is the meaning in the phrase sik~apN maA^obuwrapN , (T, S,) occurring in a trad., [q. v. voce maA^omuwrN ,] i. e. A row of palm-trees [or perhaps a tall palm-tree ] fecundated: or, as some say, this phrase means a ploughshare properly prepared for ploughing. (TA.)

A^awoSalahu ; (M, Msb, K;) namely, a thing; (M;) as, for instance, AlA^amaAnapa A_ilaY A^holihaA [ the thing committed to his trust and care, to its owner ]: (Msb:) he delivered it, gave it up, or surrendered it: (T:) he payed it, or discharged it; (S, K;) namely, his debt, (S,) a bloodwit, a responsibility, and the like; (Msb in art. grm ;) [and hence,] A^ad~aY maA Ealayohi [ he acquitted himself of that which was incumbent on him; or payed, or discharged, what he owed ]: (T:) he performed, fulfilled, or accomplished, it; namely, [for instance,] AlHaj~a [ the pilgrimage ]; (Msb in art. qDY ;) and in like manner, AlmanaAsika [ the religious rites and ceremonies of the pilgrimage ]. (Jel in ii. 196, and Msb ubi suprà.) It is said in the Kur [xliv. 17], A^ano A^ad~uwA A_laY~a EibaAda A@ll~`hi , meaning Deliver ye to me [ the servants of God, ] the children of Israel: or, as some say, the meaning is, A^ad~uwA A_ilaY~a maA A^amarakumu A@ll~`hu bihi yaA EibaAdaA@ll~`hi [ perform ye to me that which God hath commanded you to do, O servants of God ]: or it may mean listen ye, or give ye ear, to me; as though the speaker said, A^ad~uwA A_ilaY~a samoEakumo ; the verb being used in this sense by the Arabs. (T.) And one says, lahu ↓ tA^ad~ayotu , mino Haq~ihi , (K, TA,) and A_layohi , in the place of lahu , meaning A^ad~ayotuhu ; (TA;) i. e. I payed him his due, or right. (K, TA.) And a man says, ↓ maA A^adoriY kayofa A^ataA^ad~aY [ I know not how to pay ]. (TA.) One says also, A^d~Y Eanohu [meaning He payed, or made satisfaction, for him ]: and A^d~Y Eanohu AlxaraAja [ He payed for him, or in his stead, the land-tax ]. (Mgh in art. jzA^ .) [Hence,] El-Akhnas says, faA^ad~ayotu Ean~iY maA A@sotaEartu mina AlS~ibaA wa lilomaAli EinodiYi Alyawoma raAEK wa kaAsibu i. e. But I have put away from me [ what I had borrowed, or assumed, of the folishness of youth, and amorous dalliance, ] and now I am [or there is at my abode ] a keeper and collector to the camels, or cattle, or property. (Ham p. 346.) ― -b2- [ A^ad~aY A_ilY ka*aA is a phrase often used as meaning It brought, conducted, led, or conduced, to such a thing or state; as, for instance, crime to punishment or to ignominy.]

sourceDefinition: , (Mbr, S, K,) of the measure faEolFY , because you say A^adiymN maA^oruwTN , [explained below,] (Mbr, S,) the alif (Mbr, S, K) ending it (Mbr) [written Y ] being a letter of quasi-coordination, (S, K,) not to denote the fem. gender, (Mbr, S,) its n. un. being A^aroTaApN , (Mbr, S, K,) wherefore it is with tenween when indeterminate, but not when determinate: (S, K:) or it is of the measure A^afoEalN , (Mbr, * S,) the last letter being radical, (Mbr,) because you say A^adiymN maroTiy~u , (Mbr, S,) and in this case it should be mentioned among words with an infirm letter [for the last radical], and is with tenween both when determinate and when indeterminate; (S;) [but this is a mistake, for when it is determinate, it can be with tenween only if used as a proper name; therefore,] IB observes, that if you make its last letter radical, its measure is A^afoEal , and a word of this measure, if a subst., is imperfectly decl. when determinate, but perfectly decl. when indeterminate: (TA:) [the author of the K copies the error of the S, saying, “ or its alif is radical, ” (meaning its last letter,) “ and in this case it is always with tenween; ” and he adds, “ or, ” (for which he should have said “ and, ”) its measure is A^afoEal : to all which it is necessary to add, that some of the grammarians hold it to be also of the measure faEolaY , ending with a fem. alif, and therefore assign to it no n. un.:] A kind of tree, (S, K,) of those growing in sands, (S, TA,) resembling the kind called EiDaAh , growing as a branch [in the TA EaSabFA , for which I read guDonFA ,] from a single stem, to the height of the stature of a man, the leaves whereof are what are termed hadab [q. v., and are included among those termed xuwS ], (AHn, TA,) and its flower is like that of the xilaAf [or salix ægyptia ], (AHn, K,) save in being smaller, the colour being one; and the odour thereof is pleasant: it grows in sands, and therefore the poets make frequent mention of the wild bulls' and cows' taking refuge among this and other trees of the sands, burrowing at their roots to hide themselves there, and to protect themselves from the heat and cold and rain, but not among the trees in hard ground, for burrowing in the sand is easy: (AHn, TA:) its fruit is like the Eun~aAb [or jujube ], bitter, and is eaten by camels in its fresh moist state, and its roots are red, (AHn, K,) intensely red: (AHn, TA:) AHn adds, a man of the Benoo-Asad informed me, that the leaves ( hadab ) of the ArTy are red like the red pomegranate: its fruit also is red: (TA:) the dual is A^aroTayaAni : (AHn, TA:) and the pl. A^aroTayaAtN and A^araATayi and A^araATK , (AHn, K,) in the accus. case A^raATiy . (TA.)

definition: The foundation, basis, or lowest part, (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) of a building, (S, A, K,) or of a wall;
sourceDefinition: The foundation, basis, or lowest part, (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) of a building, (S, A, K,) or of a wall; (Mgh, Msb;) as also ↓ A^as~N and ↓ A_is~N (A, K) and ↓ A^asaAsN (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K) and ↓ A^asasN , (S, K,) which is a contraction of A^asaAsN : (S:) or the commencement of a building: and any commencement of a thing; as also ↓ A^as~N and ↓ A^asaAsN and ↓ A^asasN : (M:) and the origin, source, stock, or root, ( A^aSol ,) of a man; as also ↓ A^as~N : or of anything; (M, K;) as also ↓ A^as~N (M, K) and ↓ A_is~N and ↓ A^asiysN : (K:) and the heart of a man; because [the Arabs believe that] it is the first thing that comes into existence in the womb: (M, K:) pl. A=saAsN (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K) and A_isaAsN (M, Msb, K) and A^ususN ; (M, Mgh, Msb, K;) the first of which is pl. of A^Ns~N , (Mgh, Msb,) like as A^aqofaAlN is of qufolN ; (Msb;) or of A^asasN , like as A^asobaAbN is of sababN ; (S;) or, as some say, of A^ususN , [like as A^aEonaAqN is of EunuqN ,] so that it is a pl. pl.; (TA;) and the second, of A^as~N , like as EisaAsN is of Eus~N ; (Msb;) and the third, of A^asaAsN , (Mgh, Msb,) like as EunuqN is of EanaAqN . (Msb.) You say, AlA^aw~ali ↓ banaY bayotahu EalaY A^asaAsihi [ He built his house upon its first foundation. ] (A.) And qalaEahu mino A^us~ihi [ He uprooted it from its foundation ]. (A.) And A^amorihi Alka*ibu ↓ fulaAnN A^asaAsu (tropical:) [ Such a one, the foundation of his affair, or case, is falsehood ]. (A, TA.) And kaAna *`laka EalaY A^us~i Ald~ahori , (S, M, A, K,) and ↓ A^asihi , and ↓ A_isihi , (S, M, K,) (tropical:) That was in old, or ancient, time; (S, M, K;) at the beginning of time; (S, A, * K;) and in like manner, Ealay A@soti Ald~ahori . (A.) ― -b2- Also A remain, relic, trace, vestige, sign, mark, or track, of anything. (K.) You say, xu*o A^us~a AlT~ariyqi , or AlT~ariyqi ↓ A^as~a , [accord. to different copies of the K, meaning, Take thou to the track of the way, ] when one guides himself by any mark or track, or by camels' dung: but when the way is manifest, you say, xu*o $araka AlT~ariyqi . (K.) A^us~N also signifies The remains of ashes (M, K) between the A^avaAfiY , q.v.: (M:) occurring in a verse of En-Nábighah Edh-Dhubyánee; but accord. to most relates of this verse, it is A=sN . (TA.)

definition: A stable (K) for dawaAb~ [i.
sourceDefinition: A stable (K) for dawaAb~ [i. e. horses or mules or asses ]: (S [in some copies of which it is omitted] and K:) the A is radical, because an augmentative does not occur at the beginning of a word of four or five letters unless derived from a verb: (S:) [probably from the barbarous Greek σταβλίον :] AA says that it is not of the [genuine] language of the Arabs: (S:) IB says that it is a foreign word, used by the Arabs: (TA:) accord. to some, (TA,) it is of the dial. of Syria: (K, TA:) the pl. is A^aSaATibu : and the dim. A^uSayoTibN . (TA.)

A^aTorN ; (S, Msb, K;) and ↓ A^T~rhu inf. n. taA^oTiyrN ; (K;) He bent it, or curved it; (S, Msb, K, &c.;) namely, a bow, (S, A,) and a twig, or the like: (A:) he laid hold upon one of its two extremities, and curved it: he bent it, or curved it; namely, anything; EalaY $~aYo'K upon a thing: and the latter verb, [or both,] he bent it into the form of a hoop, bringing its two extremities together. (TA.) ― -b2- It is said of Adam, A@ll~`hu ↓ kaAna TuwaAlFA faA^aT~arahu He was tall, and God bent him, and diminished his height. (TA.) ― -b3- And one says, A^axa*a EalaY yadaYi AlZ~aAlimi waA^aTarahu EalaY AlHaq~i (tropical:) [ He laid hold upon the two hands, or arms, of the wrongdoer, or prevented, restrained, or withheld, him from doing that which he desired, ] and bent him to [ conformity with ] what was right. (AA, from a trad.) And A^aTarota fulaAnFA EalaY mawad~atika (tropical:) [ Thou hast bent such a one to love thee ]. (A.) ― -b4- A^aTara Als~ahoma (S, K,) aor. and , (K,) inf. n. as above, (S, K,) He wound an A^uTorap upon the arrow. (S, K.) ― -b5- A^aTara Albayota , (TK,) inf. n. as above, (K,) He made an A_iTaAr , which is a thing resembling a zone or belt, to the tent or house. (K, TK.)

definition: The place of curvature ( munoHanaY ) of a bow, and of a cloud: (K, TA:) an inf.
sourceDefinition: The place of curvature ( munoHanaY ) of a bow, and of a cloud: (K, TA:) an inf. n. used as a subst., and, being so used, admitting the dual form: or the bent, or curved, part of the extremity of a bow; to which Tarafeh likens the curving of the ribs of a she-camel: (TA:) and what resembles a curvature, seen in the clouds: an inf. n. in the sense of a pass. part. n. (Skr, TA.)

definition: Anything that surrounds another thing: (S, A, Msb, K:) as the hoop of a tambourine, (A, Mgh, TA,) and of a sieve.
sourceDefinition: Anything that surrounds another thing: (S, A, Msb, K:) as the hoop of a tambourine, (A, Mgh, TA,) and of a sieve. (S, A, Mgh, K.) ― -b2- A ring of hair surrounding the head, the middle of it being bald. (TA.) ― -b3- ― -b4- The branches of a vine, bent, or wreathed, so as to form a covering over-head. (K.) ― -b5- See also A^uTorapN , in two places. ― -b6- A_iTaAru AlHaAfiri The part of the hoof of a horse or the like which surrounds, or extends around, the A^a$oEar [q.v.]. (S.) ― -b7- A_iTaAru Al$~afapi (S, K, &c.) (tropical:) The part, (A,) or flesh, (Msb,) surrounding the lip: (A, Msb:) or the part that separates between the lip and the hairs of the mustache: (K:) or the edge of the upper lip, between the lip itself and the parts where the hair grows: (IAth:) or the rising edge, or ridge, between the part where the mustache is clipped and the lip, intermixing with the mouth. (A'Obeyd.) The Muslim should clip his mustache so that this part shall appear. (Msb, TA.) ― -b8- A_iTaAru bayotK A thing resembling a zone, or belt, of a tent or house. (K.) ― -b9- A_iTaAri mina Aln~aAsi (tropical:) A ring, or circle, of men. (K.) One says, humo A_iTaArN libaniY fulaAnK (tropical:) They have alighted and taken up their abode [ so that they form a ring ] around the sons of such a one. (A, Msb.)

definition: is from A^alaka signifying “he sent;
sourceDefinition: is from A^alaka signifying “he sent;” and is originally A^aA^olikoniY ; the [second] hemzeh being transposed and placed after the l , it becomes A^aloy^ikoniY ; then the hemzeh has its vowel transferred to the l and is thrown out; as is done in the case of malakN , which is originally maA^olakN , then maloA^akN , and then malakN : (IB in art. lwk :) it means Be thou my messenger; and bear thou my message; and is often used by the poets. (S in art. lwk .) Accord. to IAmb, one says, A^alikoniY A_ilaY fulaAnK , meaning send thou me to such a one: [but I do not know any instance in which this meaning is applicable:] and the original form is A^aloy^ikoniY ; or, if from AlA^aluwku , the original form is A^aA^olikoniY : and he also says that it means be thou my messenger to such a one. (TA.) One says also, A^alikoniY A_ilayohaA birisaAlapK , which should properly mean Send thou me to her with a message: but it is an inverted phrase; since the meaning is, be thou my messenger to her with this message [or rather with a message ]: and A^alikoniY A_ilayohaA biAls~alaAmi i. e. convey thou, or communicate thou, to her my salutation; or be thou my messenger to her [ with salutation ]: and sometimes this [prep.] b is suppressed, so that one says, A^alikoniY A_ilayohaA Als~alaAma : sometimes, also, the person sent is he to whom the message is sent; as in the saying, A^alikoniY A_ilayoka Als~alaAma [virtually meaning receive thou my salutation; but literally] be thou my messenger to thyself with salutation. (TA.) Lh mentions the phrase A^alakotuhu A_ilayohi , with respect to a message, aor. A^uliykuhu , inf. n. A_ilaAkahN ; in which case, the hemzeh [in the aor. and inf. n.] is converted into a letter of prolongation. (TA in art. lA^k .)

sourceDefinition: He sought, pursued, or desired, the most pleasing of things; (TA;) [ he affected nicety, or refinement; he was dainty, nice, exquisite, refined, or scrupulously nice and exact; or chose what was excellent, or best; and he exceeded the usual bounds; as also tanaw~aqa and tanay~aqa , in all these senses;] fiY AlmaToEami , in respect of food, never eating anything but what was clean [ and choice ]; and fiY Almalobasi , in respect of apparel, never dressing otherwise than well; and fiY AlkalaAmi , in respect of speech, never speaking otherwise than chastely; and fiY jamiyEi AlA^umuwri , in respect of all affairs. (TA in art. nTs .) tA^n~q fiyhi is like tanaw~aqa ; (JK, S, K;) i. e. He did it, or performed it (namely, a thing, or an affair,) with niyqap [i. e. daintiness, nicety, exquisiteness, refinement, neatness, or scrupulous nicety and exactness; or in a manner exceeding what is usual ]: (S:) or he chose what was excellent, or best, to be done in it, and did it admirably: (TA:) or he did it (namely, his work, Msb) firmly, solidly, soundly, or thoroughly, (Msb, K,) and skilfully. (K: [but in this last sense, 'Alee Ibn-Hamzeh allows only the latter of these two verbs. TA in art. nwq .]) You say also, tA^n~q fulaAnN fiY Al~ar~awoDapi Such a one found himself in the meadow, or garden, ( waqaEa fiyhaA ,) pleased, or rejoiced, therewith: (S:) or he found it pleasant or delightful, delighted in it, or took pleasure or delight in it, and enjoyed its beauties: and he sought after its beauties, step by step, and was pleased, or rejoiced, therewith, and enjoyed it. (TA.) And tA^n~q AlmakaAna He was pleased, or rejoiced, with the place, and attached to it, not quitting it: (L:) he loved the place. (Fr, K.) It is said in a trad. of Ibn-Mes'ood, A_i*aA waqaEotu fiY A=li H=m= waqaEotu fiy rawoDaAtK A^ataA^an~aquhun~a , or, as in the T, A^ataA^an~aqu fiyhin~a , meaning [ When I find myself in the chapters of the Kur-án commencing with Há Meem, ] I find myself in meadows, or gardens, the beauties of which I seek after step by step, and with which I am pleased, or rejoiced, and which I enjoy: i. e., I find pleasure, or delight, in reading them, or reciting them, and enjoy their beauties. (TA.)

definition: A certain bird; (S;) i. e. the raxamap [or female of the vultur percnopterus ]; (IAar, S;) called by Kumeyt *aAtu A@somayoni [ possessor of two names ] because having these two appellations: (S:) or...
sourceDefinition: A certain bird; (S;) i. e. the raxamap [or female of the vultur percnopterus ]; (IAar, S;) called by Kumeyt *aAtu A@somayoni [ possessor of two names ] because having these two appellations: (S:) or the eagle: and also the former bird: (K:) ISk cites 'Omárah as saying that it is in his opinion the eagle; but that people say it is the rxmp ; and he adds, [alluding to a prov., which see below,] that the eggs of the rxmp are found in ruins, and in plain country: (TA:) or the male of the raxam : (JK, TA:) or a certain black bird, having what resembles the Eurof [or comb of the cock ], (AA, K,) that deposits its eggs in remote places: (AA:) or a certain black bird, (AA, K,) like a great hen, (AA,) bald in the fore part of the head, (AA, K,) having a yellow bill, (K,) or having a long bill: (AA:) she guards her eggs, and defends her young one, and keeps with her offspring, and submits not herself to any but her mate, and migrates among the first of the migrating birds, and returns among the first of the returning birds, and will not fly while moulting, and will not be deceived by her small feathers but waits until they become quills and then flies, and will not remain constantly in the nests, and will not alight upon the quiver (K) knowing it to contain arrows: (TA:) the word is sing. and pl.: (TA:) or its pl. is A^unuqN . (JK.) Hence the prov., (JK, S,) A^aEaz~u mino bayoDi AlA^anuwqi [ More rare than the eggs of the anook ]: (JK, S, K:) because this bird guards its eggs, so that they are hardly ever, or never, found; for its nests are on the tops of mountains, and in difficult and distant places; (S, K;) notwithstanding which, it is said to be stupid: (S:) ISd says that the female bird called rxmp may be meant thereby; or the male, because the eggs of the male exist not; or the eggs of the latter may be meant because he often guards them, like as does the male ostrich. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (K,) and ↓ baHobaEahaA , (TA,) (assumed tropical:) He was, or became, [ established ] in the middle, or midst, [which is the best part, ] of the dAr [i. e. abode, or district, or country, &c.], (K, TA,) and became possessed of mastery, dominion, or authority, and power, over it. (TA.) Fr, however, makes tabaHobuHN to be from `AlbaAHapu [q. v.], not from a reduplicative root. (TA.) ― -b2- tbHbH also signifies (assumed tropical:) He was, or became, settled, or established, in authority and power, (syn. tamak~ana ,) in alighting, and taking up his abode, or sojourning; (S, K, TA;) and was, or became, [ established ] in the middle, or midst, [or best part, ] of the place of abode; (TA;) and so ↓ bHbH . (K, TA.) ― -b3- Also (tropical:) He took a wide, an ample, or a large, range. (A.) ― -b4- [Hence,] tbHbH AlHayaA (assumed tropical:) The rain became of wide extent, and had influence upon the land. (TA, from a trad.) ― -b5- And tabaHobaHati AlEarabu fiY lugaAtihaA (tropical:) The Arabs were copious, or took a wide range, in their dialects. (A.) ― -b6- And tbHbH fiY Almajodi (assumed tropical:) He became in an ample state of glory, honour, or dignity. (TA.) ― -b7- An Arab of the desert said, of a woman in labour, tarakotuhaA tabaHobaHu EalaY A^ayodiY AlqawaAbili [app. (assumed tropical:) I left her obtaining delivery by the hands of the midwives ]. (AZ, TA.)

definition: A garment that is worn (T, S, Msb) in service, or work;
sourceDefinition: A garment that is worn (T, S, Msb) in service, or work; (S, Msb;) that is not preserved, laid up, taken care of, or reserved; (T, M, K;) as also ↓ ba*olapN (Msb) and ↓ mbo*alN , (T,) or ↓ mibo*alapN , (S, M, K,) the pl. of which is mabaA*ilN : (S:) and an old and worn-out garment; (TA;) as also ↓ mibo*alN and ↓ mibo*alapN ; (M, K;) the last of which is mentioned on the authority of AZ, but is disapproved by 'Alee Ibn-Hamzeh, who asserts it to be without p : (IB, TA:) bi*olapN sometimes has bi*alN as pl. (TA.) You say, ↓ jaA='a naA fulaAnN fiY mabaA*ilih , i. e. fiY viyaAbi bi*olatihi or ↓ ba*olatihi [ Such a one came to us in his garments that he wore in service, or work ]. (S, accord. to different copies. [I have shown that bi*olapN and ba*olapN are dial. vars., both as inf. ns. (see 8) and as proper substs.]) The word badolapN , with fet-h, and with the unpointed d , applied by the vulgar to [a suit of] new clothes, is a mistake for bi*olapN , and this is correctly a name for old and worn-out clothes. (TA. [But this is doubtful; for badolapN commonly signifies, in modern Arabic, a change of clothes; and hence, a suit of clothes, whether new or old.]) ― -b2- IJ uses it metaphorically, in relation to poetry; saying, Alr~ajazu A_in~amaA yusotaEaAnu bihi fiY Albi*olapi wa Einoda AlAiEotimaAli wa AlHudaA='i wa Almihonapi (tropical:) [ The metre termed rejez is only used as an aid in the ordinary, or meaner, business of life, and on the occasion of doing one's work, and singing to camels for the purpose of urging them on, and performing service of any kind: but in this case it may be regarded as an inf. n.: see 8]. (M.)

definition: signifies The act of breaking: or breaking in pieces: syn.
sourceDefinition: signifies The act of breaking: or breaking in pieces: syn. HaTomN . (TA.) ― -b2- [And The act of mixing: see basiysapN . This, or the former, is probably the primary signification.] ― -b3- [And hence, app.,] bas~ahu , aor. , inf. n. bas~N , (M, Msb,) He broke it, crumbled it, or bruised or brayed it; said of wheat, &c.; thus making it what is termed basiysap : (Msb:) or he mixed it, namely, sawyq [or meal of parched barley or wheat], and flour, &c., with clarified butter, or with olive-oil; thus making it what is termed bsiysap : (M:) or he moistened it, namely, sawiyq , and flour, with a little water; (ISk, Msb;) but making it more moist than one does in the action termed lat~N : (Yaakoob, cited in the S; and ISk, in the Msb:) or bas~N signifies the making, or preparing, bsiysap , by stirring about, or moistening, sawiyq , or flour, or ground A^aqiT , with clarified butter, or with olive-oil; (S, K;) after which it is eaten, without being cooked. (S.) ― -b4- [And hence the saying in the Kur lvi. 5,] wabus~ati AljibaAlu bas~FA And the mountains shall be crumbled with a vehement crumbling, (Lh, M, A, K,) like flour, and sawiyq , (A,) and become earth: (Fr, K:) or become dust cleaving to the earth: (AO, M, TA:) or be levelled: (M, TA:) or mixed with the dust: (Zj, M, TA:) or reduced to powder and scattered in the wind. (TA.)

definition: He took anything when it was fresh, juicy, moist, or not flaccid;
sourceDefinition: He took anything when it was fresh, juicy, moist, or not flaccid; (TA;) as also ↓ Abtsr [which is more commonly used]. (M, K, * TA.) [Hence,] basarobu Aln~abaAta , aor. , inf. n. basorN , I pastured [ beasts ] upon the herbage when it was fresh and juicy, I being the first to do so. (TA.) ― -b2- Also, (K,) aor. as above, (TA,) and so the inf. n., (M,) i. q. A^aEojala [as meaning (assumed tropical:) He was quick, or beforehand, or before the proper time, with a person or thing, or in doing, or seeking, a thing]. (M, K.) [Hence,] basara Aln~aAqapa , (As, S, M, K,) aor. and inf. n. as above; (M;) and ↓ AbtsrhA , (S, A,) and ↓ tbs~rhA ; (T;) (tropical:) He (the stallion) covered the she-camel without her desiring it: (As, S, A:) or before she desired it. (M, K.) And in like manner, basara and ↓ tbs~r (tropical:) He (a stallion) covered a mare when she had only begun to feel the excitement of desire. (TA.) And ↓ Abtsr AljaAriyapa (tropical:) He deflowered the girl before she had attained to puberty. (A, and Msb in art. qD .) And basara and ↓ Abtsr (assumed tropical:) He fecundated a palm-tree before the proper time for doing so. (M, K.) And basara Als~iqaA='a , (K,) inf. n. as above, (S,) (assumed tropical:) He drank the milk of the skin, (K,) or gave it to be drunk, (S,) before it had become thick, and fit for churning. (S, K.) And basara , (M, K,) aor. as above, (M, A,) and so the inf. n., (S, M,) (tropical:) He broke a pustule: (A:) or he squeezed a pustule, or a boil, before it was ripe: (TA:) or he laid it open by peeling off its crust, or scab, before it was ripe; (S, M, K;) as also ↓ Absr . (K.) And, inf. n. as above, (assumed tropical:) He dug rivers when water was scarce: or sought for, or after, water [ when it was scarce ]: and so, accord. to Az, ↓ tbs~r . (L. [But for A*A ErA AlmA' Aw TAbh , as part of the explanation, I read A_i*aA Eaz~a AlmaA'u A^awo Talabahu .]) And basara Aln~ahora (assumed tropical:) He dug a well in [ the bed of ] the river, it being dry. (L. [But here, for w hw SAf , I read w hw jaAf~N .]) Also basara , (S, M, K,) aor. as above, (M,) and inf. n. as above (S, M) and bisaArN ; (M;) and ↓ Abtsr (M, A, K) and ↓ tbs~r and ↓ Absr ; (M, K;) (tropical:) He sought, sought for or after, demanded, or desired, a thing that he wanted, or needed, in an improper time: (M, K:) or in an improper place: (S, M:) or in an improper manner: (Jm:) or before its time. (A.) And the first of these verbs, (tropical:) He required a debt to be paid before the time when it was due. (K, TA.) And (tropical:) He required his debtor to pay a debt before the time when it was due: from basara Aln~aAqapa , explained above. (Sh, TA.) ― -b3- Also, inf. n. basorN , (assumed tropical:) He began a thing; and so ↓ Abtsr . (K.) And basara bihi (TK) and bh ↓ Abtsr (TA, TK) (assumed tropical:) He began with it. (TA, TK.) -A2- Also, aor. , inf. n. basorN , He mixed busor [or fullgrown unripe dates ] with others, in beverage of the kind called nabiy* : the doing of which is forbidden in a trad.: (S:) or he mixed busor with fresh ripe dates, or with dry dates, and made with them both together that kind of beverage. (TA.) And basara tamorFA , (M, K,) aor. and inf. n. as above; and ↓ bs~rhu (M) and ↓ Absrhu ; (K;) He made, of dry dates, that kind of beverage, and mixed busor with it. (M, K.) -A3- Also, (M, K,) aor. , inf. n. basorN and busuwrN , (M,) He frowned; contracted his face; or grinned, or displayed his teeth, frowning, or contracting his face, or looking sternly, austerely, or morosely; (M, K;) as also basara wajohahu , inf. n. busuwzN : (S:) or he did so excessively: (Jel in lxxiv. 22:) or he looked with intense dislike or hatred. (TA.)

definition: Anything fresh, juicy, moist, not flaccid.
sourceDefinition: Anything fresh, juicy, moist, not flaccid. (IF, M, Msb, K.) You say nabaAtN busorN A fresh plant: (Msb:) or a plant that has risen from the surface of the ground, but not grown tall; because it is then fresh and juicy: (TA:) or such is called busorapN [fem. of busorN ]; as also what is fresh, juicy, moist, or not flaccid, of the plant called buhomaY . (M.) A plant, or herbage, when it first appears in the ground is termed baAriDN ; then, jamiymN ; then, busorapN ; then, SamoEaA='u ; and then, [when it is dry,] basorN . (S.) ― -b2- Fresh water, (S, M, K,) recently produced by rain; (S, M;) as also ↓ basorN : (M:) or this latter signifies cold, or cool, water: (K:) pl. of the former bisaArN ; (S, K;) like as rimaAHN is pl. of rumoHN . (S.) ― -b3- (tropical:) A young, or youthful, man, and woman: (K, TA:) or young, or youthful, and fresh; fem. with p : (M, A:) applied, respectively, to a man and a woman; (M;) or to a boy and a girl. (A.) ― -b4- And, with p , (tropical:) The sun when it has just risen, (S, K, TA,) and is red, and not yet clear. (A, * TA.) [Accord. to the A, this meaning seems to be derived from that next following.] ― -b5- busorN and ↓ busurN (S, M, K) [the former, only, mentioned in the A and Msb &c., as the latter is rare; coll. gen. ns., signifying Fullgrown ] unripe dates; dates before they have become ruTab ; (M, K;) dates that have become coloured, but have not become ripe; (TA;) dates that have begun to colour, i. e., to become red or yellow; (Msb in art. bulH ;) dates beginning to ripen: (IAth, TA in art. blH :) so called because fresh and juicy, and not flaccid: (M:) n. un. busorapN and busurapN : (S, M, K:) pl. busoraAtN (S) [or busorapN ] and busuraAtN : (M:) Sb says that busurapN [or busorapN or each of these] has no broken pl.; but he allows busoraAn and tamoraAn , as meaning two sorts of busor and of takor . (M.) [J says,] busorK in their first stage are termed TaloEN ; then, xalaAlN ; then, balaHN ; then, busorN ; then, ruTabN ; then, tamorN : (S:) but this saying of J is not good: the original thereof is termed TlE ; and when they have become organized and compact ( A_i*aA AnoEaqada ), they are termed sayaAbN or say~aAbN [accord. to different copies of the K]; and when they have become green and round, jadaAlN and saraAdN and xalaAlN ; and when they have become somewhat large, bagowN ; and when they have become large, [or full-grown,] busorN ; then, muxaT~amo ; then, muwak~itN ; then, tu*onuwbN ; then, jumosapN [in the CK jamiysapN ]; then, vaEodahN and xaAliEN and xaAliEapN ; and when completely ripe, ruTabN and maEowN ; then, tamorN . (K.) ― -b6- [Hence,] busorapN signifies also (tropical:) The head, or extremity, of the penis of a dog. (K, TA.) ― -b7- And (assumed tropical:) A kind of bead; syn. xarazapN . (K.)

definition: A well-known disease;
sourceDefinition: A well-known disease; (K;) a swelling, or tumour, which nature drives to every part of the body, from a humour that comes from the anus ( AlmaqoEadap ), and the testicles, and the edges of the labia majora of the pudendum muliebre, and other parts; and when in the anus, attended by a swelling of the veins; (Msb;) sing. of ; (S, K;) which signifies a certain disease that arises in the anus ( AlmqEdp ), [namely, the hemorrhoids, or piles, to which this term generally applies when it is used absolutely,] and also in the inside of the nose; (S;) what resembles boils in the anus: (Mgh:) sometimes the s is changed into S : (Mgh, Msb:) and it is said that the word is not Arabic. (Msb.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. buEodN ; (S, L, Msb, K;) and baEida , aor. , inf. n. baEadN ; (L, K;) and ↓ AbEd , inf. n. A_iboEaAdN , which is also trans.; (Msb;) and ↓ tbAEd ; (S, Msb, K;) and ↓ AstbEd ; (S, K, &c.;) He, or it, was, or became, distant, remote, far off, or aloof: he went, or removed, or retired, or withdrew himself, to a distance, or far away, or far off: he alienated, or estranged, himself: he stood, or kept, aloof: contr. of qaruba : (S, L:) [but baEuda generally has the first of these significations; and ↓ AbEd , the others, as also ↓ tbAEd and ↓ AstbEd :] it is the general opinion of the leading lexicologists that baEida , as well as baEuda , is thus used; but some deny this; and some assert that they may be employed alike, but that baEuda is more chaste than baEida thus used. (TA.) [You say also, of a desert, and a tract of country, and the like, baEuda , meaning It extended far. ] And zayodN Eani Almanozili ↓ AbEd , meaning ↓ tbAEd [i. e. Zeyd went, or removed, to a distance, or far, from the place of alighting or abode ]. (IKt, Msb.) And min~iY ↓ tbAEd , and ↓ AbtEd , and ↓ tbE~d , [ He went, or removed, to a distance, or far, from me; he alienated, or estranged, himself from me; he shunned, or avoided, me; ] (A;) and Ean~iY ↓ tbAEd [and baEuda En~Y signify the same]. (Msb in art. k$H .) And ↓ A_i*aA A^araA*a A^aHadukumo AlHaAjapi A^aboEada , (L, Msb,) a trad., (Msb,) meaning When one of you desires to accomplish that which is needful, (i. e. to ease nature,) he goes far, or to a great distance. (L.) And fiY Alma*ohabi ↓ A^aboEadotu , meaning ↓ tabaAEadotu , (Msb,) I went far, or to a great distance, to the place of ease, i. e., to ease nature. (L.) ― -b2- [ baEuda referring to a saying or the like, and an event, means It was far from being probable or correct; it was improbable, extraordinary, or strange: (see baEiydN , and see also 10:) often occurring in these senses.] And fiY nawoEihi ↓ AbEd It reached the utmost point, or degree, in its kind, or species. (IAth.) And AbEd fiY Als~awomi He exceeded the due bounds in offering a thing for sale and demanding a price for it, or in bargaining for a thing. (A.) ― -b3- A^axa*ahu maA qaruba wa maA baEuda Recent and old griefs took hold upon him: a saying similar to A^axa*ahu maA qaduma wa maA Haduva . (Mgh in art. qdm .) ― -b4- [ baEuda is often used, agreeably with a general rule, in the manner of a verb of praise or dispraise; and in this case is commonly contracted into buEoda , like Husona ; as in the phrase, in a verse of Imrael-Keys, buEoda maA mutaA^am~alY (in which mA is redundant) Distant, or far distant, was the object of my contemplation! or (as explained in the EM p. 52) how distant, &c.!] ― -b5- baEida , aor. , inf. n. baEadN ; (S, L, Msb, K;) and baEoda , aor. , inf. n. buEodN ; (L, K;) also signify He, or it, perished: (S L, Msb:) he died: (K:) it is the general opinion of the leading lexicologists that both these verbs are used as signifying “he perished,” and both occur in different readings of v. 98 of ch. xi. of the Kur: the former is said to be used in this sense by some of the Arabs; and the latter, by others; but some disallow the latter in this sense; and some say that the former is more chaste than the latter thus used: (TA:) or both signify he became far distant from his home or native country; became a stranger, or estranged, therefrom: (L, TA:) or the Arabs say, baEida Alr~ajulu and baEuda in the sense of tbAEd , when not reviling; but when reviling, they say, baEida , only. (Yoo, TA.) You say, laA taboEadN wa A_ino baEudota Ean~aY [ Mayest thou not perish though thou be distant from me! ] (A.) [And as an imprecation against a man, you say, baEidota , meaning Mayest thou perish! (See the printed edition of the Ham, pp. 89 and 90, where baEidotaAYa hlkt is an evident mistake for aEidota A^aY halakota .)] And buEodFA lahu May God alienate him, or estrange him, from good, or prosperity! or, curse him! (A, * K, TA;) i. e. may he not be pitied with respect to that which has befallen him! like suHoqFA lahu : the most approved way being to put bEd thus in the accus. case as an inf. n.; but the tribe of Temeem say, lahu ↓ buEodN , and suHoqN , like gulaAmN lahu . (TA.) -A2- baEuda is made trans. by means of [the preposition] b : see 4. (Msb.)

definition: an adv. n. of time, signifying After, or afterwards: and allowable also, accord. to some of the grammarians, as an adv. n. of place, signifying after, or behind: (TA:) contr. of qabolu : (S, A, K:)...
sourceDefinition: an adv. n. of time, signifying After, or afterwards: and allowable also, accord. to some of the grammarians, as an adv. n. of place, signifying after, or behind: (TA:) contr. of qabolu : (S, A, K:) it is a vague adv. n., of which the meaning is not understood without its being prefixed to another noun [expressed or implied]; denoting after-time. (Msb.) When it occurs without any complement, (S, K,) a noun or the like which should be its complement being intended to be understood as to the meaning thereof but not as to the letter, (S, * TA,) it is indecl., (S, K,) because it resembles a particle, (TA,) and has damm for its termination to show that it is indecl., since it cannot have damm by any rule of desinential syntax because it cannot occur as an agent nor as an inchoative or enunciative. (S.) Sb, however, mentions [as exceptions to this rule] the phrases mino baEodK [ Afterwards ] and A^afoEalu h`*aA baEodFA [ I will do this afterwards ], as having been used by the Arabs. (K, * TA.) [The latter of these phrases is common in the present day. Another exception to the rule above-mentioned will be found in what follows.] Accord. to the primary rule, it is used as a prefixed n. governing its complement in the gen. case; (S;) [i. e., it is used in the manner of a preposition;] and when thus used, it is decl., (K,) because it does not in this case [always] resemble a particle. (TA.) You say, jaA='a zayodN baEoda EamorKw Zeyd came after 'Amr. (Msb.) And raA^ayotuhu baEodaka and mino baEodika [ I saw him after thee ]. (L.) The words of the Kur [xxx. 3], A@ll~`hi A@loA^amoru mino qabolu wa mino baEodu , meaning To God belonged the command before that the Greeks were overcome and after that they had been overcome, [thus read when the complements of qbl and bEd are intended to be understood as to the meaning thereof but not as to the letter,] are also read mino qaboli wa mino baEodi , when each complement is intended to be understood as to the meaning and the letter, and also mino qabolK wa mino baEodK , meaning To God belongeth the command first and last, [when neither complement is intended to be understood either as to the letter or as to the meaning,] but the first of these readings is the best. (L.) [You say also, baEoda *`lika and mino baEodi *`lika After that: and baEoda A^ano faEalotu and mino baEodi A^ano faEalotu and baEoda maA faEalotu and mino baEodi maA faEalotu After I did, or after my doing, such a thing: &c.] Also jiy^otu baEodayokumaA , meaning baEoda kumaA , I came after you two. (K.) And h`*aA mim~aA layosa baEodahu gaAyapN fiY Aljawodapi , and fiY Alr~adaA='ap , This is of the things after, or beyond, which there is not any extreme degree in respect of goodness, and in respect of badness: and, by way of abridgement, layosa baEodahu [with nothing following this]: and hence, app., the saying of Mohammad, waA_ino kaAna layosa biAl~a*iY laA baEoda lahu , meaning [ And though ] it be not in the utmost degree in respect of goodness: bEd being thus used as a decl. noun. (Mgh.)

sourceDefinition: [ and the like are also frequently used as meaning baEoda EahodiY and the like; as in the phrase, qado tagay~arota baEodY Thou hast become altered since I knew thee, or saw thee, or met thee, or was with thee. And similar to this are many phrases in the Kur; as, for instance, in ii. 48,] vum~a A@t~axa*otumu A@lEijola mino baEodihi Then ye took to yourselves the calf as a god, or an object of worship, after him, namely Moses, i. e., after his having gone away. (Bd.) A^am~aA baEodu (S, K, &c.) is [an expression denoting transition;] an expression by which an address or a discourse is divided; (S;) used without any complement to bEd , which in this case signifies the contr. of qabolu : (TA:) you say, A^am~aA baEodu faqado kaAna ka*aA , meaning [ Now, after these preliminary words, (Abu-l- 'Abbás in TA voce xiTaAbN ,) I proceed to say, that such a thing has happened: or] after my prayer for thee: (K:) or after praising God: (TA:) the first who used this formula was David; (K;) or Jacob; (TA;) or Kaab Ibn-Lu-eí; (K;) or Kuss Ibn-Sá'ideh; or Yaarub Ibn-Kahtán. (TA.) ― -b2- You also use the dim. form, saying ↓ buEayodahu [ A little after him, or it ], when you mean by it to denote a time near to the preceding time. (Msb.) You say also, bayonK ↓ raA^ayotuhu buEayodaAti , (S, K,) and ↓ baEiydaAtihi , (K, TA, [in the CK buEayodaAtih ,]) I saw him a little after a separation: (S, K:) or, after intervals of separation: (S, L:) or, after a while. (A'Obeyd, A.) And A_in~ahaA lataDoHaku bayonK ↓ buEayo*aAti Verily she laughs after intervals. (L.) [See also art. byn .] ↓ buEayodaAt is used only as an adv. n. of time. (S, L.) ― -b3- baEodu also sometimes means Now; yet; as yet. (TA.) [It is used in this sense mostly in negative phrases; as, for instance, in lamo yamuto baEodu He has not died yet. The following is one of the instances of its having this meaning in affirmative phrases: sum~iya AlHawoliY~u mino A^awolaAdi Albaqari tabiyEFA liA^an~ahu yanobaEu A^um~ahu baEodu The yearling of the offspring of cows is called tbyE because he yet follows his mother: occurring in the Mgh &c., in art. tbE .] ― -b4- It occurs also in the sense of maEa ; as in the words of the Kur [ii. 174 and v. 95], famani A@EotadaY baEoda *`lika , i. e., (as some say, MF,) maEa *lk [ And whoso transgresseth notwithstanding that; lit., with that ]. (Msb.) ― -b5- It has been said that it also means Before, in time; thus bearing two contr. significations: that it has this meaning in two instances; in the Kur [lxxix. 30], where it is said, wa A@loA^aroDa baEoda *`lika daHaAhaA [as though signifying And the earth, before that, He spread it forth ]; and [xxi. 105] where it is said, walaqado katabonaA fiY A@lz~abuwri mino baEodi A@l*~ikori [as though meaning And verily we wrote in the Psalms before the Kur-án ]: (MF, TA:) but Az says that this is a mistake; that God created the earth not spread forth; then created the heaven; and then spread forth the earth: (L, TA:) and Al*kr in the latter of these instances means the Book of the Law revealed to Moses: (Bd:) or Alzbwr means the revealed Scriptures; (Bd, Jel;) and Al*kr , the Preserved Tablet, (Bd,) [i. e.] the Original of the Scriptures, which is with God. (Jel.)

sourceDefinition: Distant; remote; far; far off; (S, L, K; *) as also ↓ buEaAdN , and ↓ baAEidN : (L, K:) pl. (of the first, S, L) buEodaAnN (S, L, K) and (of the first also, L, TA) buEudN (L, K) and biEaAdN (TA) and (of the first and second, L) buEadaA='u (L, K) and of the third, ↓ baEadN , [but this (which is also used as a sing. epithet, as will be shown in what follows,) is properly a quasi-pl. n.,] like as xadamN is of xaAdimN . (S.) As signifying Distant with respect to place, it is correctly used alike as masc. and fem. and sing. and dual and pl.; (L, and TA in this art. and in art. qrb , in which latter see the authorities;) but not necessarily; like its contr. qariybN : (L:) you say, hiYa baEiydN minoka [ She is distant from thee; or it is] as though you said, makaAnuhaA baEiydN : (L:) also maA A^anota min~aA bibaEiydK [ Thou art not distant from us ], and maA A^anotumo min~aA bibaEiydK [ Ye are not distant from us ]: and in like manner, maA A^anota ↓ min~aA bibaEadK , and ↓ maA A^anotumu min~aA bibaEadK . (S, TA.) [But it receives, sometimes, the fem. form when used in this sense; for] jalasotu baEiydFA minoka and baEiydapN minoka are phrases mentioned as signifying I sat distant, or remote in place, or at a distance, or aloof, from thee; makaAnFA [and naAHiyapF or the like] being understood. (L.) You say also, ↓ manozilN baEadN A distant, or remote, place of alighting or abode. (K.) And tanaH~a gayora baEiydK (S, K) and ↓ gayora baAEidK and ↓ gayora baEadK (K) [ Retire thou not far; ] meaning be thou near: (S, K:) [or] the second and third of these phrases mean retire thou not in an abject, or a mean, or contemptible, or despicable, state. (S, A.) And ↓ AinoTaliqo yaA fulaAnu gayora baAEidK [ Depart thou, O such a one, not far; ] meaning mayest thou not go away! (L.) [And raA^ayotuhu mino baEiydK I saw him, or it, from afar: and jaA='a mino baEiydK He came from afar: and the like. And baEiydN as applied to a desert and the like, meaning Far extending. ] And ↓ buEodN baAEidN A far distance. (K.) [And niy~apN baEiydapN A distant, far-reaching, or far-aiming, intention, purpose, or design. ] And fulaAnN baEiydu Alhim~api [ Such a one is far-aiming, or faraspiring, in purpose, desire, or ambition ]. (A.) And hiYa baEiydapu AlEahodi [ She was known, or seen, or met, a long time ago ]: in this case, the fem. form, with p , must be used. (L.) And qawolN baEiydN [ A saying far from being probable or correct; improbable; far-fetched; extraordinary, or strange ]. (A.) And A^amorN baEiydN An extraordinary thing or affair or case, of which the like does not happen or occur. (L.) ― -b2- Also Distant with respect to kindred or relationship: in which sense, the word receives the fem. form, [as well as the dual form, and pl. forms, like its contr. qariybN ,] by universal consent. (TA.) [Its pl.] buEadaA='u signifies Strangers, that are not relations. (IAth.) You say also, fulaAnN mino buEodaAni AlA^amiyri [meaning Such a one is of the distant dependents, or subjects, of the governor, or prince ]. (S.) And A_i*aA lamo takuno mino qurobaAni AlA^amiyri fakuno mino buEodaAnihi [ If thou be not of the particular companions, or familiars, of the governor, or prince, then be of his distant dependents, or subjects ]; i. e., be distant from him, that his evil may not affect thee. (AZ, A.) ― -b3- raA^ayotuhu baEiydaAti bayonK : see baEodN in the latter half of the paragraph. ― -b4- See also baAEidN .

definition: More, and most, distant or remote;
sourceDefinition: More, and most, distant or remote; further, and furthest: by poetic licence written A^aboEad~u : (L:) [pl. A^abaAEidu ; as in the saying,] fulaAnN yasotajir~u AlHadiyva mino A^abaAEidi A^aToraAfihi [ Such a one draws forth talk, or discourse, or news, or the like, from its most remote sources ]. (A.) ― -b2- More, and most, extreme, excessive, egregious, or extraordinary, in its kind. (IAth.) [Hence, perhaps,] A_in~ahu lagayoru A^aboEada [in the CK A^aboEadK ] and ↓ buEadK Verily there is no good in him: (K:) or, no depth in him in anything: (IAar:) [or, he is not extraordinary in his kind: see also buEodN :] said in dispraising one. (TA.) And maA Einodahu A^aboEadu and ↓ buEadN [ He has not what is extraordinary in its kind: or] he possesses not excellence, or power, or riches: or he possesses not anything profitable: (L, K:) said only in dispraising one: (AZ:) or it may mean he possesses not anything which one would go far to seek; or, anything of value: or what he possesses, of things or qualities that are desirable, is more extraordinary than what others possess. (MF.) ― -b3- Remote from good: [which is the meaning generally intended in the present day when it is used absolutely as an epithet applied to a man; but meaning also remote from him or those in whose presence this epithet is used, both as to place and as to moral condition: ] and, from continence: (L:) and stupid; foolish; or having little, or no, intellect or understanding; syn. HaAy^inN : (so in a copy of the S and in the L and TA:) or treacherous, or unfaithful; syn. xaAy^inN (So in two copies of the S and in a copy of the A.) It is used as an allusion to the name of a person whom one would mention with dispraise; as when one says, halaka AlA^aboEadu [ May such a one, the remote from good, &c., perish! ]: with respect to a woman, one says, halakati AlbuEodaY . (En-Nadr, Az.) One says also, kab~a A@ll~`hu AlA^aboEada lifiyhi , meaning [ May God cast down prostrate such a one, the remote from good, &c., upon his mouth! or,] cast him down upon his face! (S.) [It is a rule observed in decent society, by the Arabs, to avoid, as much as possible, the mention of opprobrious epithets, lest any person present should imagine an epithet of this kind to be slily applied to himself: therefore, when any malediction or vituperation is uttered, it is usual to allude to the object by the term AlA^aboEad , or AlbaEiyd , as meaning the remote from good, &c., and also the remote from the person or persons present. (A.) ― -b2- More, and most, extreme, excessive, egregious, or extraordinary, in its kind. (IAth.) [Hence, perhaps,] A_in~ahu lagayoru A^aboEada [in the CK A^aboEadK ] and ↓ buEadK Verily there is no good in him: (K:) or, no depth in him in anything: (IAar:) [or, he is not extraordinary in his kind: see also buEodN :] said in dispraising one. (TA.) And maA Einodahu A^aboEadu and ↓ buEadN [ He has not what is extraordinary in its kind: or] he possesses not excellence, or power, or riches: or he possesses not anything profitable: (L, K:) said only in dispraising one: (AZ:) or it may mean he possesses not anything which one would go far to seek; or, anything of value: or what he possesses, of things or qualities that are desirable, is more extraordinary than what others possess. (MF.) ― -b3- Remote from good: [which is the meaning generally intended in the present day when it is used absolutely as an epithet applied to a man; but meaning also remote from him or those in whose presence this epithet is used, both as to place and as to moral condition: ] and, from continence: (L:) and stupid; foolish; or having little, or no, intellect or understanding; syn. HaAy^inN : (so in a copy of the S and in the L and TA:) or treacherous, or unfaithful; syn. xaAy^inN (So in two copies of the S and in a copy of the A.) It is used as an allusion to the name of a person whom one would mention with dispraise; as when one says, halaka AlA^aboEadu [ May such a one, the remote from good, &c., perish! ]: with respect to a woman, one says, halakati AlbuEodaY . (En-Nadr, Az.) One says also, kab~a A@ll~`hu AlA^aboEada lifiyhi , meaning [ May God cast down prostrate such a one, the remote from good, &c., upon his mouth! or,] cast him down upon his face! (S.) [It is a rule observed in decent society, by the Arabs, to avoid, as much as possible, the mention of opprobrious epithets, lest any person present should imagine an epithet of this kind to be slily applied to himself: therefore, when any malediction or vituperation is uttered, it is usual to allude to the object by the term AlA^aboEad , or AlbaEiyd , as meaning the remote from good, &c., and also the remote from the person or persons present. See also AlA^axiru , which is used in a similar manner.] ― -b4- A more distant, or most distant, or very distant, relation; (Lth;) contr. of A^aqorabu : (Msb:) pl. A^abaAEidu (Lth, S, A, Msb, K) and A^aboEaduwna ; (Lth;) contr. of A^aqaAribu (Lth, S, K) and A^aqorabuwna . (Lth.)

sourceDefinition: , (T, S, Mgh, Msb,) aor. , (T, Msb,) inf. n. balaA='N , (S,) or this is a simple subst., and the inf. n. is balowN , (T, Msb,) He (God) tried, proved, or tested, him, (T, S, Msb,) bixayorK [ by, or with, good ], or bi$~arK [ by, or with, evil ]; (Msb;) for God tries his servant ( yaboluwhu ) by, or with, a benefit, to test his thankfulness; and by, or with, a calamity, to test his patience; (T;) [wherefore it often means He afflicted him; ] as also ↓ AblAhu , (T, S, Msb,) inf. n. A_ibolaA='N ; (T, S; [in both restrieted to good; but in the Msb it seems to be common to good and evil;]) and ↓ AbtlAh : (T, S, M, Msb:) and balawotuhu , inf. n. balowN (S, M, K) and balaA='N , (M, K,) [but from what has been said above, it seems that the latter is used only when the agent is God, and that it is properly a simple subst.,] I tried, proved, or tested, him; (S, M, Mgh, * K;) as also ↓ Aibotalayotuhu : (M, K:) each of these verbs implying two things; one of which is the learning the state, or condition, of the object, and becoming acquainted with what was unknown of the case thereof; and the other, the manifesting of the goodness or badness thereof; both of these things being sometimes meant, and sometimes only one of them, as when God is the agent, in which case only the latter is meant: (Er-Rághib, TA:) and ↓ Alt~abaAliY , also, signifies the act of trying, proving, or testing. (S.) It is said in the Kur [xxi. 36], wanaboluwkumo biA@l$~ari waA@lxayori fitonapF [ And we try you by, or with, evil and good, by way of probation ]. (TA.) And in the same [ii. 118], ↓ waA_i*a A@botalaY A_iboraAhiyma rab~uhu bikalamaAtK [ And when his Lord tried Abraham by certain words, meaning commands and prohibitions]. (TA.) And you say, ↓ laA tubolinaA A_il~aA biA@l~atiY hiYa A^aHosanu [ Try Thou not us save by those things that are best ]; (T;) from a trad. (TA.) [See also 4 and 8 below.] ― -b2- [Hence,] balawotuhu also signifies (tropical:) I smelt it. (T in art. bwl , and A and TA.) ― -b3- [And balaAhu He knew it, or became acquainted with it. (See baAlK .)] ― -b4- See also 4, in the latter half of the paragraph. -A2- baliY , aor. , inf. n. bilFA , or bilFY , [in the CK, erroneously, balFY ,] and balaA='N , [in the CK, erroneously, bilA' ,] (T, S, M, Msb, K,) the former with kesr and the latter with fet-h, (T, S, Msb,) said of a garment, (T, S, M, &c.,) It was, or became, old, and worn out: (Msb:) belonging to the present art. and to art. blY . (M.) [The inf. n., used as a subst., signifies Wear; attrition; wear and tear: see an ex. in a hemistich cited near the end of the first paragraph of art. AlA , where a dwelling is likened to a garment.] ― -b2- Also said of a plant [as meaning It became old and withered, or wasted ]. (K in art. Env , &c.) ― -b3- And of a corpse, meaning It became consumed by the earth. (Msb.) ― -b4- And of a bone, meaning It became old, and decayed; syn. ram~a . (S and K &c. in art. rm .) ― -b5- And of a man's reputation, meaning (assumed tropical:) It became worn out of regard or notice. (TA in art. dvr .) ― -b6- And [hence,] baliyato , (M,) or buliyato , (K,) She (a camel, M, K, or a mare, or beast of the equine kind, M) was, or became, a balay~ip ; i. e., was tied at her dead master's grave (M, K) without food or water (M) until she died (M, K) and wasted away. (M in art. blY .)

sourceDefinition: is from AlblA=' , [inf. n. of balaAhu ,] so that it signifies [properly] I shall not, or I do not, care for him, mind him, heed him, or regard him, so as to share with him my trial and his trial: (Ham p. 94:) [and hence,] one says thus, (S, Mgh, Msb,) or maA A^abaAliyhi , (M, K,) and laA A^abaAliYbihi , (Mgh, Msb,) or maA A^ubaAliY bihi , (MF, TA,) but the verb is more chastely made trans. without the preposition bi , (A, TA,) inf. n. mubaAlaApN (M, Mgh, Msb, K) and bilaA='N (M, K, TA [in the CK, erroneously, balA' ]) and baAlapN (T, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) said by some to be a quasi-inf. n. and by others to be an inf. n., (MF, TA,) [in the T it is said to be a subst., from AlmubaAlaApu ,] originally baAliyapN , like EaAfiyapN from EaAfaAhu , (T, S, Mgh, Msb,) and baAlN , [which is more strange,] (M, K,) meaning [merely] I shall not, or I do not, care for, mind, heed, or regard, him, or it; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) I shall not be, or I am not, disquieted by him, or it: (Mgh, Msb:) or, as some say, laA A^ubaAliyhi is formed by transposition from laA A^ubaAwiluhu , from AlbaAlu , i. e. I will not, or I do not, cause him, or it, to move, or occur to, my mind; nor give, or pay, any attention to him, or it: (Z, TA: [and the like is said in the T:]) or the proper [or literal] meaning is, I will not, or I do not, contend with him for superiority in goodness, or excellence, by reason of my little care, or regard, for him: (Mgh:) or it was employed to denote the contending with another for superiority in glory, or excellence, as will be shown by the citation of a verse in the latter portion of this paragraph; and then, in consequence of frequency of usage, came to denote contempt, or mean estimation: (Ham p. 31:) or its original meaning is, I will not, or I do not, strive with him to be first; neglecting him, or leaving him to himself; from tabaAlaY Alqawomu as explained below; see 6. (Msb.) It is said in a trad., laA yubaAliyhimu A@ll~`hu baAlapF , or, accord. to one reading, laA yubaAliY bihimo baAlapF , meaning God will not hold them to be of any value or weight. (TA.) And in another, h`w^ulA='i fiY Aljan~api walaA A^ubaAliY wah`w^ulaA='i fiY Aln~aAri walaA A^ubaAliY , said to mean [ These will be in Paradise, and] I shall not disapprove; [ and these will be in the fire of Hell,] and I shall not disapprove. (Az, TA.) And one says, laA A^ubaAliY maA SanaEota [ I shall not, or I do not, care for what thou didst, or hast done ]. (IDrd, TA.) And maA A^ubaAliY A^aqumota A^amo qaEadota [ I care not whether thou stand or sit ]: and maA A^ubaAliY biqiyaAmika waEadamihi [ I care not for thy standing and thy not doing so ]. (Mughnee in art. A .) And maA baAlayotu bihi (AZ, Msb, TA) I did not care for, mind, or regard, him, or it. (TA.) And baAlaY biAl$~aYo'i [ He cared for the thing; or] he was disquieted by the thing. (T.) The verb is sometimes thus used, in an affirmative manner; (Ham p. 94; [and the like is said in the TA;]) though some say that it is not; (Msb;) but it is not unless it occurs with a negative in the former part of the sentence or in the latter part thereof; as when one says, maA baAlaY bika Sadiyquka wal`kino baAlaY Eaboduka [ Thy friend cared not for thee, but thy slave cared ]; and as in the saying of Zuheyr, laqado baAlayotu maZoEana A^um~i A^awofaY wal`kino A^um~u A^awofaY laA tubaAliY [ Verily I cared for the departure of Umm-Owfà, but Umm-Owfà cares not ]. (Ham p. 94.) One says also, lamo A^ubaAli and lamo A^ubalo [ I did not care, &c.]: (T, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K: [but in the CK the latter of these is omitted:]) in the latter the A [of prolongation] is suppressed for the purpose of alleviating the utterance, like as Y is suppressed in the inf. n. [or quasi-inf. n.] baAlapN , (S, Mgh, Msb,) originally baAliyapN , (S, Msb,) and in laA A^adori : (S:) or the A is suppressed in this case to avoid the concurrence of two quiescent letters; (Kh, Sb, M, IB;) not for the purpose of alleviating the utterance; (IB, TA;) for this is done because the l is made quiescent. (Kh, Sb, M.) And, accord. to Kh, (Sb, M,) some of the Arabs say, lamo A^ubalihi [ I did not care for him, or it ], (Sb, M,) or lamo A^ubali , [in the CK, erroneously, lm Aaboli ,] with kesr to the l ; (K, TA;) [for lm A^ubaAlihi , or lm A^ubaAli ;] only suppressing the A , as they do in EulabiTN [for EulaAbiTN ]. (Sb, S, M.) ― -b2- IAar says that baAlaY , inf. n. mubaAlaApN , is like ↓ A^abolaY meaning He exerted himself in a description of a war, or battle, or of generous conduct; as when one says, A^abolaY *`lika Alyawoma balaA='F HasanFA [ He exerted himself well, that day, in a description of war, &c.]: and he cites the following verse [to which reference has been made above]: waA^anota qadomat~a mina AlhuzaAli [ What hath happened to me that I see thee standing exerting thyself in a description of generous qualities, when thou hast become like one dead by reason of leanness? ]: he says that he [the poet] heard him [whom he thus addresses] saying, “ We have eaten and we have drunk [with guests], and we have done [such and such things]; ” enumerating, or recounting, generous qualities or actions, and lying in doing so: (T, TA:) in another place he says that tubaAliY means looking to see which of them [or of thee and others ] is best in bAl [i. e. state, or condition ], while thou art dying: (TA:) he says, also, that baAlaAhu , inf. n. mubaAlaApN , signifies he contended with him for superiority in glory, or excellence; (T, TA; *) and [it is said that] tbAlY in the verse here cited means thus contending; syn. tufaAxiru : (Ham p. 31:) and accord. to IAar, baAlaAhu also signifies he contended with him in contradiction. (T, TA.)

sourceDefinition: , inf. n. A_ibolaA='N : see 1, in two places. ― -b2- [Hence,] AblAhu A@ll~`hu A_ibolaA='F HasanFA , (T,) or balaA='a HasanFA , (S,) God did to him a good deed. (T.) [And hence,] it is said in the Kur [viii. 17], waliyuboliYa Almuw^ominiyna minohu balaA='F HasanuA (TA) And that He might confer upon the believers a great benefit, or favour, or blessing: (Bd:) or a good gift; meaning spoil. (Jel.) And A^abolayotuhu maEoruwfFA [ I conferred upon him a favour, or benefit ]. (S.) Zuheyr says, jazaY A@ll~`hu biA lA_iHosaAni maA faEalaA bikumo waA^abolaAhumaA xayora AlbalaA='i Al~a*iY yaboluw (T, * S,) meaning, Al*Y yaboluw bihi EibaAdahu , (T,) or Al*Y yaxotabiru bihi EibaAda , (S,) i. e. [ May God recompense with beneficence what they two have done to you, ] and do to them two the best of the deeds wherewith He tries [the thankfulness of] his servants. (T.) ― -b3- AblAhu also signifies He made him to swear; [as though he tried his veracity by so doing;] (M, K;) or so AblAhu yamiynFA . (TA.) [See also 8.] ― -b4- And He swore to him: (M, K:) or this, (TA,) or AblAhu yamiynFA , [as above,] (T, S,) he swore [or swore an oath ] to him, and thereby soothed, or placated, his mind. (T, S, * TA.) ― -b5- And hence, (TA,) He informed him, acquainted him, or told him. (IAar, M, K, TA.) ― -b6- [And hence, He manifested it; revealed it; made it manifest, apparent, evident, clear, or plain; whence a phrase in a verse cited voce muDomarN ; and the phrase] maA lamo yuboli AlEu*ora , i. e. As long as he does not manifest, show, or make apparent, the excuse: but the verb [in this sense] is originally doubly trans.: one says, A^abolayotu fulaAnFA Eu*orFA , meaning I manifested to such a one an excuse so that I was not to be blamed after it; properly signifying I made such a one to be acquainted with my excuse, and to know the manner thereof; (Mgh;) and thus it is explained in the A: (TA: [in like manner, also, it is explained in the T:]) [or] AblAhu Eu*orFA signifies He gave him an excuse which he accepted: (M, K:) and in like manner, AblAhu juhodahu [ He gave him his endeavour, or energy, in an acceptable manner ]; and naAy^ilahu [ his gift ]. (M.) Hence, AblY Eu*orahu signifies also He strove, laboured, or exerted himself, [and thus manifested his excuse,] in work. (Mgh.) And hence, AblY fiY AlHarobi He manifested, or showed, his might, valour, or prowess, in war, or fight, [and he strove, laboured, or exerted himself, therein, ( Eu*orahu being understood,)] so that men proved him and knew him. (Mgh.) See also 3, where another explanation of AblY is given, in the latter portion of the paragraph. -A2- AblY Alv~awoba [ He wore out the garment; ] trans. of baliYa ; (T, S, M, K;) as also ↓ bal~aAhu ; (M, K;) belonging to the present art. and to art. blY . (M.) One says to the mujid~ [i. e. him who makes, or puts on, a new garment], A^aboli wa yuxolifu A@ll~`hu [ Wear out thy garment, and God will replace it with another; or, may God replace &c.]. (S.) And A^aboli wa A^ajid~a waA@Homida AlkaAsiY Wear out, and make new, [or put on new, ] and praise the Clother [meaning God]. (S in art. jd .) ― -b2- [Hence,] Als~afaru ↓ bal~aAhu [ Journeying, or travel, wore him, or wasted him ]; namely, a man; (M, K; but in the copies of the latter, ↓ balaAhu [which I think an evident mistranscription];) as also Ealayohi ↓ bl~Y ; and AblAhu : (M:) and so Alham~u [ anxiety ], (M, K,) and the like, (M,) and Alt~ajaAribu [ tryings, or trying events ]: (K:) and AblAhA Als~afaru (T, S) or ↓ bl~AhA (thus in a copy of the S) [ journeying, or travel, wore her, or wasted her ]; namely, a she-camel. (T, S.) El-'Ajjáj says, waAlmaro'u yuboliyhi balaA='a Als~irobaAlo kar~uAll~ayAliY waA@xotilaAfu AlA^aHowaAlu [ And man, the returning of the nights time after time, and the alternation of states of being, wear him out as the wearing out of the shirt ]: (S, M: *) he means, A_ibolaA='a AlsirobaAl , or fabaliYa balaA='a Als~irobaAl . (M.) And Ibn-Ahmar says, labisotu A^abiY Hat~aY tamal~ayotu Eumorahu wabal~ayotu A^aEomaAmiY wa bal~ayotu xaAliyaA he means I lived the period that my father lived [ so that I had long enjoyment of his life, and I outwore my paternal uncles, and I outwore my maternal uncle ]: or, as some say, I lived with my father for the length of his life &c. (M, TA. * [In the latter, ↓ tabal~ayotu is put in the place of tamal~ayotu ; and hence it is there said that tabal~aAhu is like bal~aAhu : but I think that tbl~yt is a mistranscription.]) ― -b3- A^abolayotu and ↓ bal~ayotu also signify I bound the foreshank of a she-camel to her arm at the grave of her [ dead ] master, and left her without food or water until she died; or I dug for her a pit, and left her in it until she died. (S, TA. [See baliy~apN , and mubal~FY .])

definition: [Hence, AubotiliYa bika*aA (vulg.
sourceDefinition: : see 1, in three places. [Hence, AubotiliYa bika*aA (vulg. AibotalaY ) He was tried, proved, or tested, by, or with, such a thing; generally meaning he was afflicted thereby, or therewith; as, for instance, by, or with, a disease.] ― -b2- Also He asked, or sought, or desired, of him information, or news, or tidings. (M, K.) And AbtlY signifies also He conjured, or adjured, and asked if any had knowledge; syn. AisotaHolafa and AisotaEorafa [explained by what here follows]. (M, K, TA. [In the CK, both the verb and the explanation are here wrong: the former is written AuboliYa ; and the latter, AsotuHolifa w AsotuEorifa .]) A poet says, tabag~aY A^abaAhaA fiY Alr~ifaAqi wa tabotaliY wa A^awoday bihi fiY luj~api AlbaHori tamosaHu [ She seeks for her father among the travellingcompanions, and conjures, or adjures, and asks. if any have knowledge, when a crocodile has destroyed him in the depth of the great river: tabag~aY is for tatabag~aY ]: he means that she says to them, “ I conjure you, or adjure you, by God, ( naA$adotukumo A@ll~`ha ,) [tell me,] do ye know any tidings of my father? ” (M, TA.) But Aboo-Sa'eed says that ttblY here means tries, proves, or tests; and that AlAibotilaA='u signifies the trying, proving, or testing, whether by an oath or otherwise. (TA.) ― -b3- [Also He desired it; he sought it. ] It is said in a trad., Aln~a*oru maA A@botuliYa bihi wajohu A@ll~`hu , i. e. [ The vow that a man makes to be binding, or obligatory, on himself is that whereby the recompense of God ] is desired, or sought. (TA.) ― -b4- And He chose him, made choice of him, or elected him. (Sh and T, from a trad.)

sourceDefinition: : see balaA='N , in two places. -A2- Also A she-camel that has her fore shank bound to her arm at the grave of her master, and is left without food until she dies: (T:) or a she-camel, (M in arts. blw and blY , and K,) or a mare, or beast of the equine kind, (M in art. blw ,) that is bound at the grave of her master, (M, K,) he being dead, and is left without food or water (M) until she dies (M, K) and wastes away; for they used to say that her master would be raised from the dead upon her: (M:) or a she-camel which, in the Time of Ignorance, had her fore shank bound to her arm at the grave of her master, and was left without food or water until she died: or for which was dug a pit, wherein she was left until she died: for they used to assert that men would be raised from the dead riding upon the balaAyaA , [pl. of baliy~apN in the sense above explained, (T, TA,)] or walking if their beasts whereon they rode were not bound, with the head turned backwards, at their graves: (S:) or a cow, or she-camel, or sheep, or goat, which, in the Time of Ignorance, they used to hamstring, or slaughter, at the grave: so in a trad. (TA.) Suh says that this custom proves that, in the Time of Ignorance, they held the doctrine of the resurrection of the body: but they who held it were the fewer number. (TA.) It is said that baliy~apN is originally ↓ mubolaApN or ↓ mubal~aApN . (TA.) Et-Tirimmáh says, manaAzilu laA taraY AlA^anoSaAba fiyhaA walaA Hufara Almubal~aY lilomanuwni [ Places of abode in which thou wilt not see the stones, or other things, that have been set up to be worshipped, nor the pits of the beast left by the grave of the master to die ]; meaning places of abode of the people of El-Islám, exclusively of the pagans. (S.) IAar says that ↓ baliY~N and baliy~apN signify Such as is wearied, or jaded, and emaciated, and dying. (TA.)

(S, M, O, K.) -A2- baADato , (S, M, Msb, K, except that in the M and Msb we find the masc. form, baADa , followed by AlT~aAy^iru ,) aor. tabiyDu , (Msb,) inf. n. bayoDN , (M, Msb,) said of an ostrich, (M,) or a hen, (K,) or any bird, (S, M, Msb,) and the like, (Msb,) She laid her eggs, (M, Msb, TA,) or egg. (Msb.) ― -b2- baADa Als~aHaAbu (tropical:) The clouds rained. (IAar, O, K.) A poet says, [using a phrase from which this application of the verb probably originated,] baADa Aln~aEaAmu bihi fanaf~ara A^aholahu A_il~aA Almuqiyma EalaY Ald~awaY AlmutaA^af~ini (IAar,) i. e. (tropical:) The nEAm , meaning the naEaAy^im , [or Twentieth Mansion of the Moon,] sent down rain upon it, and so put to flight its occupants, except him who remained incurring the risk of dying from disease, wasting away: [the last word being in the gen. case, by poetic license, because the next before it is in that case; like xaribK in the phrase h`*aA juHoru Dab~K xaribK :] the poet is describing a valley rained upon and in consequence producing herbage; for the rain of the asterism called AlnEAy^m is in the hot season, [when that asterism sets aurorally, (see manaAzilu Alqamari , in art. nzl ,)] whereupon there grows, at the roots of the HaliY~ , a plant called na$or , which is poisonous, killing beasts that eat of it: the verse is explained as above by El-Mohellebee: (IB:) or, as IAar says, the poet means rain that falls at the nawo' [by which we are here to understand the setting aurorally] of AlnEAy^m ; and that when this rain falls, the wise flees and the stupid remains. (O.) ― -b3- baADa biAlmakaAni (tropical:) He remained, stayed, or abode, in the place [like as a bird does in the place where she lays her eggs]. (O, K.) ― -b4- baADati AlA^aroDu (assumed tropical:) The earth produced kamoA^ap [or truffles, which are thus likened to eggs]: (A, TA:) or (assumed tropical:) the earth produced the plants that it contained: or (assumed tropical:) it became changed in its greenness to yellowness, and scattered the fruit, or produce, and dried up. (M, TA.) ― -b5- baADa AlHar~u (tropical:) The heat became vehement, or intense. (S, A, K.) -A3- baADa Alqawoma ; &c.: see 8, in three places.

definition: An egg (Msb) of an ostrich, (Mgh,) and of any bird, (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) and the like, i.
sourceDefinition: An egg (Msb) of an ostrich, (Mgh,) and of any bird, (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) and the like, i. e. of anything that is termed SamuwxN [or having merely an ear-hole] as distinguished from such as is termed A^a*uwnN [or having an ear that is called A^u*unN ]: so called because of its whiteness: (TA:) n. un. of ↓ bayoDN : (S, M, * Msb, K:) pl. [of the former] bayoDaAtN (M, Sgh, K) and bayaDaAtN , which latter is irreg., (M, Sgh,) and only used by poetic license; (Sgh;) and (of bayoDN , M) buyuwDN . (M, K.) You say, A^aforaxati AlbayoDapu The egg had in it a young bird. (ISh.) And A^aforaxa bayoDapu Alqawomi (assumed tropical:) What was hidden, of the affair, or case, of the people, or company of men, became apparent. (ISh.) [See also art. frx .] bayoDapu Albaladi signifies The egg which the ostrich abandons. (S, M, K.) And hence the saying, huwa A^a*al~u mino bayoDapi Albaladi (tropical:) He is more abject, or vile, than the egg of the ostrich which it abandons (S, A, * K) in the desert. (TA.) You say also, huwa bayoDapu Albaladi in dispraise and in praise. (IAar, Aboo-Bekr, M.) When said in dispraise, it means (tropical:) He is like the egg of the ostrich from which the young bird has come forth, and which the male ostrich has cast away, so that men and camels tread upon it: (IAar, M:) or he is alone, without any to aid him; like the egg from which the male ostrich has arisen, and which he has abandoned as useless: (TA:) or he is an obscure man, or one of no reputation, whose lineage is unknown. (Ham p. 250.) And when said in praise, it means (tropical:) He is like the ostrich's egg in which is the young bird; because the male ostrich in that case protects it: (IAar, M:) or he is unequalled in nobility; like the egg that is left alone: (M:) or he is a lord, or chief: (IAar, M:) or he is the unequalled of the balad [or country or the like ], to whom others resort, and whose words they accept: (K:) or he is a celebrated, or wellknown, person. (Ham p. 250.) [See also art. bld . And for another meaning of bayoDapu Albaladi see below.] ― -b2- (tropical:) A helmet of iron, (AO, S, * M, * Mgh, * K, *) which is composed of plates like the bones of the skull, the edges whereof are joined together by nails; and sometimes of one piece: (AO:) so called because resembling in shape the egg of an ostrich: (AO, M, Mgh: *) in this sense, also, n. un. of ↓ bayoDN . (S, K: [in the CK, for wAlHadiydu we should read wAlHadiydi .]) This may be meant in a trad. in which it is said that a man's hand is to be cut off for his stealing a bayoDap . (Mgh.) ― -b3- (assumed tropical:) A testicle: (S, K:) pl. biyDaAnN . (TA.) ― -b4- (tropical:) The bulb of the saffron-plant [&c.]: as resembling an egg in shape. (Mgh.) ― -b5- (assumed tropical:) [ A tuber: for the same reason.] ― -b6- (assumed tropical:) A kind of grape of Et-Táïf, white and large. (M.) ― -b7- (tropical:) The core of a boil: as resembling an egg. (M.) ― -b8- (tropical:) The fat of a camel's hump: for the same reason. (M.) ― -b9- bayoDapu Albaladi , in addition to its meanings mentioned above, also signifies (assumed tropical:) The white truffle: (O, K:) or simply truffles; syn. AlkamoA^apu ; (TA;) or these are called AlA^aroDi ↓ bayoDu . (A.) ― -b10- bayoDapN also signifies (tropical:) The continent, or container, or receptacle, ( Hawozap ,) of anything. (S, K, TA.) And [hence] bayoDapu AlA_isolaAmi (tropical:) The place [or territory ] which comprises El-Islám [meaning the Muslims ]; like as the egg comprises the young bird: (Mgh:) or this signifies the congregation, or collective body, of the Muslims. (AZ, M.) And bayoDapu Alqawomi (tropical:) The quarter, tract, region, or district, of the people, or company of men: (S, K:) the heart; or midst, or main part, of the abode thereof: (S, TA:) the principal place of abode ( A^aSol ) thereof; (M, TA;) the place that comprises them; the place of their government, or regal dominion; and the seat of their dEwp [i. e. diEowap or kindred and brotherhood ]: (TA:) the midst of them: (M:) or, as some say, their [ kinsfolk such as are termed ] Ea$iyrap : (TA:) but when you say, A^ataAhumu AlEaduw~u fiY bayoDatihimo , the meaning is [ the enemy came to them in ] their principal place of abode ( A^aSol ), and the place where they were congregated. (TA.) And bayoDapu Ald~aAri (tropical:) The midst of the country or place of abode or the like: (AZ, M, TA:) the main part thereof. (TA.) And bayoDapu Almuloki i. q. Hawozatuhu (assumed tropical:) [ The seat of regal power: or the heart, or principal part, of the kingdom ]. (S and K in art. Hwz .) ― -b11- bayoDapu Alxidori (M, A, K) (tropical:) The damsel (M, K) of the xdr [or curtain &c.]: (K: [in the CK, jaAriyatuhaA is erroneously put for jaAriyatuhu :]) because she is kept concealed within it. (TA.) You say also, hiYa mino bayoDaAti AlHijaAli (tropical:) [ She is of the damsels of the curtained bridal canopies ]. (A, TA.) bayoDapN is used by a metonymy to signify (tropical:) A woman, by way of likening her thereto [i. e. to an egg] in colour, and in respect of her being protected as beneath the wing. (B.) [See Kur xxxvii. 47.] ― -b12- bayoDapN also signifies (assumed tropical:) White land, in which is no herbage; opposed to sawodapN : (TA:) and ↓ biyDapN , with kesr, white, smooth land; (K;) thus accord. to IAar, with kesr to the b : (Sh:) and ↓ A^aroDN bayoDaA='u signifies smooth land, in which is no herbage; as though herbage blackened land: or untrodden land: as also bayoDapN . (M.) ― -b13- bayoDapu Aln~ahaAri The whiteness of day; [ daylight; ] i. q. ↓ bayaADuhu ; (K;) i. e. its light. (Har p. 222.) You say, A^atayotuhu fiY bayoDapi Aln~ahaAri I came to him in the whiteness of day. (TA.) ― -b14- bayoDapu AlHir~i (assumed tropical:) The vehemence, or intenseness, of heat. (M.) And bayoDapu AlqayoZi (tropical:) The most vehement, or intense, heat of summer, or of the hottest period of summer, from the [ auroral ] rising of Ald~abaraAn to that of suhayol ; [i. e., reckoning for the commencement of the era of the Flight, in central Arabia, from about the 26th of May to about the 4th of August, O. S.; ] (A, * TA;) as also AlqayoZi ↓ bayoDaA='u . (A, TA.) And bayoDapu AlS~ayofi (assumed tropical:) The main part of the Syf [or summer ]: (M, TA:) or the vehement, or intense, heat thereof. (Ham p. 250.)

definition: Whiteness; contr. of sawaAdN ; in an animal, and in a plant, and in other things; and, accord. to IAar, in water also; (M;) the colour of that which is termed A^aboyaDu : (S, Msb, * K:) they said...
sourceDefinition: Whiteness; contr. of sawaAdN ; in an animal, and in a plant, and in other things; and, accord. to IAar, in water also; (M;) the colour of that which is termed A^aboyaDu : (S, Msb, * K:) they said bayaADN and ↓ bayaADapN , (S, M, K,) like as they said manozilN and manozilapN : (S:) bayaADapN being applied to a whiteness in the eye. (M.) You say, h`*aA A^a$ad~u bayaADFA mino ka*aA [ This is whiter than such a thing ]: (S, K: *) but not ↓ A^aboyaDu mnohu : (S:) the latter is anomalous; (K;) [like A^asowadu minohu ; q. v.;] but it was said by the people of El-Koofeh, (S, K,) who adduced as authority the saying of the rájiz, jaAriyapN fiY diroEihaA AlfaDofaADi A^aboyaDu mino A^uxoti baniY A_ibaADi [ A damsel in her ample shift, whiter than the sister of the tribe of Benoo-Ibád ]: Mbr, however, says that an anomalous verse is no evidence against a rule commonly approved: and as to the saying of another, A_i*aA Alr~ijaAlu $atawoA waA@$otad~a A^akoluhumu faA^anota A^aboyaDuhumo sirobaAla Tab~aAxi [ When men experience dearth in winter, and their eating becomes vehement, thou art the whitest of them, or rather the white of them, in respect of cook's clothing, having little or nothing to do with entertaining them], the word in question may be considered as an epithet of the measure A^afoEalu that is followed by mino to denote excess: but it is only like the instances in the sayings huwa A^aHosanuhumo wajohFA and A^akoramuhumo A^abFA , meaning Hasanuhumo wajohFA and kariyimuhumo A^abFA ; so it is as though he said faA^anota muboyaD~uhumo sirobaAlFA ; and as he has prefixed it to a complement which it governs in the gen. case, what follows is in the accus. case as a specificative. (S.) This latter verse is by Tarafeh, who satirizes therein 'Amr Ibn-Hind; and is also differently related in respect of the first hemistich, and the first word of the second. (L, TA.) ― -b2- bayaADu Aln~ahaAri : see 3; and see bayoDapN , near the end of the paragraph. ― -b3- bayaADN is also used elliptically for *uw bayaADK ; and thus means (assumed tropical:) White clothing; as in the saying, fulaAnN yalobasu Als~awaAda waAlbayaADa Such a one wears black and white clothing. (Mgh.) [Hence, also, it has other significations, here following.] ― -b4- (assumed tropical:) Milk. (K.) See an ex., voce sawaAdN . ― -b5- [(assumed tropical:) The white of an egg.] ― -b6- bayaADu AlA^aroDi (assumed tropical:) That part of land wherein is no cultivation nor population and the like. (M.) ― -b7- bayaADu Aljilodi (assumed tropical:) That part of the skin upon which is no hair. (M.) ― -b8- (tropical:) bayaADN also signifies (tropical:) A man's person; like sawaAdN ; syn. $axoSN ; as in the saying, laA yuzaAyilu sawaAdiY bayaADaka (tropical:) My person will not separate itself from thy person.
