definition: He spared him; let him live; or left him alive; (S, Msb, K, TA;) did not slay him; (Msb;) in which sense the verb has but one form: (Msb, TA:) or he left him; let him alone; or forbore from him....
sourceDefinition: He spared him; let him live; or left him alive; (S, Msb, K, TA;) did not slay him; (Msb;) in which sense the verb has but one form: (Msb, TA:) or he left him; let him alone; or forbore from him. (Mgh.) ― -b2- Hence, as some say, (K,) A_in~a A@ll~`ha laA yasotaHoyiY A^ano yaDoriba mavalFA , (S, K,) in the Kur [ii. 24], i. e. laA yasotaboqiY [meaning Verily God will not spare to propound, or refrain from propounding, a parable, or as a parable ]. (S.) [Hence, also,] A_in~a A@ll~`ha yasotaHoyiY mino *iY Al$~ayobapi Almusolimi A^ano yuEa*~ibahu , i. e. [ Verily God ] forbears from punishing [ the hoary Muslim ]. (Er-Rághib.) ― -b3- [ AisotaHoyaY , or AisotaHoyaA , which latter is the more proper mode of writing it, also signifies He felt, or had a sense of, or he was, or became, moved or affected with, shame, shyness, or bashfulness; and particularly, but not always, honest shame, or pudency, or modesty; or his soul shrank from foul things; as also AisotaHaY ; and ↓ HayiYa , inf. n. HayaA='N .] AstHyY is of the dial. of El-Hijáz; and AstHY , with a single Y , is of the dial. of Temeem; (Akh, S, Msb;) the former being the original, (Akh, S,) and that which is used in the Kur: (Msb:) in the latter, the first Y [of the original] is suppressed, [and its vowel is transferred to the H ,] to facilitate the pronunciation, because of the occurrence of the two Y s together: this is the opinion of Sb; and with it agrees that of Aboo-'Othmán [ElMázinee]: the opinion ascribed to Sb in the S, namely, that AisotaHayotu is changed from AisotaHoyayotu in like manner as AisotabaEotu is changed from AisotabNyaEotu , is that of Kh, and is disallowed by El-Mázinee. (IB.) You say, AstHyY mnh , (S, K, [in the CK, erroneously, Eanohu ,]) or AstHyA mnh , (Mgh, Msb,) and AstHY mnh , and AstHyAhu , (S, Msb, K, TA,) and AstHAhu ; (TA, [and so in the CK in the place of AstHyAhu ;]) as also mnh ↓ HayiYa , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor. yaHoyaA , (S,) inf. n. HayaA='N ; (S, * Mgh, Msb, K;) He was ashamed of it or on account of it, or ashamed to do it, or shy of doing it; [generally meaning a foul thing;] he was ashamed for himself, or of himself, or was bashful, or shy, with respect to it, or him; he was abashed at, or shy of, it, or him; (K;) he shrank from it, or him: (Msb, K: *) and AstHyY mino ka*aA [or AstHyA ] He disdained, or scorned, such a thing; abstained from it, or refused to do it, by reason of disdain and pride; he dislike, or hated, it, and his soul was above it; he shunned it, avoided it, or kept himself far from it; syn. A^anifa minohu . (TA.)

definition: a verbal noun, (S, M, Mgh, TA,) and therefore immediately followed by EalaY , (M, TA,) used as an imperative [addressed to a single person, male or female, and to more than one];
sourceDefinition: a verbal noun, (S, M, Mgh, TA,) and therefore immediately followed by EalaY , (M, TA,) used as an imperative [addressed to a single person, male or female, and to more than one]; (S;) used in calling, or summoning, or inviting, and urging; (Lth, T, TA;) and having no verb derived from it [alone, for HayoEala is derived from HaY~a and EalaY together]; (Lth, T, Msb, TA;) meaning Come: (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K, TA, &c.:) or come quickly: or hasten. (Mgh, TA.) Hence, HaY~a EalaY AlS~alaAhN (in the A^a*aAn , TA) Come to prayer: (IKt, S, M, Msb, K:) or come ye to prayer: or come ye quickly: or hasten ye. (TA.) And HaY~a EalaY AlfalaAHo [in the same: see art. flH ]. (Mgh, TA.) definition: Living, having life, alive, or quick;
sourceDefinition: Living, having life, alive, or quick; contr. of may~itN [or mayotN ]; (S, Mgh, * Msb, * K;) and ↓ HayawaAnN is syn. with HaY~N [as meaning having animal life ]: (IB:) dim. of the former ↓ HuyaY~N : (Msb:) and pl. A^HoyaA='N . (Msb, K.) When you say of a person, layosa biHaY~K , you mean that he is dead: (Lh:) but minohaA ↓ Duriba DarobapF layosa biHaAYK , (Lh, K,) [in the CK Daraba , and] in [some of] the copies of the K, erroneously, biHaA='K , (TA,) means [ He was struck a blow ] in consequence of which he will not live: (Lh, K: *) like as the saying laA taA^okulo ka*aA faA_in~aka maAriDN means Thou wilt be sick if thou eat such a thing. (Lh, K.) Accord. to ISh, one says, A^ataAnaA HaY~u fulaAnK , meaning Such a one came to us in his life [- time ]: and samiEotu HaY~a fulaAnK yaquwlu ka*aA , meaning I heard such a one say thus in his life [- time ]: (TA:) [or the former may mean Such a one himself came to us: and the latter, I heard such a one himself say thus: for] HY [i. e. HaY~ as a prefixed noun] is sometimes redundant, like A=l and *uw : (Ham p. 308:) [and] IB says that HaY~u fulaAnK means Such a one himself. (TA.) And they say, A^aholika ↓ kayofa A^anota waHay~apu , i. e. How art thou, and those remaining alive of thy family? (TA.) ― -b2- Applied to God, Deathless. (Er-Rághib.) ― -b3- Possessing the faculty of growth, as an animal, and as a plant: (Er-Rághib:) and, applied to a plant, fresh, juicy, or succulent, and growing tall. (TA.) ― -b4- [ Sensitively alive; ] possessing the faculty of sensation. (Er-Rághib.) ― -b5- (assumed tropical:) [ Intellectually alive; ] possessing the faculty of intellect. (Er-Rághib.) [Hence,] (assumed tropical:) A Muslim; like as may~itN means an unbeliever. (TA.) ― -b6- (assumed tropical:) Lively, as meaning free from grief or sorrow. (Er-Rághib.) ― -b7- (assumed tropical:) Whole, sound, or unbroken. (L and TA in art. SA^b .) ― -b8- A^araDN Hay~apN (assumed tropical:) Fruitful land; or land abounding with herbage; (K, TA;) like as ArD mayotapN means unfruitful land. (TA.) ― -b9- Al$~amosu Hay~apN (assumed tropical:) The sun is, or was, of a clear colour, unaltered by approaching the place of setting; as though its setting were regarded as death: (TA:) or still bright and white: or still hot and powerful: but the former of these two meanings is the more probable. (Mgh.) ― -b10- naArN Hay~apN (assumed tropical:) [ A live, or burning, fire. (AHn.) ― -b11- TariyqN HaY~N (assumed tropical:) An apparent, or a distinct, road or way: (K:) pl. A^aHoyaA='N . (TA.) -A2- See also Hay~apN , first sentence. -A3- [ A tribe ] of the Arabs: (S:) the children, or descendants, of one father or ancestor, whether many or few: and a $aEob comprising qabaAy^il : (Az, TA:) or a qabiylap of the Arabs: (Msb:) or a baTon of the buTuwn of the Arabs: (K, TA:) pl. A^aHoyaA='N . (S, Msb, K.) -A4- The vulva, or external portion of the organs of generation, of a woman. (Az, K. See also HayaA='N , of which HaY~N is also said to be a pl.) Hence, saEafu AlHaY~i , applied by an Arab of the desert to The paraphernalia of a bride. (Az, TA.) -A5- laAHaY~a Eanohu means laAmanoEa minohu , (Ks, K, *) i. e. [ There is no forbiddance of him; or] nothing is forbidden him. (Fr.) -A6- laA yaEorifu AlHaY~a mina All~aY~i He knows not, or will not know, what is true from what is false; (IAar, K, Har p. 236;) and so AlHaw~a mn All~aw~i : (TA:) or the Hawiy~ap [or winding gut, &c.,] from the twisting of the rope: (K:) or overt speech from covert: or the living from the dead: or the act of turning round, or winding, [see HawaAhu , (in art. HwY ,) of which HaY~N is an inf. n.,] from the act of twisting. (Har ubi suprà.) -A7- The act of collecting. (TA. [But in this and some other senses it is an inf. n. of HawaY : see 1 in art. HwY .]) -A8- A^aHoyaA='N as pl. of HaA='N : see art. HwA^ .

sourceDefinition: [ A serpent; ] a certain thing well known: (K, TA:) [improperly explained in the Msb as syn. with A^afoEFY :] applied to the male and the female; (S, Msb;) the p being added to denote one of a kind, as in baT~apN and dajaAjapN ; [although HaY~N is not used as a coll. gen. n.; and] although the saying EalaY Hay~apK ↓ raA^ayotu Hay~FA , as meaning [ I saw ] a male [ serpent ] upon a female [ serpent ], is related as having been heard from the Arabs: (S:) but ↓ Hay~uwtN is also applied to the male; (Az, S, K;) the t being augmentative; for the word is originally Hay~uw [or Hay~uw~N ]: (Az, TA:) it is said that it does not die unless by an accident: and they say of a long-lived man, maA huwa A_il~aA Hay~apN [ He is none other than a serpent ]; and in like manner they say of a woman; as though it were called Hy~p because of its long life: [for] some, including Sb, say that it is derived from HayaApN , as the rel. n. is HayawiY~N , not HawawiY~N : and to him who objects that one says rajulN Haw~aA='N [meaning “ a man who collects serpents ”], it is replied that Hay~apN and Haw~aA='N are of different roots, like luw^oluw^N and laA^~lN , &c.: but it may be from taHaw~aY , because of its winding, or coiling, itself; and some say that it is originally HawoyapN ; some, that it is originally HayowapN : (TA:) [the dim. is ↓ Huyay~apN :] the pl. is Hay~aAtN (K) and HayowaAtN , (K, TA,) or HayawaAtN . (So in some copies of the K [agreeably with the dial. of Hudheyl].) Hence the prov. huwa A^aboSaru mino Hay~apK [ He is more sharp-sighted than a serpent ]; because of the sharpness of its sight: and A^aZolamu mino Hay~apK [ more wrongful in conduct than a serpent ]; because it comes to the burrow of the [lizard called] Dab~ , and eats its young one, and takes up its abode in its burrow. (TA.) And saqaAhu A@ll~`hu dama AlHay~aAti [ May God give him to drink the blood of the serpents ]; i. e., (assumed tropical:) destroy him. (TA.) And ↓ laA talidu AlHay~apu A_il~aA Huyay~apF [ The serpent does not bring forth anything save a little serpent ]: a prov. applied to the cunning and mischievous, or malignant. (TA.) And fulaAnN Hay~apu AlwaAdiY , or AlA^aroDi , or Albaladi , or AlHamaATi , (assumed tropical:) Such a one is cunning and mischievous, or malignant, (IAar, K,) and intelligent, in the utmost degree: (IAar:) [or] flAn Hy~p AlwAdY means (assumed tropical:) such a one is strong in resisting, a defender of his possessions. (TA.) And Hay~apu AlwaAdiY is also an appellation applied to (assumed tropical:) The lion; (K, TA;) because of his cunning, or craftiness. (TA.) One says also, humo Hay~apu AlA^aroDi , meaning (assumed tropical:) They are cunning, guileful, malignant, or mischievous, and strong, not neglecting to take blood-revenge: so in a saying of Dhu-l-Isba' El-'Adwánee cited voce Ea*iyrN . (TA.) And fulaAnN Hay~apN *akarN (S, TA) (assumed tropical:) Such a one is courageous and strong. (TA.) And raA^osuhu raA^osu Hay~apK (assumed tropical:) He is clever, or ingenious; acute, or sharp; intelligent. (TA.) And raA^ayotu fY kitaAbihi Hay~aAti waEaqaAriba (assumed tropical:) I saw in his letter slanders, or calumnies, addressed to the ruling power, in order to cause the object thereof to fall into embarrassment from which escape would be difficult. (TA.) ― -b2- AlHay~apu is also a name of (assumed tropical:) [ The constellation Draco; commonly called Alt~in~iynu ;] certain stars [ partly ] between the faroqadaAni [or B and y of Ursa Minor ] and banaAtu naEo$K [meaning the stars in the tail of Ursa Major ]: (K:) so called by way of comparison. (TA.) ― -b3- And Hay~apN also signifies (assumed tropical:) A certain mark made with a hot iron upon the neck, and upon the thigh, of a camel, twisting, or winding, like the Hay~ap [ properly so called ]. (Ibn- Habeeb, TA.) -A2- See also HaY~N .

sourceDefinition: , or ↓ Hay`wp , (as in different copies of the K, in the latter manner in copies of the S,) written with w in the Kur, to show that w follows Y in the pl. [ HayawaAtN , like SalawaAtN ], or because the sound of the A is inclined towards that of w , (ISd, TA,) and ↓ HayawopN , with sukoon to the w , (K,) which is substituted for the A of HayaApN , as is done by the people of El-Yemen in the case of every A that is changed from w , as in SalaApN and zakaApN , though the final radical letter of the verb of HayaApN is Y , (TA,) an inf. n. of HayiYa in the first of the senses explained in this art.; (IB, Mgh, Msb;) Life; contr. of mawotN ; (S, K;) as also ↓ HayawaAnN and ↓ HiY~N , (K,) or this last is asserted to be a pl. of Hay`wpN , (S,) and as also ↓ maHoyFA , (S, * Har pp. 25 and 350,) of which the pl. is maHaAYK : (S:) HayaApN signifies the faculty of growth, as in an animal, and in a plant: and the faculty of sensation: and (assumed tropical:) the faculty of intellect: and (assumed tropical:) freedom from grief or sorrow: and everlasting life in the world to come; to which one attains by that HyAp which is intelligence and knowledge: and the HyAp that is an attribute of God. (Er-Rághib.) yaA layotaniY qad~amotu liHayaAtiY , in the Kur [lxxxix. 25], means [ O, would that I had prepared, or laid up in store, ] for my everlasting state of existence. (Er-Rághib.) And ↓ faA_in~a Ald~aAra AlA=xirapa lahiYa AlHayawaAnu , in the Kur [xxix. 64], means [ And verily the last abode is ] the abode of everlasting life: (TA:) or AlHywAn here means the life that will not be followed by death: or much life; like as mawataAnN signifies much death: (Msb:) and it is also the name of a certain fountain in Paradise, [ the water of ] which touches nothing but it lives, by permission of God. (TA.) AlHay`wpu AlT~ay~ibapu , accord. to I'Ab, explaining xvi. 99 of the Kur, (TA,) means Lawful means of subsistence (K, TA) in the present world: (TA:) or Paradise. (K, TA.) ― -b2- Also (assumed tropical:) Advantage, or profit; or a cause, or means, thereof: whence the saying, layosa lifulaAnK HayaApN There is not, in such a one, profit, nor good: and so it is said to mean in the Kur [ii. 175], walakumo fiY AlqiSaASi Hay`wpN (assumed tropical:) [ And there is to you, in retaliation, an advantage ]: (TA:) or this means that the knowledge of the law of retaliation restrains from slaughter, and so is a cause of life to two persons; and because they used to slay one who was not the slayer, retaliation upon the slayer is a cause of saving the lives of the rest: or the meaning is life in the world to come; for when the slayer has suffered retaliation in the present world, he is not punished for his act in the world to come. (Bd.) ― -b3- HayaApu Al$~amosi means (assumed tropical:) The remaining of the light and whiteness of the sun: or the remaining of its heat and power: but the former of these two meanings is the more probable. (Mgh. [See Al$~amosu Hay~apN , voce HaY~N .])

definition: The two stars in the foot and before the foot of the foremost of Gemini: (Kzw:) or three stars over against AlhanoEap [which is the Sixth Mansion of the Moon ];
sourceDefinition: The two stars in the foot and before the foot of the foremost of Gemini: (Kzw:) or three stars over against AlhanoEap [which is the Sixth Mansion of the Moon ]; (IKt, K;) and sometimes the moon deviates from AlhnEp , and makes its abode in AltHAyY : (IKt:) they are between the Milky Way and the stars that follow AlEay~uwq [or Capella ]: Aboo-Ziyád El-Kilábee used to say that this name means AlhnEp , and is also pronounced Alt~aHaAy^iY , with ' : but AHn says that the moon makes its abode in these stars, and not in AlhnEp itself: (TA:) its sing. is ↓ tiHoyaApN ; (IKt, AHn, TA;) if so, of the measure tifoEalapN , like tiHolabapN , not fiEolaApN , like EizohaApN , because there is no such root as taHY ; derived from AlHayaA , because its nawo' [here meaning its auroral setting, in midwinter,] is attended with much rain: but AltHAy^Y , with ' , is irreg.; as though pl. of ↓ taHiy~apN likened to a word of the measure faEiylapN . (IB.)

definition: inf. n. of 2. (Mgh, Msb, K.) ― -b2- Also A salutation, or greeting, (A'Obeyd, AHeyth, Mgh, Msb,) pronounced by one person to another on their meeting; (AHeyth;) particularly the saying salaAmN...
sourceDefinition: inf. n. of 2. (Mgh, Msb, K.) ― -b2- Also A salutation, or greeting, (A'Obeyd, AHeyth, Mgh, Msb,) pronounced by one person to another on their meeting; (AHeyth;) particularly the saying salaAmN Ealayoka ; (Mgh, * Msb;) and the like; (Mgh;) the most comprehensive form thereof, used by the believer [to his fellow-believer], being the saying Als~alaAmu Ealayokumo waraHomapu A@ll~`hi wabarakaAtuhu : (AHeyth:) hence it is pluralized; the pl. being taHiy~aAtN and taHaAyaA . (Mgh.) ― -b3- Also Continuance, or endurance; or endless, or everlasting, existence: (IAar, Msb, K, &c.:) and so it is said to mean in the following verse of Zuheyr Ibn-Jenáb ElKelbee; who was a [kind of] king among his people: qado nilotuhu A_il~aA Alt~aHiy~aho walakul~u maA naAla AlfataY [ And indeed everything that the young man has attained, I have attained it, except endless existence ]: or, as some say, it here means security from death and from evils. (TA. [But more probably the meaning is that next following: for in the Mz, 49th nwE , where this verse is cited, but with mino kul~i in the place of walakul~u , he is said to have been (not a king, but,) “ a nobleman. ” See also, respecting him, p. x. of my Preface.]) And (tropical:) Dominion, or kingship: (Fr, AA, S, Mgh, Msb, K, &c.:) because the people of the Time of Ignorance used to greet kings [or rather those of Himyer] by the saying A^abayota Al~aEona , which they addressed to none other than a king; so that when any one of them became a king, it was said of him, fulaAnN naAla Alt~aHiy~apa [meaning (tropical:) Such a one has attained the kingship ]. (Mgh: in which, and in the S, the foregoing verse is cited as an ex. of this last meaning.) Alt~aHiy~aAtu lil~`hi means Endless existence belongs to God: (Lth, Msb, TA:) or dominion, or kingship: (Lth, Yaakoob, S, Msb, TA:) or freedom, or security, from all evils, (Khálid Ibn-Yezeed, AHeyth,) and from all causes of the cessation of existence: (AHeyth:) or endless existence, and security from evils, and dominion, and the like: (Fr:) or the expressions [ of praise ] that indicate and imply the ascription of dominion and endless existence: (Kt:) or salutations and benedictions are Gods, and at his disposal. (Mgh.) [ Alt~aHiy~aAtu is also a term applied to the following form of words repeated in the ordinary prayers: Alt~aHiy~aAtu lil~`hi waAlS~alawaAtu waAlT~ay~ibaAtu Als~alaAmu Ealayoka yaAA^ay~uhaA Aln~abiY~u waraHomapu A@ll~`hi wabarakaAtuhu Als~alaAmu EalayonaA waEalaY EibaAdi A@ll~`hi AlS~aAliHiyna A^a$ohadu A^ano laA A_ilaAha A_il~aA A@ll~`hu waA^a$ohadu A^an~a muHam~adFA Eaboduhu warasuwluhu , or (instead of Ebdh wrswlh ) rasuwlu A@ll~`hi : see 5 in art. $hd .] ― -b4- The assigning to this word, as used in the Kur iv. 88, the meaning of A gift is a mistake. (Mgh.) -A2- See also Alt~aHaAyiY .

definition: The face (S, K, Ham p.
sourceDefinition: The face (S, K, Ham p. 23) of a man, because it is specified in salutation; [see 2;] (Ham ubi suprá;) a term used only in praise; (Ham p. 640;) i. e. the face altogether: or the Hur~ of the face [i. e. the ball of the cheek; or what appears of the elevated part thereof; or what fronts one, of the face, &c.]. (K.) ― -b2- Of a horse, it is The place where the flesh is separated ( Hyv Anfrq AllHm ) beneath the forelock. (Ham p. 23.) And daAy^irapu AlmuHay~aA , in a horse, [ The feather in ] the place of separation [ of the hair ] beneath the forelock, in the upper part of the forehead. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: act. part. n. of 2; fem. muHay~iyapN : (S, TA:) for in every noun in which three Y s occur together, [the last of them being the final radical, and ending the word,] if it is not formed from a verb, the final radical letter is elided from it, as in EuTaY~N the dim. of EaTaA='N , and in A^uHaY~u the dim. of A^aHowaY : but if it is formed from a verb, that letter remains, as in muHay~iYN from Hay~aY . (S.)

definition: , (S, A, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, A, K,) aor. , (S, K,) inf. n. xaro$N , (Lth,) He, or it, (namely, a cat, A,) scratched him, or it, (namely, the skin, A,) with the nails, (Lth, S, A, * K,) in any part of the body, (Lth,) so as to cause bleeding or not; or wounded him in the outer skin, so as to make it bleed or not; or lacerated it (namely, the skin) little or much; or tore off its surface with a stick or the like; syn. xada$ahu ; (S, K;) [as also Hara$ahu ;] and so ↓ Axtr$hu : (S, K:) and biZuforihi ↓ Axtr$hu He scratched him, &c., with his nail. (TA.) You say also, xara$ahu biHadiydapK wanaHowihaA [ He scratched it with an iron thing, and the like ]. (K.) ― -b2- It (a fly) bit him; (A, TA;) as also Hara$ahu . (TA.) ― -b3- xara$a AlbaEiyra , (S, K,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (TA,) He drew the camel (S, K) towards him (S) with the mixoraA$ , i. e., the miHojan : (S, K:) or he struck the camel and then drew him to wards him therewith; desiring thereby to excite him to quicken his pace: and he struck him with its extremity in the side of his neck, or [ elsewhere ] in his skin, so as to scrape off from him his fur. (TA.) [See also Hara$ahu .] ― -b4- xara$a liEiyaAlihi , aor. as above, (S, K,) and so the inf. n., (TA,) (assumed tropical:) He earned for his family, or household; (S, K;) collected, and practised artifice, for them; (TA;) and sought sustenance for them; (S, K;) as also ↓ Axtr$ . (K.) ― -b5- You say also, fulaAnN yaxori$u mino fulaAnK Al$~aYo'a baEoda Al$~aYo'i (tropical:) Such a one takes from such a one thing after thing; as also ↓ yaxotari$uhu . (A.) And maA xara$a $ayoy^FA (tropical:) He has not taken anything. (TA.) And mino fulaAnK Al$~aYo'a ↓ fulaAnN yataxar~a$u (tropical:) Such a one takes and acquires from such a one the thing. (TA.) And ↓ muxaAra$apN signifies (assumed tropical:) The taking against one's will. (TA.)

definition: The skin, (S, K,) or slough, (A, TA,) of a serpent.
sourceDefinition: The skin, (S, K,) or slough, (A, TA,) of a serpent. (S, A, TA.) To this one likens a thin, transparent, shirt. (A, TA.) AHn applies its pl., xaraA$iY~u , metaphorically, to [the skins of] all [animals of the class termed] Ha$araAt . (TA.) ― -b2- The upper covering, (S, K, TA,) which is dry, or tough, or hard, [app. meaning the shell, ] (TA,) of an egg, (S, K, TA,) after it has been broken, and what was in it, (S, TA,) of moisture, (TA,) has been extracted: (S, TA:) or the inner skin, (T, TA,) or inner covering, (A,) of an egg; (T, A, TA;) also called giroqiy^N : (TA:) pl. as above. (TA.) ― -b3- To this is likened (assumed tropical:) Anything in which are an inflation and a bursting and holes. (AZ, * S.) ― -b4- The thin skin upon the surface of milk: (K:) or the bubbles that rise upon the surface of milk: (A:) froth, or foam. (S, TA. [See an ex. in a verse cited voce qaSara .]) ― -b5- (tropical:) Phlegm: (S, A, K:) or viscous phlegm in the chest: (TA:) and what is termed nuxaAmap , q. v. (A, TA.) You say, A^aloqaY xaraA$iY~a Sadorihi (tropical:) He cast forth the phlegm (lit. phlegms ) of his chest. (S.) [See also a tropical meaning below.] And A^aloqaY mino Sadorihi xaraA$iY~a (tropical:) He cast forth from his chest what is termed nuxaAmap (Az, A, TA) and phlegm: (A:) or thick spittle. (K.) ― -b6- xiro$aA='u AlEasali The was of honey, and the dead bees in it: (TA:) or the young bees, or the wings, that are upon honey. (M and L in art. jv .) ― -b7- TalaEati Al$~amosu fiY xiro$aA='K (tropical:) The sun rose in dust; (S, A;) syn. gabarap . (S, A, K.) ― -b8- A^aloqaY fulaAnN xaraA$iY~a Sadorihi (tropical:) Such a one cast forth what he concealed of rancours and enmities, and of grief. (A, TA.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , (Mgh, K,) inf. n. xazomN , (JK, TA,) He pierced it, or perforated it; (JK, Mgh, K;) namely, a thing of any kind: for instance, the nose of a camel, for the [ring called] xizaAmap [to which the rein is attached]: and the letter of a Kádee to another Kádee; for such a letter is pierced for the siHaA='ap [or strip of paper with which it is bound], and is then sealed [upon this strip]; and when this is done, the letter is said to be ↓ maxozuwmN . (Mgh.) You say, xazama AlbaEiyra , aor. as above, (Mgh, Msb,) and so the inf. n., (Msb,) He pierced the nose of the camel (Mgh, Msb) for the xizaAmap : (Mgh:) or xazama AlbaEiyra (S, K) biAlxizaAmapi , (S,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (TA,) he put the xzAmp in the side of the nostril, (K,) or in the partition between the nostrils, (S,) [but the former is the more common practice,] of the camel; (S, K;) as also ↓ xz~mhu ; (K;) [or] this signifies the doing so much, or often. (TA.) [Hence,] xazama A^anofahu (assumed tropical:) He brought him under, or into, subjection; rendered him submissive, tractable, or manageable. (TA.) And xazamotu AljaraAda fiY AlEuwdi I spitted the locusts in a series upon the [ skewer, or] piece of stick or wood. (S.) And xazama $iraAka naEolihi He pierced and tied the [ thong called ] $arAk [q. v.] of his sandal [app. so as to attach to it the two branches ( EaDudaA Al$~iraAki ) of the strap that encompasses the heel ]. (TA, [See also xizaAmapN .]) ― -b2- [Also He cut it. for] Alxazomu is syn. with AlqaToEu . (Ham p. 166. [It is there also said to be syn. with Al$d ; i. e. Al$~ad~u ; but this is app. a mistake for Al$~ak~u , a meaning assigned to it in the JK, agreeably with the K.])

definition: , (S,) or xAzimhu AlT~ariyqa , (K,) inf.
sourceDefinition: , (S,) or xAzimhu AlT~ariyqa , (K,) inf. n. muxaAzamapN (S in art. xSr ) [and xizaAmN ], He (a man, S) took a different way from his (another's) until they both met in one place: (S, K:) the doing so is also termed muxaASarapN : (S in art. xSr , and TA:) it is as though it were a rivalling, or imitating, in travelling. (TA.) Ibn-Fesweh says, A_i*aA huwa naH~aAhaA Eani AlqaSodi xaAzamato bihi Aljawora Hat~aY tasotaqiymu DuHaY Algadi i. e. When he turns her, meaning his she-camel, from the right way, she pursues with him a way different from the wrong, so that she overcomes him, and takes the right way, in the early daytime of the morrow. (TA.) muxaAzamapN also signifies The act of rivalling, or imitating. (JK, TA.) And one says, laqiytuhu xizaAmFA (JK, TA) and maxaAzamapF , (JK,) meaning I met him face to face: (TA:) or suddenly, or unexpectedly, and face to face. (JK.)

definition: Anything pierced or perforated: (S, Mgh:) applied in this sense, (JK,) or as meaning pierced and tied, (TA, [see 1,]) to the [thong, of a sandal, called] $iraAk ;
sourceDefinition: Anything pierced or perforated: (S, Mgh:) applied in this sense, (JK,) or as meaning pierced and tied, (TA, [see 1,]) to the [thong, of a sandal, called] $iraAk ; (JK, TA;) or, thus applied, it means cut. (Ham p. 166.) See also 1, first sentence, for its meaning as applied to a letter. ― -b2- Any animal having the nose pierced. (Msb.) And ↓ A_ibilN xazomaY means Camels having rings such as are termed xazaAy^im (pl. of xizaAmap ) in their nostrils; (IAar, K, TA;) as also ↓ muxaz~amapN . (IAar, TA.) All birds, also, are said to be maxozuwmap , (S, K,) and ↓ muxaz~amap ; (K;) because perforated in the partition between the nostrils: (S, K:) and particularly the ostrich is said to be maxozuwm (S, K *) and ↓ muxaz~am . (JK, K. *) One says, ↓ maAhumo A_il~aA kaA@loA^anoEaAmi Almuxaz~amapi , meaning (tropical:) They are none others than stupid, or foolish, persons. (TA. [But kaA@loA^anoEaAmi is app., here, a mistranscription for kaA@ln~aEaAmi ; for the ostrich is proverbial for stupidity: one says A^aHomaqu mino naEaAmapK “ More stupid than an ostrich: ” because, as Meyd says, when an ostrich happens to see the eggs of another ostrich, it will sit upon them, and forget its own eggs.])

definition: He cut herbage, (S, K,) or a tree, (A,) while it was green;
sourceDefinition: He cut herbage, (S, K,) or a tree, (A,) while it was green; (S, A, K;) as also ↓ xaDara , (A, TA,) aor. , inf. n. xaDorN . (TA.) And AuxotuDira It (herbage, TA) was taken, (K,) and pastured upon, (TA,) while fresh and juicy, (K,) and green, before it had attained its full height. (TA.) See also 9, last sentence. ― -b2- Hence, (S, TA,) the pass. form, (assumed tropical:) He died in his youth; (S, K;) in his fresh and flourishing state. (S.) Young men used to say to an old man, A^ajozarotu yaA $ayoxu (assumed tropical:) [Thou hast attained to the time for dying, (lit. for being cut,) O old man]: and he replied, A^aYo baniY~a watuxotaDaruwna (assumed tropical:) [ O my sons, and ye shall be cut off, or die, in your youth ]. (S. [See also A^ajozara .]) ― -b3- Also, the act. v., He cut off the green branches of a palm-tree with his mixolab ; (TA;) and so ↓ xaDara , (K, * TA,) aor. , inf. n. xaDorN : (TA:) and he cut off a thing, as a man's nose, entirely: (TA:) or, simply, he cut off a man's nose. (IAar.) ― -b4- And He ate fruit [ while it was green, or] before it was ripe. (A.) ― -b5- And hence, (TA,) (tropical:) He deflowered a girl: (K, TA:) or, before she had attained to puberty; (Msb in art. qD , and K;) as also Aibotasara and Aibotakara . (TA.) ― -b6- Also (assumed tropical:) He took a camel in a refractory state, not trained, and attached the nose-rein to him, and drove him. (TA.) ― -b7- And (assumed tropical:) He took up a load, or burden. (K.)

definition: ― -b2- Also A place having much verdure;
sourceDefinition: : see A^axoDaru . ― -b2- Also A place having much verdure; and so ↓ yaxoDuwrN and ↓ maxoDarapN . (K.) And A^aroDN xaDirapN and ↓ yaxoDuwrN Land in which is much verdure: and ↓ ArD maxoDarapN , as in the Kur xxii. 62, accord. to one reading, verdant land. (TA.) ― -b3- See also xiDorN , in four places. ― -b4- Also, [as a subst.,] What is green: (Akh, S, and Bd in vi. 99:) seed-produce; (Lth, Bd, K;) and so ↓ xuD~aAraY : (S:) so the former in the Kur ubi suprà: (Lth, Bd:) or goodly green herbage: (A:) and a branch: (K:) any branch. (TA.) ― -b5- And AlxaDiru The plant called ↓ Albaqolapu AlxaDoraA='u ; as also ↓ AlxaDirapu and ↓ AlxaDiyru (K) and ↓ AlxuDorapu : (TA:) it is a green and rough herb or leguminous plant, the leaves and fruit of which are like those of millet; it rises to the height of a cubit; and fills the mouth of the camel. (TA.) Also A species of plant of the kind called janobap ; (K;) which latter term is applied to herbage whereof the root is deep in the earth, like the naSiY~ and Sil~iyaAn : (TA:) [a coll. gen. n.:] n. un. with p : (K:) it is not of the slender and succulent herbs or leguminous plants, which dry up in summer. (TA.) Hence A=kilapu AlxaDiri , occurring in a trad., [properly signifying A she-camel that eats the plant above mentioned, ] applied to a man who acts justly and moderately with respect to worldly enjoyments: for the xDr is not of the slender and succulent herbs, as above observed, nor of those excellent plants which the spring produces by its consecutive rains, and which therefore become goodly and soft or tender; but of those upon which beasts pasture after others have dried up, because they find no others, and which the Arabs call janobap ; and the beasts do not eat much of it, nor do they find it wholesome. (IAth, TA.)

sourceDefinition: (S, Msb, K) [in two copies of the S, in which it is without the article, written without tenween, but in the Msb and K it has the article prefixed, and is therefore necessarily without tenween,] and xunofusaA=' , (Msb, TA,) which is more common, (Msb,) [but this I doubt, for I have found it nowhere else,] and ↓ xunofasN (S, K) and xunofusN (TA) and xinofisN , (K,) which last is of the dial. of the people of El-Basrah, (TA,) and xunofusapN and xunofusapN , (K,) [The black beetle: or a certain species thereof: ] a well-known creeping thing; (Msb;) a certain insect, (S, K,) black, (K,) of fetid odour, smaller than the juEal , found in the bottoms of walls: (TA:) the first and second of these words are both applied to the male and the female: (Msb:) or xunofasN is applied to the male, (AA, Msb,) by some of the Arabs, (Msb,) and is syn. with EunoZabN and HunoZabN , (AA, TA,) and xunofusN is not disallowable, being agree- able with analogy: (Msb:) and xunofasaA'apN is applied to the female, [which, if correct, shows xnfsA=' to be with tenween,] and so is xunofasapN : (S:) or xnfsA'p , with p , is not allowable; [and if so, xnfsA=' is without tenween;] (As, TA;) and xnfsp is [not applied to the female, but] used by the Benoo-Asad for xnfsA=' , as though they made the p a substitute for the A : (Msb:) [and this seems to indicate that the A is a fem. A , grammatically speaking, and that the word is therefore without tenween:] the pl. is xanaAfisu . (Msb.) One says, huwa A^alaH~u mina AlxunofasaA='i [ He is more persevering than the black beetle ]: because it returns to thee as often as thou throwest it away. (TA.) [Accord. to the K, the n in the words of this art. is radical; but accord. to the S and Msb, augmentative.]

sourceDefinition: He sought, desired, or asked for, xiyrap (S, Msb, K) or xiyarap (as in some copies of the K) [i. e. the blessing, prospering, or favour, of God; &c.]. [And it is trans.; for] one says, Aisotaxiri A@ll~`ha yaxiro laka [ Desire thou, or ask thou for, the blessing, prospering, or favour, of God; &c.; and He will bless, prosper, or favour, thee; &c.]. (S.) And Aisotaxarotu A@ll~`ha fiyhi faxaAra liY I desired, or asked, of God, the better of the two things, [or rather the better in it, meaning a case, or an affair,] and He chose it for me. (A.) ― -b2- See also 8.

definition: [ Good, moral or physical;
sourceDefinition: [ Good, moral or physical; anything that is good, real or ideal, and actual or potential; and, being originally an inf. n., used as sing and pl.;] a thing that all desire; such as intelligence, for instance, and equity; (Er-Rághib, and so in some copies of the K;) [or goodness; ] and excellence; and what is profitable or useful; benefit; (Er-Rághib;) contr. of $ar~N : (S, A, Msb:) pl. xuyuwrN , (Msb, K,) and also, accord. to the Msb, ↓ xiyaArN : (TA:) [but this latter seems to be properly pl. only of xayorN used as an epithet (see below) and as a noun denoting the comparative and superlative degrees: it may however be used as an epithet in which the quality of a subst. is predominant:] xyr is of two kinds: namely, absolute xyr , which is what is desired in all circumstances and by every person: and what is xyr [or good ] to one and $r~ [or evil ] to another; as, for instance, (Er-Rághib,) wealth, or property: (Zj, L in art. $d , Er-Rághib, K:) it has this last signification, namely wealth, or property, in the Kur, ii. 176 (S, TA) and ii. 274 and xxiv. 33 and xli. 49: or in the first and second of these instances it is thus called to imply the meaning of wealth, or property, that has been collected in a praiseworthy manner, or it means much wealth or property; and this is its meaning in the first of the instances mentioned above, agreeably with a trad. of 'Alee; and also in the Kur, c. 8: (TA:) [being used as a pl. (as well as a sing.), it may be also rendered good things: ] and it is also used by the Arabs to signify horses; (K, * TA;) and has this meaning in the Kur, xxxviii. 31: (TA:) [it is often best rendered good fortune; prosperity; welfare; wellbeing; weal; happiness; or a good state or condition: and sometimes bounty, or beneficence. ] rajulN qaliylu Alxayori means [ A man possessing little, or no, good; possessing few, or no, good things; or poor: and in whom is little, or no, good or goodness; or niggardly: and also] a man who does little good: (TA in art. ES :) or [ who does no good; ] who is not near to doing good; denoting the nonexistence of good in him. (Msb in art. ql .) [Thus it sometimes means the same as rajulN laA xayora fiyhi A man in whom is no good or goodness; devoid of goodness; worthless. ] And qil~apu xayorK means Poverty: and also niggardliness. (A and TA in art. jHd .) huwa mino A^aholi Alxayori waAlxiyri is explained voce xiyrN . EalaYyadaYi Alxayori waAlyumoni [May it be with the aid of good fortune and prosperity ] is a prayer used with respect to a marriage. (A 'Obeyd, TA.) And A_in~aka maA waxayorFA means maEa xayorK , i. e., Mayest thou meet with, or attain, good. (K.) ― -b2- xayorN in the phrase fulaAnN xayorN resembles an epithet [like ↓ xay~irN , and signifies Good; or possessing good ]; (Akh, S;) therefore the fem. is xayorapN , of which the pl. is xayoraAtN , (Akh, S, Msb, *) as occurring in the Kur, lv. 70; and they do not [there] mean by it [the comparative or superlative signification of the measure] A^afoEalu : (Akh, S:) you say ↓ rajulN xay~irN , (S, A, Msb,) meaning [ A good man; or] a man possessing xayor [or good ]; (Msb;) and rajulN xayorN : (S:) and in like manner, ↓ AimoraA^apN xay~irapN and xayorapN , (S, Msb,) meaning [ A good woman; or] a woman excellent in beauty and disposition: (Msb:) or xayorN and ↓ xay~irN signify possessing much xayor [or good ], (K,) applied to a man; (TA;) and in the same sense you say ↓ rajulN xayoraY , and ↓ xuwraY , and ↓ xiyarY : and the fem. of the first is xayorapN ; and of the second, ↓ xay~irapN : (K:) and the pl. [of pauc.] (of the first, TA) is A^axoyaArN , and [of mult.] xiyaArN : (A, Msb, K:) you say also xiyaAru AlmaAli , meaning The excellent of the camels or the like: (Msb, K:) and in like manner you say of men &c.: (TA:) [see also below:] and the fem. is xayorapN , of which the pl. is xayoraAtN : (Msb:) xiyaArN is contr. of A^a$oraArN , (S, Mgh,) [thus] used as an epithet: (Mgh:) and ↓ xayorapN [used as a subst.] signifies anything excellent; and the pl. thereof in this sense, xayoraAtN , occurs in the Kur, ix. 89: (S:) or xayorN , (K,) or the fem. xayorapN , (Lth,) or each, (K.) signifies excellent in beauty: (Lth, K:) and ↓ xay~irN and xay~irapN signify excellent in righteousness (Lth, K) and religion: (K:) or there is no difference in the opinion of the lexicologists [in general] between xayorapN and ↓ xay~irapN : (Az:) accord. to Zj, xayoraAtN and ↓ xay~iraAtN , both occurring in different readings of the Kur, lv. 70, signify good in dispositions: accord. to Khálid Ibn-Jembeh, xayorapN , applied to a woman, signifies generous in race, exalted in rank or quality or reputation, goodly in face, good in disposition, possessing much wealth, who, if she bring forth, brings forth a generous child: (TA:) [↓ xiyaArN is also applied as an epithet to a sing. subst., either masc. or fem.:] you say jamalN xiyaArN and naAqapN xiyaArN , meaning A he-camel [ that is excellent or] excellent and brisk and so a she-camel. (TA.) See also muxotaArN , in three places. In the saying laEamaru A^abiyka Alxayoru , the word xayor is in the nom. case as an epithet of Eamor ; [so that the phrase lit. means By the good life of thy father; ] but properly it should be laEamoru A^abiyka Alxayori [ By the life of thy good father ]: and the like is said with $ar~ . (TA.) [See also art. Emr .] ― -b3- xayorN is also used to denote superiority: one says, h`*aA xayorN mino h`*aA This is better than this: and in the dial. of the Benoo-'Ámir, ↓ h`*aA A^axoyaru mino h`*aA , with A^ , and in like manner, A^a$~aru ; but the rest of the Arabs drop the A^ in each case: (Msb:) you say, minoka ↓ huwa A^axoyaru [ He is better than thou ], and in like manner, A^a$~aru minoka ; and huwa xayorN minoka , and in like manner, $ar~N minoka ; and, [using the dim. form of xayorN ,] minoka ↓ xuyayorN , and in like manner, $urayorN minoka . (Ibn-Buzurj, TA.) You also say, when you mean to express the signification of superiority, fulaAnapN xayoru Aln~aAsi [ Such a woman is the best of mankind ]; but not xayorapu : [see, however, what will be found cited hereafter from the K,] and fulaAnN xayoru Aln~aAsi [ Such a man is the best of mankind ]; but not ↓ A^axoyaru [unless in the dial. of the Benoo-'Ámir]: and [it is said that] xayoru when thus used does not assume the dual form nor the pl., because it has the signification of [the measure] A^afoEalu : for though a poet uses the dual form, he uses it as a contraction of the dual of xay~irN , like mayotN and may~itN , and hayonN and hay~inN : (S:) [but. this remark in the S is incorrect: for both xayor and ↓ A^axoyar , when used in such phrases as those to which J here refers, have pl. forms of frequent occurrence, and of which examples will be found below; and, as is said by I 'Ak (p. 239), and by many other grammarians, you may say, Alz~ayodaAni A^afoDalaA Alqawomi , and Alz~ayoduwna A^afoDaluw Alqawomi and A^afaADilu Alqawomi , and also hinodu fuDolaYAln~isaA='i , &c.; and such concordance is found in the Kur, vi. 123; and is even said by many to be more chaste than the mode prescribed by J:] it is said in the K, that you say, ↓ huwa A^axoyaru minoka , like xayoru ; and when you mean the signification of superiority, you say fulaAnN xayorapN Aln~aAsi , with p , and fulaAnapu xayoruhumo , without p : but [SM says,] I know not how this is; for in the S is said what is different from this, and in like manner by Z in several places in the Ksh; and what is most strange is, that the author of the K quotes in the B the passage of J [from the S], and adopts the opinion of the leading authorities [as given in the S]: (TA:) or you say, fulaAnapu Alxayorapu mina AlmaroA^atayoni [ Such a woman is the better of the two women ]: and hiYa Alxayorapu , and ↓ Alxiyrapu , [so in the TA, but in the CK Alxiyarapu ,] and ↓ AlxiyraY , and ↓ AlxuwraY , [the last being fem. of A^axoyaru , originally xuyoraY , and so, app., the last but one, She is the better, or best: ] (K:) and [using the dim. form of xayorN ] you say, A^aholihi ↓ huwa xuyayoru [ He is the best of his family ]: (Ibn-Buzurj, TA:) one says also, to one coming from a journey, xayora maA rud~a fiY A^aholK wamaAlK , meaning May God make that with which thou comest [back] to be the best of what is brought back by the absent with family and property; (As, Meyd, TA;) or, as some relate it, xayoru , i. e. rad~uka xayoru rad~K [may thy bringing back be the best bringing back ]; and fY is used in the sense of maEa : (Meyd:) [ A^axoyaArN is pl. of pauc., and xiyaArN pl. of mult., and so app. is xiyraAnN , of xayorN thus used; and ↓ A^axaAyiru is pl. of A^axoyaru , and so is A^axoyaruwna applied to rational beings: in the TA, A^axaAyiru is said to be a pl. pl. of A^axoyaru , and so xiyraAnN ; but this is app. a mistake, probably of transcription:] you say rajulN mino xiyaAri Aln~aAsi and A^axoyaArihimo and ↓ A^axaAyirihimo [ A man of the best of mankind ]: (A, TA:) and laka xiyaAru h`*ihi AlA_ibili , and ↓ xiyratuhaA , [ Thine are, or is, or shall be, the best of these camels, ] alike with respect to a sing. and a pl.: (TA:) and A_ibilihi ↓ naHara xiyrapa and A_ibilihi ↓ xuwrapa [ He slaughtered the best of his camels ]: (IAar, TA:) and ↓ humu AlA^axoyaruwna [ They (meaning men) are the better, or best ]. (Ibn-Buzurj, TA.) -A2- maA xayora for maA A^axoyara : see 4, in two places. -A3- xayoru baw~aA='u [from the Persian xiyrobuwaA Lesser cardamom; ] a kind of small grain, resembling the qaAqul~ap [or common cardamom ], (K,) of sweet odour. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: a subst. from AlAixotiyaAru ; (S, Mgh, K;) meaning Choice, or option; (Msb;) and so ↓ xiyarapN in the Kur [xxviii. 68], maAkaAna lahumu Alxiyarapu They have not choice, or option; (Mgh;) or the meaning of these words is, it is not for them to choose in preference to God; (Fr, Zj;) and so, accord. to Lth, ↓ xiyrapN , as being an inf. n. [or rather a quasi-inf. n., though this seems doubtful,] of AxtAr . (TA.) You say, A_in~a fiY Al$~ar~i xiyaArFA [ Verily in evil there is a choice, or an option ]; i. e. what may be chosen: a prov. (TA.) And A^anota biA@lxiyaArK and ↓ biA@lomuxotaAri [in some copies of the K bAlmxyAr , which, as is said in the TA, is a mistranscription, Thou hast the choice, or option ]; i. e. choose thou what thou wilt. (K.) And AlbayoEu SafoqapN A^awo xiyaArN Selling is decisive or with the option of returning. (Mgh in art. Sfq .) Hence, xiyaAru Alr~uw^oyapi The choice of returning [ on seeing it ] a thing which one has purchased without seeing it. (Mgh, * Msb, * KT.) And xiyaAru Almajolisi [ The choice of returning a thing purchased while sitting with the seller ]. (TA.) And xiyaAru AlEayobi [and Aln~aqiySapi ] The choice of returning a thing to the seller when it has a fault, a defect, or an imperfection. (KT.) And xiyaAru Al$~aroTi The choice of returning a thing purchased when one of the two contracting parties has made it a condition that he may do so within three days or less. (KT.) And xiyaAru Alt~aEoyiyni The choice of specifying [ for instance ] one of two garments, or pieces of cloth, which one has purchased for ten pieces [ of money, or some other sum, ] on the condition of so doing. (KT.) ― -b2- See also muxotaArN , in three places. And see xayorN , in the middle of the paragraph, where it is explained as an epithet applied to a sing. subst., either masc. or fem. See also the first sentence of that paragraph. ― -b3- It is also a pl. of xayorN [q. v.] as an epithet, (A, Msb, K,) [and as a noun denoting the comparative and superlative degrees.] -A2- Also [ A species of cucumber; cucumis sativus Linn. a fructu minore: (Delile, Flor. Aeg. Illustr., no. 927 :)] i. q. qiv~aA='N : (S:) or resembling the qv~A=' ; (K, &c.;) which is the more suitable explanation: (TA:) or i. q. qavadN [q. v.]: an arabicized word: (Mgh:) [from the Persian xiyaArN :] not Arabic. (S.) ― -b2- xiyaAru $anobara [ The cassia fistula of Linn.;] a well-known kind of tree; (K;) a species of the xar~uwb , resembling a large peach-tree; (TA;) abounding in Alexandria and Misr; (K;) and having an admirable yellow flower: (TA:) the latter division [or rather the whole] of the name is arabicized [from the Persian xiyaAro Janobaro ]. (TA.)

(Mgh.)

definition: [from the Pers. dasobanodo ] A certain game of the Magians, which they thus call; i. q. Ald~aEokasapu : (S and K in art. dEks :) they turn round [ in a circle, as though imitating the revolutions of...
sourceDefinition: [from the Pers. dasobanodo ] A certain game of the Magians, which they thus call; i. q. Ald~aEokasapu : (S and K in art. dEks :) they turn round [ in a circle, as though imitating the revolutions of the “ host of heaven ”], having taken one another by the hand, [ in a manner ] like dancing. (K in that art.) [Hence probably originated the similar performances of certain Muslim darweeshes in celebrating what they term a *ikor , described in the works of several travellers, and in my own work on the Modern Egyptians.]

sourceDefinition: , (S, Msb, K,) aor. , (K,) inf. n. dafoEN (Msb, K) and dafaAEN (TA) and madofaEN , (K,) [ He impelled it, pushed it, thrust it, or drove it; and particularly, so as to remove it from its place; he propelled it; he repelled, or repulsed, it; he pushed it, thrust it, or drove it, away, or back; ] he put it away, or removed it from its place, (Msb, TA,) by, or with, force, or strength: (TA:) or dafoEN signifies the putting away or removing or turning back a thing before the coming or arriving [of that thing]; like as rafoEN signifies the “ putting away or removing or turning back ” a thing “ after the coming or arriving ” thereof. (Kull p. 185.) Hence the saying in the Kur [ii. 252, and xxii. 41], walawo laA dafoEu A@ll~`hi Aln~aAsa [ And were it not for God's repelling men ]; where some read ↓ difaAEu [which means the same, as will be seen in the course of what follows, though bearing also another interpretation, likewise to be seen in what follows]. (TA.) You say, dafaEotu Alr~ajula [ I impelled, pushed, &c., the man ]. (S.) And ↓ dAfEhu , inf. n. difaAEN [and mudaAfaEapN ]; and ↓ df~Ehu ; (TA;) [both, app., accord. to the TA, signifying the same; but the latter more properly relates to several objects together, or signifies he impelled it, pushed it, &c., much, or vehemently, or often; whereas] mudaAfaEapN (K, TA) and difaAEN (TA) are [often exactly] syn. with dafoEN . (K, TA.) Thus, (TA,) you say, as meaning the same, Eanohu ↓ dAfE and dafaEa [ He repelled from him; whence another explanation of these two phrases, which see in what follows]. (S, TA.) And hence, dafaEa A@ll~`hu Eanoka Almakoruwha , inf. n. dafoEN , (tropical:) [ May God repel, or avert, from thee what is disliked, or hated, or evil ]: (TA:) and A@ll~`hu Eanoka Als~uwo'a ↓ daAfaEa , inf. n. difaAEN , (tropical:) [ May God repel, or avert, from thee evil ]. (S, TA.) And dafaEotu Eanohu AlA^a*aY (tropical:) [ I repelled, or averted, from him what was hurtful, or annoying; as also ↓ daAfaEotu ]. (Msb, K, TA.) Sb mentions, as a saying of the Arabs, AidofaEi Al$~ar~a walawo A_iSobaEFA (tropical:) [ Repel thou, or avert thou, evil, or mischief, though but with a finger: the last word being in the accus. case by reason of the subaudition of the prep. b ; the meaning being biA_iSobaEK ]. (TA.) [See also an ex. voce dafuwEN .] When dafoEN is made trans. by means of Eano , [and has a single objective complement, a second objective complement is understood, and in general] it has the meaning or the act of (assumed tropical:) Defending; as in the Kur [xxii. 39], A_in~a A@ll~`ha yadofaEu Eano A@l~a*iyna A=manuwA (assumed tropical:) [ Verily God defendeth those who have believed; i. e. repelleth from them aggression and the like]; (B;) and ↓ yudaAfiEu , in the same, (K, TA,) accord. to another reading, signifies the same; (K, TA;) or this latter signifies (assumed tropical:) defendeth energetically, with the energy of him who contendeth for superiority in so doing. (Bd.) And Eanohu ↓ daAfaEotu signifies [also] (assumed tropical:) I pleaded, or contended in arguments, in defence of him. (Msb.) [Exceptions to the statement cited above form the B will be found in what follows in this paragraph; and another exception, voce mudaf~aEN .] ― -b2- [In the exs. which follow, the verb is used in senses little differing, essentially, from those assigned to it in the first sentence of this art.] ― -b3- dafaEotu mina AlA_inaA='i dafoaEapF [ I poured forth from the vessel a single pouring ]: the last word, which is with fet-h, is an inf. n. [of un.]. (Msb.) ― -b4- dafaEati All~ibaA^afiY DaroEihaA qubayola Aln~itaAji (tropical:) [ She (a ewe, or goat, S, or a camel, S, K) infused the first milk into her udder, i. e. secreted it therein, a little before bringing forth ]. (S, K.) And dafaEati All~abani EalaY raA^osi waladihaA likavoratihi (tropical:) [ She (a ewe or goat, or a camel, TA) secreted the milk in her udder when about to produce her young, by reason of its abundance ]; for the milk becomes abundant in her udder only when she is about to bring forth: the inf. n. [app. the inf. n. of un.] is dafoEapN . (TA.) And dafaEato alone, said of a ewe or goat, signifies (assumed tropical:) She secreted milk in her udder when about to produce the young; expl. by A^aDoraEato EalaY raA^osi Alwaladi [which see in art. DrE ]. (S, TA.) Accord. to En-Nadr, one says dafaEato bilabinihaA , and biAll~abani , when her young is in her belly; but when she has brought forth, one does not say dafaEato . (TA.) ― -b5- In the saying, ga$iyitonaA saHaAbapN fadafaEonaAhaA A_ilaY gayorinaA [lit. A cloud overspread us, and we drove it away to other persons ], meaning (tropical:) it departed from us to other persons, dfEnAhA is for dafaEatonaA , which means dufiEato Ean~aA [lit. it was driven away from us ]. (TA.) ― -b6- dafaEahu biHuj~apK (assumed tropical:) [ He refelled him, or refuted him, by an argument or the like ]. (MF in art. kfH .) ― -b7- dafaEotu Alqawola (assumed tropical:) I rebutted the saying; repelled it by an argument, an allegation, or a proof. (Msb.) ― -b8- AidofaEo h`*aA (tropical:) Leave thou this, sparing him. (As, TA.) [See mudaf~aEN .] ― -b9- [In several exs. here following, the verb resembles AndfE ; nafosahu , or the like, being understood after it.] ― -b10- dafaEa AlmaA='u [ The water poured out, or forth, as though it impelled, or propelled, itself ]: (TA: [where it is followed by waA@noSab~a , as an explicative adjunct:]) and so Als~ayolu [ the torrent ]. (ISh.) [See also 6.] And dafaEa AlwaAdiY biAlmaA='i [ The valley poured with water ]. (TA in art. H$k .) ― -b11- dafaEa fiY Eadowihi (assumed tropical:) [ He pushed, or pressed, on, or forward, as though he impelled himself, in his running ]. (S in art. gwr ; &c.) [See also 7.] ― -b12- dafaEa Alqawomu (assumed tropical:) The people, or company of men, came at once. (Msb.) ― -b13- dafaEa A_ilaY AlmakaAni , (TA,) and dufiEa A_ilayohi , (Msb, TA,) in the pass. form, (Msb,) (tropical:) He reached, or came to, the place. (Msb, TA.) You say also, h`*aA TariyqN yadofaEu A_ilaY makaAni ka*aA (tropical:) This is a road which reaches to such a place. (TA.) ― -b14- dafaEa mino EarafaAtK (assumed tropical:) He commenced the journey from 'Arafát, and impelled and removed himself thence, or impelled his she-camel, and urged her to go. (TA, from a trad.) And dafaEotu Eani AlmawoDiEi (assumed tropical:) I removed, went, went away, or journeyed, from the place. (Msb.) [See again 7.] ― -b15- dafaEa also signifies (assumed tropical:) He returned. (MF.) ― -b16- When dafoEN is made trans. by means of A_ilaY , it [generally, but not always, as has been shown above,] has the meaning of the act of Giving, or delivering; as in the Kur [iv. 5], faA@dofaEuwA A_ilayohimo A^amowaAlahumo [ Then give ye, or deliver ye, to them their property ]. (B.) You say, dafaEotu A_ilaYY fulaAnK $ayoy^FA [ I gave, or delivered, to such a one a thing ]. (S, K. *) And dafaEotu AlwadiyEapa A_ilaY SaAHibihaA I restored the deposit to its owner. (Msb.) And dafaEotu lahu qiToEapF mina AlmaAli [ I gave him a part, or portion, of the property ]. (S in art. zEb ; and the like is said in that art. in the K.) And dafaEahu [alone] He gave it; syn. A^aEoTaAhu . (Er-Rághib, MF.)

sourceDefinition: [in its primary acceptation] signifies The contending, or striving, with another, to push him, or repel him; or the pushing, or repelling, another, being pushed, or repelled, by him; or the pushing against another; syn. muzaAHamapN . (TA.) [Hence, yudaAfiEu AlA^axobavayoni He is striving to suppress the urine and ordure: see A^axobavu . And mudaAfaEapu AlEayo$i The striving to retain life: see 2 in art. zlj . ― -b2- But it is often used in the same sense as dafoEN :] see the verb and its two inf. ns. in seven places in the former half of the first paragraph of this article. ― -b3- Also (assumed tropical:) i. q. mumaATalapN : (S, K, TA:) in some of the copies of the S, muTaAwalapN . (TA.) You say, daAfaEotuhu biHaq~ihi , (Jm, TA,) or Eano Haq~ihi , (Msb,) (assumed tropical:) I deferred with him, delayed with him, or put him off, in the matter of his right, or due, by promising time after time to render it to him; [and so repelled him, or strove to repel him, from it; ] syn. maATalotuhu . (Jm, Msb, TA.) And dAfE biHaAjatihi (assumed tropical:) He deferred, delayed, postponed, or put off, his (another's) needful affair. (L in art. rvd .) ― -b4- dAfE Alr~ajulu A^amora ka*aA (assumed tropical:) The man attached, or devoted, himself to such an affair, and exerted himself, and persisted, or persevered, in it. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: [ They contended, or strove, together, to push, or repel, one another; or] they pushed, or repelled, one another; or pushed against one another. (Msb.) (TA.) [See also dafaEa . definition: , applied to a camel, (tropical:) Held in high estimation by his owner;
sourceDefinition: , applied to a camel, (tropical:) Held in high estimation by his owner; (A, K, * TA;) so that when he comes near to the load, he is sent back: (A, TA:) one that is reserved for covering, and not ridden nor laden; of which, when he is brought to be laden, one says, AidofaEo h`*aA , i. e. sourceDefinition: , (T, M, Mgh, Msb, K, &c.,) first pers. danawotu , (T, S,) aor. yadonuw , (T, Msb,) inf. n. dunuw~N (T, S, M, Msb, K) and danaAwapN , (M, K,) He, or it, was, or became, near; drew near, or approached; (T, M, Mgh, Msb, K;) as also ↓ AdnY ; (IAar, T, K;) and ↓ dn~Y , inf. n. tadoniyapN ; (IAar, T;) and ↓ dAnY , inf. n. mudaAnaApN ; (KL, but only the inf. n. is there mentioned;) and ↓ Aid~anaY , inf. n. Aid~inaA='N : (TA:) it is either in person, or substance, or in respect of predicament, and in place, and in time: (El-Harállee, TA:) you say, danaA minohu , (M, Mgh, Msb,) and danawotu minohu , (T, S,) and A_ilayohi , (M, Msb,) and lahu , (TA,) and Ealayohi occurs in a verse of Sá'ideh as meaning minohu , (M,) He, or it, and I, was, or became, near, &c., to him, or it: (T, M, Mgh, Msb:) [and in like manner you use the other verbs mentioned above, except ↓ dAnY , which is immediately trans.: or danaA minohu with danaAwapN for its inf. n. means, or means also, He was near to him in respect of kindred; was related to him: for] danaAwapN is syn. with qaraAbapN (S, M, K) and qurobaY : (M, K:) you say, bayonahumaA danaAwapN meaning qaraAbapN [i. e. Between them two is relationship ]; (S;) and maA tazodaAdu min~aA A_il~aA qurobFA wadanaAwapK [ Thou increasest not save in nearness and relationship to us ]. (ISk, T, S.) A rájiz says, maA liY A^araAhu daAlifFA qadodunoYa lahu meaning duniYa lahu [i. e. What hath happened to me that I see him walking gently or with short steps, or rendered lowly by age, having been approached by death?]: it is from danawotu , but the w is changed into Y because of the kesreh before it, and then the n is made quiescent: and there are similar instances of contraction of verbs: but [ISd says,] I know not dunoYa except in this instance; and As used to say of the poem in which this occurs, This rejez is not ancient: it is app. of Khalaf ElAhmar or some other of the Muwelleds. (M.) One says also, danati Al$~amosu lilomaguruwbi and ↓ A^adonat [ The sun was, or became, near to setting ]. (M.) -A2- daniYa , (T, M, K, TA, [in the CK, mA kAna danoyaA wlqd danA is erroneously put for maA kaAna daniyFA walaqado daniYa ,]) like raDiYa , (TA,) aor. yadonaY , (T,) inf. n. danFA (T, M, K) and danaAyapN , (T, K, TA,) or dinaAyapN ; (M, accord. to the TT; and so in the CK; [app. a mistranscription occasioned by a misunderstanding of what here follows;]) the Y [in daniYa ] being substituted for w because of the nearness of the kesreh; all on the authority of Lh; (M;) and danuwa , aor. yadonuw , without ' , inf. n. danaA='apN , with ' , (ISk, T,) and dunuw~N ; (T;) or danaA , aor. yadonuw , inf. n. danaAwapN ; i. q. danaA^a and danuw^a ; (Msb;) [i. e.] He (a man, T, M) was, or became, such as is termed ↓ daniY~N ; (T, M, Msb, K;) and daniYo'N ; (Msb;) meaning weak; contemptible ( xasiysN ); not profitable to any one; who falls short in everything upon which he enters: (T: [like mudan~K :]) or low, ignoble, or mean; ( saAqiTN ;) weak; (M, K;) such as, when night affords him covert, will not quit his place, by reason of weakness: (M:) or low, ignoble, or mean, ( lay^iymN ,) in his actions, or conduct; bad, evil, or foul; accord. to the explanation of danaA by Es-Sarakustee: but some distinguish between daniYo'N and daniY~N ; making the former to signify “ low, ignoble, or mean; ” ( lay^iymN ;) and the latter, xasiysN [app. as meaning contemptible ]. (Msb, and so the latter is explained in the Mgh.)

definition: He made him, or it, to be, or become, near;
sourceDefinition: He made him, or it, to be, or become, near; to draw near, or to approach; he drew near, or brought near, him, or it; (S, M, Mgh, K;) as also ↓ dn~Ahu , (M, K,) inf. n. tadoniyapN . (K.) ― -b2- [Hence,] A^adonato vawobahaA EalayohaA She (a woman) let down her garment upon her, and covered, or veiled, herself with it. (Mgh.) And A^adonayotu Als~itora I let down the veil, or curtain, [ for the purpose of concealment. ] (Msb.) It is said in the Kur [xxxiii. 59], yudoniyna Ealayohin~ mino jalaAbiybihin~a [ They shall let down upon them a portion of their outer wrapping-garments ]; (Mgh;) meaning they shall let down a portion of their outer wrapping-garments over their faces, when they go forth for their needful purposes, except one eye. (Jel.) -A2- AdnY is also intrans.: see 1, in two places. ― -b2- [Hence,] A^adonato , said of a she-camel, (S, TA,) and of a woman, (TA,) She was, or became, near to bringing forth. (S, TA.) And A^adonato EalaY raA^osi Alwaladi [a phrase similar to A^aDoraEato EalaY raA^osi Alwaladi , q. v.]. (Occurring in a verse cited in the TA in art. fkh .) ― -b3- And AdnY He lived a strait life, (IAar, T, K,) after easiness and plenty. (IAar, T.)

definition: and dinoyFA and dinoyaA and ↓ dunoyaA mean [ He is a son of a paternal uncle ] closely related;
sourceDefinition: and dinoyFA and dinoyaA and ↓ dunoyaA mean [ He is a son of a paternal uncle ] closely related; syn. laH~FA [q. v.]: when you pronounce the d with damm, you do not make the word perfectly decl.: when you pronounce it with kesr, you make it either perfectly or imperfectly decl.: but when you prefix Eam~ to a determinate noun, dinoY may not be in the gen. case: for instance, you say, huwa A@bonu Eam~ihi dinoyFA , i. e. [ He is the son of his paternal uncle ] closely related; as also ↓ dinoyapN ; because dinoY , being indeterminate, cannot be an epithet applied to that which is determinate: (S:) and [in like manner] you say, huwa A@bonu Eam~iY , or Abn xaAliY , or Abn Eam~atiY , or Abn xaAlatiY , or Abn A^axiY , or Abn A^uxotiY , (M, K,) all mentioned by Lh, the last two as on the authority of Aboo- Safwán, but all except the first and second as unknown to Ks and to As, (M,) followed by ↓ dinoyapN and dinoyFA and dinoyaA and ↓ dunoyaA , (M, K, TA,) the last two without tenween, (TA; [and so written in the M; but in the CK and my MS. copy of the K, in the place of these two is put dunoyFA , which is disallowed by J;]) meaning [ He is the son of my paternal uncle, and the son of my maternal uncle, &c.,] closely related: (M, K:) and ↓ huwa Eam~uhu dunNyaA and ↓ dinoyapF and dinoyFA and dinoyaA [ He is his paternal uncle closely related ]: (Ks, T:) Lh says that the w is changed into Y in ↓ dinoyapF and dinNyFA because of the nearness of the kesreh and the weakness of the intervening letter, as is the case in fitoyapN and EiloyapN : but it seems that these words are originally ↓ dunoyaA , i. e., by a relationship, or uterine relationship, nearer to me than others; and that the change of the letter is made only to show that the Y is that of the fem. of A^adonaY . (M.) You say also, ↓ humo rahoTuhu dinoyapF They are his people, and his tribe, closely related. (S and TA in art. rhT .)

definition: Nearer, and nearest;
sourceDefinition: Nearer, and nearest; opposed to A^aqoSaY : (TA:) fem. dunoyaA ; (M, TA;) in which the [radical] w is changed into Y , as in EuloyaA and quSoyaA : (ISd, TA voce buqowaY :) [the pl. of the masc. is A^adaAnK and A^adonawona ; the latter in the accus. and gen. A^adonayoni : and] the pl. of the fem., dunFY , (S, K, TA,) like kubarN pl. of kuboraY , and SugarN pl. of SugoraY ; (S, TA;) said by some to be extr. and strange [in respect of usage]; and El-Mutanebbee has been blamed for using it; (MF, TA;) but in the case referred to he has used Ald~unaY for Ald~unoyaA , [not as a pl.,] suppressing the Y by poetic license. (TA.) [Hence,] gulibati Alr~uwmu fiY A^adonaY AlA^aroDi , in the Kur xxx. 1 and 2, The Greeks have been overcome in the nearer, or nearest, part of the land. (Bd, Jel.) And Aljamorapu Ald~unoyaA [ The nearest heap of pebbles; ] the heap of pebbles nearest to Minè. (TA. [See art. jmr .]) And Als~amaA='u Ald~unoyaA [ The nearest heaven; i. e. the lowest; ] the heaven that is the nearest to us: (T, TA:) also called samaA='u Ald~unoyaA [which means the heaven of the present world; as will be seen from what follows]. (TA.) See also exs. of the fem. in the paragraph commencing with the words huwa A@bonu Eam~K dinoYK , in four places. ― -b2- Also Former, and first; and fore, and foremost; opposed to A=xirN . (TA.) [Hence,] ↓ laqiytuhu A^adonaY daniY~K (S, K, TA) and ↓ A^adonaY danFA , (K, TA, [in the CK, erroneously, AdnY dan~Y` and AdnY daniY~K ,]) i. e. I met him the first thing. (S, K.) [And A^adonaY Alfami The fore, or foremost, part of the mouth. ] And Ald~unoyaA [for Ald~aAru Ald~unoyaA , and AlHayaApu Ald~unoyaA , The former dwelling, or abode, and life; i. e. the present world, and life, or state of existence ]; contr. of AlA=xirapu : (M, K:) [or] it is so called because of its nearness: (T, S:) [and may be rendered the sublunary abode, &c.: and the inferior abode, &c. It also signifies The enjoyments, blessings, or good, of the present world, or life; worldly blessings or prosperity, &c.] And sometimes it is with tenween, (K, TA,) when used indeterminately: (TA:) [thus,] IAar mentions the saying maA lahu dunoyFA wa laA A=xirapN [as meaning He has none of the enjoyments, or blessings, of the present world, nor in prospect any enjoyments, or blessings, of the world to come ]; with tenween. (M, TA.) And you say, baAEa dunoyaAhu biA=xiratihi [ He purchased his enjoyments of the present world at the expense of his enjoyments of the world to come ]. (Z, TA in art. byE .) And Aabonu Ald~unoyaA means The rich man. (Msb in art. bnY .) ― -b3- Also More, and most, apt, fit, or proper: thus in the Kur [xxxiii. 59], in the phrase *`lika A^adonaY A^ano yuEarafona [ That will be more, or most, apt, fit, or proper, that they may be known ]; (Ksh, Mgh;) i. e., that they may be known to be free women, as distinguished from female slaves, who did not cover their faces. (Jel.) ― -b4- Also Less [ in number or quantity &c.], and least [ therein ]; opposed to A^akovaru . (TA.) walaA A^adonaY mino *`lika walaAA^akovara , in the Kur [lviii. 8], means Nor less in number than that, nor more in number. (Bd.) And walanu*iyqan~ahumo mina A@loEa*aAbi A@loA^adonaY duwna A@loEa*aAbi A@loA^akobari , in the Kur [xxxii. 21, lit. And we will assuredly make them to taste of the smaller punishment besides the greater punishment ], means, accord. to Zj, whatever punishment is inflicted in the present world and the punishment of the world to come. (M.) ― -b5- Also Worse, [or inferior in quality,] and worst; or more, and most, low, ignoble, base, vile, mean, or weak; opposed to xayorN . (TA.) It is said in the Kur [ii. 58], A^atasotabodiluwna A@l~a*iY huwa A^adonaY biA@l~a*iY huwa xayorN [ Will ye take in exchange that which is worse, or inferior, for that which is better? or], accord. to Zj, meaning that which is less in value [ for that which is better ]? definition: [ A kind, or species, of fungus;
sourceDefinition: [ A kind, or species, of fungus; perhaps a species of phallus; ] a certain plant, (T, S, K,) of the same kind as the Eurojuwn and the Turovuwvi , which grows in the winter, and, when the day becomes hot, rots, and goes away; (IAar, T;) said by Abu-l-'Omeythil to be, in form, like the hiloyawon [or asparagus ]: (T:) pl. *aA=niynu : (T, S:) and some pronounce the sing. *uwnuwnN , without ' ; and make the pl. *awaAniynu : (T, TA:) a certain plant that grows at the roots of the A^aroTaY and rimov and A^alaA=' ; the ground cleaving, and disclosing it, it comes forth like the sawaAEid [app. here meaning the upper arms, above the elbows, ] of men; has no leaves; is black ( A^asoHamu ), and dustcoloured; is pointed [ and roundish ] in its extremity, like the glans of the penis in form; has envelopes ( A^akomaAmu ) like those of the [ bean called ] baAqil~aY ; and has a yellow fruit at its upper part: some say that it is a plant that grows like the [ fungi called ] EaraAjiyn , of the plants termed fuTor : AHn says that what are termed *aA=niyn are things of the [ fungi called ] fuquwE , that come forth from beneath the ground like thick Eumud [or poles ]; nothing eats them, except that camels feed upon them in the year of drought, and goats eat them and fatten upon them; they have a root-stock ( A^aruwmap ); and are used as medicines; and none but the hungry will eat them, because of their bitterness: he also says in one place, they grow at the roots of trees, most like to the asparagus ( hiloyawon ), except that they are larger and thicker; and have no leaves; but they have a buroEuwmap [app. here meaning a head, such as is termed a pileus, or cap ], which assumes a roseate colour, and then changes to yellow: the *w^nwn is all [ full of ] water [or juice ]; and is white, except what appears thereof, of that buroEuwmap ; and nothing eats it, except when men are afflicted with drought and have nothing [ else ] to eat: the n. un. is with p : (M:) ISh says that it is of a tawny colour, smooth and round, having leaves that stick to it, tall like the Turovuwv , not eaten save by sheep or goats, [ and grows ] in plain, or soft, tracts: IB says that it is the wild hiloyawon . (TA.) One says of a people who were characterized by courage and excellence, and who have perished, their state having changed, *aA=niynu laA rimova lahaA wa TaraAviyvu laA A^aroTaY [ Dhu-noonehs having no rimthehs, and turthoothehs having no artáhs ]: meaning that they have been extirpated, and that none of them remains: (TA:) or *A=nyn lA rmv lhA is a prov. applied to him who is ruined, and has nothing remaining, after having had a family and dignity and wealth. (TA voce TurovuwvN .)

definition: , (M, K,) aor. , inf. n. rab~N , (M,) [ He was, or became, its rab~ , or lord, possessor, owner, &c.;] he possessed, or owned, it; had possession of it, and command, or authority, over it; (M, K;)...
sourceDefinition: , (M, K,) aor. , inf. n. rab~N , (M,) [ He was, or became, its rab~ , or lord, possessor, owner, &c.;] he possessed, or owned, it; had possession of it, and command, or authority, over it; (M, K;) namely, a thing; (K;) syn. malakahu . (M, K.) [And in like manner, He was, or became, his rab~ , or lord, &c.] You say, rababotu Alqawoma , [inf. n. as above and marab~apN and ribaAbapN ,] I ruled, or governed, the people; syn. susotuhumo ; i. e. I was, or became, over them [ as their lord, master, or chief ]. (S.) And TaAlato marab~atuhumu Aln~aAsa and ribaAbatuhum Their ruling, or governing, the people continued long. (M, K. *) The saying of Safwán, (T, S,) on the day of Honeyn, (T,) laA^ano yarub~aniY rajulN mino qurayo$K A^aHab~u A_ilaY~a mino A^uno yarub~aniY rajulN mino hawaAzina means [ Assuredly that a man of Kureysh ] should be over me (T, S) as rab~ [or lord, &c.], and as master, or chief, having command, or authority, over me, (T,) [ is more pleasing to me than that a man of Hawázin should be lord, &c., over me. ] ― -b2- Also, (S, M, Mgh, K,) aor. , (S, M,) inf. n. rab~N , (S, Mgh, M,) He reared, fostered, brought up, fed, or nourished, him; i. q. rab~aAhu ; (S, M, Mgh, K;) namely, his child, (S,) or a child, (M, K,) either his own or another's; taking good care of him, and acting as his guardian, (M,) until he attained to puberty, or to the utmost term of youth: (M, K:) and so ↓ rb~bhu , (Lh, S, M, Mgh, K,) or this has a more emphatic signification, (TA,) inf. n. tarbiybN (Lh, M, Mgh, K) and tarib~apN ; (Lh, M, K;) and ↓ trb~bh ; (S, M, K;) and ↓ Artb~hu : (M, K:) [in like manner, also,] ↓ raboraba signifies he reared, fostered, or brought up, an orphan: (AA, T:) and accord. to IDrd, (M,) rabibotuhu is a dial. var. [of rababo=tuhu ]: (M, K:) he says also that the verb is used in like manner in relation to the young one of an animal other than man; and he used to cite this ex.: kaAna lanaA wahowa faluw~N nirobibuho [ He belonged to us when he was a young weaned, or one-year-old, colt, we rearing him ]; with the letter characteristic of the aor. meksoor, to show that the second letter of the preterite is meksoor, accord to the opinion of Sb in respect of a case of this kind; and this, he says, is peculiar to the dial. of Hudheyl in this species of verb. (M, TA.) rab~ati AlmaroA^apu Sabiy~ahaA , used tropically, means (tropical:) The woman patted her child repeatedly on its side in order that it might sleep. (A, TA.) [See 2 in art. rbt .] [It is said that] the primary signification of Alr~ab~u is Alt~arobiyapu ; i. e. The bringing a thing to a state of completion by degrees. (Bd in i. l.) A poet says, (S,) namely, Hassán Ibn-Thábit, (TA,) mino dur~apK bayoDaA='a SaAfiyapK HaAy^iru AlbaHori ↓ mim~aA tarab~aba [ Than a white, clear, pearl, of those which the depth of the sea has brought to maturity ]; meaning a pearl which the shell has reared, or brought to maturity in the bottom of the water. (S, TA.) And the phrase laka niEomapN tarub~uhaA occurs in a trad., meaning [ Thou hast wealth ] which thou preservest, and of which thou takest care, and which thou fosterest like as the man fosters his child. (TA.) ― -b3- [Hence,] AlmaTaru yarub~u Aln~abaAta waAlv~araY The rain causes the plants, or herbage, and the moisture [ of the earth ] to increase. (M.) And Als~aHaAbu yarub~u AlmaTara The clouds collect and increase the rain. (M.) And rab~a , (T, S, M, K, TA,) aor. , inf. n. rab~N and ribaAbN and ribaAbapN ; (Lh, M, TA;) and ↓ rb~b ; (M, TA;) (tropical:) He increased, (M, K, TA,) or rightly disposed, and completed, (T, S,) a benefit, or benefaction. (T, S, M, TA.) ― -b4- rab~a AlA^amora , (M, Msb, K,) aor. , inf. n. rab~N (M, Msb) and ribaAbapN , (M,) (tropical:) He put the affair into a right, or proper, state; adjusted it, arranged it, ordered it, or rightly disposed it; (M, K;) and established it firmly: (M:) or he managed, conducted, or regulated, the affair: (Msb:) [perhaps from rab~a signifying “ he reared, ” &c.; but more probably, I think, from what next follows.] ― -b5- rab~a , (T, S, M, K,) aor. , (T, M,) inf. n. rab~u (T, M, K) and rub~N ; (K) and ↓ rb~b ; (M;) He seasoned a skin (T, S, K) for clarified butter (T, S) with rub~ [i. e. rob, or inspissated juice ], (T, S, K,) of dates, (TA,) which imparts a good odour to it, (S, TA,) and prevents the flavour and odour of the butter from being spoiled: (TA:) or he seasoned a skin with rub~ , and a jar with tar or pitch: or, as some say, rababotuhu signifies I smeared it over, and prepared it properly. (M.) ↓ rab~a and ↓ rb~b , (K,) or the latter, but the former also is allowable, (M,) (tropical:) He made oil, or ointment, good, and sweet, or fragrant, or he perfumed it, (M, K, * TA,) accord. to Lh, by infusing in it jasmine or some other sweet-smelling plant. definition: A lord, a possessor, an owner, or a proprietor, syn.
sourceDefinition: A lord, a possessor, an owner, or a proprietor, syn. maAlikN , (T, IAmb, S, M, A, Msb, K,) of a thing, (T,) of anything, (S, M, A, K,) or of an irrational thing; (Msb;) a person who has a right, or just title or claim, to the possession of anything; or its SaAHib [which is syn. with maAlik ]; (M, A, K;) rab~N and maAlikN and SaAHibN all signifying in Pers. xudaAwanod : (KL:) and a lord, master, or chief; (Msb, TA;) or a lord, master, or chief, to whom obedience is paid: (IAmb, TA:) and a lord, ruler, governor, regulator, or disposer; (TA;) an orderer, a rectifier, or a reformer: (IAmb, TA:) a rearer, fosterer, bringer-up, feeder, or nourisher: and a completer, or an accomplisher: (TA:) it is an epithet, like nam~N from nam~a : or an inf. n. used as an intensive epithet; like EadolN ; (Ksh and Bd * in i. l;) originally signifying the “ bringing (a thing) to a state of completion by degrees;” (Bd, ibid.;) then used in the sense of maAlikN : (Ksh and Bd ibid.:) the pl. [of pauc.] is A^arobaAbN and [of mult.] rubuwbN , (M, K,) and accord. to Sh, ribaAbN also, (TA,) signifying A^aSoHaAbN , (K,) and ↓ rabuwbN is app. a quasi-pl. n.: (M:) the fem. is ↓ rab~apN ; of which the pl. is rab~aAtN . (T.) Whoever possesses a thing is its rab~ : you say, huwa rab~u Ald~aAb~api [ He is the possessor, or owner, or master, of the beast ], and Ald~aAri [ of the house ], (T,) and AlmaAli [ of the property, or cattle ]; (Msb;) and Albayoti ↓ hiYa rab~apu [ She is the owner, or mistress, of the house or tent ]. (T.) With the article Al , it is [properly] applied only to God: (T, S, M, A, Msb, K:) He is rab~u AlA^arobaAbi [ The Lord of lords ]. (T. [Thus the pl. with the article Al is applied to created beings.]) To any other being it is not [properly] applied but as a prefixed noun governing another noun as its complement in the gen. case [or in a similar manner]. (S.) The pagan Arabs, however, sometimes applied it to A king, (S,) or to a lord as meaning a master or chief: (Msb:) El- Hárith says, (S, Msb,) i. e. Ibn-Hillizeh, (S,) wahuwa Alr~ab~u waAl$~ahiydu EalaY yuwo mi AlHiyaArayoni waAlbalaA='u balaA='u (S, Msb,) i. e. And he (meaning El-Mundhir Ibn-Má-es-Semà, or, as some say, 'Amr Ibn-Hind,) was the king [or lord ] and witness of our fighting on the day of El-Hiyárán (the name of a place), and the trial was a hard trial. (EM, p. 285: [in which AlHayaArayoni is erroneously put for AlHiyaArayoni .]) Some forbid that a man should be called the rab~ of his slave: (Msb:) it is said in a trad. that the slave shall not say to his master, rab~Y , because it is like attributing a partner to God: (TA:) but rab~ is sometimes used in the sense of lord as meaning master or chief prefixed to a noun signifying a rational being governed by it in the gen. case: thus in the saying of the Prophet, Hat~aY talida AlA^amapu rab~ahaA [ So that the female slave shall bring forth him who will become her master ], or ↓ rab~atahaA [ her mistress ], accord. to different transmitters; (Msb;) relating to the signs of the hour of resurrection: i. e., the female slave shall bring forth to her master a child that shall be as a master [or mistress] to her because like his [or her] father in rank: meaning that captives and concubines shall be numerous. (TA.) As to the phrase in the Kur [xii. 42], Au*okuroniY Einoda rab~ika [ Mention thou me in the presence of thy lord ], Joseph thus addressed his fellow-prisoner agreeably with the acceptation in which he [the latter] understood the words. (TA.) A similar instance also occurs in the same chapter, in the verse immediately preceding. (Msb.) In another verse, [23 of the same ch.,] A_in~ahu rab~iY [ Verily he is my lord ] may refer to Joseph's master or to God. (M, TA.) The words of the Kur [lxxxix. 28 and 29], AirojiEiY A_ilaY rab~iki raADiyapF maroDiy~apF faA@doxuliY fiY EabodYi , as some read, [instead of EibaAdiY ,] may mean Return to thine owner, [ approving, approved, ] and enter into my servant. (M, TA.) ― -b2- Without the article Al , as some say, (L, TA,) it is sometimes written and pronounced ↓ rabN , without teshdeed; (L, K;) as in the following verse, cited by El-Mufaddal, waqado Ealima AlA^aqowaAmu A^ano layosa fawoqahu rabN gayoru mano yaEoTiY AlHuZuwZa wayarozuqu [ And the peoples have known that there is not above him a lord beside Him who gives the portions of mankind and of others and grants the means of subsistence ]. (L.) And Ahmad Ibn-Yahyà [i. e. Th] mentions the phrase laA warabiyka laA A^afoEalu , for laA warab~ika [i. e. No, by thy Lord, I will not do such a thing]; the [latter] b being changed into Y because of the reduplication. (M, K: * in the CK raboyika .)
