rawSourceText: A lord, a possessor, an owner, or a proprietor, syn. maAlikN , (T, IAmb, S, M, A, Msb, K,) of a thing, (T,) of anything, (S, M, A, K,) or of an irrational thing; (Msb;) a person who has a right, or just title or claim, to the possession of anything; or its SaAHib [which is syn. with maAlik ]; (M, A, K;) rab~N and maAlikN and SaAHibN all signifying in Pers. xudaAwanod : (KL:) and a lord, master, or chief; (Msb, TA;) or a lord, master, or chief, to whom obedience is paid: (IAmb, TA:) and a lord, ruler, governor, regulator, or disposer; (TA;) an orderer, a rectifier, or a reformer: (IAmb, TA:) a rearer, fosterer, bringer-up, feeder, or nourisher: and a completer, or an accomplisher: (TA:) it is an epithet, like nam~N from nam~a : or an inf. n. used as an intensive epithet; like EadolN ; (Ksh and Bd * in i. l;) originally signifying the “ bringing (a thing) to a state of completion by degrees;” (Bd, ibid.;) then used in the sense of maAlikN : (Ksh and Bd ibid.:) the pl. [of pauc.] is A^arobaAbN and [of mult.] rubuwbN , (M, K,) and accord. to Sh, ribaAbN also, (TA,) signifying A^aSoHaAbN , (K,) and ↓ rabuwbN is app. a quasi-pl. n.: (M:) the fem. is ↓ rab~apN ; of which the pl. is rab~aAtN . (T.) Whoever possesses a thing is its rab~ : you say, huwa rab~u Ald~aAb~api [ He is the possessor, or owner, or master, of the beast ], and Ald~aAri [ of the house ], (T,) and AlmaAli [ of the property, or cattle ]; (Msb;) and Albayoti ↓ hiYa rab~apu [ She is the owner, or mistress, of the house or tent ]. (T.) With the article Al , it is [properly] applied only to God: (T, S, M, A, Msb, K:) He is rab~u AlA^arobaAbi [ The Lord of lords ]. (T. [Thus the pl. with the article Al is applied to created beings.]) To any other being it is not [properly] applied but as a prefixed noun governing another noun as its complement in the gen. case [or in a similar manner]. (S.) The pagan Arabs, however, sometimes applied it to A king, (S,) or to a lord as meaning a master or chief: (Msb:) El- Hárith says, (S, Msb,) i. e. Ibn-Hillizeh, (S,) wahuwa Alr~ab~u waAl$~ahiydu EalaY yuwo mi AlHiyaArayoni waAlbalaA='u balaA='u (S, Msb,) i. e. And he (meaning El-Mundhir Ibn-Má-es-Semà, or, as some say, 'Amr Ibn-Hind,) was the king [or lord ] and witness of our fighting on the day of El-Hiyárán (the name of a place), and the trial was a hard trial. (EM, p. 285: [in which AlHayaArayoni is erroneously put for AlHiyaArayoni .]) Some forbid that a man should be called the rab~ of his slave: (Msb:) it is said in a trad. that the slave shall not say to his master, rab~Y , because it is like attributing a partner to God: (TA:) but rab~ is sometimes used in the sense of lord as meaning master or chief prefixed to a noun signifying a rational being governed by it in the gen. case: thus in the saying of the Prophet, Hat~aY talida AlA^amapu rab~ahaA [ So that the female slave shall bring forth him who will become her master ], or ↓ rab~atahaA [ her mistress ], accord. to different transmitters; (Msb;) relating to the signs of the hour of resurrection: i. e., the female slave shall bring forth to her master a child that shall be as a master [or mistress] to her because like his [or her] father in rank: meaning that captives and concubines shall be numerous. (TA.) As to the phrase in the Kur [xii. 42], Au*okuroniY Einoda rab~ika [ Mention thou me in the presence of thy lord ], Joseph thus addressed his fellow-prisoner agreeably with the acceptation in which he [the latter] understood the words. (TA.) A similar instance also occurs in the same chapter, in the verse immediately preceding. (Msb.) In another verse, [23 of the same ch.,] A_in~ahu rab~iY [ Verily he is my lord ] may refer to Joseph's master or to God. (M, TA.) The words of the Kur [lxxxix. 28 and 29], AirojiEiY A_ilaY rab~iki raADiyapF maroDiy~apF faA@doxuliY fiY EabodYi , as some read, [instead of EibaAdiY ,] may mean Return to thine owner, [ approving, approved, ] and enter into my servant. (M, TA.) ― -b2- Without the article Al , as some say, (L, TA,) it is sometimes written and pronounced ↓ rabN , without teshdeed; (L, K;) as in the following verse, cited by El-Mufaddal, waqado Ealima AlA^aqowaAmu A^ano layosa fawoqahu rabN gayoru mano yaEoTiY AlHuZuwZa wayarozuqu [ And the peoples have known that there is not above him a lord beside Him who gives the portions of mankind and of others and grants the means of subsistence ]. (L.) And Ahmad Ibn-Yahyà [i. e. Th] mentions the phrase laA warabiyka laA A^afoEalu , for laA warab~ika [i. e. No, by thy Lord, I will not do such a thing]; the [latter] b being changed into Y because of the reduplication. (M, K: * in the CK raboyika .)

definition: is a word of which there are seventy dial.
sourceDefinition: is a word of which there are seventy dial. vars., all mentioned by Zekereeyà El-Ansáree in his great Expos. of the “ Munferijeh, ” but only eighteen of which are mentioned in the K, including some that are formed with the affix t , some with the affix maA , and some with both these affixes together; as follows: (TA:) rub~a (T, S, M, Msb, Mughnee, K, &c.) and rab~a (T, M, Mughnee, K) and rub~u , (Mughnee,) and ↓ ruba (T, S, M, Mughnee, K) and raba (T, M, Mughnee, K) and rubu and rubo (Mughnee, K) and rabo ; (Mughnee;) and ↓ rub~ata (T, S, M, Msb, Mughnee, K) and rab~ata (M, Mughnee, K) and rub~uta and rub~atu and rab~atu and rub~utu and rub~ati and rab~ati and rub~uti and rab~ut (TA) and rub~ato and rab~ato (Mughnee) and rub~uto , (TA,) and ↓ rubata (T, Mughnee, K) and rabata (Mughnee, K) and rubuta and rubota and rabota and rubatu and rabatu and rubutu and rubotu and rabotu and rubati and rabati and rubuti and rabuti and ruboti and raboti (TA) and rubato and rabato (Mughnee) and rubuto ; (TA;) and rub~amaA (T, S, M, K) and rab~amaA (M, K) and rub~umaA , (TA,) and ↓ rubamaA (T, K) and rabamaA (K) and rubumaA and rubomaA and rabomaA ; (TA;) and ↓ rub~atamaA (T, S, M, K) and rab~atamaA (M, K) and rub~utamaA and rub~atumaA and rab~atumaA and rub~utumaA and rub~atomaA and rab~atomaA and rub~utomaA , (TA,) and ↓ rubatamaA and rabatamaA (M, K) and rubutamaA and rubotamaA and rabotamaA and rubatumaA and rabatumaA and rubutumaA and rubotumaA and rabotumaA and rubatomaA and rabatomaA and rubutomaA : (TA:) [of all these, the most common are rub~a and rub~amaA : and] ↓ rub~ata is the most common of the forms that have the affix t : (Mughnee and K on the letter t :) and the forms with teshdeed are more common than the [corresponding] forms without teshdeed. (M.) It is a word, (M,) or particle, (T, S, Mughnee, K,) governing the gen. case: (S, M, Mughnee, K:) or a noun, (K, TA,) [i. e. an indecl. noun,] in the opinion of the Koofees and some others; but this opinion is rejected by Ibn-Málik in the Tesheel and its Expos., and by AHei, and by IHsh in the Mughnee. (TA.) Accord. to some, (K, TA,) it is used to denote a small number, (T, M, Msb, K, TA,) always, (TA,) or mostly: (Msb, TA:) [thus it may be rendered Few if we render the noun following it as a pl.; and scarce any if we render the noun following as a sing. or a pl.:] it is the contr. of kamo when this latter is not used interrogatively: (T:) [and with maA affixed, restricting it from government, it may be rendered Few times, or seldom: ] or it is used to denote a large number; (K, TA;) i. e. always: so says IDrst: (TA:) [thus used, but such is not always the case, it may be rendered Many, whether we render the noun following it as a sing. or as a pl.: and with maA affixed, Many times, many a time, oftentimes, ofttimes, often, or frequently: ] or it is used to denote a small and a large number; (Mughnee, K;) often the latter, and seldom the former: (Mughnee:) or it is used in a case of boasting, or glorying, (K, TA,) exclusively of other cases, (TA,) to denote a large number: (K, TA:) or it does not denote by itself either a small number or a large number; but one or the other of these meanings is inferred from the context: (K:) [but sometimes neither of these meanings can be clearly inferred from the context: in these cases, it may be rendered Some: and with maA affixed, Sometimes: ] accord. to Er-Radee, its primary meaning is to denote a small number, but it has been so much used to denote a large number as to be in this latter sense as though it were proper, and in the former sense as though it were tropical, requiring context [to explain it]. (Marginal note in my copy of the Mughnee.) [Without the affix mA ,] it governs an indeterminate noun (T, * S, Msb, Mughnee, K) only, (T, S, K,) and a pronoun. (S, M, Mughnee.) You say, rub~a yawomK bak~arotu fiyhi [ Few, or many, days have I gone forth early therein ]: (T:) and rub~a rajulK qaAy^imN [ Few, or many, men are standing ]: (M:) and rub~a rajulK qaAma [ Few, or many, men stood ]: (Msb:) and in like manner, rajulK ↓ rub~ata ; (Msb;) for the t in this case is not a denotative of the fem. gender. (Msb.) The pronoun affixed to it is of the third pers., (S, M,) and is [generally] sing. and masc., (S, Mughnee,) though it may be followed by a fem. and by a dual and by a pl.: (S:) notwithstanding its being determinate in the utmost degree, its use in this manner is allowable because it resembles an indeterminate noun in its being used without the previous mention of the noun to which it relates; and hence it requires a noun to explain it: (IJ, M:) it annuls the government of rub~a ; (TA;) and the indeterminate noun that follows it is put in the accus. case as a specificative: (S, Mughnee:) thus you say, rub~ahu rajulFA qado Darabotu [ Few, or many, men I have beaten ]: (S, M: *) but accord. to the Koofees, you say rub~ahu rajulFA , (S,) and rub~ahaA A@moraA^apF , (M,) and rub~ahumaA rajulayon$ , and rub~ahumo rijaAlFA , and rub~ahun~a nisaA='F : he who puts the pronoun in the sing. [in all cases] holds it to be allusive to something unknown; and he who does not put it in the sing. [when it is not followed by a sing. noun] holds it to be used in reply to a question, as though it were said to a man, “ Hast thou not any young women? ” and he answered, rub~ahun~a jawaArK qado malakotu [ Few, or many, young women have I possessed ]: Ibn-Es-Sarráj says that the grammarians are as though they were of one consent in holding rub~a to be a replicative [app. meaning in a case of this kind, with an affixed pronoun]: (S:) [but it is not always a replicative in a case of this kind; though perhaps it was originally:] AHeyth cites as an ex. warub~ahu EaTibFA A^anoqa*otu mi AlEaTabi [ And many a perishing man have I saved from perdition ]. (TA. [But the reading commonly found in grammars is mino EaTabiho from his state of perdition. ]) The following is an ex. of the use of rub~a to denote a small number, [or rather to denote singleness,] A^alaA rub~a mawoluwdK walayosa lahu A^abN wa*iY waladK lamo yalodihi A^abawaAni [ Now surely scarce an instance is there of anyone born not having a father, and of anyone having offspring whom two parents have not procreated ]; meaning [our Lord] Jesus and Adam: (Mughnee: [but I have substituted yalodihi for yalodahu , the reading in my copy of that work: lamo yalodihi is for lamo yalidohu , for the sake of the metre; like as limo A^ajodi is for lamo A^ajido :]) and among the many exs. of its use to denote a large number, is the saying, in a trad., yaA rub~a kAasiyapK fiY Ald~unoyaA EaAriyapN yawoma Alqiy`mapi [ O, many a female having clothing in the present state of existence will be naked on the day of resurrection! ]; and the saying of an Arab of the desert, after the ending of Ramadán, yaA rub~a SaAy^imihi lano yaESuwmahu wayaA rub~a qaAy^imihi lano yaquwmahu [ O, many a keeper of its fast shall not keep its fast again! and O, many a passer of its nights in prayer, or per- former of its taraAwiyH , shall not pass its nights in prayer, or perform its trAwyH , again!]. (Mughnee.) [But in this last ex., and in others, it relates to few in comparison with others, though many abstractedly.] ― -b2- maA is affixed to rub~a &c. in order that a verb may follow it; (S, Mughnee;) and the verb that follows it is generally a preterite, (T, Mughnee,) as to the letter and the meaning: (Mughnee:) you say, rub~amaA jaA='aniY fulaAnN [ Seldom, or often, such a one came to me, or has come to me ]: (T:) sometimes the verb is a future; (T, Mughnee;) but only when it expresses an event of which one is certain: (T:) so in the saying in the Kur [xv. 2], rub~amaA yawad~u A@l~a*yna kafaruwA lawo kaAnuwA musolimiyna , (T, S, M, Mughnee), meaning Often [ will those who have disbelieved wish that they had been Muslims ]; (Mughnee, Jel;) or seldom, (Zj, T, M, Jel,) because terrors will bereave them of their reason so that they will but seldom recover reason to wish this; (Jel;) for God's threat is true, as though it had come to pass, and therefore the verb here is equivalent to a preterite [which is often used in the Kur and elsewhere in this manner]. (T.) maA is also sometimes affixed when a noun follows, (T, Mughnee,) or a nominal proposition, and generally restricts rub~a &c. from governing: thus, Aboo-Duwád says, rub~amaA AljaAmilu Almuw^ab~alu fiyhimo waEanaA jiyju bayonahun~a AlmihaAru [ Sometimes, or often, the numerous herd of camels is among them, and there are swift horses, among which are the colts ]: another says, making rub~a , with maA affixed, to govern, rub~amaA DarobapK bisayofK SaqiylK qayoni buSoraY waTaEonapK najolaA='a [ Many a stroke with a polished sword of the forging of Busrà, (the Bozrah of the Bible, a city famous for its sword-blades,) and many a wide spear-wound; or, perhaps, few strokes &c.]: (Mughnee: [but I have substituted qayoni for bayona , which is the reading in my copy of the Mughnee, an evident mistranscription:]) and another, cited by IAar, says, gaArapK ↓ maAwiY~a yaA rub~atamaA $aEowaA='a kaA@ll~a*oEapi biA@lomiysami [ Máweeyeh, ( maAwiY~a being an apocopated proper name of a woman, originally maAwiy~apu ,) O, many a raid spreading widely and dispersedly, like the burn with the branding-iron ]. (T. [In the TT, as from the T, I find, here, balo in the place of yA , which I find in a copy of the T, and which is the reading commonly known.])

definition: A party, division, sect, or distinct body or class, of men: (M:) or a large assembly or company: (K:) or a myriad;
sourceDefinition: A party, division, sect, or distinct body or class, of men: (M:) or a large assembly or company: (K:) or a myriad; i. e. ten thousand: (M, K:) or thereabout: (M:) and ↓ rib~pN signifies the same: (M, K:) or this signifies a company [ of men ]: (T:) the pl. of the former is ribaAbN : (S, M:) and that of the latter is A^arib~apN : (T, K:) by Th [and in the K], the former pl. is said to be a pl. of rib~apN ; but this is a mistake. (M.) ― -b2- [Hence, the pl.] ribaAbN signifies Companions. (K.) ― -b3- And hence [also], i. e., as pl. of Alr~ubapu , (S, M,) Alr~ibaAbu is an appellation of The [ confederate ] tribes of Dabbeh; (M, K, TA;) or Teym and 'Adee and 'Okl; (T, TA;) or Teym and 'Adee and 'Owf and Thowr and Ashyab; (TA; [but for the orthography of the last of these names I have found no authority; it is written in the TA A$yb , without any syll. signs;]) and Dabbeh was their paternal uncle; (TA;) or five tribes which united in a confederacy, consisting of Dabbeh and Thowr and 'Okl and Teym and 'Adee: (S:) they were thus called because of their division into distinct bodies; (M;) or because they collected themselves (As, Th, S, TA) in distinct bodies: (Th, M, TA:) or because they united in a confederacy against Temeem Ibn-Murr: (AO, M, TA:) or because they dipped their hands in some rub~ , and formed a confederacy over it: (As, T, M, K:) or, as some say, because they congregated, and became like the ribaAb [or bundle] of arrows [used in the game called Almayosir ]: (TA:) the rel. n. is ↓ rub~iY~N , formed from the sing., (Sb, S, M,) accord. to a rule generally observed except when a [single] man has a pl. word for his name, as kilaAbN &c. (S, TA.) ― -b4- The sing. ( rub~apN ) also signifies Plenty, or abundance, of the means of subsistence: (K:) and constant, or inseparable, prosperity. (Khálid Ibn-Jembeh, TA.) -A2- See also rub~aY .

definition: Reared, fostered, brought up, fed, or nourished;
sourceDefinition: Reared, fostered, brought up, fed, or nourished; [ and taken good care of, until the age of puberty; (see 1;)] as also ↓ marobuwbN ; (S, M, K;) both applied to a boy: (S, M:) and in like manner applied to a horse: (M:) or the latter epithet, applied to a horse, (tropical:) tended well, or taken good care of: (A:) the former is also applied to a gazelle; (IAar, K in art. dxl ;) [as meaning (assumed tropical:) brought up in, or near, the house or tent, and there fed; ] like A^aholiY~N : (TA in that art.:) and [its fem.] rabiybapN is applied to a ewe or she-goat, ( $aApN , K,) meaning (assumed tropical:) brought up in the tent, or house, for the sake of her milk; (S, K; [see also rub~aY ;]) pl. rabaAy^ibu ; (S;) this last being applied to sheep or goats that are tied near to the tents, or houses, and there fed, and that do not go forth to pasture; (M, TA;) of which it is said that none are to be taken for the poor-rate. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence, A step-son, ] a man's wife's son (T, S, M, A, Msb, K) by another husband; (T, S, M, A, K;) as also ↓ rabuwbN : (T, K:) pl. A^arib~aA='u . (Msb.) And rabiybapN [ A step-daughter; ] a woman's husband's daughter by another wife: (S:) or a man's wife's daughter (T, M, A, Mgh, Msb, K) by another husband; (T, M, A;) because he rears her: (Mgh:) pl. rabaAy^ibu (A, Mgh, Msb) and sometimes rabiybaAtN . (Msb.) ― -b3- Also, and ↓ raAb~N , (T, M, K,) both syn., like $ahiydN and $aAhidN , and xabiyrN and xaAbirN , (TA,) or the latter, (T, S,) mentioned by IAar, is the correct term, (T,) [ A step-father; ] the husband of a mother (T, S, M, K) who has a child by another husband. (T.) And rabiybapN and ↓ raAb~apN , (T,) or the latter [only], (S, K,) [ A stepmother; ] the wife of a father (T, S, K) who has a child by another wife. (T.) rabiybapN also signifies [ A foster-mother; ] a woman who has the charge of a child, who carries him, and takes care of him, and rears, or fosters, him; (Th, S, M, Msb, K;) like ↓ raAb~apN ; the former being of the measure faEilaypN in the sense of faAEilapN . (Msb.) A^arb~aA='u Aln~abiY~ [meaning The foster-fathers of the Prophet ] is an appellation given to the people [of the tribe of Saad] among whom Mohammad was suckled; as though Arb~A=' were pl. of rabiybN [as it is said to be in one of the senses mentioned above]. (TA.) ― -b4- And rabiybN signifies also A confederate; a person with whom one unites in a confederacy, league, or covenant. (M, K.) ― -b5- And A king. (M, K.)

(TA.) [See an ex. in a verse cited voce A^afaADa in art. fyD .]

definition: , applied to a ewe or she-goat ( $aApN ), (S, M, &c.
sourceDefinition: , applied to a ewe or she-goat ( $aApN ), (S, M, &c.,) That has brought forth: (M, Msb, K:) and so if her young one has died: (M, K:) or that has recently brought forth: (Lh, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K:) or that has brought forth twenty days before: (M:) or that has brought forth two months before: (El-Umawee, S, M:) or that is followed, (M,) or accompanied, (As, Mgh,) by her young one: (As, M, Mgh:) or that is confined in the tent, or house, for the sake of her milk: (Msb: [see also rabiybapN , voce rabiybN :]) accord. to AZ, (S, Msb,) it is applied to a she-goat, (S, M, Msb,) and raguwvN is applied to a ewe: (M:) accord. to others, the former is applied to a she-goat and a ewe, and sometimes to a she-camel: (S, Msb:) the pl. is ↓ rubaAbN , (As, T, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) which is extr. [in form]: (M, K:) Lh mentions the phrase ganamN rubaAbN , or ribaAbN , which, he says, is rare. (M.) ― -b2- See also rub~aAnN , in two places. -A2- A benefit, favour, boon, or good. (AA, T, K.) [See an ex. in the first paragraph of art. j$A^ .] ― -b2- A want; (AA, T, K;) as in the saying, liY Einoda fulaAnK rub~aY [ I have a want for such a one to supply, or accomplish ]. (AA, T.) -A3- A child's nurse; syn. daAyapN . (AA, T. In one copy of the T bAbh ; and in the TA rAyp . [Perhaps the right reading is raAb~apN , meaning a foster-mother. ]) -A4- A firm knot: (AA, T, K:) [and so, app., ↓ rub~aAnN , if correctly written thus, in the instance here following.] You say, A_ino kunota A_izorika ↓ biY ta$hd~u Zahoraka faA^aroxi birub~aAni , (TA,) or birub~aA A_izorika (so in the TT, as from the M, [as though for birub~aY ,]) and minE rub~aY A_izorika , (T, TA,) a prov., meaning (assumed tropical:) If thou place thy reliance upon me, then let me weary myself, and enjoy thou relaxation and rest: (T, TA:) here rub~aY [properly] signifies a firm knot. (T.) [See also a similar prov. in Freytag's Arab. Prov. i. 24.]) -A5- Also a name of Jumádà-l-Oolà [the fifth month of the Arabian calendar]; and so ↓ rub~N : (M, K:) and likewise, (K,) or accord. to Kr, (M,) a name of Jumádà-l-Ákhireh [the sixth month]; and so ↓ rub~apu : (M, K:) and this last likewise, (K, there expressly said to be with damm,) or ↓ rab~apu , (so accord. to the M as transcribed in the TT,) a name of Dhu-l-Kaadeh [the eleventh month]: (M, K:) thus these months were called in the Time of Ignorance. (M. [See also $ahorN : and see run~aY or Alr~un~aY , in art. rn .])

sourceDefinition: sing. of rib~iy~uwna (T, S, K,) which signifies Thousands (Fr, Th, T, S, K) of men: (S, K:) accord. to Akh, it is from Alr~ab~u ; and if so, it is ↓ rab~iy~uwna , with fet-h to the r : but accord. to Fr, it is from rib~apN , meaning “ a company: ” (Th, T:) Zj says that it is rib~iy~uwna and ↓ rub~iy~uwna , with kesr to the r and also with damm to the r , and signifies a numerous company: he adds that rib~apN is said by some to signify “ ten thousand; ” and that rb~yuwn is said to signify learned, pious, patient men; and that each of these sayings is good: accord. to Aboo-Tálib, it signifies numerous companies: (T:) [in the Kur iii. 140,] El-Hasan read ↓ rub~iy~uwna ; and Ibn-' Abbas, ↓ rab~iy~uwna ; the former with damm, and the latter with fet-h, to the r . (L, TA.) ― -b2- See also rab~aAniY~N .

sourceDefinition: The first, or beginning, or commencement, or the first and fresh state, of anything; (As, A 'Obeyd, T;) [and so ↓ rab~aAnN &c., as appears from what follows.] You say, A^atayotuhu fiY rub~aAni $abaAbihi , (T,) and $bAbh ↓ rab~aAni , or $bAbh ↓ rib~aAni , (accord. to different copies of the T,) and $bAbh ↓ rubaAbi , (T,) and $bAbh ↓ rabaAbi , or $bAbh ↓ ribaAbi , (accord. to different copies of the T,) and $bAbh ↓ rub~aY , all meaning [ I came to him ] in the beginning, or first and fresh state, of his youth. (T.) And AifoEalo *`lika AlA^amora birub~aAnihi Do thou that thing in its first and fresh state: so accord. to ISk: and hence, he says, ↓ $aApN rub~aY [explained above]. (S.) And A^axa*otu Al$~aYo'a birub~aAnihi , (As, S, K, *) and ↓ birab~aAnihi , with damm and with fet-h, (K,) i. e. [ I took the thing ] in its first state: (K:) or altogether, (As, S, K,) not leaving of it aught. (As, S.) They said also, *arohu birub~aAnK [app. meaning Leave thou him early, before he acquire more power ]: and Th cites the following [as an ex.]: fa*arohumo birub~aAnK waA_il~aA ta*arohumu yu*iyquwka maA fiyhimo waA_ino kaAna A^akovaraA [which seems to mean Then leave thou them early, before they acquire more power; for if thou do not, or wilt not, leave them, they will make thee to taste what is in them, though it be more ]. (M.) ― -b2- Also, accord. to A 'Obeyd, The chief, or main, part or portion of a constellation: or, accord. to As, the aggregate thereof: or, accord. to AO, ↓ rab~aAnN , with fet-h, has this meaning: (T:) or both signify a company or an assembly, or an aggregate or assemblage. (K, TA.) -A2- Also A captain of sailors (Sh, K) in the sea; (Sh;) and so ↓ rub~aAniY~N : (Sh, K:) one skilled in navigation: pl. [or rather coll. n. of the latter] rub~aAniy~apN . (TA voce rahonaAmajN .) -A3- See also rub~aY , in two places.

definition: (T, S, M, A, K) and ↓ rib~iY~N (M,) or ↓ rib~iY~N , (A, KL,) One who devotes himself to religious services or exercises, or applies himself to acts of devotion;
sourceDefinition: (T, S, M, A, K) and ↓ rib~iY~N (M,) or ↓ rib~iY~N , (A, KL,) One who devotes himself to religious services or exercises, or applies himself to acts of devotion; (S, A, K;) who possesses a knowledge of God: (T, S, K, KL:) or a learned man: (T:) or the first signifies, (M,) or signifies also, (K,) and so the second, (M,) i. q. HaborN [i. e. a learned man, or particularly of the Jews, &c.; or a good, or righteous, man ]; (M, K;) and a lord, or master, of knowledge or science: or a worshipper of the Lord ( Alr~ab~ ): (M:) or a learned man, a teacher of others, who nourishes people with the small matters of knowledge, or science, before the great: (IAar, T:) or a learned man firmly grounded in knowledge, or science, and religion: or a learned man who practices what he knows and instructs others: or one of high rank in knowledge, or science: or learned with respect to what is lawful and what is unlawful, and what is commanded and what is forbidden: (TA:) rab~aAniY~N is a rel. n. from rab~aAnN ; or from Alr~ab~u meaning “ God: ” (TA, and some copies of the K:) the A and n being added to give intensiveness to the signification; (M;) or, as Sb says, to denote a special reference to the knowledge of the Lord, as though the word signified one possessing a knowledge of the Lord exclusively of other branches of knowledge; (T;) so that it is like liHoyaAniY~N , (T, M, and so in some copies of the K,) meaning “ long-bearded, ” (T,) or “ largebearded, ” (M,) and raqabaAniY~N , “ thick-necked, ” and $aEoraAniY~N , “ having much hair: ” (T:) or it is a Syriac word; (TA, and some copies of the K;) or Hebrew; and was unknown to the [pagan] Arabs, and known only to the men of law and science: (TA:) the pl. is rab~aAniy~uwna , (T, S,) occurring in the Kur iii. 73 (S) [and v. 48 and 68].

definition: Softness, tenderness, or smoothness: (O, L, K: *) this is the primary signification, accord.
sourceDefinition: Softness, tenderness, or smoothness: (O, L, K: *) this is the primary signification, accord. to the O and L: accord. to MF, softness, tenderness, or smoothness, and uncleanness, or dirtiness; but this addition is wrong; and he has wrongly ascribed this explanation to Er-Rághib, who mentions in his book only the words of the Kur-án. (TA.) ― -b2- Ampleness, or abundance, of the means of subsistence; and abundance of herbage, or of the goods, conveniences, or comforts, of life: (S, K, * TA:) and so ↓ rafaAgapN , (JK, * S, * TA,) an inf. n., (S,) and ↓ rafaAgiyapN , [also, app., an inf. n., like rafaAhiyapN ;] (JK, * S, * TA;) and ↓ rufagoniyapN , like bulahoniyapN (K, TA) and rufahoniyapN , (TA,) [in which the last three letters, following the g , are all augmentative,] signifies [the same, or] ampleness, or abundance, of the means of subsistence. (K, TA.) -A2- Also, (S, Msb, K, &c.,) and ↓ rufogN , (S, Msb, TA,) the former of the dial. of Temeem, and the latter of the dial. of the people of El- 'Áliyeh and of El-Hijáz, (Aboo-Kheyreh, Msb, TA,) [The groin; ] the root of the thigh; (ISk, Jm, Msb, K; and Mgh in art. whm ;) and any of the other magaAbin [or places of flexure or creasing ]; (ISk, Msb;) and any place of the body in which dirt collects, (ISk, Jm, L, Msb, K,) such as the armpit and the crease of the belly and the like: (L:) or the inner side of the thigh, at the root: (JK:) or the inner side of the root of each thigh, next the upper parts of the sides of the pubes, where the upper parts of the inner sides of the thighs and the upper part of the belly [app. a mistake for the lower part of the belly ] meet: (TA:) [or each of the two inguinal creases; for] the rufogaAni are between the pubes and the thigh, [ one on each side, ] and are also called the magaAbin : (Zj in his “ Khalk el-Insán: ”) the latter ( rufogN ) also particularly signifies the armpit: (Fr, Mgh, K:) or, as some say, the root [or innermost part ] of the armpit: (TA:) and the same, (ISh, K,) or each, (Msb,) the parts around the faroj [or vulva, or external portion of the organs of generation, ] (ISh, Msb, K) of a woman: (ISh, K:) and sometimes the faroj itself: (Msb:) the pl. is A^arofaAgN (S, Mgh, Msb, K) and rufuwgN (Msb, K) and rifaAgN and [of pauc.] A^arofugN , the first of which four is pl. of rufogN , [and is properly a pl. of pauc.,] the rest being pls. of rafogN : (Msb:) [accord. to J,] A^arofaAgN signifies the magaAbin [or places of flexure, or creasing, ] of the armpits, and of the roots of the thighs: (S:) accord. to As, the armpits, and the [ other ] magaAbin of the body: (Mgh in art. whm :) IAar says that ↓ maraAfigu signifies the roots of the arms and of the thighs, and has no proper sing.: and AlArfAg is the sing. of Alr~ufagu ( wAHd Alr~ufagi [but this is app. a mistranscription for wuAHiduhu Alr~ufogu meaning that A^arofaAgN has for its sing: rufogN ]): and ↓ rufagN signifies the magaAbin and maHaAlib [by which latter are app. meant the places that sweat ] of the body: accord. to As, what is thus termed is in camels and in human beings. (TA. [But the sing. verb in this last clause suggests that there is another mistranscription here, and a looseness of explanation; and that we should read thus: “ and rufogN (not rufagN ) signifies any of the magaAbin and of the maHaAlib of the body. ”]) ― -b2- Also, both words, The dirt of the nail: (K:) or the dirt that is between the end of the finger and the nail, when the nail is not pared, after scratching the A^arofaAg [or groins and armpits and the like ]: (TA:) or the former [or each] signifies the dirt of the magaAbin [or places of flexure, or creasing, of the body ]; (K;) or the dirt and sweat that collect in the mgAbn of the armpits, and of the roots of the thighs, and other places of folding of the limbs. (TA.) ― -b3- Also the former word, ( rafogN ,) (assumed tropical:) A soft, or plain, tract, or piece, of land: (JK, K: *) pl. rifaAgN . (K.) ― -b4- (assumed tropical:) Land having much soil or dust. (L, K.) [Hence,] one says, jaA='a fulaAnN bimaAlK karafogi Alt~uraAbi (assumed tropical:) Such a one came with, or brought, wealth, or cattle, abundant as the soil, or dust, thus termed. (L.) ― -b5- (assumed tropical:) A place affected with drought, or barrenness, (L, K,) thin, or shallow, [ in its soil, ] of middling quality. (L.) ― -b6- (tropical:) The vilest place in a valley, and the worst in re spect of soil: (Aboo-Málik, K, * TA:) the lowest part of a valley and of a desert: (TA:) or A^arofaAgu AlwaAdiY signifies the sides of the valley. (AHn, JK, TA.) ― -b7- (tropical:) A side, or lateral part or region: (Akh, IAar, K:) pl. A^arofugN . (K.) You say, huwa fiY rafogK mino qawomihi , and mina Alqaroyapi , (tropical:) He is in a side, or lateral part, not in the middle, of his people, or party, and of the town, or village. (IAar, TA.) ― -b8- Also sing. of A^arofaAgN meaning (tropical:) The lower, or lowest, baser or basest, meaner or mean est, sort, or the rabble, or refuse, of mankind; (JK, K, TA;) likened to the A^arofaAg of a valley: or the sing. of ArfAg in this sense is ↓ rufogN . (TA.) ― -b9- (assumed tropical:) A skin for water, or for milk, that is thin, or rendered thin, (accord. to different copies of the K,) and of little worth. (K, TA.) ― -b10- (assumed tropical:) The straw of [ the species of millet called ] *urap : so accord. to the author of the L; but accord. to others, it is dafogN , with dAl , if this be not a mis transcription. (TA.) -A3- As an epithet, rafogN sig nifies Soft; applied to dust, or earth, and to food, or wheat, ( TaEaAm ,) and to kilos [or quicklime, &c.]. (K, * TA.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. yaroqaY , inf. n. ruqiY~N (JK, K, TA, [but this inf. n. is omitted in the CK,]) and raqoYN , (K, TA, [but this is omitted in my MS. copy of the K,]) He ascended, A_ilayohi [ to him, or it ]; as also ↓ ArtqY , and ↓ trq~Y : (K:) or he ascended a ladder, or a stair: (JK:) or raqiytu fiyhi , (S, Msb, in the Mgh raqiYa fyh ,) inf. n. ruqiY~N (S, Mgh, Msb) and raqoYN ; (S, Msb;) and ↓ Artqyt , (S, Mgh, * Msb,) and ↓ trq~yt ; (Mgh, * Msb;) I ascended it; (S;) namely, a ladder, or a stair, (S, Mgh, Msb,) &c.: (Msb:) and raqiytu Aljabala (Msb,) and Als~aToHa , (Mgh, Msb, TA,) the verb being thus trans. by itself, (Msb, TA,) without fiY (Mgh,) and likewise with fY , (TA,) I ascended, or mounted, upon the mountain, and upon the house-top: (Msb:) and ↓ ArtqY is in like manner trans. without fY ; whence the saying, laqadi SaEobFA ↓ A@rotaqayota murotaqFY [ Thou hast indeed ascended a difficult place of ascent ]. (Mgh.) ― -b2- [Hence,] Airoqa EalaY ZaloEika Ascend thou, and go, [ according to thy limping, or halting, i. e.] as far as thou art able to do so, and impose not upon thyself that which thou art not able to perform. (Mgh.)

Euw*apN [as meaning A charm, or spell, either uttered or written ], (K, TA,) by which a person having an evil affection, such as fever and epilepsy &c., is charmed: (TA:) when it is in any other language than that of the Arabs, and one knows not what is in it, it is disapproved, lest it should involve enchantment ( siHor ) and infidelity; but in such as is from the Kur-án or any of the forms of prayer, there is no harm: (Mgh in art. tm : [see tamiymapN :]) [but Euw*apN generally signifies “ an amulet to charm the wearer against the evil eye &c. ”:] 'Orweh says, famaA tarakaA mino Euw*apK yaEorifaAnihaA walaA ruqoyapK A_il~aA bihaA raqayaAniY [ And they two left not any amulet that they knew, nor any charm, or spell, but with it they charmed me ]: (TA:) [sometimes, also, it signifies anything by which one enchants, or fascinates: and hence it is said,] AlmaroA^apu ruqoyapN [ Woman is a thing by which one is enchanted, or fascinated ]: (Msb:) pl. ruqFY . (S, Msb, K.)

definition: The saying in the Kur [lxxv.

sourceDefinition: [a coll. gen. n.] A kind of tree of sweet odour, (AO, T, S, A, Msb, K,) which distils much ( say~aAlN ); (A;) of the trees of the desert; (AO, T, S, A, Msb;) a kind of tree of the desert, of sweet odour, with the wood of which the teeth are cleaned; not large; and having a berry; ( Hab~ap ); called [i. e., the tree is called, and not the berry, for the verb is masculine,] gAr [a name commonly and properly applied to the laurus nobilis, or sweet bay ]: n. un. ranodapN : (M:) or the myrtle ( A=s ); (M, A;) this is also called rnd , (Kh, Msb, K,) on account of its sweet odour; (Kh, Msb;) and Ahmad Ibn-Yahyà says that the rnd is the A=s accord. to all the lexicologists except Aboo- 'Amr Esh-Sheybánee and IAar, who assert that the rnd is the plant called Hanowap , and is of sweet odour; but AO also denies it to be the A=s ; (T;) and so does As: (S:) or aloes-wood, ( Euwd ,) with which one fumigates; (M;) Ewd (or Euwdu AlT~iybi , with which one fumigates, AO, and T,) is also thus called, (AO, As, T, S, K,) sometimes: (AO, As, T, S:) [and accord. to Forskål, (Flor. Aeg. Ar., cxix.,) the artemisia pontica bears this name.]

definition: , (S, K,) inf. n. taroniyqN , (IAar, S,) He rendered water turbid, thick, or muddy; (IAar, S, K;) as also ↓ Arnq . (S, K.) ― -b2- And the former, He cleared it; rendered it clear: thus it bears two...
sourceDefinition: , (S, K,) inf. n. taroniyqN , (IAar, S,) He rendered water turbid, thick, or muddy; (IAar, S, K;) as also ↓ Arnq . (S, K.) ― -b2- And the former, He cleared it; rendered it clear: thus it bears two contr. significations. (IAar, K.) [Hence,] one says, rn~q A@ll~`hu qa*aAtaka May God clear away thy q*Ap [or mote in the eye; probably meaning (assumed tropical:) that which annoys thee ]. (IAar, K) -A2- Also, as an intrans. verb, He was, or became, confounded, or perplexed, and unable to see his right course. (TA.) And taroniyqN signifies A man's standing, not knowing whether to go or come. (TA.) And The being weak, or infirm, [and, app., disordered, or perturbed, ] in sight, and in body, and in an affair or case. (S, K.) Hence, (TA,) rn~qwA fiY AlA^amori They confused the judgment, or opinion, [ that they formed, or they were confused in judgment or opinion, ] in, or respecting, the affair, or case. (S, K.) ― -b2- Also He paused and waited. (TA.) [Hence the saying,] ram~adati AlmiEozaY faran~iqo ran~iqo , (JK, S, K,) i. e. The she-goats have secreted milk in their udders; (JK;) but wait thou, wait thou, (JK, S, TA,) for their bringing forth, (S, TA,) for they show signs, but do not bring forth until after some time: (S:) thou wilt have to wait long for them: (TA:) sometimes it is said with m [in the place of n ], and also with d [in the place of r ]: (S, TA:) it is mentioned in art. rbq [q. v.]. (K. [See also art. rmq .]) ― -b3- Also He continued looking; (S, K, TA, in this art. and in art. rmq ;) like rm~q . (S and TA in the same two arts.) And you say also, rn~q A_ilayohi Aln~aZura and dn~q [meaning He continued looking at it ]. (S in art. dnq .) And rn~q Aln~aZara meaning [ He looked covertly, or clandestinely; or] he concealed the looking. (TA.) ― -b4- Said of a company of men, They remained, stayed, dwelt, or abode, in a place ( bimakaAnK ), (S, K,) and confined themselves therein. (S.) ― -b5- Said of a bird, He flapped his wings in the air, (S, K,) and remained steady, (S,) not flying: (S, K:) or flapped his wings in the air without alighting and without quitting his place: or it has two meanings: i. e. he expanded his wings in the air without moving them: and he flapped his wings. (TA.) Hence, said of a captive, He stretched out his neck on the occasion of slaughter, like the bird expanding his wings. (TA.) [Hence also,] rn~qt Als~afiynapu (JK, TA) fiY makaAnihaA (JK) The ship turned round in its place without proceeding in its course. (JK, TA.) ― -b6- rn~qt Al$~amosu The sun became near to setting. (TA. [See also dn~qt .]) And rn~qt minohu Almaniy~apu (tropical:) Death was near to befalling him: a metaphorical phrase from rn~q said of a bird. (TA.) ― -b7- rn~N Aln~awomu (S, K) fiY Eayonayohi (K) (tropical:) Sleep pervaded ( xaAlaTa ) his eyes, (S, Z, Sgh, K,) without his sleeping. (Z, TA.) -A3- taroniyqN also signifies The breaking of the wing of a bird by a shot or throw, or by disease, so that he, or it, falls. (Lth, K.) [You say of the bird run~iqa or run~iqa janaAHuhu His wing was broken &c. See the pass. part. n., below.]

[And accord. to Freytag, ↓ ranoqaA='u occurs in the Deewán El-Hudhaleeyeen as meaning A small quantity of turbid water. ] Accord. to Ibn-'Abbád, (TA,) one says, SaAra AlmaA='u ranoqapF , (K, TA,) or ↓ ruwonaqapF , (JK, and so in the CK and in my MS. copy of the K,) meaning The water became such that mud predominated in it: (JK, K, TA:) but the correct phrase, as given in the “Nawádir” by Lh, is, SaAra AlmaA='u ranoqapF waAHidapF [ The water became one puddle in which mud predominated ]. (TA.) See also ranoqN .

definition: The maA=' [or water ] of a sword;
sourceDefinition: The maA=' [or water ] of a sword; (S, K, TA;) i. e. its firinod [or diversified wavy marks, streaks, or grain ]; (TA;) and its beauty; (S, K;) or the semblance of water that is seen upon a sword. (JK.) ― -b2- And (hence, S) of the DuHaY [or early part of the forenoon], (S, K,) &c.; (S;) meaning (tropical:) The first, or beginning, thereof; (JK, * TA;) and its clearness. (TA.) One says, A^atayotuhu fiY rawonaqi AlD~uHaY I came to him in the first, or beginning, of the DHY ; like as one says fiY wajohi AlD~uHaY . (TA.) And rawonaqu Al$~abaAbi means (tropical:) The prime of youth; and its freshness, or brightness, and beauty. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: (JK, S, K) and taronuwqN and turonuwqaA='u (K) The mud that is in rivers, and in a channel of water, (S, K,) when the water has sunk therefrom into the earth: (K:) or the thin, and viscous, cohesive, or slimy, mud remaining in a pool of water left by a torrent: (JK:) or the slime of a well, and of the channel of a torrent, mixed with black, or black and fetid, mud. (Mgh voce tiqonN , from the “Jámi'” of El-Ghooree.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, A, K,) EalaY A^amori ka*aA , (S,) or EalaY ka*aA , (A,) inf. n. muraAwaDapN , (Mgh,) (tropical:) He coaxed, wheedled, beguiled, or deluded, him; (S, A, Mgh, K;) and he endeavoured to deceive or beguile him; like as he does who is training a beast not yet rendered perfectly tractable; (Mgh;) in order to make him enter into such a thing or affair; (S;) or until he entered into such a thing. (A.) ― -b2- Hence, (Mgh,) bayoEu AlmuraAwaDapi (tropical:) That mode of selling which is termed bayoEu AlmuwaASafapi ; (Mgh, K; *) which is when one describes to a man an article of merchandise not present with him: (Sh, K:) this is said in a trad. to be an action that is disapproved: (K:) but some of the professors of practical law allow it when the article of merchandise agrees with the description. (L.)

sourceDefinition: (Yaakoob, S, A) and A^arowaDa (Yaakoob, S) It (a place) became abundant in its riyaAD [pl. of rawoDapN , q. v.]; (Yaakoob, S, A;) as also ↓ AstrAD . (A.) And A^arowaDati AlA^aroDu and A^araADat The land became clad with plants, or herbage (M.) ― -b2- [And hence,] ArAD (tropical:) It (a valley) had water stagnating, or remaining, or collecting, in it; (S, A, Msb, K;) concealing its bottom; (A;) as also ↓ AstrAD : (S, M, A, Msb, K:) and so the former verb, (S,) or ↓ both, (A,) said of a watering-trough: (S, A:) or, when said of a watering-trough, the former verb signifies (assumed tropical:) it had its bottom, or lower part, covered with water: (M:) and ↓ the latter, (assumed tropical:) the water spread widely upon the surface thereof; (M;) and so the former too: (TA:) or ↓ the latter, (tropical:) it had a sufficient quantity of water poured into it to conceal its bottom; (O, K;) or to cover its bottom, or lower part. (L, TA.) ― -b3- And from ArAD , said of a watering-trough, has originated the saying, (S,) $aribuwA Hat~aY A^araADuwA (assumed tropical:) (assumed tropical:) They drank until they thoroughly satisfied their thirst. (S, K. *) And ArAD also signifies (assumed tropical:) He drank a second draught after a first. (K.) -A2- ArAD A@ll~`hu AlA^aroDa : see 2. ― -b2- [Hence,] ArAD AlHawoDa (assumed tropical:) He poured into the watering-trough a sufficient quantity of water to conceal its bottom. (TA.) ― -b3- And hence, (TA,) A^araADahumo , said of a vessel, (tropical:) It satisfied their thirst: (S, * K:) or it satisfied their thirst in some degree. (M, TA.) Hence the saying, fadaEaA biA_inaA='K yuriyDu Alr~ahoTa (tropical:) And he called for a vessel which would satisfy (K, TA) in some degree (TA) the [ number of men termed a ] rahoT ; (K, TA;) occurring in a trad., (TA,) accord. to one relation, but the more common is yurobiDu , (K, TA,) with the singlepointed b . (TA.) ― -b4- ArAD also signifies (assumed tropical:) He poured milk upon milk; (K;) accord. to A 'Obeyd; but he deems it strange. (TA.)

definition: in selling and buying is syn.
sourceDefinition: in selling and buying is syn. with Alt~aHaA*iY ; i. e. (tropical:) The increasing [ of the sum offered ] and diminishing [ of the sum demanded ] which take place between the two parties bargaining; as though each of them were making his companion easy and tractable; from Alr~iyaADapu as inf. n. of raADa in the first of the senses expl. above. (TA.) In the phrase taraAwaDaA Als~iloEapa , meaning (assumed tropical:) They coaxed, wheedled, beguiled, or deluded, each other, with respect to the article of merchandise, [ in the manner explained above, or otherwise, ] the omission of the prep. [ fiY ] requires consideration. (Mgh.) You say also, taraAwaDaA fiY AlA^amori (assumed tropical:) They practised dissimulation, or showed feigned affection, each to the other, in, or respecting, the thing, or affair; as also tanaAZaraA : (TK in art. nZr :) Alt~araAwuDu fiY AlA^amori is syn. with Alt~anaAZuru . (M and K in art. nZr .)

definition: (S, M, A, Msb, K) and ↓ riyDapN (AA, A, K) and ↓ riy~iDapN (TA) [seem to be best rendered, in general, A meadow;
sourceDefinition: (S, M, A, Msb, K) and ↓ riyDapN (AA, A, K) and ↓ riy~iDapN (TA) [seem to be best rendered, in general, A meadow; meaning, a verdant tract of land, somewhat watery; or (as in Johnson's dictionary) ground somewhat watery, not ploughed, but covered with grass and flowers: and sometimes, a garden: accord. to the following explanations:] verdant land: a place where water collects, and the herbage becomes abundant, without trees: or fresh green herbage, with water, or having water by its side; not otherwise: or, accord. to Aboo-Ziyád El-Kilábee, a tract of plain land, producing [ lote-trees of the kind called ] sidor ; which may be of the extent of Baghdád: and also, of herbs, or leguminous plants, and fresh green herbage: (M:) or this last [ only ]: (S:) or a tract of plain land, in which are jaraAviym [perhaps here meaning ants' nests, as these are generally found in soft soil,] and soft hillocks, in the low, or best and most productive, parts of a country, where water stagnates, or remains, or collects, at least a hundred cubits in extent: (M:) or a tract of sand, and of fresh green herbage, where water stagnates, or remains, or collects; so called because of the stagnation, or remaining, or collecting, of the water therein: (A, K, TA:) it is said that rawoDapN is mostly applied to a place where beasts pasture at pleasure: some say that it signifies a land having waters and trees, and sweet, or pleasant, flowers: (TA:) or a place that is pleasant with flowers; said to be so called because the waters that flow thither rest there: (Msb:) it is said in the 'Ináyeh, that ↓ rawoDN [perhaps a mistake for rawoDapN ] signifies a garden; and in common conventional language, one having rivers, or rivulets: MF says that rivers, or rivulets, do not necessarily belong to the signification; but that having water does; though not in common conventional language: (TA:) accord. to Th, rawoDapN signifies a beautiful garden: (M:) the pl. of rawoDapN is ↓ rawoDN , (S, M, K,) [or rather this is a coll. gen. n.,] and riyaADN , (S, M, A, Msb, K,) originally riwaADN , (S,) and riyDaAnN , (Lth, M, K,) originally riwoDaAnN , (TA,) or rather riyDaAnN is pl. of ↓ rawoDN , (M,) and rawoDaAtN , (M, Msb,) in the dial. of Hudheyl rawaDaAtN : (Msb:) Az says that the ryAD of the hard and stony and rugged tracts in the desert are low level places, in which the rainwater stagnates, or remains, or collects, and which consequently produce various kinds of herbage, that do not quickly dry up and wither: that sometimes a rawoDap contains thickets of wild sidor : and sometimes it is a mile in length and breadth: but such as are very wide are termed qiyEaAn . (TA.) It is said in a prov., A^aHosanu mino bayoDapK fiY rawoDapK [ More beautiful than an egg in a meadow, or garden ]. (A, TA.) And one says, A^anaA Einodaka fiY rawoDapK (tropical:) [ I, in thy presence, am as though I were in a meadow, or garden ]: and majolisuka rawoDapN mino riyaADi Aljan~api (tropical:) [ Thy sittingplace is like a meadow, or garden, of the meadows, or gardens, of Paradise ]. (A, TA.) Mohammad is related to have said, “Between my grave, or between my house, and my pulpit is a rawoDap of the riyaAD of Paradise:” meaning, accord. to Th, that he who abides in this place is as though he abode in a rwDp of the ryAD of Paradise. (M.) [See another tropical meaning of riyaADu Aljan~api voce rataEa , last sentence.] ― -b2- rawoDapN also signifies (assumed tropical:) Any water that collects in pools left by torrents, or the like, and in places in land or in the ground to which the rain-water flows and which retain it. (K, * TA. [In the CK, AlAax~A*At and Almus~AkAt are erroneously put for AlA_ixaA*aAt and Almas~aAkaAt .]) ― -b3- Also, (K,) or ↓ rawoDN , (S, M,) (assumed tropical:) About the half of a firobap [or water-skin ] (S, M, K) of water: (S:) and the former, (tropical:) as much of water as covers the bottom of a watering-trough. (S, M, A.)

definition: [ Fresh butter of the cow or buffalo or sheep or goat;
sourceDefinition: [ Fresh butter of the cow or buffalo or sheep or goat; ] what is produced by churning from milk (Mgh, Msb) of cows [or buffaloes ] and of sheep or goats; what is thus produced from camels' milk being termed jubaAbN , not zubodN ; (Msb;) the zubod of samon before it is clarified over the fire; (L;) [i. e. butter before it is clarified over the fire; ] the zubod [in the CK, erroneously, zabad ] of milk; (S, K;) what is extracted from milk; (M;) and ↓ zub~aAdN signifies the same as zubodN : (K:) ↓ zubodapN is a more particular term, (S, M, L, Msb,) meaning a piece, bit, portion, or somewhat, of zubod : (L:) and zubodu All~abani signifies also the froth ( ragowap ) of milk [if this be not a mistake occasioned by finding Alz~ubodu expl. as meaning zabadu All~abani instead of zubodu All~abani ]. (L.) qado Sar~aHa AlmaHoDu Eani Alz~ubodi [ The clear milk has become distinct from the fresh butter ] is a prov., relating to the appearance of the truth after information that has been doubted. (L.) And ↓ Airotajanati Alz~ubodapu is another prov. [expl. in art. rjn ]. (L.) ― -b2- ↓ zubodapN has for its pl. zubadN , which is metonymically applied to (tropical:) The choice, or best, portions, [or what we often term the cream (by which word the sing. also may be rendered) of anything; as, for instance,] of discourse, or of a story or the like. (Har p. 222, q. v.) ― -b3- [And it also means (assumed tropical:) An issue, or event: (see an ex. voce maxaDa :) generally, such as is relishable, or pleasing. Hence, app.,] one says, AlEumuri ↓ kaAna liqaAw^uka zubodapa (tropical:) [ The meeting with thee was emphatically the event of life; meaning, the most relishable, or pleasing, event of life ]. (A, TA.)

definition: [ Civet; ] a certain perfume, well known: the lawyers and the lexicologists err in saying that it is a certain beast, [meaning the civet-cat, ] from which the perfume is milked: (K:) or this...
sourceDefinition: [ Civet; ] a certain perfume, well known: the lawyers and the lexicologists err in saying that it is a certain beast, [meaning the civet-cat, ] from which the perfume is milked: (K:) or this assertion is not to be reckoned as a mistake, the word being tropically thus applied: so says El- Karáfee: and Z and other authors worthy of confidence thus apply it [as a coll. gen. n.]: Z also mentions a saying in which ↓ zabaAdapN is applied [as a n. un.] to an animal of the kind from which the perfume is obtained: (TA:) this animal is the cat, (K,) i. e. the wild cat, which is like the tame, but longer and larger, and its hair inclines more to blackness: it is brought from India and Abyssinia: (TA:) the perfume above mentioned is a fluid, or matter, exuded, ( ra$aHN , thus in the TA and in my MS. copy of the K, but in the CK wasaxN [i. e. dirt ],) resembling black viscous dirt, (TA,) which collects beneath the animal's tail, upon the anus ( Almaxoraj ), (K,) and in the inner sides of the thighs also, as says Ed-Demámeenee: (TA:) [see also zuhomN :] the beast is taken, and prevented from struggling, and the said exuded fluid or matter, or dirt, ( ra$aH , or wasax , accord. to different copies of the K,) collected there, is scraped off with a piece of the exterior part of a cane, (K,) or, more commonly, with a spoon, (TA,) or with a piece of rag, (K,) or a thin [silver coin such as is called] diroham . (TA. [Other accounts of this perfume, which are less correct, I omit.]) -A2- See also zub~aAdN .

sourceDefinition: A certain perfume: or certain sweetsmelling trees: (K:) or a species of sweet-smelling plant: (S:) it consists of slender round twigs, between [ maA bayona , misprinted mlyn ,] the thickness of the large needle and the thickness of writingreeds, black inclining to yellowness, not having much taste nor odour, its little odour being of a fragrant kind like that of the citron: (Ibn-Seenà, book ii. p. 168:) [Freytag says, as on the authority of the K, but he seems to have taken it from the TK, that, “ accord. to some, it signifies the leaves of a sweet-smelling plant, which has the name of rjl AljrAd , locusts' foot: ” and he adds, as though on the authority of Ibn-Seenà ubi suprá, “ salix Aegyptiaca: ” referring also to Sprengel, Hist. rei. herb., t. i. p. 270:] also saffron: (K:) it is of the measure faEolalN ; (S, TA;) and is a genuine Arabic word, though asserted by Ibn-El-Kutbee to be arabicized. (TA.) A rájiz says, yaA biA^abiY A^anoti wafuwki AlA^a$onabu kaA^an~amaA *ur~a Ealayohi Alz~aronabu [ O, with my father thou shouldst be ransomed, and thy mouth that is cool and sweet, as though zaronab were sprinkled upon it ]. (S.) In the trad. of Umm-Zara, where it is said, Almas~u mas~u A^aronabK waAlr~iyHu riyHu zaronabK [ The feel is the feel of a hare, and the odour is the odour of zaronab ], IAth says that it signifies saffron; and she may mean the sweetness of his odour, or the perfume of his garments among the people. (TA.) ― -b2- Also The [ dung such as is termed ] baEor of wild animals. (K.) -A2- Also, [and, as appears from what follows, ↓ zaronabapN likewise, if this be not a mistranscription,] The vulva of a woman: (K, * TA:) or such as is large: or the external portion thereof: (K:) or a piece of flesh (K, TA) within the zrwAn [a mistranscription for zaradaAn , a name for the vulva ], (TA,) behind the kayonap [or kayon , q. v.]: (K, TA:) behind the ↓ zaronabap is another piece of flesh: so says IAar. (TA.)

definition: A slippery place, from which the feet slip because of its moistness (S, K) or its smoothness;
sourceDefinition: A slippery place, from which the feet slip because of its moistness (S, K) or its smoothness; (K;) for it is [like smooth rock, or is] smooth rock; (S, TA;) as also ↓ zalixN . (K.) And one says also mazal~apN zaloxN [using the latter word as a corroborative]. (TA.) ― -b2- It is also an inf. n. used as an epithet; (TA;) meaning (assumed tropical:) Slippery; (S, A, TA;) applied to a standing-place, (S,) or to a place [absolutely]; (A, TA;) like zalojN ; (S, TA;) as also ↓ zalixN . (A, TA. [In this sense, zaloxN is said in the A to be tropical: app. because it is an inf. n. used as an epithet.]) It is also applied to a well ( rakiy~ap ), meaning Smooth and slippery at its top [or mouth ], so that he who stands upon it slips into it; (TA;) and so ↓ zaluwxN , (S, TA,) and zaluwjN . (L, TA.) [See also zalojN .]

And ziyla zawiyluhu and zawiyluhaA and zawaAluhu : see zawiylN , in art. zwl ; and for the first, see also zawaAlN , in that art. ― -b3- zilotuhu , (S, K,) aor. A^aziyluhu , inf. n. zayolN , (S,) [first pers. of zaAlahu ,] signifies also I put it, or set it, apart, away, or aside; removed it; or separated it; (S, K, TA;) namely, a thing, (S, TA,) from another thing: (TA:) and ↓ AzAlhu also signifies he separated it; like zaAlahu . (TA.) See also 4. One says, zilo DaA^onaka mino miEozaAka Remove, or separate, thy sheep from thy goats. (S, * TA.) And ↓ zilotuhu falamo yanozalo I separated it [partly], but it did not become [wholly] separated. (S, K.) -A2- maA zaAla yafoEalu ka*aA (S in art. zwl , and Msb,) is like maA bariHa , both in its [original] measure, [which is maA zayila accord. to most authorities,] and in its meaning, which is [ He ceased not to do such a thing, or he continued to do such a thing, for it denotes] the continuing to do a thing [as in the ex. above], and a constant state [as in the phrase maA zaAla zayodN qaAy^imFA Zeyd ceased not to be, or continued to be, standing ]: (Msb:) [using the first pers.,] one says, maA zilotu A^afoEaluhu [and maA zalotu , as appears from what follows], meaning maA bariHotu [i. e. I ceased not to do it, or I continued to do it ], (K,) aor. A^azaAlu [supposing the measure of the pret. to be originally faEilotu ] (Msb, K) and A^aziylu [supposing the measure of the pret. to be originally fEalotu ]: (K:) the verb is seldom [in the Msb “ never ”] used without a negative particle: (Az, TA:) one says zilotu A^afoEalu meaning maA zilotu A^afoEalu ; but this is rare: (K:) and maA ziyla yafoEalu ka*aA , (S, Msb, K,) a phrase used by some of the Arabs, (Msb,) mentioned by Akh, (S, TA,) as is meant in [some of the copies of] the K by the addition Eanohu , though Akh is not mentioned in what precedes. (TA.) The verb in maA zaAla and laA yazaAlu is used in the manner of kaAna in governing the noun [which is its subject] in the nom. case and the predicate in the accus. case [as in maA zaAla zayodN qaAy^imFA , expl. above]; but one may not say, maA zaAla zayodN A_il~aA munoTaliqFA , like as one says, maA kaAna zayodN A_il~aA munoTaliqFA ; for zaAla denotes a negation, [meaning he did not a thing, or he was not doing &c.,] and maA and laA denote negation, and two negations together denote an affirmation; so that mA zAl is affirmative like kaAna ; and as one may not say, kaAna zayodN A_il~aA manoTaliqFA , so one may not say, maA zaAla zayodN A_il~aA munoTaliqFA . (Er-Rághib, TA.) One says also, maA zilotu bizayodK Hat~aY faEala *`lika and maA zilotu wazayodFA [ I desisted not with Zeyd until he did that ], (Sb, K, * TA,) inf. n. ziyaAlN . (Sb, TA.) lamo yazalo [ He, or it, has not ceased to be &c., i. e., has ever been &c., (see A^azalN ,)] is said of God, as meaning He has never been nonexistent; and laA yazaAlu , said of Him, He will never be nonexistent. (Kull p. 31.) This [incomplete i. e. non-attributive] verb and the complete [i. e. attributive, which signifies “ it ceased to be ” or “ exist, ” &c.,] differ in their components; the latter being composed of l w z ; and this, of l Y z : or the incomplete is altered from the complete; being made to be with kesr to its medial radical letter, [for it is generally held to be from zayila or zawila ,] after its having been [originally zawala ,] with fet-h: or it is from zaAlahu , aor. yaziyluhu , meaning “ he put it, ” or “ set it, apart, ” &c. (K.)

A^azaAlu [supposing the measure of the pret. to be originally faEilotu ] (Msb, K) and A^aziylu [supposing the measure of the pret. to be originally fEalotu ]: (K:) the verb is seldom [in the Msb “ never ”] used without a negative particle: (Az, TA:) one says zilotu A^afoEalu meaning maA zilotu A^afoEalu ; but this is rare: (K:) and maA ziyla yafoEalu ka*aA , (S, Msb, K,) a phrase used by some of the Arabs, (Msb,) mentioned by Akh, (S, TA,) as is meant in [some of the copies of] the K by the addition Eanohu , though Akh is not mentioned in what precedes. (TA.) The verb in maA zaAla and laA yazaAlu is used in the manner of kaAna in governing the noun [which is its subject] in the nom. case and the predicate in the accus. case [as in maA zaAla zayodN qaAy^imFA , expl. above]; but one may not say, maA zaAla zayodN A_il~aA munoTaliqFA , like as one says, maA kaAna zayodN A_il~aA munoTaliqFA ; for zaAla denotes a negation, [meaning he did not a thing, or he was not doing &c.,] and maA and laA denote negation, and two negations together denote an affirmation; so that mA zAl is affirmative like kaAna ; and as one may not say, kaAna zayodN A_il~aA manoTaliqFA , so one may not say, maA zaAla zayodN A_il~aA munoTaliqFA . (Er-Rághib, TA.) One says also, maA zilotu bizayodK Hat~aY faEala *`lika and maA zilotu wazayodFA [ I desisted not with Zeyd until he did that ], (Sb, K, * TA,) inf. n. ziyaAlN . (Sb, TA.) lamo yazalo [ He, or it, has not ceased to be &c., i. e., has ever been &c., (see A^azalN ,)] is said of God, as meaning He has never been nonexistent; and laA yazaAlu , said of Him, He will never be nonexistent. (Kull p. 31.) This [incomplete i. e. non-attributive] verb and the complete [i. e. attributive, which signifies “ it ceased to be ” or “ exist, ” &c.,] differ in their components; the latter being composed of l w z ; and this, of l Y z : or the incomplete is altered from the complete; being made to be with kesr to its medial radical letter, [for it is generally held to be from zayila or zawila ,] after its having been [originally zawala ,] with fet-h: or it is from zaAlahu , aor. yaziyluhu , meaning “ he put it, ” or “ set it, apart, ” &c. (K.)

sourceDefinition: The ma$iymap [or membrane enclosing the fœtus in the womb ], which come forth with the young: (S, K:) or a thin pellicle over the nose of the fœtus, which dies if it be not removed from it at the birth: (K:) or the water that comes forth upon the head of the fœtus, (T, M,) [i. e.] at the birth: (T:) pl. sawaAbiY [or sawaAbK ]. (S.) ― -b2- Hence, as being likened thereto, because of its fineness, (M,) (assumed tropical:) The dust of the burrows, or holes, of the jerboa; (K;) or fine dust which the jerboa extracts from its burrow, or hole: said by Abu-l-'Abbás to be [ one ] of the burrows, or holes, of the jerboa; but this saying of his has been rebutted. (M.) ― -b3- Hence also, (M,) (tropical:) Increase or offspring [ of camels or the like ]; (S, M, K, TA;) called by the name of that from which they come: (M, TA:) or (so accord. to the M, but accord. to the K “ and ”) camels for breeding: and numerous cattle: (M, K:) or also sheep, or goats, having numerous offspring: (T, S, K:) and it is also applied to denote a large number [app. of animals &c.]. (TA.) One says, liA=li fulaAnK saAbiyaA='u , meaning (tropical:) [ To such a one belong ] numerous cattle. (TA.)

definition: , (S, A, K, TA,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, A, K, TA,) aor. , (K, TA,) inf. n. saHojN , (TA,) He abraded, or otherwise removed, its outer integument, or superficial part; (S, A, K, TA;) relating to one's skin: (S, A, TA:) and he scratched him; or wounded him in the outer skin: also he rubbed it, namely, a thing, with another thing, so as to abrade, or remove, its superficial part: and it, namely, a thing, hitting another thing, abraded from it a little of its superficial part; as when a thing hits the solid hoof previously to [that state of attenuation and abrasion which is termed] AlwajaY . (TA.) You say, saHajotu jilodahu I abraded, or removed, the outer integument [i. e. the cuticle ] of his skin. (S.) And A^aSaAbahu $aYo'N fasaHaja wajohahu [ A thing hit him, and abraded the cuticle of his face ]. (S.) And saHaja AlEuwda biAlmiboradi He abraded the outer part of the wood, or piece of wood, or stick, with the file. (TA.) And yasoHaju AlA^aroDa bixuf~ihi , referring to a camel, (S, K, TA,) He pares the surface of the ground with his foot, so that he is not slow in becoming attenuated and abraded in the sole. (TA.) And saHajati Alr~iyaAHu AlA^aroDa [ The winds pared the surface of the earth, removing the dust and pebbles: like sahajat ]. (A.) ― -b2- Also He bit him so as to make a mark, or marks, upon him; [or so as to lacerate his skin; ] used especially in relation to wild asses; and so ↓ sH~jhu , [but in an intensive sense, i. e. he so bit him much, or many times, (see musaH~ajN ,)] inf. n. tasoHiyjN and musaH~ajN [of which latter see an ex. in the next paragraph]. (TA.) ― -b3- also signifies The combing gently upon the skin of the head: (K, TA:) [ combing the hair with a gentle pressure upon the skin of the head: ] one says, saHaja $aEarahu biAlmu$oTi , inf. n. saHojN , He combed his hair [ pressing the comb ] gently [ upon the skin of his head ]. (TA.) ― -b4- And The going quickly [as though paring the surface of the earth with the feet, or making marks upon it]. (O, K.) You say, mar~a yasoHaju He passed along going quickly: and [so] yasoHaju Als~ayora . (O, TA.) ― -b5- And A running of beasts falling short of such as is vehement. (K.) ― -b6- And [hence, app.,] saHaja AlA^ayomaAna , (TA,) aor. as above, (K, TA,) (assumed tropical:) He made the oaths to follow one another with little, or no, interruption. (K, * TA.) -A2- See also 7.

definition: It (the night) became dark;
sourceDefinition: It (the night) became dark; (S, M, K;) accord. to some, after the jinoH [app. as meaning the first part thereof; or about the half; or a great, or the greater, part ]: (M:) or let down its curtains, and became dark: and Azdf and Asdf signify the same. (AO, TA.) ― -b2- And Asdf Alqawomu The people, or party, entered upon the [ period of the night called ] sudofap . (M.) ― -b3- And Asdf He slept; (AA, K, TA;) as also Azdf . (AA, TA.) ― -b4- And (tropical:) His eyes became dark by reason of hunger or age: (K, TA:) said of a man. (TA.) ― -b5- Also, said of the daybreak, or dawn, It shone: (S, K, TA:) [thus,] as AO says, it has two contr. significations. (TA.) ― -b6- And He lighted the lamp: (K:) or one says, in the dial. of Hawázin, A^asodifuwA , i. e. A^asorijuwA [ Light ye a lamp, or with a lamp]; from Als~iraAju : (S, TA:) or one says in that dial., A^asodafuwA lanaA , i. e. A^asorajuwA [ They lighted for us a lamp, or with a lamp]. (M.) ― -b7- Also He moved away or aside [ in order that the light might enter a place ]. (K.) When a man is standing at a door or an entrance, one says to him, A^asodifo , i. e. Move thou away or aside from the door, or entrance, in order that the chamber, or tent, may become light. (AA, TA. [See also the last sentence of this paragraph.]) ― -b8- [In all of these senses, perhaps excepting one, it is intrans.: in others, trans.] -A2- You say of a woman, Asdft AlqinaAEa , (S, TA,) and AlHijaAba , (TA,) She let down [ the head-covering, and the veil, or curtain ]. (S, TA.) ― -b2- And Asdf Als~itora He raised [ the veil, or curtain ]. (K.) ― -b3- One says also, A^asodifi AlbaAba Open thou the door, or entrance, in order that the chamber, or tent, may become light. (S.)

definition: and ↓ sadofapN i.
sourceDefinition: and ↓ sadofapN i. q. ↓ sadafN , (As, S, M, K,) as meaning The darkness, (As, S, K,) in the dial. of Nejd, (As, S,) or of Temeem; (K;) or as meaning the darkness of night; or, as some say, after the jinoH [which here app. means the first part of the night; or about the half; or a great, or the greater, part ]: (M:) and also as meaning the light, (As, S, K, and M in explanation of the first word,) in the dial. of others, (As, S,) or of Keys: (K:) thus having two contr. significations; (S, K;) or the darkness and the light are called by one and the same name because each of them comes upon the other: (K:) or the first, (S, M, K,) and second, (K,) the commingling of the light and the darkness, (S, M, K,) as in the time between the rising of the dawn, (S,) or as in the time between the prayer of the dawn, (M,) and that when the sun becomes white, (S, M,) accord. to some, as is said by A 'Obeyd; (S;) or, as 'Omárah says, the first signifies darkness in which is light, of the former part of the night and of the latter part thereof, between the redness after sunset and the darkness and between the dawn and the prayer [ of the dawn ]; And Az says that this is the correct explanation: (TA:) and the first and second, a portion of the night: (M, K:) or the first, a remaining portion of the night: (Ibn- Habeeb, TA:) or the first of five divisions of the night: (TA in art. xdr : see xudorapN , voce xadarN :) and the first, (K, TA,) i. e. with damm, (TA,) or the second, (CK,) as also ↓ sadafN , the blackness of night: (K:) the pl. of the first is sudafN ; as in the saying of 'Alee, ka$afotu Eanohumo sudafa All~ayoli I removed from over them the darknesses of night: (TA:) and the pl. of ↓ sadafN is A^asodaAfN . (TA.) -A2- Also the first, A door, or an entrance: (M, K:) or its sud~ap [i. e. vestibule, or porch, &c.]: (K:) and a sort of covering over a door to protect it from the rain. (K, * TA.)

definition: , aor. yasoEaY , inf. n. saEoYN (S, Msb, K, &c.) [and masoEFY , agreeably with general analogy], He walked, went, or went along, (Er-Rághib, Msb, K, TA,) quickly: (Er-Rághib, Mgh, TA:) this, accord....
sourceDefinition: , aor. yasoEaY , inf. n. saEoYN (S, Msb, K, &c.) [and masoEFY , agreeably with general analogy], He walked, went, or went along, (Er-Rághib, Msb, K, TA,) quickly: (Er-Rághib, Mgh, TA:) this, accord. to Er-Rághib, is the primary signification: and hence, Als~aEoYu bayona AlS~afaA waAlmarowapi [ The tripping to and fro between Es-Safà and ElMarweh ]: (TA:) and saEaY fiY ma$oyihi [app. meaning He tripped along, or he trudged along, in his walking ]: (Msb:) [or] Als~aEoYu signifies the going along with vigorousness, and with lightness, activity, or quickness. (Ham p. 665.) ― -b2- He (a man, S) ran; syn. EadaA ; (IAar, S, K, TA;) or jaraY : by the former of which is meant [ he went ] a pace below what is termed Al$~ad~u and above what is termed Alma$oYu . (IAar, TA.) ― -b3- I. q. qaSada [as meaning He repaired, or betook himself ]. (K.) The saying, in the Kur [lxii. 9], faA^osoEawoA A_ilaY *ikori A@oll~`hi is expl. as meaning faAqoSiduwA [ Then repair ye to prayer to God ]: (TA:) or then go ye ( faA^omoDuwA ) to prayer [ to God ]: (Jel:) and Ibn-Mes'ood read faA^omoDuwA . (TA.) Or saEaY A_ilaY AlS~alaApi means He went to prayer, in any manner [i. e. whether quickly or not ]. (Msb.) ― -b4- He was active, or busy and bustling, in procuring the means of subsistence: (TA:) he strove, laboured, or exerted himself; employed himself vigorously, strenuously, or with energy; in any affair, whether good or evil; but mostly used in relation to what is praiseworthy, or praised: (Er-Rághib, TA:) he occupied himself according to his own judgment or discretion or free will, in any work, or deed: (Msb:) he worked, or wrought, or did, (S, Msb, K, TA,) any work, or deed, good or evil: (TA:) he earned, or gained. (S, K, TA.) One says, huwa yasoEaY EalaY qawomihi He manages, conducts, orders, regulates, or superintends, the affairs of his people, or party. (Ham p. 771, Msb. *) And saEaY lahumo and Ealayohimo He worked, or wrought, and earned, or gained, for them. (TA.) And Almaro'u yasoEaY ligaArayohi , a prove., meaning The man earns for his belly and his pudendum. (TA.) And saEaY AlmukaAtibu fiY Eitoqi raqabatihi , (S,) or fiY faki raqabatihi , i. e. [ The slave who had made a contract with his master to pay him a certain sum for his emancipation ] laboured to earn the means of releasing himself: (Msb:) the inf. n. of the verb thus used is sEaAyapN : (S, Msb:) and this term is employed when a slave emancipated in part, and in part retained in slavery, labours and earns for the completion of his release. (IAth, TA.) The saying, in the Kur [liii. 40], layosa liloA_inosaAni A_il~aA maA saEaY means [ There is nothing imputable to the man ] but what he hath wrought, or done. (Msb.) And falam~aA balaga maEahu A^ols~aEoYa , in the same [xxxvii. 100], means And when he attained to working with him: or and when he was able to assist him in his working. (TA.) ― -b5- Also He superintended, managed, or conducted, in his own person, the collection of the poor-rates; (K, TA;) he went to exact them, and received them; (TA;) and the inf. n. in this case also is siEaAyapN : (K, TA:) or saEaY EalaY AlS~adaqapi , (S, Msb,) aor. yasoEaY , inf. n. saEoYN , (Msb,) he officiated in the exacting, or receiving, or collecting, of the poor-rate. (S, * Msb.) [And saEaY is trans. without a prep. as meaning He exacted the poor-rate:] a poet says, (namely, 'Amr Ibn-'Addà, TA,) saEaY EiqaAlFA falamo yatoruko lanaA sabadFA fakayofa lawo qado saEaY EamorNw EiqaAlayoni [ He exacted the poor-rate of a year, and left not to us camels' fur, or goats' hair: then how would be the case if 'Amr had exacted the poor-rate of two years? ]. (S.) ― -b6- saEayotu fiY A^amori fulaAnK is said when one rectifies, redresses, or reforms, the affair of such a one, or mars, vitiates, or perverts it, by his saEoY [or striving, or labouring; and may be rendered I strove, or laboured, in respect of the affair of such a one, either to rectify, redress, or reform, it, or to mar, vitiate, or pervert, it ]: and waA@l~a*iyna saEawoA fiY A=yaAtinaA , in the Kur xxii. 50 [and xxxiv. 5], means And they who strive, or labour, in respect of our signs, to mar, or vitiate, or pervert, their meaning, by impugning their character; seeing that they called them enchantment, and poetry, and tales, or legends, or fictions: (Ksh in xxii. 50:) or these words of the Kur mean and they who strive, or labour, to falsify, or nullify, our signs; i. e. the Kur-án. (Jel.) ― -b7- saEaY bayonahumo means He created, or excited, disorder, or discord, between them, or among them; made, or did, mischief between them, or among them; as also saA^aA , which is app., in this case, a dial. var. of saEaY . (TA in art. sA^w .) [Hence,] saEaY bayona Aln~aAsi biAln~amaAy^imi [ He created, or excited, disorder, &c., among the people by calumnies, or slanders: or it may be well rendered he busied himself among the people with propagating calumnies, or slanders ]. (S and O in art. Akl ; &c.) ― -b8- And saEaY (tropical:) He calumniated him, or slandered him, (S, Msb, K, * TA,) A_ilaY AlwaAliY [ to the ruler, or magistrate ]; (S, Msb, K;) inf. n. saEiAyapN . (TA.) ― -b9- saEato , said of a female slave, (K, TA,) aor. tasoEaY , inf. n. saEoYN , (TA,) She committed fornication, or prostituted herself. (K, TA.) [See also 3.] -A2- saAEaAniY fulaAnN fasaEayotuhu : see 3.

(S, K, TA.) One says, huwa yasoEaY EalaY qawomihi He manages, conducts, orders, regulates, or superintends, the affairs of his people, or party. (Ham p. 771, Msb. *) And saEaY lahumo and Ealayohimo He worked, or wrought, and earned, or gained, for them. (TA.) And Almaro'u yasoEaY ligaArayohi , a prove., meaning The man earns for his belly and his pudendum. (TA.) And saEaY AlmukaAtibu fiY Eitoqi raqabatihi , (S,) or fiY faki raqabatihi , i. e. [ The slave who had made a contract with his master to pay him a certain sum for his emancipation ] laboured to earn the means of releasing himself: (Msb:) the inf. n. of the verb thus used is sEaAyapN : (S, Msb:) and this term is employed when a slave emancipated in part, and in part retained in slavery, labours and earns for the completion of his release. (IAth, TA.) The saying, in the Kur [liii. 40], layosa liloA_inosaAni A_il~aA maA saEaY means [ There is nothing imputable to the man ] but what he hath wrought, or done. (Msb.) And falam~aA balaga maEahu A^ols~aEoYa , in the same [xxxvii. 100], means And when he attained to working with him: or and when he was able to assist him in his working. (S.) ― -b6- saEayotu fiY A^amori fulaAnK is said when one rectifies, redresses, or reforms, the affair of such a one, or mars, vitiates, or perverts it, by his saEoY [or striving, or labouring; and may be rendered I strove, or laboured, in respect of the affair of such a one, either to rectify, redress, or reform, it, or to mar, vitiate, or pervert, it ]: and waA@l~a*iyna saEawoA fiY A=yaAtinaA , in the Kur xxii. 50 [and xxxiv. 5], means And they who strive, or labour, in respect of our signs, to mar, or vitiate, or pervert, their meaning, by impugning their character; seeing that they called them enchantment, and poetry, and tales, or legends, or fictions: (Ksh in xxii. 50:) or these words of the Kur mean and they who strive, or labour, to falsify, or nullify, our signs; i. e. the Kur-án. (Jel.) ― -b7- saEaY bayonahumo means He created, or excited, disorder, or discord, between them, or among them; made, or did, mischief between them, or among them; as also saA^aA , which is app., in this case, a dial. var. of saEaY . (TA in art. sA^w .) [Hence,] saEaY bayona Aln~aAsi biAln~amaAy^imi [ He created, or excited, disorder, &c., among the people by calumnies, or slanders: or it may be well rendered he busied himself among the people with propagating calumnies, or slanders ]. (S and O in art. Akl ; &c.) ― -b8- And saEaY (tropical:) He calumniated him, or slandered him, (S, Msb, K, * TA,) A_ilaY AlwaAliY [ to the ruler, or magistrate ]; (S, Msb, K;) inf. n. saEiAyapN . (TA.) ― -b9- saEato , said of a female slave, (K, TA,) aor. tasoEaY , inf. n. saEoYN , (TA,) She committed fornication, or prostituted herself. (K, TA.) [See also 3.] -A2- saAEaAniY fulaAnN fasaEayotuhu : see 3.

definition: ↓ saAEaAniY fulaAnN fasaEayotuhu , aor.
sourceDefinition: ↓ saAEaAniY fulaAnN fasaEayotuhu , aor. of the latter A^asoEiyhi , means [ Such a one strove with me in walking, or going along, quickly, &c.,] and I overcame him [ therein ]. (S, TA.) The inf. n. musaAEaApN signifies The walking, or going, quickly [&c., or rather the striving, or contending, in doing so, ] with any one. (KL.) Hence the trad. of 'Alee, in discommendation of worldly enjoyments, mano saAEaAhaA faAtatohu , meaning mano saAbaqahaA [i. e. He who runs a race with them, they evade him, or escape his pursuit ]. (TA.) ― -b2- musaAEaApN also signifies One's committing fornication with a female slave: and a female slave's committing fornication with any one: (KL:) you say, of a man, zanaY and Eahara , and this is with a free woman and with a female slave; but one says in the case of a female slave, peculiarly, qado saAEaAhaA [ He has committed fornication with her ]; musaAEaApN not being with any but with female slaves: thus in a trad., A_imaA='N saAEayona fiY AljaAhiliy~api [ Female slaves that committed fornication in the Time of Ignorance ]: and A^utiYa Eumara birajulK saAEaY A^amapF [ There was brought to 'Omar a man who committed fornication with a female slave ]: (S, TA: *) [and hence, waladu AlmusaAEaApi (occurring in the L, in art. bhv , as mentioned by IAar on the authority of Abu-l-Mekárim), meaning The offspring of fornication, begotten on a slave: ] or sAEAhA , (K, TA,) inf. n. as above, (TA,) signifies [or rather signifies also] He sought her for the purpose of fornication: (K, [in which the context seems to indicate that it relates to a female slave,] and TA:) accord. to Th, relating to the free woman and the female slave: it is also said that musaAEaApu AlmaroA^api signifies The imposing upon the woman, by her owner, an impost which she is to pay by means of [ the gain of ] prostitution: and it is said in a trad. that there shall be no musaAEaAp in El-Islám. (TA.) -A2- [It is said in the TA in art. rbE , that musaAEaApN from Als~aAEapu is like mua$aAharapN from Al$~ahoru and muraAbaEapN from Alr~abiyEu &c.; but I think that msAEAp in this instance is a mistranscription for musaAwaEapN : see art. swE .]

sourceDefinition: act. part. n. of 1. (Msb.) A messenger; a courier, or messenger that journeys with haste; or a messenger on a beast of the post; syn. bariydN . (TA.) [See an ex. at the end of the first paragraph of art. rym .] ― -b2- Any manager, conductor, orderer, regulator, or superintendent, (S, K,) of a thing, over a people, or party, (S,) or of an affair, and of a people, or party, whatever it be: (K:) pl. suEaApN . (S, * TA.) Mostly, (S, TA,) or when used without restriction, (Msb,) applied to The intendant, or collector, of the poor-rate: pl. as above. (S, Msb, TA. [See rakiybN .]) And particularly The headman of the Jews and Christians, (K, TA,) from whose opinion, or judgment, they do not deviate, and without whom they do not decide an affair. (TA.) And [the pl.] suEaApN signifies Persons who take upon themselves responsibility for the prevention of the shedding of blood, and for the stilling of sedition, or discord, or the like; because they labour in the reforming, or amending, of the circumstances subsisting between parties. (TA.) ― -b3- Also A calumniator, or slanderer; [and especially] to the ruler, or magistrate: whence the saying, in a trad., Als~aAEiY ligayori ri$odapK The calumniator is not trueborn: and in another trad., Als~aAEiY muvalitN [ The calumniator of another to the ruler is a trebler of evil]; meaning that he destroys, by his calumny, himself, and the calumniated, and the ruler. (TA.)
