definition: , (S, O, Msb, K,) said by some to be of the class of qaruba , being made by them to accord in from with its contr.
sourceDefinition: , (S, O, Msb, K,) said by some to be of the class of qaruba , being made by them to accord in from with its contr., which is qaSura , and by others said to be of the class of qaAla , (Msb,) first pers. Tulotu , [said to be] originally Tawulotu , because one says TawiylN , [not TaAy^ilN , when using it as an intrans. v.,] (S, O,) aor. yaTuwlu , (TA,) inf. n. TuwlN , (S, * O, * Msb, K,) It (a thing, S, O, Msb) was, or became, elongated, or extended; [i. e. it was, or became, long; and it was, or became, tall, or high; which meanings are sometimes more explicitly denoted in order to avoid ambiguity, as when one says TaAla EalaY wajohi AlA^aroDi it was, or became, elongated, or extended, upon the surface of the earth or ground; and TaAla fiY Als~amaA='i it was, or became, elongated, or extended, towards (lit. into ) the sky; ] (S, O, Msb, K;) and ↓ AstTAl signifies the same. (S, O, K.) It is also said of any time that is extended; and of anxiety that cleaves to one continually; and the like: [see TuwlN , below:] thus one says TaAla All~ayolu [ The night became long, or protracted ]: (TA:) [and thus TaAla Ealayohimu AlA^amadu , in the Kur lvii. 15, means The time became extended, or prolonged, unto them: ] and Ealayohimu AlEumuru ↓ taTaAwala , in the Kur xxviii. 45, means, in like manner, [ Life was prolonged unto them; or] their lives became long, or prolonged: (Jel:) and TAl Almajolisu The time of the assembly was, or became, extended, or prolonged: (Msb:) and TAl Alham~u [ Anxiety became protracted ]. (TA.) [One says also TaAlamaA faEala ka*aA Long time did he thus; and the like; with the restrictive mA : see Har p. 17.] -A2- When trans. [without a particle it is of the class faEala ; not faEula , because this is not trans.: (TA:) one says Tulotuhu meaning I exceeded him, or surpassed him, in AlT~uwl [i. e. tallness; or I overtopped him ]: and also in AlT~awol [i. e. beneficence, and excellence, &c.]. (S, O, K.) See 3. A poet says, A_in~a Alfarazodaqa SaxorapN EaAriyapN TaAlato falayosa tanaAluhaA AlA^awoEaAlu [ Verily El-Farezdak is a bare rock that has exceeded in height the mountain-goats so that the mountain-goats do not reach it ]: he means TaAlati AlA^awoEaAla . (TA.) And it is said in a trad., faTaAla AlEab~aAsu Eumara i. e. And El-'Abbás exceeded 'Omar in tallness of stature. (TA.) And you say, TaAlahu fiY AlHasabi [ He excelled him in the grounds of pretension to respect or honour ]. (K and TA in explanation of $arafahu : in the CK [erroneously] TAwalahu .) -A3- One says also, TAl Ealayohi , (S,) or Ealayohimo , (Msb, K,) the verb in this case being of the class of qaAla , aor. yaTuwlu , (Msb,) inf. n. TawolN ; (S, * Msb;) and ↓ tTw~l ; (S, Msb, K;) and ↓ ATAl ; (Msb;) He bestowed, or conferred, a benefit or benefits, or a favour or favours, (S, Msb, K,) upon him, (S,) or upon them. (Msb, K.) And EalayonaA bi$aYo'K ↓ tTw~l He gave to us a thing; like tanaw~ala ; but the latter is said by Aboo-Mihjen to be used only in relation to good; and the former, sometimes, in relation to good and to evil. (TA in art. nwl .)

sourceDefinition: , (S, O, Msb, K,) inf. n. taTowiylN ; (O;) and ↓ ATAlhu , (S, O, Msb, K,) and ↓ A^aTowalahu , (S, O, K,) inf. n. A_iTaAlapN ; (O;) both signify the same; (S, O, Msb, K;) He elongated it; extended it; lengthened it; or made it long, or tall or high; (S, * O, Msb;) syn. mad~ahu , (S, * O, * Msb,) and jaEalahu TawiylFA . (O, TA.) You say, Taw~alotu AlHadiydapa I elongated, or lengthened, the piece of iron. (Msb.) And A@ll~`hu baqaA='ahu ↓ ATAl God extended, or prolonged, his continuance [ in life ]; or may God extend, &c. (Msb.) And Almajolisa ↓ ATAl He extended, or prolonged, the time of the assembly. (Msb.) And Tw~al lilofarasi , (S, O,) or lild~aAb~api , (Msb, K,) He slackened [or lengthened ] (S, O, Msb, K) the tether, (S, O, K,) or rope, (Msb,) of the horse, (S, O,) or of the beast, (Msb, K,) in the place of pasture, (S, O, K,) or that it might pasture [more largely]: (Msb:) and lahaA AlT~iwala ↓ ATAl and AlT~iyala [signify the same]. (TA, from a trad.) And [hence] Tw~l lahu (inf. n. as above, S) He granted him a delay, or respite; (S, O, Msb, K;) said of God: (S:) and fiY ↓ AlmuTaAwalapu AlA^amori means Alt~aTowiylu fiyhi ; (Msb;) [i. e.] TAwlhu signifies he delayed, or deferred, with him, (S, O, K, TA,) fiY AlA^amori [ in the affair ], (S, O,) or fiY Ald~ayoni [ in the case of the debt ] and AlEidapi [ the promise ]. definition: [is originally an inf.
sourceDefinition: [is originally an inf. n.: (see TaAla Ealayohi :) and, used as a simple subst.,] signifies Beneficence; and bounty: (S, TA:) and [ a benefit, a favour, a boon, or] a gift. (Har p. 58.) ― -b2- And, (O, K, TA,) as also ↓ TaAy^ilN and ↓ TaAy^ilapN , (K, TA,) Excellence, excess, or superabundance: and power, or ability: and wealth, or competence: and ampleness of circumstances: (O, K, TA:) and superiority, or ascendancy. (O, TA.) One says, lifulaAnK EalaY fulaAnK TawolN To such a one belongs excellence, or superabundance, above such a one. (O. [And the like is said in the Mgh.]) And it is said in the Kur [iv. 29], wamano lamo yasotaTiEo minokumo TawolFA A^ano yanokiHa A@lmuHoSanaAti , meaning And such of you as is not able to obtain superabundance so that he may marry the free women, let him marry a female slave; (Mgh;) i. e. such as is not able to give the dowry of the free woman, (Mgh, O, TA,) as expl. by Zj. (Mgh, TA.) In the phrase Tawolu AlHur~api , the former word is originally the inf. n. of the verb in TaAla EalayohaA meaning “ he benefited her; ” because, when one is able to give the dowry of the free woman, and pays it, he benefits her: or, as some of the lawyers says, this phrase means The superabundance of the means of sustenance that suffices for the marrying of the free woman, agreeably with a saying of Az: or, as some say, Twl means wealth, or competence; and the phrase is originally TawolN A_ilaY AlHur~api , i. e. ampleness of wealth such as supplies the means of attaining to the free woman: or originally TawolN EalaY AlHur~api , meaning power, or ability, for the marrying of the free woman: (Msb:) Esh-Shaabee is related to have used the phrase AlT~awolu A_ilaY AlHur~api ; and in like manner are I'Ab and Jábir and Sa'eed Ibn-Jubeyr. (Mgh.) *iY AlT~awoli in the Kur xl. 3 means The Possessor of all-sufficiency, and of superabundance, or of bounty: (O:) or the Possessor of power: or of bounty, and beneficence. (TA.) And A^uwluw AlT~awoli minohumo in the Kur ix. 87 means Those, of them, who are possessors of superabundance, and of opulence. (Bd.) ― -b3- See also TiwalN , latter half, in two places.

definition: Elongated, or extended;
sourceDefinition: Elongated, or extended; [i. e. long; and tall, or high; ] (S, O, Msb, K;) as also ↓ TuwaAlN ; (S, O, K; but see Tuw~aAlN ;) and ↓ musotaTiylN : and ↓ A^aTowalu is used in the sense of TawiylapN , [being syn. sometimes with TawiylN and TawiylapN ,] in a verse of El-Farezdak cited voce EaziyzN : (O, TA:) [it seems, from a comparison of explanations of suroHuwbN and salohabN &c. in the S and K, that TawiylN applied to a horse or the like generally signifies long-bodied: ] TawiylN is the only epithet, known to IJ, of the measure faEiylN having the f and l sound and having w for its E , except SawiybN and qawiymN ; for EawiySN is [held by him to be only] used as a subst.: (M in art. Swb :) the pl. (of TawiylN and TuwaAlN , TA) is TiwaAlN (S, O, Msb, K) and TiyaAlN ; (S, O, K;) the latter anomalous, and said by IJ to occur only in one verse: (TA:) the fem. is TawiylapN (Msb, K) and TuwaAlapN ; (K, * TA;) and the pl. of the former of these is TawiylaAtN . (Msb.) ― -b2- They said, A_in~a All~ayola TawiylN walaA yaTulo A_il~aA bixayorK [ Verily the night is long, and may it not be long save with good fortune ]: mentioned by Lh, as expressing a prayer. (TA.) And qaSiyrapN mino TawiylapK [ A short thing from a tall thing]; meaning a date from a palm-tree: a prov., alluding to the abridging of speech, or language. (IAar, Meyd, K.) See also 4. ― -b3- AlT~awiylu is also the name of A certain kind of metre of verse; (S, O, K;) [namely, the first; ] consisting of faEuwluno mafaAEiyluno eight [a mistake for four ] times: (O, TA:) so called because it is the longest of all the metres of verse; originally comprising forty-eight letters: (TA:) a postclassical term. (S, O, K.)

sourceDefinition: Exceeding, or surpassing, in AlT~uwl [i. e. length, and tallness or height ]: (S, O, Msb, * K:) and also in AlT~awol [i. e. beneficence, and excellence, &c.]: (S, O, K:) fem. TuwlaY : (S, O, Msb, K:) pl. of the former, applied to men, A^aTaAwilu ; (S, O;) and of the latter TuwalN . (S, O, Msb, K. *) Als~aboEu AlT~uwalu , i. e. The seven longer chapters of the Kur-án, (O, TA,) are the chapter of Albaqarap and the next five chapters of which the last is AlA^aEoraAf , and one other, which is the chapter of yuwnus , or AlA^anofaAl and baraA='ap together, these being regarded as one chapter, (O, K, TA,) or, as some say, Alkahof , and some say Alt~awobap [which is the same as baraA='ap ]; and some say [ the chapters vulgarly called ] the HawaAmiym [which are the fortieth and six following chapters ]: but the first of all these sayings is the right. (TA.) And TuwlaY AlT~uwlayayoni [ The longer of the two longer chapters of the Kur-án], occurring in a trad. of Umm-Selemeh, was expl. by her as meaning the chapter of AlA^aEoraAf : (O:) AlT~uwlayaAni meaning AlA^anoEaAm and AlA^aEoraAf . (TA.) A^asoraEukun~a luHuwqFA biY A^aTowalukun~a yadFA , or, as some relate it laHaAqFA , as saying of the Prophet to his wives, means [ The quickest of you in attaining to me is, or will be, ] the most extensive of you in giving. And TuwlaY AlT~uwlayayoni [ The longer of the two longer chapters of the Kur-án], occurring in a trad. of Umm-Selemeh, was expl. by her as meaning the chapter of AlA^aEoraAf : (O:) AlT~uwlayaAni meaning AlA^anoEaAm and AlA^aEoraAf . definition: A wall which is placed between the two [ main lateral ] walls of the winter-chamber, not reaching to the further end thereof, (S, O, K, TA,) then the beam is laid from the inner extremity of that...
sourceDefinition: A wall which is placed between the two [ main lateral ] walls of the winter-chamber, not reaching to the further end thereof, (S, O, K, TA,) then the beam is laid from the inner extremity of that wall to the further end of the chamber, (TA,) and it is roofed over, (S, O, K, TA,) i. e. the whole chamber is roofed over: what is between the two walls [ above mentioned ] is [ called ] a sahowap [q. v.], and what is beneath the beam [app. with what is screened by the middle wall from the portion ( of the chamber ) in which is the entrance ] is the muixodaE : (TA:) this is done for the sake of more warmth, and only in cold countries: (S, O, K, TA:) and it is called in Pers. byjh [correctly PyJh ]: (S, TA:) and EaroSN is [said to be] a dial. var. thereof. (TA.)

definition: (Az, S, Msb, K) and ↓ EurusN (Az, S, K) substs.
sourceDefinition: (Az, S, Msb, K) and ↓ EurusN (Az, S, K) substs. from A^aEorasa as signifying “ he had his wife conducted to him on the occasion of his marriage, ” and “ he went in to her: ” (Az, TA:) The ceremony of conducting a bride to her husband: (Msb:) or the ministration, or performance, of a marriage, and of the ceremony of conducting the bride to her husband: (TA:) or [simply] marriage: or coitus: syn. nikaAHN : (K, TA:) because this is the real thing intended by AlA_iEoraAs : (TA:) in the first of these senses, it is masc. and fem.; or, accord. to some, fem. only: as masc., its pl. is A^aEoraAsN ; and as fem., its pl. is EurusaAtN . (Msb.) Hence [the trad.], A_i*aA duEiYa A^aHadukumo A_ilaY waliymapi EurosK faloyujibo When any one of you is invited to a marriage-feast, or a feast given on the occasion of the conducting of a bride to her husband, let him consent. (Mgh.) ― -b2- And hence, (Az, TA,) A marriage-feast: (A 'Obeyd, Az, S, O, K:) or a feast made on the occasion of conducting a bride to her husband: (Msb:) in this sense it is masc.: (Msb:) or mase, and fem.: (S, O:) or fem., and sometimes mase. (Az, TA.) A rájiz says, A_in~aA wajadonaA Eurusa AlHan~aATi lay^iymapF ma*omuwmapa AlHuw~aATi [ Verily we found the marriage-feast of the wheatseller to be mean, discommended for the managers: see also HuwaATapN ]. (Az, S, O, TA.) Pl. as above, i. e., A^aEoraAsN and EurusaAtN . (S, O, K.) [See an ex. voce xurosN .] ― -b3- [And hence,] A state of rejoicing. (IB, voce maA^otamN , q. v.) ― -b4- The dim. is [ EurayosN ,] without p ; which is extr., [accord. to those who hold it to be fem. only,] for [accord, to them] it should have p , being a fem. n. of three letters. (TA.)

definition: A man's wife: (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K:) and a woman's husband: (O, Msb, K:) pl.
sourceDefinition: A man's wife: (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K:) and a woman's husband: (O, Msb, K:) pl. (in both senses, TA) A^aEoraAsN : (S, O, Msb, K, TA:) the dual, EirosaAni , is sometimes applied to the male and female, (S, O,) or husband and wife: (TA:) and to a male and female ostrich: (IB:) and the sing., to the mate of the lion: (S, A, O, K:) and the pl. is applied, metaphorically, by Málik Ibn-Khuweylid El-Hudhalee, to lions. (TA.) -A2- Aibonu EirosK [ The weasel; and a weasel; ] a certain small animal, (Lth, S, O, Msb, K,) well known, (TA,) resembling the rat ( AlfaA^orap ), (Msb,) smaller than the cat, (Lth, O, TA,) having the lower lip cleft ( A^a$otaru ), and very short ears, as though they were amputated, (Lth, O, K,) and having a canine tooth; (TA;) called in Persian raAsuwo : (S, Mgh:) the name is determinate and indeterminate: (TA:) pl. banaAtu EirosK , (S, Msb, K,) applied to the males and the females; (O, K;) like as you say Aibonu A=waY and Aibonu maxaADK and Aibonu labuwnK and Aibonu maA='K , and in the pl. banaAtu A=waY and banaAtu maxaADK and banaAtu labuwnK and banaAtu maA='K ; or, accord. to Akh, you say banaAtu EirosK and banuw EirosK , like banaAtu naEo$K and banuw naEo$K . (S, O.)

definition: A bridegroom: and a bride: i.
sourceDefinition: A bridegroom: and a bride: i. e., a man, and a woman, during the period of their A_iEoraAs or A^aEoraAs [thus differently written in different MSS.]; (S, A, O, Msb, K;) or when the one goes in to the other: (IAth:) you say rajulN EaruwsN [ a bridegroom, vulgarly, in the present day, ↓ Eariys ,] and AimoraA^apN EaruwsN [ a bride, vulgarly, in the present day, ↓ Earuwsap ]: (S:) and EuruwsN is a dial. var. of the same: (IAar, TA:) pl. mase. EurusN (S, O, Msb, K) and A^aEoraAsN ; (TA;) and pl. fem. EaraAy^isu . (S, O, Msb, K.) [See Earisa , in two places.] It is said in a prov., kaAda AlEaruwsu yakuwnu A^amiyrFA [ The bridegroom was near to being a prince ]. (S: in the O, malikFA .) The dim. is Euray~isN , without the addition of p to distinguish the fem., because of the fourth letter. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] A^aboyaAtN EaraAy^isu (tropical:) Verses of which the words are marked with diacritical points: for, as Esh-Shereeshee says, the Arabs used to adorn the bride by speckling her cheeks with saffron: opposed to A^aboyaAtN EawaATilu . (Har p. 610.) ― -b3- [Hence also,] EaraAy^isu AlA_ibili (assumed tropical:) The high-bred of camels. (A.)

definition: A party of men (S, Msb, K) such as is termed EuSobapN [i.
sourceDefinition: A party of men (S, Msb, K) such as is termed EuSobapN [i. e., as expl. in the O in art. ESb , who league together to defend one another ], (K, TA,) above, or exceeding, [ such as compose ] a Haloqap : (TA:) or, accord. to Er-Rághib, a company of men who assert their relationship, one to another, either by birth or by the leaguing together for mutual aid: (TA:) [for] the p is a substitute for the final radical letter which is w : (Msb:) or, as some say, it is from EazaY signifying “ he was, or became, patient; ” as though they were a company who took patience by one another's example: (TA:) [for, accord. to J,] the p is a substitute for Y : (S:) the pl. is Eizuwna (S, Msb, K) and Euzuwna and EizFY , but they did not say EizaAtN : (S:) hence Eiziyna in the Kur lxx. 37, (S, TA,) [expl. as] meaning companies in a state of dispersion: (TA:) or separate, or sundry, parties: pl. of EizapN , which is [said to be] originally EizowapN , from [the inf. n.] AlEazowu : as though each party asserted their relationship [as sons] to other than those to whom the other party asserted their relationship: (Ksh, Bd:) Eizuwna is expl. by Et-Tarasoosee as meaning companies coming in a state of dispersion. (Msb.) One says, fiY Ald~aAri Eizuwna , meaning [ In the house, or abode, are ] several sorts of men. (As, S.)

definition: Large weaned camels: (O, K:) small ones are called laTiymapN .
sourceDefinition: Large weaned camels: (O, K:) small ones are called laTiymapN . (TA.) ― -b2- And, (O, K,) accord. to El-Mufaddal, (TA,) Camels on which kings ride; [and particularly] certain camels which were decked, or adorned, for En-Noamán (S, O, K, TA) Ibn-El-Mundhir; or, accord. to AO, camels on which kings ride, which bear [ fine housings or the like, of the kind of stuff called ] diq~ [q. v. voce daqiyqN ] of great price: (TA:) and, (O, K, TA,) by El-Mázinee, (TA,) it is said to signify (O, TA) camels that carry gold; (O, K, TA;) but IAar rejected this assertion: (O:) it is said (O, TA) by Nasr, on the authority of As, (TA,) to be a [fem.] rel. n. from the name of a certain market in which is Easojad , i. e. gold: (O, TA:) IAar relates, on the authority of El-Mufaddal, that it is a rel. n. from the name of a certain stallion of generous race, called ↓ EasojadN ; and he is said to have been called AlEasojadiY~u also: (TA:) in the T, (TA,) or by AO, (O,) it is said that AlEasojadiY~u , (O, TA,) or AlEasojadiy~apu , (O,) was a horse or mare ( faras ) of the offspring of Ed-Deenáree (O, TA) Abu-l-Humeys Ibn-Zád-er-Rá- kib: (TA:) in the K, AlEasojadiy~apu is said to have been [the name of] a mare ( faras ) of the offspring of Ed-Deenáree. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. and , (S, O, K,) inf. n. EasolN , (TA,) He made, or prepared, the food with Easal [i. e. honey ]: (S, O:) or, as also ↓ Es~lhu , (K, TA,) inf. n. taEosiylN , (TA,) he mixed the food with honey, (K, TA,) and made it pleasant and sweet. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] Easalahu (tropical:) He made him an object of eulogy. (IAar, K, TA.) And (tropical:) He (i. e. God) made him an object of love to men. (K, TA.) Accord. to an explanation by the Prophet, of a saying of his in which it occurs, (tropical:) He (i. e. God) granted him, or permitted him, (O, TA,) i. e. disposed him, (TA,) to do a good deed, before his death, so that those around him were pleased with him, and eulogized him; the good deed being likened to honey. (O, TA.) ― -b3- And He fed him with honey. (TA.) See also 2. ― -b4- The inf. n. EasolN also signifies The extracting honey from a bee-hive. (KL.) ― -b5- And Easala AlmaroA^apa , aor. , (K, TA,) inf. n. EasolN , (TA,) (tropical:) He compressed the woman: (K, TA:) the verb in this sense may be derived from a phrase mentioned voce EusayolapN , or it may be a word independently coined: ISd says, “ In my opinion it is derived. ” (TA.) ― -b6- Easala mino TaEaAmihi , inf. n. EasalN , [in form] like Halaba , inf. n. HalabN , He tasted his food. (AA, O, K.) -A2- Easala , said of a spear, aor. , inf. n. EasalaAnN (S, O, K) and EasolN [correctly EasalN ] and EusuwlN , (K,) It quivered: (S, K:) or quivered much. (K. [In the CK, EasolFA and EasolAnFA are put for EasalFA and EasalaAnFA .]) ― -b2- And Easala said of water, inf. n. EasalN and EasalaAnN , (K, TA,) both with fet-h to the s , (TA, [but the former in the CK is with the s quiescent,]) It became agitated (K, TA) and rippled, (TA,) being put in a state of commotion by the wind. (K, TA.) ― -b3- And Easala said of a wolf, (S, O, K,) or of a horse, (K,) or of a fox, (TA,) inf. n. EasalN and EasalaAnN , (S, O, K, TA, [but both in the CK with the s quiescent,]) He went the pace termed Eanaq , or xabab , [i. e., with wide steps, ] and quickly: and in like manner said of a man: (S, O:) or he was in a state of agitation in his running, and shook his head, (K, TA,) going along quickly: (TA:) or EasalaAnN signifies the shaking of the limbs in running; and is mostly used in relation to the wolf: (Er-Rághib, TA:) and, as some say, Easalu Alfarasi and EasalaAnuhu signify the horse's being vehement, or ardent, ( A^ano yaDoTarima ,) in his running, bending down his head, and having his back even: and Easala AlT~ariyqa , said of a fox, occurs in a verse of Sá'ideh Ibn-Ju-eiyeh, for Easala Eani AlT~ariyqi [app. a mistranscription for Esl fiY AlTryq ], like the phrase daxalotu Albayota [for dxlt fiY Albayoti ]. (TA. [See what next follows.]) One says also, of a guide, Easala biA@lomafaAzapi , (K, TA,) or fiY AlT~ariyqi , (Ham p. 353,) He went quickly, (K,) or went with wide steps, like the wolf, (TA,) [ in the desert, or waterless desert, or in the way ]. ka*aba Ealayoka AlEasalu (S, K) and AlEasala , (K,) occurring in a trad., means Keep thou to going along quickly; (S, K, TA;) from AlEasalaAnu signifying the going along of the wolf and the quivering of the spear: or, as some say, by AlEasalu is here meant Easalu Aln~aHoli [ the honey of bees ]. (TA. See also art. k*b .) -A3- Easila biAl$~aYo'i , (O, TA,) with kesr [to the s ], (O,) like Ealima , (TA,) or Easala bAl$~Y' , (so in two copies of the S, [in one of my copies of the S omitted,]) inf. n. EasalN , with fet-h to the s , (O,) or EusuwlN (S, TA) and EasolN , (TA,) He kept, or clave, to the thing. (S, O, TA.)

definition: [ Honey; ] the fluid that is discharged from the mouths of bees, (K, TA,) when they have eaten, of the flowers and the leaves, what fills their bellies, these substances being then converted by God,...
sourceDefinition: [ Honey; ] the fluid that is discharged from the mouths of bees, (K, TA,) when they have eaten, of the flowers and the leaves, what fills their bellies, these substances being then converted by God, within their bellies, into Easal , which they eject from their mouths: (TA: [in which, and in the K, several other explanations are added, too fanciful to deserve notice:]) the word is mase. and fem.; (S, O, Msb, K;) in most instances fem.: (S, O, Msb:) EasalapN signifies a portion, or somewhat, thereof; (S, Mgh, O, TA;) being the n. un.: (TA:) the dim. is ↓ EusayolapN , with p , because EasalN is mostly fem., or as meaning EasalapN ; (S, O, Msb;) or it is the dim. of EasalapN : (Mgh:) the pl. of EasalN is A^aEosaAlN [a pl. of pauc.] and EusulN and EusolN and EusuwlN and EusolaAnN ; (AHn, K;) and these pls. are used when one means sorts of Easal . (AHn, TA.) ― -b2- [It is also used tropically for naworN , i. e. (assumed tropical:) Flowers, or blossoms; because honey is made therefrom. (See jarasa .) ― -b3- And it is applied also to (assumed tropical:) The sweet, thick, inspissated, or melligenous, juice of fruit:] and it signifies [particularly] (assumed tropical:) the juice that flows from fresh ripe dates; (O, K, * TA;) because of its sweetness. (O.) [See also dibosN .] ― -b4- Also (assumed tropical:) The gum of the [ species of mimosa called ] EurofuT [q. v.]; (O, K;) because of its sweetness. (O.) And Easalu All~ubonaY is (assumed tropical:) The gum that flows from the species of tree called All~ubonaY , having no sweetness; (O;) a thing [or substance ], (M, TA,) or a certain odoriferous substance, (K,) that exudes from the species of tree above mentioned, (M, K, * TA,) i. e. AlmayoEapu [generally applied to storax, or styrax ], (TA in art. lbn ,) used for fumigation, and called by the vulgar HaSaY lubaAnK . (K. [See art. HSw and HSY .]) And Easalu Alr~imovi is A white thing [or substance, a species of manna, ] that comes forth from the [ shrub called ] rimov , [q. v.], resembling jumaAn [i. e. pearls, or silver beads like pearls ]. (K, * TA.) ― -b5- Also (assumed tropical:) A good, or righteous, deed, the eulogy for which is deemed sweet. (AZ, O.) See EaAsilN . -A2- And The HabaAb [app. as meaning ripples ] of running water, (IAar, O, K,) [ arising ] from the blowing of the wind. (IAar, O.) ― -b2- [In one place in the CK, AlEasalu is erroneously put for AlEasolu : see EanosalN , below.]

sourceDefinition: The broom, or implement for sweeping, of the seller of perfumes, (S, O, K, * TA, kamikonasapi in the K being a mistake for mikonasapu , TA,) with which he gathers together the perfume; (S, O, TA;) it is a hair-broom, with which he sweeps up the perfume from his paved floor: (TA:) or a feather with which [ the compound of perfumes called ] gaAliyap is detached, or displaced: (Fr, IAar, O, K:) pl. EusulN . (TA.) A poet says, fari$oniY bixayorK laA A^akuwnano wamidoHatiY kanaAHiti yawomFA SaxorapK biEasiyli [ Then amend thou my condition by means of wealth: I will assuredly not be, with my mode of praising, like a hewer, one day, of a rock with a hair-broom, or a feather, of a seller of perfumes ]: he means, kanaAHiti SaxorapK yawomFA , this last word intervening between the prefixed noun and its complement because the noun of time is held by them to be like what is redundant. (S, O, TA. [One of my copies of the S has A^akuwnFA ; the O, AakuwnaA : and each of my copies of the S has SaxorapF ; and one of them, yawomK .]) ― -b2- And The pizzle of an elephant, (S, O, K,) and of a camel: pl. as above. (K.) ― -b3- See also Eisolu maAlK . ― -b4- And see EasilN .

EaATaY AlS~abiY~u A^aholahu means The boy wrought for his family, and gave them, or handed to them, what they desired. (ISd, Z, K, TA.)

And AlmuEaATaApu signifies A man's meeting, face to face, a man having with him a sword, and saying, “ Bring near thy sword, ” and he gives it, and thereupon each acts with the other awhile in a manner resembling the slaying with the edge of the sword ( yagur~uhu [see gar~a fulaAnN fulaAnFA ]); they being in a marketplace or a mosque: the doing of which is forbidden. (TA.)

EaATayotu AlA^aroTaAla means [ I joined in mutually, or reciprocally, giving, or presenting, the pints of wine; i. e.] A^aEoTayotu Aln~adaAmaY waA^aEoTawoniY A^aroTaAla Alxamori [ I gave, or presented to, the cup-companions, and they gave, or presented to, me, the pints of wine ]. (Har p. 650.)

definition: , (K, MF, TA,) and ↓ muEaATaApN (S, Msb, K) and EiTaA='N , (K,) The act of giving, presenting, or offering;
sourceDefinition: , (K, MF, TA,) and ↓ muEaATaApN (S, Msb, K) and EiTaA='N , (K,) The act of giving, presenting, or offering; or giving with the hand in the way of presenting or offering; syn. munaAwalapN (S, Msb, K, MF, TA) EalaY jihapi Alt~aqoriybi ; and A_iEoTaA='N has been expl. as syn. with A_iytA='N ; but several authors make a distinction between these two words, saying that the latter is sometimes obligatory and sometimes by way of favour, whereas the former is never but by way of sheer favour; as El-Fakhr Er-Rázee says; though most of the leading lexicologists know not this distinction. (MF, TA.) One says, A^aEoTaAhu Al$~aYo'a ; and A_iy~aAhu ↓ EaATaAhu , inf. n. muEaATaApN and EiTaA='N ; He gave him, &c., the thing. (TA.) And AETAhu maAlFA [ He gave him, &c., property ]. (S.) And A^aEoTayotuhu dirohamFA I gave him, &c., a dirhem. (Msb.) And as the signification of this verb does not depend upon the condition of taking, or receiving, but only upon giving, or delivering, one may say, A^aEoTayotuhu famaA A^axa*a [ I gave, or delivered, &c., to him, and he did not take, or receive ]. (Msb.) [See also a verse cited in the first paragraph of art. rA^m , in which this verb has a single objective complement with bi redundantly prefixed to it.] ― -b2- AETY , (S,) inf. n. as above, (K,) signifies also (tropical:) He was, or became, tractable, manageable, or submissive; (S, K, TA;) said of a camel: (S:) and AETY biyadihi [lit. he gave his hand, said of a man,] signifies the same: accord. to Er-Rághib, AETY , said of a camel, primarily signifies he gave his head, and did not resist. (TA.) [Hence,] one says to a tractable camel, when his haltering becomes loosed (lit. opened) from his muzzle, A^aEoTi [meaning Give thy head ]; whereupon he bends his head towards his rider, and he renews his haltering. (TA.) ― -b3- maA A^aEoTaAhu lilomaAli [ How large a giver is he of property! ] is like the phrase maA A^awolaAhu lilomaEoruwfi , and maA A^akoramahu liY ; anomalous, because the verb of wonder is not formed from the measure A^afoEala , and only what has been heard, of this kind, from the Arabs, is allowable. (S, TA.)

definition: The act of taking [a thing that is given, presented, or offered, or that is as though it presented, or offered, itself], or taking with the hand;
sourceDefinition: The act of taking [a thing that is given, presented, or offered, or that is as though it presented, or offered, itself], or taking with the hand; as also ↓ EaTowN ; syn. of both tanaAwulN . (K.) One says, tEATAhu He took it, or took it with his hand; syn. tanaAwalahu : (S:) and huwa yataEaATaY ka*aA He takes, or takes with his hand, such a thing; [as, for instance, food, and beverage;] syn. yatanaAwaluhu : (TA:) and zayodN dirohamFA ↓ EaTaA Zeyd took, or took with his hand, a dirhem; syn. tanaAwalahu : (Msb:) and Al$~aYo'a ↓ EaTawotu I took the thing with the hand; syn. tanaAwalotuhu biAloyadi : (S:) or Al$~aYo'a ↓ EaTaA , and A_ilayohi [i. e. A_ilaY Al$~aYo'i ], inf. n. EaTowN , He took the thing, or took it with his hand; syn. tanaAwalahu : and biyadihi A_ilaY AlA_inaA='i ↓ EaTaA He took the vessel, or took it with his hand, ( tanaAwalahu ,) before its being put upon the ground. (TA.) ― -b2- And The taking with the hand ( tanaAwul ) what is not right, or just, or due. (K.) ― -b3- And The contending in taking. (K.) One says, taEaATawuA Al$~aYo'a They took the thing, or took it with the hand, one from another, and contended together in doing it. (TA.) ― -b4- [And The contending in giving, presenting, or offering. ] One says also, ↓ taEaATayonaA faEaTawotuhu , (S, K, TA,) aor. A^aEoTuwhu , (TA,) i. e. [ We contended in giving, and it may also mean in taking, and ] I overcame, or surpassed, him [ therein ]. (S, K, TA.) ― -b5- [And simply The giving, presenting, or offering, mutually, reciprocally, or by one to another. See an ex. voce $abarN . ― -b6- And hence, The reciting, one with another, or the vying, one with another, in reciting, verses, or poetry.] One says taEaATawuA Alr~ajaza bayonahumo (TA and TK in art. rjz ) (assumed tropical:) They recited, one with another, [or they vied, one with another, in reciting, ] verses, or poetry, of the metre termed rajaz ; as also tanaAzaEuwhu . (TK in that art.) ― -b7- And The standing upon the extremities of the toes, with raising the hands to a thing. (K.) And hence, (K, TA,) as some say, (TA,) fataEaATaY faEaqara , (K, TA,) in the Kur [liv. 29]: (TA:) for this is said to mean And he stood upon the extremities of his toes, then raised his hands, and smote her: (S, TA:) or this means and he took the sword, (Ksh, Bd, Jel,) or the she-camel, (Ksh,) and slew her: (Ksh, Bd, Jel:) or and he emboldened himself &c.: (Ksh, Bd:) [for] ― -b8- taEaATK signifies also The being bold, daring, or courageous, so as to attempt, or venture upon, a thing without consideration or hesitation: (TA:) or, as also ↓ taEaT~K , the venturing upon, or embarking in, or doing, (K, TA,) a thing, or an affair, (K,) or a bad, or foul, thing or affair: (TA:) or the former is used in relation to that which is noble, or honourable; and ↓ the latter, in relation to that which is bad, or foul. (K, TA.) And one says, fulaAnN yataEaATaY ka*aA (S, Msb) i. e. Such a one enters into such a thing: (S:) or ventures boldly, daringly, or courageously, upon such a thing, and does it. (Msb.). [And Such a one takes, or applies himself, to such a thing; as wine, or the drinking thereof; and gaming: you say, tEATY Alxamora ; and Almayosira : see Ksh and Bd and Jel in ii. 216.] And taEaATaY qawola Al$~iEori He affected to be a poet but was not. (TA in arr. $Er .) And taEaATaY AlbalaAgapa walayosa mino A^aholihaA [ He affected, or attempted, eloquence, not being of those endowed therewith ]. (TA in art. blg .)

sourceDefinition: [ Giving, &c.]. When thou desirest Zeyd [i. e. any person] to give thee a thing, thou sayest, halo A^anota muEoTiy~ahu [lit. Art thou my giver of it? ], with fet-h and teshdeed to the Y : and in like manner thou sayest to a pl. number, halo A^anotumo muEoTiy~ahu , because the n [of the word muEoTuwna ] falls out by reason of the word's becoming a prefixed noun, and the w is changed into Y and incorporated [into the pronominal Y ], and the Y is pronounced with fet-h because [originally] preceded by a quiescent letter [i. e. the w which is changed into Y ]: and to two persons thou sayest, halo A^anotumaA muEoTiyaAyahu , with fet-h to the Y : and thus you do in similar cases. (S, TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] qawosN muEoTiyapN (assumed tropical:) A pliable bow, not rigid nor resisting to him who pulls the string: or, as some say, that has been bent and not been broken. (TA.) [See also EaTowaY .]

definition: , aor. , (A, * Msb, K, *) inf. n. EakosN , (S, A, O, Msb, K,) He reversed it; made the last part of it to be first, and the first to be last; or turned it kind part before, and fore part behind. (S,...
sourceDefinition: , aor. , (A, * Msb, K, *) inf. n. EakosN , (S, A, O, Msb, K,) He reversed it; made the last part of it to be first, and the first to be last; or turned it kind part before, and fore part behind. (S, A, O, Msb, K.) [Hence,] Eakasa AlkalaAma wanaHowahu , (A, O, K,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (O,) He inverted, reversed, converted, or transposed, the language or sentence, and the like; [as, for instance, a word;] he changed its order by inversion or transposition: (A, O, K:) sometimes a word, when this is done, remains as at first; as in the instances of baAbN and xawoxN and EakawokaEN : (TA:) or he perverted its order (TA) [or its meaning: see maEokuwsN ]. [Hence the phrase biA@loEakosi Vice versâ. ] One says to him who speaks wrongly, lAa taEokiso [ Pervert not thou ]. (A.) And ↓ muEaAkasapN with respect to language and the like is like EakosN . (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence, said of a mirror and the like, It reflected it; namely, an object before it; because the object seen in it is reversed.] ― -b3- From the first of the significations mentioned above is derived the expression [used by the Arabs in the “ Time of Ignorance ”], Eakosu Albaliy~api Einoda Alqabori [ The tying, with her head turned backwards, of the she-camel that is left to die at the grave in which her master is buried ]; because they used to tie her with her head turned backwards towards the part next her breast and belly, or, as some say, towards her hinder part next the back, and to leave her in that state until she died. (S, O.) And [hence, app.,] AlEakosu also signifies The confining a beast ( daAb~ap ) without fodder. (TA.) You say also, Eakasa raA^osa AlbaEiyri , aor. , He turned the head of the camel [app. meaning backwards ]. (TA.) And Eakasa AlbaEiyra , (IKtt, O, L, Msb,) aor. , (Msb, [in the L, , which is evidently a mistranscription,]) inf. n. EakosN (S, IKtt, O, L, K) and EikaAsN , (IKtt, L,) He tied the camel's neck to one of his fore legs while he was lying down: (IKtt, L, Msb:) or he tied the camel's fore shank to his (the camel's) arm with a rope, and then turned back the rope beneath his belly and tied it to his flank: (IDrd, O:) or he tied a cord in the fore part of the nose, or mouth, of the camel, (S, O, K,) [ attaching it ] to his fore legs, (K,) or to the pastern of [ each of ] his fore legs, (S, O,) to render him submissive, or tractable: (S, K:) or he put a halter ( xiTaAm ) upon the head of the camel, and then tied it in a knot upon his knee, to prevent his being impetuous: (El-Jaadee:) or, accord. to an Arab of the desert, he pulled the rein ( jariyr ) of the camel, and kept fast hold of his head, so that he went an easy and a quick pace: and Eakasa Ald~aAb~apa is said to signify he pulled the head of the beast towards him, to make him go backwards. (TA.) ― -b4- Eakasotu Ealayohi A^amorahu i. q. radadotuhu Ealayohi [ I reversed to him his affair, or case; I made his affair, or case, to become the contrary of what it was to him ]. (Msb.) ― -b5- Eakasotuhu Eano A^amorihi I prevented him from executing his affair. (Msb.) It is said in a trad. of Er-Rabeea Ibn-Kheythem, (TA,) AiEokisuwA A^anofusakumo Eakosa Alxayoli biA@ll~ujumi Rein in, or refrain, (TA,) or turn back, (A, TA,) yourselves [ as one reins in, &c., horses by means of the bits and bridles ]. (TA.) ― -b6- And Eakasa Al$~aYo'a He pulled the thing towards the ground, and pressed it, or squeezed it, hard, then smote the ground with it. (TA.) -A2- One says also, Eakasotu , aor. , inf. n. EakosN , [app. meaning I poured milk upon broth; for it is said to be] from EakiysN in the first of the senses assigned to it below: (O:) or AlEakosu signifies the pouring Eakiys , meaning as first expl. below, upon TaEaAm [or food ]: (K:) and All~abana ↓ AiEotakasa signifies the same as Eakasa : (TA:) [or both of these verbs are intrans.;] Eakasa and AEtks from EakiysN signify the same [app. without All~abana ]. (JM.)

(S, O, K.) ― -b5- And (tropical:) The thread of the needle. (Lth, O, TA.) ― -b6- And [hence] AlEilaATu , (K, TA,) or EilaATu Al$~amosi , (Lth, O,) (tropical:) What is, when one looks at it, as though it were thread [ proceeding from the sun, app. when its light enters through an aperture in a wall or the like into a dark, or shady, place ]. [But this is app. a conjectural explanation, suggested by a verse of Umeiyeh Ibn-Abi-s- Salt, incorrectly cited by Lth, and after him by Az, in which what are termed A^aEolaATu Aln~ujuwmi , or A^aEolaATu AlkawaAkibi , (see EuluTN ,) are described as being kaHaboli Alfaroqi , i. e. “ like the cord of flax, ” thus expl. by Az; whereas the right reading, as is stated in the O and TA, is kaxayoli Alqiroqi ; by Alqiroq being meant the game thus called, and also called Als~ud~aru ; to which is added in the TA, that the xayol thereof are the stones used therein.] -A2- Also (tropical:) Contention, altercation, dispute, or litigation; and evil, or mischief; (K, TA;) and inimical, or hostile, treatment; or evildoing that obliges one to return evil: (TA:) or the branding, or stigmatizing, with evil. definition: An adulterer or a fornicator;
sourceDefinition: An adulterer or a fornicator; (S, O, Msb;) as also ↓ EahorN [originally an inf. n.]: and ↓ EuhoyarapN occurs in a trad. in the same sense, as a dim. of EahorN : or, accord. to ISh, on the authority of Ru-beh, EaAhirN signifies one who follows evil, whether by committing adultery or fornication, or by stealing: (O, TA:) or, as in the L, whether by committing adultery or fornication, or by transgressing [ in any other manner ], or quitting the way of truth or justice, or forsaking the command of God; A^awo faAsiqFA being put in the L in the place of Aw saAriqFA : (TA:) or any one who does that which induces doubt, or suspicion or evil opinion, or doubt combined with suspicion or evil opinion: (A, TA:) pl. Euh~aArN . (Ham p. 131.) It is said in a trad., Alwaladu lilofiraA$i waliloEaAhiri AlHajaru , (S, Mgh, O, &c.,) i. e., The child is for the master of the bed, (Mgh, Msb, TA,) meaning, the husband (Msb, TA) of the child's mother, or, if she be a slave, her owner; (TA;) and for the adulterer, or fornicator, disappointment; (Msb;) meaning, he shall have no right of relationship, (A'Obeyd, S, Mgh, O, Msb,) nor any share in the child: (TA:) like the saying lahu Alt~uraAbu , (A'Obeyd, Mgh, O, Msb,) which means “ [he has, or shall have, or may he have,] disappointment, ” (Msb,) or “ nothing: ” (Mgh, O, TA:) for some of the Arabs used to establish relationship arising from adultery or fornication; therefore the law annulled this: (Msb:) some, however, explain it agreeably with the apparent [or literal] meaning, and for the adulterer, or fornicator, stoning. (Mgh.) [See also art. Hjr .] ― -b2- Also EaAhirapN (AZ, S) and EaAhirN , (K, TA,) if not a verbal epithet, [but a possessive epithet meaning properly *aAtu EihorK ,] (TA,) A woman who comes to a man by night for the purpose of fujuwr [ adultery or fornication ], or by day; as also ↓ muEaAhirapN (K) and ↓ muEaAhirN : (CK: [but this is app. a mistake:]) an adulteress or a fornicatress; as also ↓ muEaAhirapN (AZ, S, O) and ↓ EayoharapN ; (S;) which last is originally ↓ EaharapN , like vamarapN , with an augmentative Y : (Th, Mbr:) or EayoharapN signifies a woman light, or active, and volatile, (Kr, O, K,) who does not remain fixed in her place, (Kr, O,) without continence: (K, not added by Kr:) and ↓ EahirapN signifies the same as EaAhirapN , applied to a woman. (O, TA.)

definition: A red [?] bright star in, or on, the right [?] edge of the Milky Way, following, not preceding, Alv~uray~aA [ the Pleiades ];
sourceDefinition: A red [?] bright star in, or on, the right [?] edge of the Milky Way, following, not preceding, Alv~uray~aA [ the Pleiades ]; rising before AljawozaA=' [by which may be meant either Orion or Gemini ]: (TA:) when it has risen, it is known that Alv~uray~aA has risen: (O:) [it is the well-known name of the star Capella, notwithstanding its being described above as “ red, ” and as in, or on, the “ right ” of the Milky Way; for Capella, though not now red, has been observed to alter in brightness by astronomers in very recent times; and I think that the word rendered above “ right, ” which is A^ayoman , is probably a mistranscription for A^ayosar , i. e. “ left: ” the description here following plainly indicates Capella:] it is the bright star [a] upon the left shoulder of Auriga: that upon the left elbow is AlEanozu : the two on the left wrist together with AlEy~wq are called AlEinaAzu : [see EanozN :] it is also called the raqiyb [or watcher] of Alv~uray~aA , because it rises therewith at many places: and the star on the right shoulder [i. e. β ] with the two upon the ankle-joints [which may be θ and ι , for the constellation, is variously figured,] are called tawAbiEu AlEay~uwqi : (Kzw:) it is [said to be] called AlEy~wq because of its [being regarded as] impeding Ald~abaraAn from meeting Alv~uray~aA : (TA:) Eay~uwq , (Lth, Az, S, O,) is originally Eayowuwq , (S, O,) its medial radical being w ; or it may be Y . (Lth, Az, TA.) definition: Intense heat that almost takes away the breath.
sourceDefinition: Intense heat that almost takes away the breath. (S, K.) A rájiz says, (S,) namely, Mes'ood Ibn-Keyd [?] El-Fezáree, (TA,) describing camels, (S in art. fl ,) Har~aqahaA HamoDu bilaAdi fil~i wagatomu najomK gayori musotaqil~i [ The pasturage termed HmD of tracts of country not rained upon and not having fresh herbage rendered them thirsty, and the intense and almostsuffocating heat of a star not high ( above the horizon ), i. e. not having become high so as to be concealed by the rays of the sun]; i. e. [a star] not high ( gayori murotafiEK ) because of the constancy of the heat attributed to it [at the time of its auroral rising]; the heat becoming intense only at the time of the [auroral] rising of Al$~iEoraY , [meaning Sirius, the star to which allusion is here made,] which is in [correctly after] AljawozaA=' . (S. [See Al$~iEoraY .]) ― -b2- See also 8.

definition: see 1, in four places. -A2- gr~z Aln~aAqapa He abstained from milking the she-camel: (A:) and gr~z Alganama he ceased to milk the ewes or she-goats, desiring that they should become fat: (TA:) and...
sourceDefinition: see 1, in four places. -A2- gr~z Aln~aAqapa He abstained from milking the she-camel: (A:) and gr~z Alganama he ceased to milk the ewes or she-goats, desiring that they should become fat: (TA:) and gur~izati Aln~aAqapu , inf. n. tagoriyzN , the she-camel was left unmilked: or her udder was dashed with cold water in order that her milk might cease: or she was left unmilked once between two milkings: (K:) this is when her milk has withdrawn: (TA: [see also 2 in art. gzr :]) or tagoriyzN signifies the sprinkling a she-camel's udder with water, then daubing the hand with earth or dust and slapping the udder, so that the milk is driven upwards, then taking her tail and pulling it vehemently, and slapping her with it, and leaving her; whereupon she goes away for a while at random. (AHn, TA.) It is said in a trad. of 'Atà, that he was asked respecting the tgryz of camels; and answered, “ If it be for emulation, [to make them more fat than those of other men,] no; but if from a desire of putting them in a good state for sale, yes: ” and IAth says that the tgryz thereof may mean them increase, or offspring, ( nitaAj ,) and fatness; from garozu Al$~ajari [the planting of trees]; but that the more proper explanation is that before given [which appears to be one of the explanations here preceding]. (TA.)

definition: The stirrup (S, Mgh, K) of the camel's saddle, (S, Mgh,) made of skin, (S, K,) sewed;
sourceDefinition: The stirrup (S, Mgh, K) of the camel's saddle, (S, Mgh,) made of skin, (S, K,) sewed; (TA;) that of iron [or brass] or wood being called rikaAbN ; (S;) the camel's stirrup: (Msb:) IAar says that it is to the she-camel like the HizaAm to the horse: but others say, that it is to the camel like the rikaAb , to the mule. (TA.) -A2- Also sing. of guruwzN , which signifies Sprigs ingrafted upon the branches of the grape-vine. (K.)

definition: A species of panic grass ( vumaAm ), (K, TA,) small, growing upon the banks of rivers, having no leaves, consisting only of sheaths ( A^anaAbiyb ) set one into another;
sourceDefinition: A species of panic grass ( vumaAm ), (K, TA,) small, growing upon the banks of rivers, having no leaves, consisting only of sheaths ( A^anaAbiyb ) set one into another; and it is of the plants called HamoD : or, as some say, the [ kind of rush called ] A^asal : and spears are so called as being likened thereto: As says, it is a plant which I have seen in the desert, growing in plain, or soft, tracts of land: (TA:) or its growth is like that of the [ sweet rush called ] A_i*oxir ; of the worst of pasture: (K, TA:) AHn says, it is an unwholesome pasture; for when the she-camel that pastures upon it is slaughtered, the garaz is found in her stomach separate from the water, not diffused: and it does not beget the cattle strength: the n. un. is with p : it has been erroneously mentioned as being called Earaz , with the unpointed E (TA.)

definition: A locust that has stuck her tail into the ground to lay her eggs;
sourceDefinition: A locust that has stuck her tail into the ground to lay her eggs; as also gaArizapN , and ↓ mugar~izapN . (K.) ― -b2- [Hence the saying, maA TalaEa Als~imaAku qaT~u A_il~aA gaArizFA *anabahu fiY barodK [(assumed tropical:) Es-Simák has never risen aurorally unless in conjunction with cold ]; meaning Als~imaAku AlA^aEozalu , a well-known star in the sign of Libra, [a mistake for Virgo, for it is Spica Virginis, the Fourteenth Mansion of the Moon,] which rises with the dawn on the 5th of Tishreen el-Owwal, [or October O. definition: , (S, A, Msb, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, A, Msb, K,) aor. yaguD~u , (Msb, * TA,) [and yagoDuDo may be used, in the dial. of El-Hijáz, instead of its contracted form yaguD~a ,] imp. guD~a , (S, A,) in the dial. of Nejd, (S,) and AugoDuDo , in the dial. of El-Hijáz, (S,) inf. n. gaD~N (Msb, K) and giDaADN , with kesr, (A, K,) and gaDaADN and gaDaADapN , with fet-h, (K,) He lowered his eye, or eyes; (S, A, Msb, K;) as also gaD~a mino Tarofihi ; (Msb;) [the mn being redundant, accord. to some; but see what is said on this point below:] and he contracted his eye, or eyes; syn. kasarahu ; [ so as to wrinkle the lids; ] or he blinked; i. e. he contracted his eyelids, or drew them near together, and looked: [this signification is very common:] and he contracted ( kasara ) his eye, or eyes, and looked towards the ground, not opening his eye [or eyes ]: and sometimes it indicates a state of abasement. (TA.) Also gaD~a alone, inf. n. gaDaADapN , He contracted his eyelids; like A^agoDaY : he looked languishingly. (TA.) It is said in the Kur [xxiv. 30], qulo lilomuw^ominiyna yaguD~uwA mino A^aboSaArihimo , in which some of the grammarians hold mn to be redundant; but the meaning is obvious, i. e. [ Say thou to the believers ] that they shall abridge their look, or view, from what is prohibited to them: (Sgh:) or that they shall restrain somewhat of their look, or view. (TA.) ― -b2- [And hence,] (assumed tropical:) He bore with forgiveness and silence what was disagreeable, or hateful, or evil. (S, A, K.) ― -b3- gaD~a Sawotahu , (Msb,) or mino Sawotihi , (S, TA,) or both, (Msb,) in like manner signifies He lowered his voice. (S, Msb.) It is said in the Kur [xxxi. 18], waA@goDuDo mino Sawotika , (S, A,) i. e. And lower thy voice: or diminish the loudness of thy voice. (TA.) ― -b4- gaD~a mino lijaAmi farasihi He lowered the rein of his horse, in order to lessen his sharpness of temper. (A, TA. *) ― -b5- gaD~a minohu , (S, Msb, K,) aor. yaguD~u , (S, TA,) inf. n. gaD~N (Msb, TA) and gaDaADapN , (Msb,) He lowered and lessened his estimation, dignity, or rank: (S, K, TA:) or he detracted from his reputation; or attributed or imputed to him, charged him with, or accused him of, a vice, fault, or the like: (Msb:) and, inf. n. gaDaADapN , he disdained it, or scorned it; as also minohu ↓ AgtD~ . ('Alee Ibn-Hamzeh, TA.) ― -b6- Also gaD~ahu , (K,) aor. as above, inf. n. gaD~N , (TA,) He lessened it, diminished it, or made it defective or deficient; (K, TA;) and so ↓ gaDogaDahu , (K,) inf. n. gaSogaDapN . (TA.) You say gaDaDotu Als~iqaA='a I lessened, diminished, or made defective or deficient, [ the contents of ] the skin. (Msb.) And AlmaA='a ↓ gaDogaDotu I lessened, &c., the water. (S.) And ↓ fulaAnN baHorN laA yugaDogaDu Such a one is a sea, or great river, that will not be lessened, &c.: (S:) or that will not become exhausted. (Har p. 418.) [See also R. Q. 1 below, and R. Q. 2.] And [you make the former verb doubly trans., saying,] maA gaDaDotuka $ayoy^FA I have not abridged thee, deprived thee, or defrauded thee, of anything. (TA.) And laA A^aguD~uka dirohamFA I will not abridge thee, deprive thee, or defraud thee, of a dirhem. (TA.) You also say, gaD~a mina Al$~aEari He shortened the hair. (M in art. qSr .) And [in like manner] one says, gaD~a mino raA^osihi , i. q. Tam~a raA^osahu . (K voce Tam~a , q. v.) ― -b7- Also He broke it (i. e. a branch, or stick, or the like,) but did not break it thoroughly; (L, K, TA;) and so ↓ gD~Dhu . (L, TA.) ― -b8- And gaDaDotuhu also signifies I withheld, restrained, or prevented, it; whatever it were. (S.) [Hence the phrase in the Kur xxiv, 30, accord. to an explanation given above.] You say gaD~a AlEa*ola , or AlmalaAmapa , aor. as above, inf. n. gaS~N , He withheld blame. (Lth.) And you say to a rider, in asking him to stop a little where you are, guD~a saAEapF , (TA,) and AugoDuDo liY saAEapF , (A, TA,) i. e. Restrain for me thy beast, and stop, or pause, where I am, a while. (A, TA.) -A2- gaD~a , [first pers. gaDaDotu ,] aor. yagiD~u ; (Msb;) or the first pers. is gaDiDotu and gaDaDotu , (S, K,) and the aor. of each is yagaD~u ; (K;) or, accord. to the T, some say gaDiDota , aor. tagaD~u , and some say gaDaDota , aor. tagaD~u : (IB, TA;) but the latter of these requires consideration; (TA;) inf. n. guDuwDapN (IAar, S, K) and gaDaADapN ; (S, K;) or the former only, accord to Alee Ibn- Hamzeh; but the saying baDaADapN and buDuwDapN , to denote the quality of that which is termed baD~N , strengthens what J says [in the S] with respect to gaDaADapN ; (IB;) It (a thing) was, or became, fresh, juicy, sappy, moist, not flaccid. (S, Msb:) or flourishing and fresh; or luxuriant: (IAar:) or beautiful and bright: (K:) and gaD~ato , aor. tagiD~u and tagaD~u , inf. n. gaDaADapN and guDuwDapN , said of a woman, (tropical:) she was, or became, fine-skinned, or thin-skinned, so that the blood appeared [ through the skin ]. (Lh, TA.)

It is said in the Kur [xxiv. 30], qulo lilomuw^ominiyna yaguD~uwA mino A^aboSaArihimo , in which some of the grammarians hold mn to be redundant; but the meaning is obvious, i. e. [ Say thou to the believers ] that they shall abridge their look, or view, from what is prohibited to them: (Sgh:) or that they shall restrain somewhat of their look, or view. (TA.) ― -b2- [And hence,] (assumed tropical:) He bore with forgiveness and silence what was disagreeable, or hateful, or evil. (S, A, K.) ― -b3- gaD~a Sawotahu , (Msb,) or mino Sawotihi , (S, TA,) or both, (Msb,) in like manner signifies He lowered his voice. (S, Msb.) It is said in the Kur [xxxi. 18], waA@goDuDo mino Sawotika , (S, A,) i. e. And lower thy voice: or diminish the loudness of thy voice. (TA.) ― -b4- gaD~a mino lijaAmi farasihi He lowered the rein of his horse, in order to lessen his sharpness of temper. (A, TA. *) ― -b5- gaD~a minohu , (S, Msb, K,) aor. yaguD~u , (S, TA,) inf. n. gaD~N (Msb, TA) and gaDaADapN , (Msb,) He lowered and lessened his estimation, dignity, or rank: (S, K, TA:) or he detracted from his reputation; or attributed or imputed to him, charged him with, or accused him of, a vice, fault, or the like: (Msb:) and, inf. n. gaDaADapN , he disdained it, or scorned it; as also minohu ↓ AgtD~ . ('Alee Ibn-Hamzeh, TA.) ― -b6- Also gaD~ahu , (K,) aor. as above, inf. n. gaD~N , (TA,) He lessened it, diminished it, or made it defective or deficient; (K, TA;) and so ↓ gaDogaDahu , (K,) inf. n. gaSogaDapN . (TA.) You say gaDaDotu Als~iqaA='a I lessened, diminished, or made defective or deficient, [ the contents of ] the skin. (Msb.) And AlmaA='a ↓ gaDogaDotu I lessened, &c., the water. (S.) And ↓ fulaAnN baHorN laA yugaDogaDu Such a one is a sea, or great river, that will not be lessened, &c.: (S:) or that will not become exhausted. (Har p. 418.) [See also R. Q. 1 below, and R. Q. 2.] And [you make the former verb doubly trans., saying,] maA gaDaDotuka $ayoy^FA I have not abridged thee, deprived thee, or defrauded thee, of anything. (TA.) And laA A^aguD~uka dirohamFA I will not abridge thee, deprive thee, or defraud thee, of a dirhem. (TA.) You also say, gaD~a mina Al$~aEari He shortened the hair. (M in art. qSr .) And [in like manner] one says, gaD~a mino raA^osihi , i. q. Tam~a raA^osahu . (K voce Tam~a , q. v.) ― -b7- Also He broke it (i. e. a branch, or stick, or the like,) but did not break it thoroughly; (L, K, TA;) and so ↓ gD~Dhu . (L, TA.) ― -b8- And gaDaDotuhu also signifies I withheld, restrained, or prevented, it; whatever it were. (S.) [Hence the phrase in the Kur xxiv, 30, accord. to an explanation given above.] You say gaD~a AlEa*ola , or AlmalaAmapa , aor. as above, inf. n. gaS~N , He withheld blame. (Lth.) And you say to a rider, in asking him to stop a little where you are, guD~a saAEapF , (TA,) and AugoDuDo liY saAEapF , (A, TA,) i. e. Restrain for me thy beast, and stop, or pause, where I am, a while. (A, TA.) -A2- gaD~a , [first pers. gaDaDotu ,] aor. yagiD~u ; (Msb;) or the first pers. is gaDiDotu and gaDaDotu , (S, K,) and the aor. of each is yagaD~u ; (K;) or, accord. to the T, some say gaDiDota , aor. tagaD~u , and some say gaDaDota , aor. tagaD~u : (IB, TA;) but the latter of these requires consideration; (TA;) inf. n. guDuwDapN (IAar, S, K) and gaDaADapN ; (S, K;) or the former only, accord to Alee Ibn- Hamzeh; but the saying baDaADapN and buDuwDapN , to denote the quality of that which is termed baD~N , strengthens what J says [in the S] with respect to gaDaADapN ; (IB;) It (a thing) was, or became, fresh, juicy, sappy, moist, not flaccid. (S, Msb:) or flourishing and fresh; or luxuriant: (IAar:) or beautiful and bright: (K:) and gaD~ato , aor. tagiD~u and tagaD~u , inf. n. gaDaADapN and guDuwDapN , said of a woman, (tropical:) she was, or became, fine-skinned, or thin-skinned, so that the blood appeared [ through the skin ]. (Lh, TA.)

sourceDefinition: , [aor. ,] inf. n. fataxN , He, or it, had one, or another, of the qualities denoted by the following explanations of fataxN : (L:) the primary signification is softness, or suppleness: (As, S, L:) in a man, it is width, or breadth, and softness, or suppleness, of the hand and foot: (S:) or it signifies laxness, and softness, or suppleness, (L, K,) and width, or breadth, (L,) in the joints: (L, K:) or softness, or suppleness, in the joints &c.: (L:) or width, or breadth, and length, of the hand and foot: (L, K:) and in a lion, it is width, or breadth, of the claws, and softness, or suppleness, of the joints: (L:) in camels, i. q. TaraqN [i. e. weakness in the knees; &c.; as inf. n. of Tariqa , q. v., the having weakness in the knees; &c.]; (L;) or in camels it is the like of TaraqN : (K, TA: [in the CK, erroneously, Taroq :]) and in the legs, or hind legs, ( fiY Alr~ijolayoni ,) it is length of the bone, and paucity of the flesh. (T, TA.) [See also fataHa .]

definition: Having the quality termed fataxN [expl.
sourceDefinition: Having the quality termed fataxN [expl. in the first sentence of this art.]: as an epithet applied to a man, wide, or broad, in the hand and foot, with softness, or suppleness: (S:) or it signifies lax, or relaxed, and soft, or supple, and wide, or broad, in the joints: or soft, or supple, in the joints &c.: (L:) and, applied to a lion, wide, or broad, in the fore and hind feet, with softness, or suppleness: (L, K: *) fem. fatoxaA='u : and pl. futoxN . (S, L.) [See an ex. in a verse cited voce rawaHN .] ― -b2- The fem., applied to a she-camel, means Having what is termed TaraqN [expl. above: see 1]. (L.) And fatoxaA='u AlA^axolaAfi , so applied, Whose teats rise towards her belly; denoting a quality discommended; but the like in the woman and in the cloven-hoofed animal is commended. (K) ― -b3- Also (i. e. the fem.) Any female bird having lax, or relaxed, wings: afterwards used as a name for the eagle: (MF:) or it is an epithet applied to an eagle; you say EuqaAbN fatoxaA='u , (S, L, K,) meaning an eagle having soft, or supple, wings; (L, K;) because, when it descends, it contracts its wings, and this is only from softness, or suppleness. (S, L.) ― -b4- And, applied to a foot, accord. to As, Soft, or supple: and accord. to AA, having in it a crookedness, or curvature. (TA.) Frogs are futoxu AlA^arojali [app. meaning Soft, or supple, in the hind legs ]. (A, TA.) ― -b5- A^afotaxu AlT~arofi , applied to a gazelle, (A,) or to a man, (K,) means Languid in respect of the eye. (A, K.) -A2- And fatoxaA='u signifies also A thing, (K, TA,) four-sided, (TA,) resembling a miloban [app. here meaning the thing thus called upon which bricks are carried from place to place ], of wood, upon which the gatherer of [ wild ] honey sits: (K, TA:) then he is drawn, or pulled, [ up ] from above, until he reaches the place of the honey [ which is generally in a cliff ]. (TA.)

definition: Having a strong, or loud, voice, (S, M, A, L, K,) and rude, coarse, or uncivil, in speech;
sourceDefinition: Having a strong, or loud, voice, (S, M, A, L, K,) and rude, coarse, or uncivil, in speech; (L, K;) as also ↓ fudofudN and ↓ fudafidN . (Lh, M, L, K.) ― -b2- Having a vehement tread. (M, L, K.) Hence, in a trad., qado kunota tamo$iY fawoqiY fad~aAdFA i. e. [ Thou usedst to walk upon me ] treading vehemently, as said by the earth, (M, L,) to a dead man buried in it. (L.) ― -b3- Proud, (K, TA,) and exulting. (TA.) ― -b4- And Possessing camels in number from two hundred (in some copies of the K [and in a copy of the T] from hundreds, TA) to a thousand, (AO, T, Nh, L, K,) and therewithal rude, coarse, or uncivil, and proud. (AO, T.) ― -b5- Pl. fad~aAduwna . (L, K, &c.) ― -b6- The pl. occurs in a trad., in the saying, A_in~a AljafaA'a waAlqasowapa fiY Alfad~aAdiyna , (T, S, L,) meaning [ Verily rudeness, or coarseness, and hardness, are in ] the men whose voices are high, or loud, in their corn-fields and among their cattle: (El-Ahmar, As, T, S, L, K:) or (in the K “ and ”) the tenders of camels, and pastors, and tenders of oxen and of asses: (Th, T, K:) or (in the K “ and ”) the tillers of the ground; (M, A, Mgh, K, TA;) because they vociferate in their corn-fields: (A, Mgh:) or (in the K “ and ”) the people of the deserts; (M, K, TA;) the men who dwell in the fadaAfid [pl. of fadofadN , q. v.]; (MF;) because of the roughness of their voices, and their rudeness, or coarseness: (M:) or (in the K “ and ”) the possessors of many camels. (M, K, TA.) [See also art. fdn .] ― -b7- ↓ Alfad~aAdapu signifies The frog: (A, K:) so called because of its croaking. (A.) ― -b8- Also, ↓ fad~aAdapN , (IAar, Th, M, L, K,) and ↓ fudaAdapN , (IAar, L,) or ↓ fadaAdapN , (M, K,) A cowardly man. (IAar, Th, M, L, K.) ― -b9- Also, ↓ fad~aAdapN , (L,) or ↓ fudaAdapN , (M, K,) A certain bird: (M, L, K:) n. un. of fad~aAdF , (L,) or ↓ fudaAdu . (M.)

sourceDefinition: , (O, K,) aor. , (TA,) inf. n. furuwTN , (K,) He (a man, TA) preceded; went before; was, or became, before, beforehand, first, or foremost; had, or got, priority, or precedence; (O, K, TA;) as also fariTa , aor. , [inf. n. faraTN ; which is therefore used as an epithet applied to one and to more;] (O, TA;) and so ↓ AftrT , in the phrase AftrT A_ilayohi fiY h`*aA AlA^amori [ He was foremost in attaining to him in this affair ]. (TA.) [See mufotariTN .] ― -b2- faraTa Alqawoma , (S, O, Msb, K, &c.,) aor. , (S, Msb,) or , (K,) inf. n. faroTN , (S,) or furuwTN , (Msb,) or both, (O,) or the former and faraATapN , (M, K,) He preceded, or went before, the people, or company of men, (S, M, O, Msb, K,) to the water, (S, O,) or in search of water, (Msb,) or to come to water, (M, K,) for the purpose of preparing the buckets and ropes, (Msb,) or for the purpose of putting into a right state the watering-trough (M, K) and ropes (M, O) and buckets, (M, O, K,) i. e. to prepare these for them. (TA.) [See also 5.] ― -b3- An Arab of the desert said to El-Hasan, Eal~imoniY diynFA wasuwTFA laA *aAhibFA furuwTFA walaA saAqiTFA suquwTFA , meaning Teach thou me a religion of the middle sort, not passing beyond the due mean, nor falling short of it. (TA.) ― -b4- faraTa minohu It proceeded from him hastily, before reflection, or without premeditation; [ as thought it preceded his judgment; ] syn. badara , and sabaqa , and taqad~ama . (TA.) [See 3.] You say, faraTa minohu kalaAmN , aor. , Speech proceeded from him hastily, before reflection, or without premeditation; syn. sabaqa , and taqad~ama . (Msb.) And faraTa A_ilayohi min~iY qawolN A saying proceeded to him from me hastily, before reflection, or without premeditation; syn. sabaqa . (S.) And in like manner you say of an evil action. (TA.) ― -b5- faraTa Ealayohi He hasted to do him an evil action: (O, TA:) he acted hastily and unjustly towards him. (S, O, TA.) Hence, in the Kur [xx. 47], A_in~aA naxaAfu A^ano yaforuTa EalayonaA Verily we fear that he may act hastily and unjustly towards us: (S:) or that he may hastily do to us an evil action: (Ibn-'Arafeh, O:) or that he may hasten to punish us. sourceDefinition: , inf. n. taforiyTN , He, or it, made him to precede; to be, or become, before, beforehand, first, or foremost; to have, or get, priority, or precedence; (TA;) as also ↓ AfrThu . (O, TA.) ― -b2- He emboldened him, in contention, or altercation; as also ↓ AfrThu . (TA.) fr~T A_ilayohi rasuwlFA , (IDrd, O, K,) inf. n. as above, (IDrd,) He sent to him a messenger (IDrd, O, K) among his particular, or special, friends; sent him forward, or in advance, to him: (IDrd, O:) or he made him his deputy in a litigation: (O:) and rasuwlFA ↓ AfrT he sent a messenger specially and expressly respecting his needful affairs: (IAar, O, L, K: *) and A_ilayohi rasuwlahu ↓ faraTa he sent forward, or in advance, his messenger to him, and hastened him: (K, TA: [in the CK, instead of waA^aEojalahu , we find wAarosalahu :]) but [SM says,] I do not find this last form mentioned by any of the leading authorities. (TA.) ― -b3- fr~Thu also signifies He sent it before, remaining behind it: or he quitted it, and sent it before: (TA:) he left it, and quitted it: (S:) he left him; (AA;) as also ↓ AfrThu : (Ks, S:) he left him, and became behind him; as also ↓ AfrThu : (TA:) he left him, and went before him: (S, O, K:) and ↓ AfrThu [has a similar meaning,] he left him behind, and forgot him: (Fr:) and he forgot it, namely a thing, or an affair: (K:) firaATN , also, [inf. n. of ↓ fArT ,] signifies the act of leaving: (TA:) and fr~T Eanohu he left, forsook, or relinquished, him, or it; or he abstained, or desisted, from it: (TA:) and fr~T fiyhi he neglected it; and preferred backwardness ( qad~ama AlEajozi ) in it, or with respect to it; and failed, or fell short, of doing what he ought, or flagged, or was remiss, with respect to it; as also fr~Thu ; (K; [but accord. to the TA, only the former of these two phrases signifies “ he failed of doing what he ought, ” &c.;]) or simply he neglected it; (ISd, TA;) or he failed of doing what he ought, or flagged, or was remiss, with respect to it, and neglected it, (S, O, Msb,) so that it escaped him; (S, O;) as also fyh ↓ faraTa , (S, O, K, * [in the K, the words rendered “ so that it escaped him ” are omitted,]) aor. , (S, O,) inf. n. faroTN : (S, O, K:) and fr~T alone, he flagged, or was remiss; was lazy, or indolent: (TA:) its second pers. sing. is used in cautioning a man against a thing before him, or in commanding him to go forward, or to advance; and is intransitive. (Sb, TA.) Sakhr-el-Gheí says, *`lika baz~iY falano A^ufar~iTahu A^axaAfu A^ano yunojizuwA Al~a*iY waEaduwA That is my weapon, and I will not send it before, remaining behind it: [ I fear lest they perform that which they have threatened: ] or I will not quit it, nor send it before: or I will not be behind it: (TA:) or I will not neglect it. (ISd, TA.) And Sá'ideh Ibn-Ju-eiyeh says, maEahu siqaA='N laA yufar~iTu Hamolahu With him is a skin, the carrying of which he will not leave, nor quit. (S.) You say also, far~aTotuka fiY ka*aA wa ka*aA I left thee in such and such [ a state, &c.]: (AA, O:) and mina Alqawomi A^aHadFA ↓ A^aforaTotu I did not leave, of the people, or company of men, any one. (Ks, S, O.) And fr~T fiY janobi A@ll~`hi He neglected the things of God, and did them not: (TA:) or the command of God. (O, TA.) [See also art. jnb .] And it is said in a trad., layosa fiY Aln~awomi taforiyTN A_in~amaA Alt~aforiyTu A^ano laA yaSoHaY Hat~aY yadoxula waqotu AlA^uxoraY [ There is no falling short of one's duty in sleeping: the falling short of one's duty is only the not awaking until the time of the other (prayer) commences ]. (TA.) ― -b4- Also He let him alone, or left him, for a while; or granted him a delay, or respite; [and so ↓ fArThu ; for] A^aTalotu firaATahumo means I long let them alone, or left them, or granted them delay or respite. (TA.) ― -b5- You say also, fr~T A@ll~`h Eanohu maA yakorahu God put away, or removed, or averted, from him what he dislikes, or hates: (Kh, S, O, K:) but this expression is seldom used except in poetry. (S, O.) -A2- fr~Thu , (O, K,) inf. n. taforiyTN , (TA,) also signifies He praised him immoderately; (O, K, TA;) like qr~Zhu : (O, TA:) Sgh has expressed, in the TS, his fear that the former may be a mistranscription for the latter; but seems to have afterwards conceded the correctness of the former, from his mention of it in the O. (TA.)

definition: They vied, or strove, one with another, to precede, outgo, outstrip, or get before.
sourceDefinition: They vied, or strove, one with another, to precede, outgo, outstrip, or get before. (S, O. *) Bishr says, [using the verb transitively,] yunaAziEona AlA^aEin~apa muSoEabaAtK kamaA yatafaAraTu Alv~amada AlHamaAmu [ They contend with the reins, being unbroken and refractory, like as the pigeons vie, one with another, in striving to get first to the scanty remains of rainwater ]. (S.) ― -b2- [Hence,] tfArT fulaAnN Such a one preceded, or got before, and made haste. (O, K, TA.) ― -b3- And hence, (TA,) tafaAraTatohu Alhumuwmu , (O, K, TA,) and AlA^umuwru , (O, TA,) (assumed tropical:) Anxieties, and affairs, or events, came to him [ as though ] vying, one with another, to be first: (K, TA:) or befell him at an indefinite time, (O, * K, * TA,) but only at such a time. (O, TA.) You say also, ↓ faAraTatohu Alhumuwmu (assumed tropical:) Anxieties ceased not to come to him at one indefinite time after another. (TA.) ― -b4- tfArT Al$~aYo'u The time of the thing past; as also ↓ tfr~T , which occurs in a trad., relating to a time of prayer, and meaning its time passed before its being performed: (TA:) and both of these verbs are used in the sense next following in relation to a warring, or warring and plundering, expedition. (O.) The time of the thing became postponed, or delayed, so that he who desired it did not attain it. (K.) You say, tafaAraTati AlS~alaApu Eano waqotihaA The prayer became delayed after its time. (TA.)

definition: Excess; extravagance; exorbitance; an exceeding degree; an exceeding of the due bounds, or just limits. (S, O, K, * TA.) You say, A_iy~aAka waAlfaroTa fiY AlA^amori [ Avoid thou, or beware thou of,...
sourceDefinition: Excess; extravagance; exorbitance; an exceeding degree; an exceeding of the due bounds, or just limits. (S, O, K, * TA.) You say, A_iy~aAka waAlfaroTa fiY AlA^amori [ Avoid thou, or beware thou of, excess in the affair ]. (S, O.) ― -b2- Mastery, ascendency, prevalence, or predominance: (K, TA:) as, for instance, of eager desire, and of grief. (TA.) -A2- A time, whether long or short; an indefinite time; syn. HiynN . (S, O, K.) You say, laqiytuhu fiY AlfaroTi baEoda AlfaroTi I met him time after time. (S, O.) And A^anaA A=tiyhi AlfaroTa I come to him, or will come to him, at some time. (TA.) ― -b2- It also denotes one's meeting a man, (TA,) or coming to him, (K,) after some days, (K, TA,) accord. to A 'Obeyd; (TA;) not more than fifteen days, (K,) or than fifteen nights, accord. to the same, (S, O,) nor less than three. (K.) You say, A^anaA A^aloqaAhu fiY AlfaroTi [ I meet him, or will meet him, or shall meet him, after some days ]. (TA.) [But the above-mentioned restriction does not apply when it is prefixed to a noun signifying a period of time: for] you say also, A^atayotuhu faroTa yawomK A^awo yawomayoni [app. meaning I came to him after a day or two days ]. (S, O.) [It is said in the TA that, accord. to ISk, it is used in the saying A=tiyka faroTa yawomK A^awo yawomayoni , and that it is a day between two days; but this seems to me to be a mistake for between a day and two days: it is afterwards said in the TA that faroTa yawomK A^awo yawomayoni means after two days; but the complete explanation should doubtless be after a day or two days. ] Lebeed says, hali Aln~afosu A_il~aA mutoEapN musotaEaArapN tuEaAru fataA^otiY rab~ahaA faroTa A^a$ohuri [ Is the soul aught but a borrowed thing to be enjoyed, which is lent, and goes to its Lord after some months? ]. (S.) And an Arab said, maDayotu faroTa saAEapK walamo A^uwmino A^ano A^anofalita ; and being asked “ What is frT sAEp ? ” he answered, “ Like since thou begannest to speak: ” he meant [ I went away after a little while, or a little while ago, and ] by lm and what follows it, I did not feel sure of my escaping. (TA.) -A3- Also A small mountain; (K;) pl., accord. to Kr, furuTN [q. v.]: (TA:) or the head of an [ eminence such as is termed ] A^akamap . (K.) ― -b2- And the same, (K,) or ↓ faraTN , (thus as written in the O,) An erect way-mark, or thing set up for guidance to the right way: (O, K:) pl. A^aforuTN and A^aforaATN : (K:) [but] it is said in the A that badato lanaA A^aforaATu AlmafaAzapi is a tropical saying, signifying maA A@sotaqodama mino A^aEolaAmihaA [as though meaning (tropical:) The foremost of the way-marks of the desert, or waterless desert, appeared to us ]. (TA.)

(L, TA.) ― -b2- A case, or an affair, in which the due bounds, or just limits, are exceeded: (S, O, K:) or neglected; (S, * TA;) as also ↓ faraTN : (TA:) or despised and neglected. (AHeyth, O, TA.) You say, kul~u A^amori fulaAnK furuTN The whole of the case of such a person is one in which the due bounds, or just limits, are exceeded. (A, TA.) And it is said in the Kur [xviii. 27], wakaAna A^amoruhu furuTFA , meaning, And whose case is one in which the due bounds, or just limits, are exceeded: (S, O:) or in which obedience is neglected and unheeded: (TA:) or [ one of ] preference of backwardness ( taqodiymu AlEajozi ): (Zj:) or [ one of ] repentance: or, accord. to some, the meaning is that which here next follows: (O, TA:) wrongdoing; injustice; transgression: (O, K, TA:) some say also, that it means hastening, or acceleration. (TA.) -A2- furuTN (S, O) and ↓ furoTN (O) An [ eminence such as is termed ] A^akamap , resembling a mountain: (S, O:) or the second, accord. to Zbd, the base ( safoH ) of a mountain: (TA:) pl. A^aforaATN (Zbd, S, O) and A^aforuTN . (O.) [See also faroTN , last sentence but one.]

definition: Sent before, or first, or foremost.
sourceDefinition: Sent before, or first, or foremost. (TA.) Hence the saying in the Kur [xvi. 64], (TA,) waA^an~ahumo muforaTuwna And that they shall be sent before, or first, or foremost, to the fire [of Hell], and hastened thither; (Az, O, K, TA;) this being the primary signification: (Az, O, TA:) or forgotten (Mujáhid, Fr, O) in the fire [of Hell]: (Fr:) or neglected, or left: (TA:) or forgotten, and neglected or left, in the fire: and another reading is ↓ muforiTuwna , meaning [they are] exceeding the limits assigned to them: (O, K:) and another is ↓ mufar~iTuwna , meaning [ falling short of their duty ] to themselves, in respect of sins. (TA.) ― -b2- [ Filled, or] full; applied to a pool of water left by a torrent. (S, TA.)

definition: Exceeding the due bounds, or just limits;
sourceDefinition: Exceeding the due bounds, or just limits; acting extravagantly; applied to a man: excessive; applied to anything; as, for instance, tallness, and shortness. (TA.) It is said in a trad. of 'Alee, ↓ laA taraY AljaAhila A_al~aA muforiTFA A^awo mufar~iTFA Thou wilt not see the ignorant otherwise than exceeding the due bounds in what he doth or falling short of what he ought therein. (TA.) See also muforaTN .

definition: , (S, A, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, A, K,) aor. , inf. n. fa$~N , (S, TA,) He made the wind, (S, A, K,) and the butter, (TA,) to come forth from the milk-skin, or butterskin, (S, A, K, TA,) by loosing the tie round its mouth. (TA.) And fa$~a Als~iqaA='a He loosed the tie of the skin, and opened its mouth, after blowing into it, so that the wind came forth from it. (Mgh.) [Hence the prov.,] lA^afu$~an~aka fa$~a AlwaTobi (assumed tropical:) I will assuredly make thine anger to come forth from thy head, as one makes the wind to come forth from the milk-skin, or butter-skin: said to a man who is angry: (T, S:) or I will assuredly remove thy boastfulness, &c.: (TA:) or I will assuredly take away thy pride, and thy vanity, or vain glory, or conceit, &c.: (Th:) or the meaning is laA^aHoluban~aka [ I will assuredly mulet thee, &c.; lit., milk thee]. (Kr.) See also fa$aA$i . ― -b2- [Hence,] fa$~a Aln~aAqapa , (S, K,) aor. as above, (TA,) and so the inf. n., (S, TA,) He milked the she-camel quickly. (S, K.) And fa$~a AlD~aroEa He exhausted all the milk of the udder. (TA.) ― -b3- [Hence also, fa$~a Alwarama It (a medicament) caused the swelling, or tumour, to subside. ] (See also 7.) ― -b4- And fa$~a Alqufola , (IKtt, L,) or AlbaAba , (Mgh, Msb,) [aor. ,] inf. n. fa$~N , (IKtt, L,) He opened the lock, (IKtt, L,) or the lock of the door, by artifice, (Mgh, Msb,) without a key, (IKtt, L,) or without its key: (Msb:) from fa$~a Als~iqaA='a . (Mgh.) ― -b5- And accord to Lth, (O,) Alfa$~u signifies tatab~uEu Als~ariqapi Ald~uwni [app. meaning The seeking repeatedly, or in a leisurely manner, after pilfering, or petty theft ]: (O, Msb, K:) it is the inf. n. of fa$~ahu , aor. : (O, Msb:) and Lth, (O,) or Az, (Msb,) cites as an ex., naHonu waliynaAhu falaA nafu$~uhu [which seems to mean We have had charge of it, and we will not seek repeatedly, or in a leisurely manner, bit by bit, after pilfering from it ]. (O, Msb.) ― -b6- And fa$~a , aor. , inf. n. fa$~N , He compressed a woman. (IKtt, TA.) ― -b7- And He ate; as a trans. verb. (TA.) ― -b8- And fa$~a Alr~ajulu , (S, O, K,) aor. , (O,) [inf. n. fa$~N ,] The man eructed, or belched. (S, O, K. [A meaning assigned by Freytag to 4 also, as on the authority of the S, in which I find it assigned to fa$~a only.]) ― -b9- And Alfa$~u also signifies The blowing gently, or softly. (TA.) ― -b10- And The breaking wind gently, or softly. (IAar, TA.) ― -b11- And The uttering calumny; (O, K;) thus accord. to IAar, with f , (O,) bayona Aln~aAsi [ among the people ]. (TK.) ― -b12- And fa$~a Alqawomu , inf. n. fu$uw$N , The people, or party, became in good condition, or fat, after leanness: mentioned here, and also in art. q$ , in the L. (TA.) ― -b13- And fa$~a is syn. with faA$a as meaning He gloried, or boasted, and magnified himself, imagining [ in himself ] what he did not possess. (TA in art. fy$ .)

definition: , (S, K, * TA,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, K, * TA,) aor. , (TA,) inf. n. faqamN , It, or he, was, or became, full: (S, K, TA:) it is said of a vessel: (TA:) and one says [also] A^aSaAba mina AlmaA='i Hat~aY faqima [ He obtained, or took, of the water until he became full ]; mentioned by IDrd. (S, TA.) ― -b2- And A^akala Hat~aY faqima He ate until he became affected with indigestion, or oppressed by much eating. (K.) ― -b3- faqima maAluhu His property, or wealth, became much, or abundant: or it has the contr. meaning, i. e., passed away; came to an end; or became spent, exhausted, or consumed. (K, TA.) -A2- faqima , aor. , (K, TA,) inf. n. faqamN (S, K, TA) and faqomN , (K, TA,) He had the lower central incisors prominent, (S, TA,) so that they did not close against the upper, (S,) or so that the upper did not close against them when he (the man) closed his mouth: so in the L: or he had the lower jaw long and the upper short: but accord. to the K, he had the upper central incisors prominent, so that they did not close against the lower: (TA:) the epithet applied to him is ↓ A^afoqamu ; (S, K, TA;) fem. faqomaA='u . (TA [in which it is added that one says rjl fuqomN ; but rjl is app. here a mistranscription for rijaAlN ].) ― -b2- And [hence] faqima falaAnN i. q. baTira and A^a$ira (tropical:) [i. e. Such a one exulted; or exulted greatly, or excessively; and behaved insolently and unthankfully, or ungratefully: &c.]: (K, TA:) because AlbaTaru and AlA^a$aru are departure from the limit of rectitude. (TA.) ― -b3- And faqima AlA^amoru , (K, TA,) aor. , (TA,) inf. n. faqamN and faqomN and fuquwmN , (tropical:) The affair did not proceed in a right course. (K, TA.) ― -b4- And faqima and faquma are syn. with tfAqm , q. v. (K.) ― -b5- And faquma signifies also It (a thing) was, or became, wide, or ample. (TA.) -A3- faqama AlmaroA^apa : see 3. -A4- faqama Atkaloba He took hold of the fuqom [i. e. muzzle ] of the dog; (K;) as also ↓ tfq~mhu . (Z, K.)
