definition: A ship: (S, O, Msb, K, &c.
sourceDefinition: A ship: (S, O, Msb, K, &c.:) [also particularly applied to the ark of Noah; as in the Kur-án vii. 62, &c.:] the word is generally thus only; but some say ↓ fulukN also, with two dammehs; and it is held that this may be the original form; and that fulokN may be a contraction, like as EunoqN is [of gunuqN accord. to Sb]: (MF, TA:) it is masc. and fem., (S, O, K, *) and sing. and pl., (S, O, K,) and Ibn-'Abbád says that it has fuluwkN also for a pl.: (O:) [it is said that] it may be sing., and in this case masc.; and pl., and in this case fem.: (IB, Msb:) [but see what here follows:] it occurs in the Kur-án in the following (and other) places: in xxvi. 119, &c.; where it is sing. and masc.: (S, O, TA:) and in [xvi. 14 and] xxxv. 13; where it is pl. [and fem.]: (TA:) and in ii. 159; where it is fem., and may be either pl. or sing.: it seems that, when it is sing., it is regarded as meaning the marokab , and is therefore made masc.; or the safiynap , and is therefore made fem.: (S, O, TA:) or, (K,) as Sb used to say, (S, O, TA,) the fulok that is a pl. [in meaning] is a broken pl. of that, (S, O, K, TA,) i. e. of the fulok , (IB, O, K, TA,) that is a sing. [in meaning]: and it is not like Aljunubu , which is sing. and pl. [in meaning], and the like thereof (S, O, K, TA) among substs., such as AlT~ifolu &c.; (S, O, TA;) for fulokaAni has been heard from the Arabs as dual of fulokN , but not junubaAni [or the like] as dual of junubN [or the like]; and they say that what has not been dualized is not a pl. [form], but [is, or may be,] a homonym, and what has been dualized [is, or may be,] a pl. [form]: (MF, TA:) Sb then says in continuation, (TA,) for fuEolN and faEalN share in application to one thing [or meaning], as AlEurobu and AlEarabu , (S, O, K, TA,) &c.; (S, O, TA;) and as it is allowable for faEalN to have for its pl. fuEolN , as in the instance of A^asadN and A^usodN , so too fuEolN may have for its pl. fuEolN . (S, O, K, TA.) ↓ fulokiY~N is a dial. var. of fulokN ; and Abu-d-Dardà read, [in the Kur x. 23,] kunotumo fiY A@lofulokiY~i [ When ye are in the ships; where others read fY Alfuloki ; and where the context shows that the pl. meaning is intended]. (IJ, TA.) -A2- [It may also be a pl. of the word next following].

definition: The place of the revolving of the stars;
sourceDefinition: The place of the revolving of the stars; (O, K, TA;) [ the celestial sphere: but generally imagined by the Arabs to be a material concave hemisphere; so that it may be termed the vault of heaven; or the firmament: ] the astronomers say that it is [a term applied to every one, by itself, of ] seven A^aTowaAq [by which they mean surrounding spheres ], exclusive of the samaA=' [or sky, as meaning the region of the clouds ]; wherein have been set the seven stars [i. e. the Moon, Mercury, Venus, the Sun, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn ], in every Tawoq [or surrounding sphere ] a star, some being higher than others; revolving therein: (TA:) [it is also commonly imagined that above these is an eighth sphere, called by the astronomers falaku Alv~awaAbiti ( the sphere of the fixed stars ), and by others falaku AlkurosiY~i ; and above this, a ninth, called falaku AlA^aTolasi and falaku AlEaro$i , and also called AlA^aviyru (q. v.):] the pl. is A^afolaAkN [a pl. of pauc.] (S, O, Msb, K, TA) and fulukN (K, TA) and fulokN may be another pl., like as A^usodN and xu$ubN are pls. of A^asadN and xa$abN (S, O, TA. [Thus accord. to both of my copies of the S, as well as the O and TA: but it may be that A^usodN and xu$obN are mistranscriptions for A^usudN and xu$ubN ; and therefore that for fulokN (which is not mentioned as a pl. of falakN in the K) we should read fulukN .]) And falaku Als~amA='i signifies The pole of heaven; [generally the north celestial pole; ] likened to the pivot, or axis, of the mill-stone. (TA.) ― -b2- Also (i. e. Alfalaku ) The revolving of the heaven [or celestial sphere ]. (TA.) ― -b3- And falakN signifies also The circuit, and main part, of any- thing. (K.) ― -b4- And Waves of the sea in a state of commotion, (O, K, TA,) circling, (TA,) and going to and fro. (O, TA.) This, (O, TA,) or what is next mentioned, (TA,) or the place of revolving of the stars, (O,) or the pole of heaven, (TA,) is meant in a trad. where it is said of a horse smitten by the [evil] eye, that he was as though he were turning in a falak . (O, TA.) And Water put in motion by the wind, (O, K, TA,) going to and fro, in a state of commotion: (O, TA:) mentioned by Z. (TA.) ― -b5- Also A hill, or mound, of sand, having around it a wide expanse of land: (IAar, O, K, TA:) or falakN mina Alr~amoli signifies rugged, round A^ajowibap [app. a pl. of jawobap (though I do not find it mentioned as such), and meaning depressed and clear places ], of the sands, like [ tracts of ] what are termed ka*~aAn [or soft stones resembling dry pieces of clay ], hollowed out by the gazelles. (TA.) ― -b6- And Pieces of land, (S, O, K, TA,) or of sand, (S,) having a circular form, and elevated above what is around them, (S, O, K, TA,) with ruggedness and evenness; (TA;) one whereof is termed ↓ falokapN , (S, O, K, TA,) with the l quiescent; pl. filaAkN ; (K, TA;) i. e. [this is pl. of falokapN ,] like qaSoEapN and qiSaAEN : (TA:) in [the book entitled] El-Ghareeb ElMusannaf, [by Aboo-'Amr Esh-Sheybánee, we find] ↓ falakapN and falakN , [each] biAlt~aHoriyk ; [accord. to which, falakapN is a n. un., and falakN is a coll. gen. n.;] but in “ the Book ” of Sb, [agreeably with the K, we find] ↓ falokapN [as a sing.] and falakN [as a quasi-pl. n.], like HaloqapN and HalaqN . (IB, TA.) ― -b7- See also falokapN , in two places.

sourceDefinition: is the contr. of taHot ; (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K;) [primarily signifying The location that is above, or over; ] and is an adv. n. (Mgh, Msb, K) of place; (Mgh, Msb;) and a simple noun, indecl., [with dammeh for its termination, when the noun to which it should be prefixed is suppressed, and the meaning of this is intended to be understood, but not the word itself;] but when it is prefixed to another noun [which is either expressed or itself (and not merely its meaning) meant to be understood, and when the noun to which it should be prefixed is suppressed and neither this nor its meaning is meant to be understood,] it is declinable. (K. [For the words yakuwnu A@somFA waZarofFA maboniY~N , the reading of the K in the TA and CK, my MS. copy of the K (which I follow in this case) has ykwn ZrfA wAsmA mbny~A .]) One says, zayodN fawoqa Als~aToHi [ Zeyd is above, or rather upon, the house-top ]. (Mgh, Msb.) And AlEimaAmapu fawoqa Alr~aA^osi [ The turban is above, or upon, the head ]. (Mgh.) And TafaA fawoqa AlmaA='i It floated upon the water. (S &c. in art. Tfw .) Ks has mentioned the saying, A^afawoqa tanaAmu A^amo A^asofala [ Dost thou, or wilt thou, sleep in the part that is above of the house &c., or in the part that is below? i. e., in the upper part, or in the lower part? ] with fet-h, as suppressing the noun to which fwq is [meant to be understood as] prefixed. (TA.) Lth says that he who uses it as a Sifap [by which (like other old writers) he means an adv. n. of place] should use the accus. case, as when one says, Eabodu A@ll~`hi fawoqa zayodK [ 'Abd-Allah is above Zeyd ]: but if you make it simply a noun, you use the nom. case, and say, fawoquhu raA^osuhu [ His superior (meaning upper ) part is his head ]; for in this instance it is the head itself, and you make each to be governed in the nom. case by the other. (TA.) In the saying in the Kur [xvi. 28], faxar~a Ealayohimu A@ls~aqofu mino fawoqihimo [ And the roof fell on them from above them ], the utility of the phrase mn fwqhm is hardly apparent, because Elyhm sometimes serves in its stead: but IJ says that mn fwqhm may here have a useful office; for EalaY is sometimes used in relation to deeds [or events] that are difficult, and deemed onerous; [for instance,] you say, qado sironaA Ea$orFA wabaqiyato EalayonaA layolataAni [ We have journeyed ten nights and the journeys two nights have remained as though incumbent on us ]; &c.; so that if it were said fxr~ Elyhm Alsqf without the adding mn fwqhm , it might be supposed to be like the saying Ealayohimo daAruhumo qado xaribato [ Their abode had become in a state of ruin as a punishment upon them ]; but when He [referring to God] says mn fwqhm , that meaning which was supposable ceases to be so; and the meaning becomes this, that it [the roof] fell when they were beneath it. (TA.) definition: The part, of the arrow, which is the place of the bow-string;
sourceDefinition: The part, of the arrow, which is the place of the bow-string; [i. e. the notch thereof;] (S, O, Msb, K;) as also ↓ fuwqapN : (Msb, K;) the former is masc., and also, like the latter, fem. (IAmb, Msb:) and AlfuwqaAni signifies the zanamataAni [or two cusps of the fuwq , between which is put the bow string ]; (O, K;) thus these are termed by the tribe of Hudheyl; but a poet who has used the dual form is said by AO to has mead thereby a single fuwq : (O:) the pl. [of mult.] is fuwaqN and [of pauc.] A^afowaAqN ; (S, O, Msb, K;) or, accord. to ISk, these are pls. of fuwqapN ; (TA;) and qufFA also is a pl., formed by transposition; [see an ex. in a verse cited voce EuroquwbN ;] (K, TA;) one says fuqowapN and fuqFA [for fuwqapN and fuwaqN ]. (TA.) sahomN *uw fuwqK means An arrow rendered complete by its having a fuwq : ― -b2- and hence *aA fuwqK occurring in a trad. [as meaning (assumed tropical:) A complete share; for sahomN signifies “ a share ” as well as “ an arrow ”]. (A'Obeyd, O.) And A^aEolaAhumo fuwqFA , meaning (tropical:) He, or they, of them, haring the largest share of religion, is a metaphorical phrase, from the fuwq of the arrow. (TA.) ― -b3- And they say, A^aqobilo EalaY fuwqi nabolika , [or, app., fuwaqi nabolika , for nabolN is a coll. n., meaning “ arrows, ” or “ Arabian arrows, ”] meaning (assumed tropical:) Betake thyself to thy affair, and that which concerns thee. (TA.) ― -b4- And ramayonaA fuwqFA , (O, K,) or fuwqFA waAHidFA , (TA,) meaning ri$oqFA [i. e. (tropical:) We shot in one direction; or we shot one bout, in one direction ], (O, K, TA.) ― -b5- [Hence, app.,] one says, kAn fulaAnN liA^aw~ali fuwqi , meaning (tropical:) Such a one was [for the first discharge from the bow, i. e.,] the first shot and dying. (A, TA.) ― -b6- And [hence, perhaps.] fuwqN signifies also (tropical:) A mode, or manner, of speech: (A, O, K:) pl. fuwaqN . (TA) One says to a man when he enters upon a mode, or manner, of speech, xa*o fiY fuwqi A^aHosana minohu (tropical:) [ Enter upon a mode, or manner, of speech better than it ]. (A, TA.) ― -b7- And (tropical:) The first way (AA, O K, TA.) ― -b8- Hence. app., [they say, AirojaEo A_in $i}ota fiY fuwqK (tropical:) Return thou, if thou wilt, to the state of close, or loving, communion in which we were. (Ibn-'Abbád, Z, O,TA.) -b8- And the Arabs say, in imprecating, fuwqihi laA rajEa fulaAnN A_ilaY i.e.(assumed tropical:) May such a one die: so says AA; and he cites the following verse of El-'Uleykim El-Kindee, maA baAlu EirosiY $ariqato biriyqihaA vum~ata laA yarojiEo lahaA mino fuwqihaA meaning (assumed tropical:) [ What is the case of my wife that she is choked by her spittle? (O.) ― -b9- And one says (O, K) or a man when he has gone away, (O,) maA A@rotad~a EalaY fuwqihi , meaning (assumed tropical:) He went away and he did not return [ to the place whence he departed ] (O, K) ― -b10- fuwqN also signifies, (O, K.) accord. to Ibn-'Abbád, (O, TA.) (assumed tropical:) The vulva of a woman: (O, K. TA) but As says that this is with q [in the place of the f ]: (TA:) [it is, however, also said that] fuwqu Alr~aHimi signifies (tropical:) the rima of the vulva, by way of comparison [to the notch of the arrow]. (TA, in the supplement to this art.) ― -b11- [And app. (assumed tropical:) The front edge of the lobe of the ear: see 1 in art Hrm , when it is mentioned in such a manner as seems to preclude its being a mistranscription for qawf ] ― -b12- And (as Ibn-'Abbád says, O) (assumed tropical:) The place of opening ( maforaj , O. TA, in the K erroneously, maxoraj , TA, and jawobap, O, K, TA) of the mouth: or (as some say, O) the extremity of the tongue. (O, K, TA.) ― -b13- And (assumed tropical:) The uppermost part of the penis, (En-Nadr, O, K, TA,) or of the glans thereof. (TA.) -A2- And, accord. to the K, A certain bird; mean ing a certain aquatic bird: but this is correctly [ quwqN ,] with two káfs. (TA.) ― -b2- See also faAqN , last sentence but one.

definition: ― -b3- Also (tropical:) The time between two milkings;
sourceDefinition: : see 1, former half, in two places: -A2- and see 1 again, latter half: ― -b2- and 4, in two places. ― -b3- Also (tropical:) The time between two milkings; (S, O, Msb, K;) for the she-camel was milked, and then left a little while for her young one to suck her in order that she might yield her milk copiously, after which she was milked again; (S, O;) and likewise the time between two suckings; (Ksh in xxxviii. 14;) and ↓ fawaAqN signifies the same; (S, O, Msb, K:) or, (Msb, TA,) accord. to IF, (Msb,) the fwAq of the she-camel is the retuning of the milk into the udder after the milking: (Msb, TA:) or fuwaAqN signifies the time between the opening of one's hand and the grasping with it the udder (K, TA) of the camel: or when the milker grasps the udder and then lets it go, in milking: (TA:) the pl. is A^afowiqapN and A=fiqapN ; (O, K;) and Fr says that fwAq has for its pl. A^afiyqapN , originally A^afowiqapN , the kesreh of the w being transferred to the f , and the w being then changed into Y because of the kesreh before it; and A^afowiqapN has for its pl. A^afowiqaAtN . (TA.) One says, maA A^aqaAma Einodahu A_il~aA fuwaAqFA (tropical:) [ He did not remain at his abode save as long as the time between two milkings ]. (S, O, TA.) And it is said in a trad., AlEiyaAdapu qadoru fuwaAqi Aln~aAqapi (assumed tropical:) [The period of the visiting of a sick person is the space of time between the two milkings of the she-camel ]. (S.) And in a trad. of 'Alee occurs the saying, qaAla lahu AlA^asiyru A^anoZironiY fuwaAqa naAqapK i. e. (assumed tropical:) [ The captive said to him, ] Grant thou me a delay, or respite, as long as the time between two milkings [ of a she-camel ]. (TA.) maA lahaA mino ↓ fawaAqK and fuwaAqK in the Kur [xxxviii. 14], accord. to different readings, (S,) the latter the reading of the Koofees except 'Ásim, and the former that of the rest, (O,) means (assumed tropical:) [ There shall not appertain to it ] any postponement, or delay, and resting: (S:) or, accord. to AO, the latter is the meaning of the former reading; and the latter reading means, any waiting, or expecting: (TA:) or [both mean] any pausing as much as the time between two milkings, (Ksh, Bd,) or two suckings: (Ksh:) or any returning, and repeating; (I'Ab, Ksh, Bd;) from A^afaAqa “ he (a sick man) returned to a healthy, or sound, state ”; and the fwAq of the she-camel, when the supply of milk returns to her udder; (Ksh;) or because in it [i. e. the fwAq ] the milk returns to the udder; (Bd;) i. e. the blast [to which the words refer] shall be one only; it shall not be repeated. (Ksh.) The saying (Mgh, O, TA) of the Prophet, (O,) related in a trad., (O, TA,) qasama ganaAy^ima xayobara Eano fuwaAqK , (Mgh,) or qasama ↓ AlganaAy^ima yawoma badorK Eano fawaAqK (O, TA) and fuwaAqK , (TA,) means (assumed tropical:) He divided the spoils [ of Kheyber, or on the day of Bedr, ] in the space of the rest between two milkings of a she-camel: (TA:) or quickly; (Mgh, O;) En fwAq meaning SaAdirFA Eano suroEapK [i. e. qasomFA SaAdirFA Eano suroEapK with a dividing proceeding from quickness ]: (Mgh, O: *) or, as some say, the meaning is, making some of them [i. e. of those who composed his army] to be more highly distinguished (↓ A^afowaq ) than others (O, TA *) in the proportion of their spoils and of the trial undergone by them. (TA.) -A3- See also faAqN , last sentence but one.

definition: Superior, excellent, or surpassing: (Mgh, Msb: *) anything excellent, or choice, (O, K, TA,) and pure, in its kind.
sourceDefinition: Superior, excellent, or surpassing: (Mgh, Msb: *) anything excellent, or choice, (O, K, TA,) and pure, in its kind. (TA.) You say, huwa faAy^iqN fiY AlEilomi [ He is superior, excellent, or surpassing, in knowledge ], and fiY AlfinaY [ in wealth, &c.]. (Mgh.) And jaAriyapN faAy^iqapN [ A young woman excelling in beauty, or comeliness]. (Msb.) And fawaqapN [an irreg. pl. of faAy^iqN , like as xawanapN is of xaAy^inN , for by rule these pls. should be faAqapN and xaAnapN ,] signifies Elegant scholars, and orators. (IAar, O, K.) -A2- Also The place of junction of the neck with the head: (S, O, K:) therefore when this is high, the neck is long. (S, O.)

definition: -A2- Also An arrow of which the fuwq [or notch ] is broken: (S, O, Msb, K, TA:) [and] an arrow having no fuwq : (L voce A^aqa*~u :) pl.
sourceDefinition: : see fuwaAqN , last sentence but one. -A2- Also An arrow of which the fuwq [or notch ] is broken: (S, O, Msb, K, TA:) [and] an arrow having no fuwq : (L voce A^aqa*~u :) pl. fuwaqN [perhaps a mistranscription for the regular form of pl., i. e. fuwoqN ; or it may be that the w is with fet-h to distinguish it from fuwqN signifying “ a notch ” of an arrow]: but IAar explains this as signifying arrows of which the heads have fallen. (TA.) One says, rajaEa fulaAnN biA^afowaqa naASalK (assumed tropical:) Such a one returned with an arrow having a broken notch and without a head upon it; meaning, with an incomplete share of good fortune: (S, O:) or, disappointed of attaining what he desired, or sought: a proverb. (TA.) And radadotuhu biA^afowaqa naASilK (assumed tropical:) [ I turned him back, or away, with a paltry benefit; or] I made his share of good fortune to be little, or incomplete. (TA.) And maA balilotu mino fulaAnK biA^afowaqa naASilK , expl. in the first paragraph of art. bl . ― -b2- maHaAlapN fawoqaA='u [ A large sheave of a pulley ] of which every sin~ [or tooth, perhaps meaning cog, though I do not remember to have met with any description of a cogged mHAlp ,] has two cusps ( fuwqaAni ), (O, K,) like the fwqAn [ of the notch ] of the arrow. (O.) [The strangeness of this explanation induces me to think that fawoqaA='u is here a mistranscription for fawohaA='u , (see maHaAlapN fawohaA='u , in art. fwh ,) and that the explanation is partly conjectural.] ― -b3- And kamarapN fawoqaA='u A glans of a penis whereof the extremity is tapering in form, (O, K,) like that which is termed HawoqaA='u . (O.)

sourceDefinition: He cut off for him a portion, to be requited, or compensated, for it. (Sgh, K.) [And hence,] He gave him, or granted him, a qaroD [or loan, or the like ]; (S, M, A, * Mgh, * K;) and ↓ qaAraDahu signifies the same as AqrDhu . (L, TA.) You say also, AqrDhu AlmaAla , (M, Msb,) wagayorahu , (M,) [ He lent him the property, &c.; ] he gave him the property, &c., as a qaroD ; (M;) he gave him the property, [ &c., ] to demand its return. (Msb.) It is said in the Kur, [lxxiii. 20,] waA^aqoriDuwA A@ll~`ha qaroDFA HasanFA [lit. And lend ye to God a good loan; meaning (assumed tropical:) give ye to God good service for which to be requited ]: (S, TA:) it is not here said A_iqoraADFA because the simple subst. [as distinguished from the inf. n.] is what is meant. (TA.) And again, in the same, [ii. 246, and lvii. 11,] mano *aA A@l~a*iY yuqoriDu A@ll~`ha qaroDFA HasanFA , meaning, accord. to Aboo-Is-hák the Grammarian, (assumed tropical:) [ Who is he who will offer unto God ] a good action or gift, or anything for which a requital may be sought? or, as Akh says, (assumed tropical:) Who will do a good action by following and obeying the command of God? (TA.) The Arabs say, qado A^aqoraDotaniY qaroDFA HasanFA (assumed tropical:) Thou hast done to me a good deed [ which I am bound to requite ]. (TA.) And it is said in a trad., A^aqoriDN EiroDaka liyawomi faqorika (assumed tropical:) [ Lend thou thine honour for the day of thy poverty ]; meaning, when a man defames thee, do not thou requite him, but reserve his recompense undiminished for thee, as a loan for the payment of which he is responsible, that thou mayest receive it from him in the day of thy need thereof: (TA:) [but see EiroDN .] ― -b2- [And hence,] A^aqoraDaniY Al$~aYo'a He gave, or paid, to me the thing. (M.) -A2- maA Ealayohi maA yuqoriDu Eanohu AlEuyuwna fayasoturuhu (assumed tropical:) [ There is not upon him what will turn aside, or away, from him the eyes, and cover him ]. (Ibn- 'Abbád, Sgh.) -A3- See alse 1, latter half.

And lend ye to God a good loan; meaning (assumed tropical:) give ye to God good service for which to be requited ]: (S, TA:) it is not here said A_iqoraADFA because the simple subst. [as distinguished from the inf. n.] is what is meant. (TA.) sourceDefinition: is the sing. of maqaAriyDu ; (S, Msb, K;) and a pair thereof is called miqoraADaAni : (Msb, K:) the miqoraAD is [ A single blade of a pair of shears or scissors; ] a thing with which one [ shears, or clips, or] cuts; and when you speak of the two together, you do not say miqoraADN , as the vulgar say, but miqoraADaAni ; (Msb;) which last is syn. with jalamaAni [ a pair of shears ]; a word, accord. to the lexicologists having no sing.; but Sb mentions miqoraADN , thus using the sing. form: (M:) or miqoraADN and miqoraADaAni signify the same; [ a pair of shears; ] like jlamN and jalamaAni , and qalamN and qalamaAni : (Msb in art. jlm :) or miqoraADN signifies jalamN SagiyrN [ a small pair of shears; i. e. a pair of scissors ]: (JK:) 'Adee Ibn-Zeyd uses the expression $aforataA miqoraADK [ the two blades of a pair of shears or scissors ] in a poem; (IB;) and other poets use the sing., mqrAD : (TA:) and miforaASN , with f and S , signifies the same. (IB.) Hence the saying, lisaAnu fulaAni miqoraADu AlA^aEoraADi (tropical:) [ The tongue of such a one is the detractor of reputations ]. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. qiSarN (S, M, Msb, K, &c.) and qaSorN (IAar, M, K) and qaSaArapN , (Lh, M, K,) It (a thing, S, Msb, i. e. anything, M) was, or became, short; contr. of TaAla . (S, M, Msb, K.) ― -b2- [And It was, or became, too short. And qaSura Eanohu It was, or became, too short for him, or it. ― -b3- Hence, qaSurato yaduhu , and qaSura baAEuhu , (tropical:) He had little, or no, power: and he was, or became, niggardly. ] -A2- And qaSara Als~ahomu Eani Alhadafi , (S, M, Msb,) aor. , (Msb,) inf. n. quSuwrN , (M, Msb,) The arrow fell short of the butt; did not reach it; (S, Msb;) fell upon the ground without reaching the butt: (M:) and qaSara Eano manozilihi [ he fell short of his place of alighting or abode; did not reach it ]. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] qaSara Eani AlA^amori , (S, Msb, K,) [and qaSara duwnahu ,] aor. , (Msb, TA,) inf. n. quSuwrN ; (S, Msb, K;) and ↓ AqSr , (K,) inf. n. A_iqaSaArN ; (TA;) and ↓ qS~r , (K,) inf. n. taqoSiyrN ; (TA;) and ↓ tqASr ; (K;) [ He fell, or stopped, or came, short of doing the thing, or affair; he failed of doing, or accomplishing, it; ] he lacked power, or ability, to do, or accomplish, the thing, or affair; (S, Msb, K;) he could not attain to it: (S:) or the first has this signification; (ISk, S, Msb;) and [in like manner] Eanohu ↓ qS~r , (M, K,) inf. n. taqoSiyrN , (TA,) he left or relinquished it, or abstained from it, being unable to do or accomplish it: (M, K:) but Eanohu ↓ AqSr , he desisted or abstained from it, being able to do or accomplish it: (ISk, S, M, Msb:) such, at least, is generally the case, though both sometimes occur in one and the same sense, that which AqSr Enh generally bears: (TA:) and fiY AlA^amori ↓ qS~r [ he fell, or stopped, or came, short in the affair: it signifies nearly the same as AqSr Enh , i. e., he fell short of accomplishing the affair; he fell short of doing what was requisite, or due, or what he ought to have done, ( Eam~aA kaAna yanobagiY , or the like, being understood,) in, or with respect to, the affair: a meaning very common, and implied, though not expressed, in the M: and] he flagged, or was remiss, in the affair; syn. tawaAnaY : (S, TA:) or ↓ qS~r signifies he left, desisted from, neglected, or left undone, a thing, or part thereof, from inability: but ↓ AqSr , he left it, &c., or part thereof, with ability to do it. (Kull p. 128.) [And ↓ qS~r duwnahu He fell short of reaching, or attaining, it: see an ex. voce yaEoquwbN .] [Hence also,] qaSarato binaA Aln~afaqapu The money for expenses [ fell short of what we required; ] did not enable us to attain our object; (Msb;) meaning, that they were unable to pay the expenses: (Mgh:) and bihi ↓ qaS~ara A^amaluhu [ his hope fell short of what he required ]: 'Antarah says, faA@loyawoma qaS~ara Eano tiloqaAy^ika AlA^amalu [ but to-day, hope hath fallen short of extending to the meeting with thee ]. (TA.) [And hence, app.,] bika*aA nafosuka ↓ qaS~arato [ Thy mind, or wish, fell short of what was requisite with respect to such a thing ], said to him who has sought, or desired, little, and a mean share or lot. (TA.) And, bifulaAnK ↓ qaS~ara [ He fell short of what was required by such a one, or due to him; or] he acted meanly, and sparingly, with such a one, in a gift. [&c.] (JK [see muqaS~irN : and see two exs. of qaS~ara bihi voce A^azoraY in art. zrY .] ― -b3- [Also, qaSara Eani AlA^amori , (M, K,) aor. , (M,) inf. n. quSuwrN ; and ↓ AqSr ; and ↓ qS~r and ↓ tqASr ; (M, K;) He refrained, abstained, or desisted, from the thing, or affair. (M, K.) A poet says, A_i*aA gam~a xiro$aA='u Alv~umaAlapi A^anofahu minohaA lilS~ariyHi faA^aqonaEaA ↓ taqaASara [ When the froth of the water remaining in the drinking-trough covers his nose, he refrains from it, turning to the clear, and raises his head ]: or mnhA ↓ tqASr here signifies he contracts his neck from it: and it is said that Enh ↓ qS~r signifies as explained above, he left or relinquished it, &c. (M.) qaSara Ean~iY AlwajaEu , and AlgaDabu , (M, K,) aor. , inf. n. quSuwrN , (M,) The pain, and anger, ceased from me; quitted me; (M, K;) as also qaSira ; (M, TA;) which latter is erroneously written in the copies of the K, qaS~ara : (TA:) and qaSarotu A^anaA Eanohu [ I ceased from it ]. (M.) And A@lomaTaru ↓ A^aqoSara The rain left off. (TA.) -A3- qado qaSara AlEa$iY~u , aor. , inf. n. quSuwrN , [ The afternoon, or evening, has come, ] is said when you enter upon the masaA=' [i. e. afternoon, or evening]: (S:) or it means has almost drawn near to night. (TA.) [See also qaSorN , below.] ― -b2- Hence, (S,) qaSaronaA and ↓ A^aqoSaronaA We entered upon the Ea$iY~ [i. e. afternoon, or evening ]; (M, K;) the former signifies A^amosayonaA ; and the latter, daxalonaA fiY qaSori AlEa$iY~i , like as you say A^amosayonaA from AlmasaA='u : (S:) or the former, we came to be in the last part of the day; and the latter, we entered upon the last part of the day. (IKtt.) -A4- qaSarahu , (Msb, K,) aor. , (Msb,) or , (K,) inf. n. qaSorN ; (TA;) and ↓ qS~rhu , (M, Msb, TA;) inf. n. taqoSiyrN ; (TA;) and ↓ AqSrhu ; (Msb;) He made it short; (M, K, TA;) he shortened it; took from its length. (Msb.) You say qaSara Al$~aEara , (M, Msb, K,) and qaSara mina Al$~aEari , (S,) aor. , (Msb,) or ; (K;) and ↓ qS~rh , (Mgh, Msb, TA,) and minohu ↓ qS~r ; (S;) and ↓ AqSrhu ; (Msb;) He shortened the hair; (M, K, * TA;) took from its length; (Msb;) cut its ends; (Mgh;) clipped, or shore, it. (TA.) And qaSara AlS~alaApa , (M, Msb, TA,) and qaSara mina AlS~alaApi , (S, M, Msb,) aor. , inf. n. qaSorN ; (S, M, Msb, TA;) and ↓ qS~rhA , (M, Msb, TA,) and ↓ qS~r mnhA , (S, M,) inf. n. taqoSiyrN ; (S;) and ↓ AqSrhA , (Msb, TA,) and ↓ AqSr mnhA ; (S;) but AqSrhA is extr.; (TA;) He curtailed [or contracted ] the prayer; (M;) he performed a prayer of four rek'ahs ( rakaEaAt ) making it of two; (Mgh;) in a journey. (Mgh, TA.) And AlxuTobapa ↓ AqSr He made the [ form of words called ] xTbp [ delivered from the pulpit ] short, or concise: (Mgh, TA: *) the doing so being commanded. (Mgh.) qaSorN also signifies the contr. of mad~N ; (M, K;) and the verb is qaSara [ He contracted, or straitened ]. (M.) You say qaSarotu qayoda AlbaEiyri ; (Msb;) and qaSarotu lahu mino qayodihi ; (M;) aor. , inf. n. qaSorN ; (M, Msb;) I contracted the shackles of the camel; syn. Say~aqutuhu ; (Msb;) and I contracted his shackles; syn. qaArabotu . (M.) [And in like manner, AlEaTiy~apa ↓ qaS~ara , inf. n. taqoSiyrN , He made the gift scanty, or mean: or, accord. to the TK, qS~r fiY AlEaTiy~api , which properly signifies he fell short of what he ought to have done with respect to the gift: but, though each of these phrases is doubtless correct, the former expression I hold to be that which is indicated when it is said that] Alt~aqoSiyru signifies A_ixosaAsu AlEaTiy~api . (M, K.) -A5- qaSarahu , (S, M, Msb,) aor. , (S, M,) inf. n. qaSorN , (S, M, Msb, K,) He confined, restricted, limited, kept within certain bounds or limits, restrained, withheld, hindered or prevented, him, or it; syn. Habasahu . (S, M, Msb, K. *) It is said in a trad. of Mo'ádh, lahu maA qaSara fiY bayotihi To him belongeth what he hath held confined in, or kept within, his house or tent: (TA:) or what he hath held in possession &c. (Az, TA in art. xmr : see 10 in that art.) You say also qaSarotu Ald~aAra , inf. n. as above, I [ confined and so ] defended the house by walls. (TA.) And qaSara AljaAriyapa biA@loHijaAbi He [ confined and so ] kept safe the girl by means of the veil, or covering, or the like: and in like manner you say of a horse. (TA.) And in a trad. of 'Omar it is said, qaSara bihimu All~ayolu , (TA,) or ↓ qaS~ara , (L,) The night withheld them; namely a company of riders upon camels on other beasts. (L, TA.) You also say qaSara Alr~ajula Eani AlA^amori [and qaSara bihi and bh ↓ qS~r ] He withheld the man from the thing, or affair, that he desired to do. (TA.) [See an ex. in a verse cited voce Tal~aAE .] And qaSarotu nafasiY Eano $aYo'K I withheld, or restrained, myself from a thing: (JK, TA: *) and I restrained myself from inordinate desire of a thing. (TA.) Lebeed says falasotu waA_ino A^aqoSarotu Eanohu bimuqoSiri meaning, But although thou blame in order that I may be restrained, I do not refrain from that which I desire to do. (El-Mázinee, L.) Also, qaSarotu TarofiY [ I restrained my eye, or eyes; ] I did not raise my eye, or eyes, towards that at which I ought not to look. (TA.) And qaSara AlbaSara He turned away the eye. (TA.) It is also said in a trad. of I'Ab, quSira Alr~ijaAlu EalaY A^arobaEK mino A^ajoli A^amowaAli AlyataAmaY Men were restricted to marrying no more than four [ because of the property of the orphans which they might leave]. (TA.) And one says qaSarotu nafosiY EalaY Al$~aYo'i I confined, or restricted, myself to the thing, and obliged myself to do it. (TA.) [See also 8.] Hence what is said of Thumámeh, in a trad., fA^abaY A^ano yusolima qaSorFA But he refused to become a Muslim by constraint and compulsion: or by force, as some say, from Alqasuru ; the s being changed into S , as is done in many other cases. (TA.) You say also qaSarotu Al$~aYo'a EalaY ka*aA I restricted the thing to such a thing. (S, TA.) And qaSarahu EalaY AlA^amori , meaning, rad~ahu A_ilayohi , (M, K,) i. e., [ He reduced him, to the thing, or affair; or] he appropriated him [or it, restrictively, ] to the thing, or affair. (TK.) [Hence,] qaSarotu All~iqoHapa EalaY farasiY I appropriated the milk of the milch-camel [ restrictively ] to my horse. (S, TA.) [And hence,] qaSarotu EalaY nafosiY naAqapF I retained for myself [ restrictively ] a she-camel, that I might drink her milk. (Msb.) Aboo-Du-ád says, describing a horse, faquSirona Al$~itaA='a baEodu Ealayohi wahuwa lil*~awodi A^ano yuqas~amona jaArN meaning, So they were restricted to him, that he might drink their milk, during the severity of the winter, afterwards; and he is a protector to the few she-camels from their being suddenly attacked and divided in shares; mino being understood before A^ano . (M.) -A6- qaSara Alv~awoba , (S, M, Msb,) aor. , (S,) inf. n. qaSorN (S, Mgh, Msb) and qiSaArapN ; (Sb, M, TA;) and ↓ qS~rhu , (S, M,) inf. n. taqoSiyrN ; (S;) He beat, (S, TA,) washed, (Mgh,) and whitened, (M, Msb, TA,) the cloth, or garment. (S, M, &c.)

Say~aqutuhu ; (Msb;) and I contracted his shackles; syn. qaArabotu . (M.) Habasahu . sourceDefinition: and ↓ qaSarN and ↓ quSorapN [like the inf. n. quSuwrN ] The falling, or stopping, or coming, short of accomplishing an affair; or of doing what one ought, or is commanded, to do; or flagging, or remissness: you say to a man whom you have sent to accomplish some needful affair, and who has fallen short of doing what you commanded him to do, on account of heat or some other cause, maA manaEaka A^ano taboluga AlmakaAna Al~a*iY A^amarotuka bihi A_il~aA A^an~aka A^aHobabota AlqaSora , and AlqaSara , and AlquSorapa , i. e. A^ano tuqaS~ira [ Nothing prevented thy reaching the place to which I commanded thee to go but thy loving to fall short &c.; or to flag, or be remiss ]. (M, K *.) And ↓ qaSarapN , (K,) or ↓ qaSarN , without p , accord. to the Nawádir of IAar, as cited in the L, and so in the handwriting of Sgh, (TA,) and ↓ qaSaArN , (K,) signify Laziness; slothfulness. (IAar, Sgh, K.) An Arab of the desert is related to have said ↓ A^aradotu A^ano A=tiyaka famanaEaniY AlqaSaAru [ I desired to come to thee, but laziness prevented me ]. (TA.) -A2- qaSoruka A^ano tafoEala ka*aA and ↓ qaSaAruka , (S, M, K,) and ↓ quSaAruka , (M, K,) and ↓ quSaAraAka , (S, M, K,) and ↓ quSayoraAka , (M, K,) Thine utmost, or the utmost of thy power or of thine ability or of thy deed, ( juhoduka , M, K, [or app., jahoduka , (see art. jhd ,)] and gaAyatuka , S, M, K,) and the end of thy case, and that to which thou hast confined or restricted or limited thyself, (S, TA,) [or that to which thou art confined or restricted or limited, ] is, or will be, thy doing such a thing. (S, M, K.) It is from qaSorN signifying the “ act of confining, restricting, limiting, ” &c. (TA.) And ↓ quSoraY also signifies the end of an affair. (Sgh, TA.) A poet says A_in~amaA A^anofusunaA EaAriy~apN waA@loEawaAriY~u qaSaArN A^ano turado [ Our souls are only a loan: and the end of loans is their being given back; turado being for turad~a ]. (S, TA.) You also say, kul~i balaA='K wa$id~apK ↓ Almawotu quSaAriY [ Death is the end of every trial and distress ]. (TA, art. HmA^ .) -A3- qaSorN (S, M) and ↓ maqoSarN (K) and ↓ maqoSarapN and ↓ maqoSirN (M, K) The afternoon: or evening: syn. Ea$iY~N : (S, M, K:) or the first signifies the last part of the day: (IKtt:) or the time before the sun becomes yellow: (JK:) or the first and second signify the time of the approach of the Ea$iY~ , a little before the EaSor : (A, TA:) and the first (S, K) and second (A'Obeyd, TA) and third, (A'Obeyd, S, TA,) [the time of ] the mixing of the darkness: (A'Obeyd, S, K, TA:) pl. of the second (TA) and third (S, M) and fourth, (M,) maqaASiru (S, M) and maqaASiyru , which latter is extr.; (M;) in the first sense, as signifying Ea$aAyaA ; (M;) or in the last sense; (S;) not signifying, as it is said to do in the K, AlEi$aA='u AlA=xirapu ; for this is a great mistake, app. occasioned by F's seeing the passage [in the T] of Az, [or in the M, in which I find it,] waAlmaqaASiru waAlmaqaASiyru AlEa$aAyaA AlA^axiyrapu naAdirapN , and not properly considering it. (TA.) Sb says, that qaSorN has no dim.; the Arabs being content to use in its stead the dim. of masaA='N . (M.) You say A^atayotuhu qaSorFA I came to him in the afternoon, or evening; syn. Ea$iy~FA . (S.) And jiy^otu qaSorFA , and ↓ maqoSarFA , I came at the approach of the Ea$iY~ , a little before the EaSor . (A, TA.) And AlEi$aA='i ↓ A^aqobalato maqaASiyru [ The times of the mixing of the darkness of nightfall came, or advanced ]. (A, TA.) -A4- qaSorN [ A palace: a pavilion, or kind of building wholly or for the most part isolated, sometimes on the top of a larger building, i. e., a belvedere, and sometimes projecting from a larger building, and generally consisting of one room if forming a part of a larger building or connected with another building; the same as the Turkish kw$k : to such buildings we find the appellation to have been applied from very early times to the present day:] a well-known kind of edifice: (M:) a mansion, or house; syn. manozilN : (Lh, M, K:) or any house or chamber ( bayot ) of stone; (M, K;) of the dial. of Kureysh: (M:) so called because a man's wives and the like are confined in it: (M:) pl. quSuwrN . (S, M, Msb.) qaSoru A@lomaliki [ The palace, or pavilion, of the king ]. (Msb.) -A5- Also qaSorN Large and dry, or large and thick, or dry, fire-wood; HaTabN jazolN . (M, K.) So in the Kur, lxxvii. 32, accord. to El-Hasan, as related by Lh. (M.)

sourceDefinition: Short; and low, i. e. having little height; contr. of TawiylN ; (S, M, Msb, K;) and so ↓ qaASirN , app. a kind of rel. or possessive n., not a verbal epithet: (M:) fem. of the former [and of the latter] with p : (M, K:) pl. of the former, masc., (S, M, Msb, K,) and fem., (M, K,) qiSaArN , (S, M, &c.,) and pl. masc. [applied to rational beings,] quSaraA='u , (M, K,) and pl. fem. qiSaArapN ; (K;) p being added by the Arabs to any pl. of the measure fiEaAlN , as in jimaAlapN and HibaAlapN and *ikaArapN and HijaArapN ; (Fr;) or qiSaArapN is syn. with qaSiyrapN , and is extr. (Sgh, K.) ― -b2- qaSiyrapN mino TawiylapK [lit. A short thing from a tall thing; meaning,] a date from a palm-tree: a proverb; alluding to the abridgment of speech or language. (K.) ― -b3- huwa qaSiyru Alyadi , [and AlbaAEK , (tropical:) He has little, or no, power: or is niggardly: ] and lahumo A^ayodK qiSaArN [ they have little, or no, power: or are niggardly ]. (TA.) ― -b4- qaSiyru Alhim~api [ Having little ambition ]. (O in art. bjl .) ― -b5- A_in~ahu laqaSiyru AlEilomi (tropical:) [ Verily he has little knowledge ]. (M.) ― -b6- qaSiyru Aln~asabi [ Having a short pedigree; ] whose father is well known, so that when the son mentions him it is sufficient for him, without his extending his lineage to his grandfather. (K.) [See also a verse below, in this paragraph.] ― -b7- HadiyvN qaSiyrN , and ↓ muqotaSarN , A [ concise, or] comprehensive, and profitable, story, or narration. (TA.) -A2- [ I. q. ↓ maqoSuwrN and ↓ maqoSuwrapN , Shortened; contracted: and confined; restricted; limited; &c.] ― -b2- A_imoraA^apN qaSiyru AlxuTaY , and AlxaTowi ↓ maqoSuwrapu , [ A woman whose steps are shortened, or contracted; ] likened to one who is shackled, whose steps are shortened, or contracted, by the shackles. (Fr.) ― -b3- farasN qaSiyrN A mare that is brought near [ to the tent or dwelling ], and treated generously, and not left to seek for pasture, because she is precious: (S, K:) and a mare that is kept confined. (TA.) ― -b4- qaSiyrapN , [which is extr., for by rule it should be without p ,] and ↓ qaSuwrapN , (Az, S, M, K,) and ↓ maqoSuwrapN , (K,) A woman confined in the house, or tent, not suffered to go forth: (S, M, K:) a woman kept behind, or within, the curtain: (TA, in explanation of the last of these three epithets:) a girl kept with care, that does not go out: (Az:) the pl. of qSwrp is qaSaAy^iru :] [and so, app., of qSyrp :] when you mean short in stature, you say qaSiyrapN [only], and the pl. is qiSaArN . (TA.) Kutheiyir says waA^anoti Al~atiY Hab~aboti kul~a qaSiyrapK A_ilaY~a wamaA tadoriY bi*aAka AlqaSaAy^iru Eanayotu qaSiyraAti AlHijaAli walamo A^urido qiSaAra AlxuTaY $ar~u Aln~isaA='i AlbaHaAtiru (S, M) or, as Fr relates it, kul~a qaSuwrapF (S) [ And thou art the person who hath made every female confined within the house to be an object of love to me, while the females confined within the house know not that: I mean those confined within the curtained canopies: I do not mean the short in step: the worst of women are the short and compressed ]. And a poet says waA^ahowaY mina Aln~iswaAni kul~a qaSiyrapK lahaA nasabN fiY AlS~aAliHiyna qaSiyru [ And I love, of women, every one that is confined within the house, that has a short pedigree, among the good ]; i. e., every ↓ maqoSuwrap , of whom it suffices to mention her descent from her father, because of his being well known. (M.) Hence, in the Kur, [lv. 72,] HuwrN maqoSuwraAtN fiY AlxiyaAmi [ Damsels having eyes whereof the white is intensely white and the black intensely black, ] confined in the pavilions, (Az, Msb,) which are of pearls, for their husbands; (Az;) concealed by curtains: (Az, Bd:) or confined to their husbands, and not raising their eyes to others: (Fr:) or having their eyes restricted to their husbands. (Bd.) And ↓ naAqapN maqoSuwrapN , (TA,) or maqoSuwrapN EalaY AlEiyaAli , (Msb,) A she-camel retained [ restrictively ] for the household, that they [ alone ] may drink her milk. (Msb, TA. *) ― -b5- See also quSorapN .

sourceDefinition: and maqoSuwrapN : see qaSiyrN , in five places. ― -b2- See also quSorapN . ― -b3- maqoSuwrapN An ample or a spacious [ house or mansion such as is called a ] dAr , which is defended by walls: (M, * K, * TA:) or it is less than a dAr ; (M, K;) as also ↓ quSaArapN ; and is not entered by any but the owner: (K:) such a part of a house is called the mqSwrp of a dAr , and the qSArp thereof: (Useyd, TA:) any apartment ( naAHiyapN ), by itself, of a dAr , when the latter is ample, or spacious, and defended by walls: (Lth, TA:) a [ chamber such as is called a ] Hujorap , of a house: (Mgh, Msb:) pl. maqaASiyru and maqaASiru . And AlmaqoSuwrapN , (Lth,) and maqoSuwrapu masojidK , (Mgh, Msb,) and maqoSuwrapu jAmiEK , (S,) The part which is the station of the Imám [or Khaleefeh ] in a mosque: (Lth, Mgh:) so called because confined [by a railing or screen]: (S:) or, accord. to some, mqSwrp , thus applied, is changed from its original form, which is qaASirapN , an act. part. n.: (Msb:) [and, as used in the present day, that part of a mosque which is the principal place of prayer, when it is partitioned off from the rest of the building: and the railing, or screen, which surrounds the oblong monument of stone or brick or wood over a grave in a mosque; sometimes enclosing a kind of baldachin over the monument. maqoSuwrapN also signifies The chancel of a church: see ma*obaHN .] And maqoSuwrapN and ↓ qaSuwrapN A Hajalap [or kind of curtained canopy or baldachin, such as is prepared for a bride ]. (Lh, M, K.) And the former word, A piece of ground which none but the owner thereof is allowed to tread. (TA.)

What is white in one half, black in the back, that walks contractedly, and makes water in drops? An enigma: to which the answer is, The qunofu* [q. v.]. (L.) ― -b2- qunofu*u layolK One who sleeps not [ during the night ]; because the qnf* sleeps not: (L:) and a calumniator; a slanderer; (L, K;) as also A^anoqadu layolK . (L.) ― -b3- Also qunofu*N and qunofa*N The rat, or mouse; syn. faArN : (K:) fem. with p . (TA.) ― -b4- qunofu*N (assumed tropical:) The part behind the ear of a camel, whence the sweat exudes. (S, L, K.) ― -b5- And, with p , (assumed tropical:) The part of the head that is below that which is called the qamaHoduwap . (L.) ― -b6- qunofu*N (assumed tropical:) A place that produces tangled herbage: (S, L, K:) an elevated place abounding with trees: AHn says, that what is thus termed is in hard ground, between what is termed quf~ and sand. (L.) ― -b7- qunofu*u ramolK (assumed tropical:) Sand collected together, (Aboo-Kheyreh, L, K,) and elevated, (K,) or somewhat elevated: (Aboo-Kheyreh, L:) or the abundance of trees of sand: or, as some say, qunofa*u ramolK , with fet-h, signifies abundance and tallness of trees of sand. (L.) ― -b8- qunofu*N (L, K) and with p (L) (assumed tropical:) A tree in the midst of sand. (L, K.) ― -b9- qanaAfi*u (assumed tropical:) Mountains that are not long: or long and narrow tracts, ( A^aHobul , L, K, TA: in the CK, A^ajobul , or mountains, ) of sand: (L, K:) or hills with pointed heads ( nabakN ) lying in the way, or road. (Th, L, K.)

definition: The portion, of a bow, that is between the part that is grasped by the hand and the curved extremity: to every bow there are qaAbaAni : (S, O, Msb, K:) or, accord.
sourceDefinition: The portion, of a bow, that is between the part that is grasped by the hand and the curved extremity: to every bow there are qaAbaAni : (S, O, Msb, K:) or, accord. to El-Khafájee, it is [the space ] between the string and the part that is grasped by the hand, of the bow; as also ↓ qiybN : (TA:) in the Kur [liii. 9], fakaAna qaAba qawosayoni accord. to some, is an inverted phrase, meaning fkAn qaAbaYo qawosK [i. e. And he was at the distance of the measure of the two portions between the part that is grasped by the hand and each of the curved extremities of a bow ]: (S, O:) [but] qaAbN signifies also a measure, or space; and so ↓ qiybN : (S, O, K:) one says, bayonahumaA qaAbu qawosK and qawosK ↓ qiybu , [ Between them two is the measure of a bow ], and likewise qaAdu quwosK and qiydu qawosK : (S, O: *) and it is said that qaAba qawosayoni [in the case mentioned above] means at [ the distance of ] the length of two bows: or as Fr says, at [ the distance of ] the measure of two Arabian bows. (TA.) [ qAbu qawosK is also a term often used in astronomy to denote the distance between two stars; and seems to be syn. with *iraAEN (q. v.) as so used, thus meaning A cubit; which is the measure of each qAb of a bow, or nearly so.]

sourceDefinition: A young bird; (S, A, O, K;) as also ↓ qaAy^ibapN and ↓ qaAbapN : (K:) or ↓ qaAy^ibapN signifies, (S, A, O,) or signifies also, (K,) an egg; (S, A, O, K;) and so does ↓ qaAbapN : (K;) ↓ qaAy^ibapN is used in the latter sense as meaning *aAtu quwbK , i. e. *aAtu faroxK : (Az, * O, TA: *) or it is like raADiyapN in the phrase Eiy$apN raADiyapN [meaning maroDiy~apN ]: (A:) [or as being originally the part. n. of qaAbat in the phrase qaAbati AlbayoDapu : and it may be used in the former sense as being originally the act. part. n. of qaAbat in the phrase qaAbati AlbayoDapa said of a hen-bird:] and ↓ qaAwibapN signifies an egg from which the young bird has come forth: (Az, TA:) or quwbN signifies an egg: and ↓ qaAbapN , a young bird: (AHeyth, TA:) the pl. of quwbN is A^aqowaAbN . (K.) It is said in a prov., mino quwbK ↓ bariy^ato qaAy^ibapN , (S, A, O,) or mino quwbK ↓ taxal~aSato qaAy^abipN , (K,) or mino quwbK ↓ qaAbapN , (tropical:) An egg became or has become, freed from a young bird [that was in it]: (S, A, O, K:) or a young bird, from an egg: (AHeyth, TA:) applied to him who has become separated from his companion. (A, * K.) An Arab of the desert, of the tribe of Asad, (S,) or Asd, (O,) said to a merchant who asked him to be his safeguard, mino ↓ A_i*aA balagotu bika makaAna ka*aA bariy^ato qaAy^ibapN quwbK , meaning (assumed tropical:) [ When I shall have reached with thee such a place, ] I shall be clear of obligation to protect thee. (S, O.) El-Kumeyt says lahun~a waliloma$iybi wamano EalaAhu waquwbu ↓ mina AlA^amovaAli qaAy^ibapN [ To them (i. e. women), and to hoariness and him upon whom it has come, relates, among the proverbs, “ An egg and a young bird ”]: he likens the fleeing of women from old men to the fleeing of the quwb , or young bird, from the qaAy^ibap , or egg; and [virtually] says that the beautiful woman will not return to the old man, like as the young bird will not return to the egg. (TA.) And Aboo-'Alee El-Kálee mentions the saying, mino quwbK ↓ laA waAl~a*iY A^axoraja qaAy^ibapF , as meaning [ No, by Him who has produced ] a young bird from an egg: but Aboo-'Obeyd El-Bekree says that this is inverted. (MF, TA.) ― -b2- A^um~u quwbK [in the TA said to be bAlftH , a mistranscription for biAlD~am~i ,] Calamity, or misfortune. (O, K.)

definition: A certain nation;
sourceDefinition: A certain nation; [ the Gordiæi: (Golius:) n. un. kurodiY~N :] pl. A^akoraAdN : (S, L, K:) respecting their origin authors differ: it is said that their ancestor was Kurd the son of 'Amr Muzeykiyà the son of 'Ámir Má-es-Semà, not 'Ámir the son of Má-es-Semà, as in the K, for Má-es-Semà was a surname of 'Ámir: (TA:) or they are the remains of the people whom Beewarásf, also called Ed-Dahhák, used to eat: (IKt, MF, TA:) or their ancestor was Kurd the son of Ken'án (or Canaan) the son of Koosh (or Cush) the son of Hám (or Ham) the son of Nooh (or Noah): they consist of countless tribes, differing in language and condition, but all are reduced to four principal tribes, the swrAn and the kwrAn and the kulhr and the lur : (Mohammad Efendee El-Kurdee:) or their ancestor was Kurd the son of 'Amr the son of 'Ámir the son of Saasa'ah: (Abu-l-Yakdhán:) El-Mes'oodee says, that some assert them to be of the descendants of Rabee'ah the son of Nizár: others, that they are of the descendants of Mudar the son of Nizár: others, that they are descended from Kurd the son of Ken'án the son of Koosh the son of Hám: and he adds, that they are apparently of the offspring of Hám, like the Persians: that among the known tribes of which they consist are the swrAny~p , the kwrAnyp , the EmAdyp , the HkAryp , the mHmwdyp , the bxtyp , the b$wyp , the jwbyp , the zrzAy^yp , the mhrAnyp , the jAwdAnyp , the rDAy^yp , the srwjyp , the hArwnyp , and the lryp : and that their countries are Persia, and 'Irák el-'Ajam, and Ádharbeeján, and Irbil, and El-Mósil. (Mo- hammad Efendee El-Kurdee.) [Many other assertions as to the origin of this people are made by other authors.]

sourceDefinition: , occurring in the Kur [liii. 19,] (TA,) so accord. to the reading of Ibn-'Abbás and 'Ikrimeh and some others, (K,) and so originally accord. to Fr.: (TA:) afterwards contracted into All~aAtu : (Fr, K:) which is the common reading: (Fr:) A certain idol; thus called by the appellation of a man who used to moisten sawiyq with clarified butter at the place thereof: (K:) the man who did this was thus called, and afterwards the idol itself. (TA.) Some of the lexicologists say, that it was a mass of rock, at the place whereof was a man who used to moisten swyq for the pilgrims, and which, when he died, was worshipped: (L:) but ISd says, I know not what is the truth in this case. (TA.) In the R it is said, that the man who used to do this was 'Amr Ibn-Lu-eí; that when the tribe of Khuzá'ah obtained the dominion over Mekkeh, and banished the tribe of Jurhum, the Arabs made him a Lord, or an object of worship; and that he was El-Látt, who used to moisten swyq for the pilgrims upon a well-known rock, called Sxorapu All~aAt~i : or, it is said, that the man in question was of the tribe of Thakeef; and that when he died, 'Amr Ibn-Loheí ( lHY : so in the TA) said to the people, “ He hath not died, but hath entered the rock: ” and ordered them to worship it, and built over it a house called AllAt : it is also said to have continued thus during the life of this man and that of his son, for three hundred years: then that rock was named All~aAtu , without teshdeed to the t , and was taken for an idol, to be worshipped. (TA.) It is disputed whether it were [an idol] of the tribe of Thakeef at Et-Táïf, or of the tribe of Kureysh at En-Nakhleh. (MF.) Some say, that the t is originally without teshdeed, and to denote the fem. gender: Ks used to pronounce the word in a case of pause All~aAho ; and Aboo-Is-hák [Zj] says, that this is agreeable with analogy; but that the more approved mode is to pronounce it in such case with t . AM says, that the manner in which Ks pronounced it in a case of pause shows that he did not derive it from lat~N . The polytheists who worshipped this idol used to compare its name with the name of All~`h . It is also said, that All~aAtu , without teshdeed, is of the measure faEalapN [originally All~awayapu ] from the root lwY ; [and that the said idol was so called] because they used to compass it, or perform circuits round it. (TA.) [See art. lwY : and see also arts. lwh and lyh : and Alr~ab~apu , in art rb .]

definition: He instigated against him;
sourceDefinition: He instigated against him; and aided against him; and acted wrongfully, or injuriously, towards him. (JK.) ― -b2- Alhd He did, or acted, wrong, wrongfully, unjustly, or injuriously; (L, K;) [as also AlHd ]. ― -b3- Alhd bihi is said of a man, with respect to another, when the former withholds one of two men and leaves the other at liberty, fighting him. [The object is, app., the former of these two, as he is the injured one.] (AA, S, L, K.) ― -b4- It is also said of a man, with respect to another, when the former acquaints one of the men with the contention or dispute of the other, or with that which the other would say to him, and makes known to him a matter which he understands from him, but which is obscure to others, and informs him of the other's argument. [The object is, app., the latter of these two, as he is the injured one.] (AA, L.) ― -b5- Also, waA@ll~`hi maA qulotahaA A_il~aA A^ano tulohida EalaY~a By God, thou saidst it not save that thou mightest aid against me, is said when a man has acquainted one of the two men with that which the other would say. [It is, app., said by the latter of these two, as he is the injured one.] (AA, S, L.) ― -b6- Alhd He made, or prepared, the kind of food called lahiydap . (IKtt.) ― -b7- Alhd bihi , (inf. n. sourceDefinition: , (S, L, K,) aor. , (L,) inf. n. mad~N ; and mad~a bihi ; and ↓ md~dhu ; [or this has an intensive or a frequentative signification;] and ↓ tmd~dhu ; (L, K;) and ↓ mAd~hu , or mAddhu , (as in different copies of the K, TA,) inf. n. mumaAd~apN and midaAdN ; (K;) He drew it (namely a rope, &c., A); pulled it: strained it: extended it by drawing or pulling; stretched it. (L, K, El-Basáïr.) You say also mad~a Alqawosa [ He drew the bow ]; (S, Msb, K, in art. nzE ;) and mad~a mina Albiy^ori [ He drew water from the well ]. (S, K, art. mtH .) [Hence, app., mad~a biA^arofaAdiY : see rifodN .] ― -b2- qaAy^ilu kalimapi Alz~uwri waAl~a*iY yamud~u biHabolihaA fiY AlA_ivomi sawaA='N [ The utterer of falsehood and he who transmits it are in respect of the sin alike ]: a trad. of 'Alee; in which the utterer of the falsehood is likened to him who fills the bucket in the lower part of the well, and the relater thereof to him who draws the rope at the top. (L.) ― -b3- mad~a He extended, or stretched forth, his hand or arm, foot or leg, &c. (The Lexicons passim.) ― -b4- bayonanaA ↓ tamad~adonaAhu We drew, pulled, strained, or stretched, it between us, or together. (L.) [But in a copy of the M, it is tamaAdadonaAhu .] ― -b5- mad~a AlHarofa , aor. , inf. n. mad~N , He lengthened the letter. (L.) ― -b6- mad~a Sawotahu (tropical:) He prolonged, or strained, his voice [as the Arab does in chanting]: (L:) and fiY AlS~awoti ↓ tamad~ada Einoda AlwaEiydi (assumed tropical:) [ He strained the voice in threatening ]. (K, art. nmr .) ― -b7- mad~a , inf. n. mad~N , (tropical:) It (his sight) was, or became, stretched, and raised, A_ilaY $aYo'K towards a thing. (K.) ― -b8- mad~a baSarahu A_ilaY $aYo'K , aor. , [inf. n. mad~N ,] (tropical:) He stretched, and raised, his sight towards a thing. (A, * L.) ― -b9- madadotu EayoniY A_ilaY ka*aA (tropical:) I looked at such a thing desirously. (IKtt, El-Basáïr.) ― -b10- mad~aha , aor. , (Lh, L,) inf. n. mad~N , (Lh, L, K,) He expanded it, or stretched it out: (L, K:) he extended it, elongated it, or lengthened it. (L.) ― -b11- mad~ A@ll~`hu AlA^aroDa God expanded, or stretched out, and made plain, or level, the earth. (Lh, L.) ― -b12- mad~a A@ll~`hu AlZ~il~a (tropical:) God extended, or stretched forth, the shade. (A.) See 8. ― -b13- mad~a A@ll~`hu fiY Eumorihi (tropical:) God made his life long; (S, A, * L;) as also ↓ Amd~a . (IKtt.) ― -b14- mad~a A@ll~`hu fiY Eumorika (tropical:) May God make thy life long! (L.) ― -b15- mud~a fiY Eumorihi (tropical:) He had his life lengthened. (L.) ― -b16- AlA^ajala ↓ A^amad~a , inf. n. A_imodaAdN , (tropical:) He deferred, or postponed, the term, or period of duration. (K.) ― -b17- lahu fiY AlA^ajali ↓ Amd~ (tropical:) He deferred, or postponed, to him the term, or his term. (TA.) ― -b18- mad~ahu , aor. , (L,) inf. n. mad~N ; and ↓ Amd~hu , inf. n. A_imodaAdN ; (L, K;) but the latter is little used; (L;) (tropical:) He made him to continue; to go on long; left him, or let him alone, long, or for a while; granted him a delay, or respite. (L, K. *) Ex. mad~ahu fiY gay~ihi , (S, L,) and ↓ Amd~hu , (L,) (tropical:) He made him to continue, &c., in his error. (S, L.) And in like manner, mad~a A@ll~`hu lahu fiY AlEa*aAbi (tropical:) God made him to continue, or go on long, in a state of punishment. (L.) See also 3. ― -b19- mad~a fiY Als~ayori (tropical:) He made much advance in journeying. (L.) ― -b20- mad~ahu , inf. n. madadN and midaAdN , He made it much in quantity; increased it. (L, TA.) ― -b21- mad~a , (S, L, Msb,) aor. , [contr. to analogy,] (L,) inf. n. mad~N ; (S, L, K;) It (water, L, and a river, S, L, and a sea, or great river, L) flowed: (S, L, K:) it (water, L, and a sea, or great river, L, Msb) increased; as also ↓ Amd~ ; both of which verbs are also used transitively: (Msb:) or became much in quantity, copious, or abundant, in the days of the torrents; as also ↓ Amtd~ : (L:) contr. of jazara [it ebbed]. (Lth, S, M, K in art. jzr .) ― -b22- waAdiY ka*aA yamud~u fiY nahori ka*aA Such a valley flows into and increases such a river. (A, L.) ― -b23- mad~ahu , (Lh, S, L, Msb,) aor. , (Lh, L,) inf. n. mad~N ; (Lh, L, Msb;) and ↓ Amd~hu ; (L, Msb;) It (a thing) entered into it, (i. e., a like thing,) and increased it, or made it copious or abundant: (Lh, L:) it (a river, S, L, or sea, or great river, L, Msb) flowed into it, (i. e., another river, or sea, or great river,) and increased it, replenished it, or made it copious or abundant: (S, * L, Msb: *) it (a well) fed it, i. e., another well: (L:) [see an ex. in a verse cited in art. grw , conj. 3]: both these verbs are also used intransitively. (Msb.) ― -b24- [ mad~~ti Als~uwqu (assumed tropical:) The market was full of people and of goods for sale. See the part. n.] ― -b25- mad~a Alqawoma , [aor. , inf. n. mad~N ,] He became an auxiliary to the people: (K:) and madadonaAhumo We became auxiliaries to them: somewhat differing from ↓ A^amadonaAhumo , which signifies We aided them, or succoured them, by others than ourselves: (AZ, S, L, K:) you say, bimadadK ↓ A^amodadotuhu I aided him, and strengthened him, [or increased his numbers and strength, ] with an army: (S, * Msb:) and AlA^amiyru junodahu biAlxayoli waAlr~ijaAli ↓ A^amad~a The commander aided, or succoured, his army with cavalry and infantry, or with horses and men: and bimaAlK kaviyrK ↓ Amd~humo He aided them with, or, as some say, gave them, much wealth: (L:) and [it is said in the Kur, lii. 22,] waA^amodadonaAhumo bifaAkihapK (S, L) And We will increase their provision time after time with fruit: (Beyd, Jel:) or with relation to evil, you say madadotuhu ; and with relation to good, ↓ A^amodadotuhu : (K:) so says Yoo: (L:) this is generally the case; and the following are examples: A^amodadonaAhumo bifaAkihapK [explained above]: and namud~uhumo mina AlEa*aAbi (ElBasáïr) [Kur, xix. 82,] We will prolong and increase to them punishment: (Beyd;:) but Z relates, that Akh said the reverse, like waEada and A^awoEada : the usage of the Arabs, however, does not accord with either of these assertions. (MF.) ― -b26- mad~a It (anything) became full, and rose. (Sh, L.) ― -b27- mad~a Als~iraAja , (aor. , A, [inf. n. mad~N ,]) He put oil (or the like, K) into the lamp. (A, L, K.) ― -b28- mad~a Ald~awaApa , (aor. , inf. n. mad~N , Msb,) and ↓ Amd~haA , He put ink into the receptacle thereof; (S, * Msb;) he increased its water, and its ink. (L.) ― -b29- In like manner, mad~a Alqalama , and ↓ Amd~hu , He supplied the reed-pen with ink. (L.) ― -b30- mad~ahu mud~apF mina Ald~awaApi , aor. ; and mud~apF ↓ A^amad~ahu is also allowable; (L;) or simply mad~ahu (A) and A^amad~ahu ; (S, A, K;) He gave him a dip of ink from the receptacle thereof with a reed-pen. (S, TA.) ― -b31- mad~a , inf. n. mad~N , He dipped the reedpen in the receptacle of ink a single time for writing. (Msb.) See also 10. ― -b32- mad~a AlA^aroDa , (aor. , A, inf. n. mad~N , L,) He manured the land with dung: (A, K:) or he added to the land manure composed of dung and ashes, or of earth or dust and dung, or of strong earth; or simply earth; or sand; to render it more productive. (L.) ― -b34- mad~a AlA_ibila , (AZ, S, A, L, K.) aor. , inf. n. mad~N ; (AZ, L;) and ↓ Amd~hA ; (S, A, L;) He gave madiyd (or water upon which had been sprinkled, or with which had been mixed, some flour, or the like, &c. ) to the camels to drink: (AZ, S, A, L, K:) or he put some barley coarsely ground, and then moistened, into the camel's mouths: (AZ, L:) or mad~ahu bimadiydK , aor. , inf. n. mad~N , signifies, as some say, he fed him with fodder. (M.)

sourceDefinition: See 1 throughout. ― -b2- Amd~ fiyhi He (God) made it (the means of subsistence) ample: made it (wealth or the like) abundant: increased it, namely, a sea or river. (IKtt.) ― -b3- Amd~hu He made it (anything) to become full, and to rise. (Sh, L.) See also 1. ― -b4- Amd~ , inf. n. A_imodaAdN , He aided, or succoured: and he gave. (K.) See mad~a Alqawoma . ― -b5- Amd~ fiY mi$oyatihi He (a man) walked with an elegant, and a proud, and self-conceited, gait, with an affected incline of his body from side to side. (TA.) See also 5. ― -b6- Amd~ (inf. n. A_imodaAdN , L, &c.) It (a wound) produced midap , or thick purulent matter. (S, L, Msb. K.) ― -b7- Amd~ (inf. n. A_imodaAdN , K) It (the plant called Earofaj , S, L, K, and the Sil~iyaAn , and the Tariyfap , TA) became succulent, the sap running in it: (S, L, K:) and it, (the twig, or wood, of any of the three plants above mentioned,) being rained upon became soft, or supple. (L.)

definition: A certain kind of beverage, prepared from honey, (S, L, K,) which the Khaleefehs of the sons of Umeyyeh used to drink: (L:) so called in relation to a town in Syria, (S, L,) called maqadN ;
sourceDefinition: A certain kind of beverage, prepared from honey, (S, L, K,) which the Khaleefehs of the sons of Umeyyeh used to drink: (L:) so called in relation to a town in Syria, (S, L,) called maqadN ; or in relation to a town in Syria in the province of El-Urdunn: (L:) or this is a mistake; for the name of the town is with teshdeed [ maqad~N ]: IB says, that the orthography of the word as best known to the lexicologists is maqadiY~N , without teshdeed; but that A 'Obeyd and others write it with teshdeed; and that IAmb cites in confirmation of its being thus a verse of 'Amr Ibn-Maadeekerib, at the end of which occurs the expression $agaluwhu Eano $arobi Almaqad~i ; without Y ; [app. for maqad~iY ;] adding, that it is thus called in relation to maqad~N , a town of Damascus, in the mountain overlooking El-Ghór: (L:) A 'Obeyd says, I hold it to be correctly maqad~iY~N ; and I heard Rejà Ibn-Selemeh explain this as signifying “ wine diminished to half its quantity by boiling; ” as though it were divided ( qud~a ) in halves: (Sh, L:) IB adds, that Aboo-t-Teyyib the lexicologist says, that the word in question is with d without teshdeed; from maqadN ; and is only written with teshdeed by poetic licence: and in confirmation of this assertion, IB cites verses in which the name of the town and that of the beverage are written without teshdeed. (L.) ― -b2- vawobN maqadiY~N A certain well-known kind of cloth, or garment: (L, TA:) you say viyaAbN maqadiy~apN . (K. [In the CK, erroneously, maqad~iy~apN .])

definition: [ A child's cradle, or bed;
sourceDefinition: [ A child's cradle, or bed; ] a place prepared for a child, and made plain, even, or smooth, (S, * L, K,) that he may sleep in it: (L:) a bed; a thing spread to lie, recline, or sit, upon; (A, Msb;) as also ↓ mihaAdN ; (S, A, L, Msb, K;) so called because of its plainness, evenness, or smoothness: (L:) Az says, that the latter word is more comprehensive than the former: (L:) it is applied to the ground, or earth; [meaning a plain, an even, or a smooth expanse; see a verse of Lebeed cited voce xawaAliqu :] (Az, L, K:) and so is mahodN : (K:) some say, that mahodN and ↓ mihaAdN are [originally] two inf. ns., of the same meaning: or that the former is an inf. n., and the latter a simple subst.: or that the former is sing., and the latter pl.: (MF:) the pl. of the former [in common use] is muhuwdN , (L, Msb, K,) and mihaAdN ; and of the latter, [pl. of pauc.,] A^amohidapN (L, K) and [of mult.,] muhudN . (L, Msb, K.) ― -b2- ↓ A^alamo najoEali A@loA^aroDa mihaAdFA [Kur, lxxviii. 6,] Have we not made the earth an expanse ( bisaAT ) adapted to be travelled over. (K, TA.) ― -b3- ↓ labiy^osa AlmihaAdu [Kur. ii. 202,] (tropical:) Evil is that which he hath prepared for himself in his final place. (K.) Such is said to be the meaning. (TA.) ― -b4- sahodN mahodN Good; goodly: the latter word is an imitative sequent. (L.)

definition: He begot a generous, noble, or liberal, child;
sourceDefinition: He begot a generous, noble, or liberal, child; such as is termed najiybN . (S.) [This verb, being coupled in the K with najuba , might be imagined syn. therewith; but this, accord. to the TA, is not the case.] El-Aashà says, A^anojaba A^azomaAna waAlidaAhu bihi A_i*o najalaAhu faniEoma maA najalaA (S) He begot a generous son in the times when his parents ( rejoiced ) in him, when they produced him; and excellent was that which they produced. Accord. to one reading, the second word is A^ay~aAma : and A^ay~aAmu waAlidayohi is also read in place of AzmAn wAldAh ; in which case, Ay~aAm is fig. the agent of Anjb . (TA.) ― -b2- Anjbt is said of a woman, in the same sense. (TA.) See also Anxb . ― -b3- Anjb [as also Anxb ] He begot a cowardly child: (from najabN , the “ bark ” of a tree: TA:) thus the verb bears two contr. significations: (K:) or the two significations are not necessarily contr.; for a courageous man may be not generous, or liberal; and a generous, or liberal, man may be not courageous. (MF.)

definition: A generous, noble, liberal, man;
sourceDefinition: A generous, noble, liberal, man; (S, K;) one distinguished by rank or quality, nobility or eminence, reputation or note or consideration; (K;) excellent; of great worth in his kind; one who is like his father in generosity and actions: (TA:) as also ↓ najobN (K) [explained as signifying “ liberal, generous ”] and ↓ nujabapN : (S, K:) or you call a man njyb when he is generous, noble, or liberal; but when he is unequalled among his people in generosity, &c., you say qawomihi ↓ huwa najabapu , in measure like Halamap : (El-'Alam Es-Sakháwee:) [but MF doubts the correctness of this measure; and seems to think that the correct word is ↓ nujabap :] Alqawomi ↓ hw nujabapu is said of a man when he is the man, among them, who is distinguished by generosity, &c.: (S:) pl. nujabaA='u and A^anojaAbN and nujubN . (K.) ― -b2- najiybN Excellent, as an epithet applied to any animal; (IAth;) a generous, excellent, camel or horse; one of high breed; (ISd;) a strong, light, swift, camel: (TA:) you say naAqapN najiybapN as well as nAqp najiybN : (K:) pl. najaAy^ibu (S, K) and nujubN . (S.) ― -b3- najaAy^ibu AlquroA=ni The most excellent, and the purest, parts of the Kur-án. Of such is the suwrapu AlA^anoEaAm . (TA.) In like manner, ↓ nawaAjibuhu The heart thereof that has [as it were] no najab [or bark] upon it: or the best, or most excellent, thereof. (K.)

definition: A young person past the age of puberty: (TA:) or a boy or girl past the age of childhood: (S, K:) or a comely young man: (IAar:) or a youth who has attained the stature of a man: (AHeyth:) a girl, as well as a boy, is called thus;
sourceDefinition: A young person past the age of puberty: (TA:) or a boy or girl past the age of childhood: (S, K:) or a comely young man: (IAar:) or a youth who has attained the stature of a man: (AHeyth:) a girl, as well as a boy, is called thus; (TA;) and they also say, jaAriyapN naA$iy^apN . (AA.) Pl. na$o'N and na$aA^N (S, K [or these two are rather quasi-pl. ns.,] or the ↓ former is an inf. n. used as an epithet, Aboo-Moosa,) and naA$iy^uwna (AHeyth) and nawA$iy^u : (TA:) or the last is a pl. of nA$y^ as applied to a girl. (MF.) Lth says that ↓ na$o'N signifies Young people; or youths; and is used in the sing. also: ex. huwa na$o'u sawo'K He is a bad youth: and he says that he had never heard nA$y^ used as an epithet for a girl. Fr says that the ' of the pl. na$o'N is sometimes suppressed, and they say, in the nom. na$uw SdoqK [ Excellent youths ]; acc., na$aA Sdq ; gen. na$iY Sdq . (TA.) ― -b2- naA$iy^N Clouds not completely collected together. Hence, it is said, is derived the expression na$aA^a AlS~abiY~u ; which is therefore tropical. (TA.) ― -b3- naA$iy^N Whatever happens ( and, perhaps, appears TA,) in the night: pl. naA$iy^apN ; (K;) a strange form of pl. of a word of the measure qaAEilN : (M, F:) or naA$iy^apN [see Kur, lxxiii. 6,] is an inf. n. (K) in the sense of qiyaAmN : (TA:) AM says, that nA$y^pu All~ayoli signifies qyAm Allyl the rising in the night: (TA:) or nA$y^p signifies the first part of the night, and of the day: or the first of the hours of the night: (S, K:) or a pious act of the night; i. e., performed in the night: (S:) or every hour of the night in which one rises: (K:) or every hour of the night: (Zj:) or a rising after a sleeping, (K,) in the first part of the night; (TA;) as also ↓ na$iyoy^apN . (K.)

definition: The young one of a raven, or crow: syn faroxu guraAbK : or a raven, or crow, [absolutely]: syn.
sourceDefinition: The young one of a raven, or crow: syn faroxu guraAbK : or a raven, or crow, [absolutely]: syn. EuraAbN . In a prayer of David occur the words yaA raAziq Aln~aE~aAbi fiY Eu$~ihi [ O Sustainer of the young raven (or young crow ) in his nest! ]. It is said that the young raven (or young crow), when it comes forth from its egg, is white, like a lump of fat, and that the old bird, on seeing it, dislikes and abandons it; that thereupon God sends to it gnats, which light upon it on account of its foul greasy smell, and that it lives upon them until it is fledged and becomes black, when its parents return to it. (L.)

And nafarati AlmaroA^apu mino zawojihaA (tropical:) [ The woman was averse from her husband; or shunned or avoided him ]. (All from the A.) And you say of a man's disposition, Eani AlHaq~i ↓ tanaf~ara (tropical:) [ It shunned, or was averse from, the truth ] (Bd, lxvii. 21.) ― -b3- A_il~aA nufuwrFA , in the Kur, [xvii. 43, and xxxv. 40,] means (tropical:) Save in aversion and nafiyrN is like nufuwrN : and the subst. is nafarN , with two fet-hahs. (A'Obeyd, T, S. *) You say also, nafarati AlEayonu , aor. and , inf. n. nufuwrN . (tropical:) His eye became inflamed and swollen: and so you say of other parts of the person. And nafara Aljilodu (tropical:) The skin became swollen, (S, A,) and the flesh receded from it. (A.) (IKtt) ― -b7- nafaruwA , (Msb,) inf. n. naforN , (M, Msb, K,) They became separated, or dispersed: (M, * Msb, K: *) and so nafarto , said of camels. (TA.) [And gaDiba mino gayori SayoHK walaA nafKro ; explained in the same art.] ― -b8- nafara AlHaAj~u mino minFY , (M, Msb, K,) aor. , (S, M, K,) inf. n. naforN (M, Msb, K) and nafarN (M) and nufuwrN (K) [and nafiyrN ], The pilgrims removed from Minè. (Msb.) (M.) And naqaruwA , alone, They went forth to war against unbelievers or the like. So in the Kur, is 82. waqaAlwA laA tanofiruwA fY AlHr~i qulo naArN jahan~ama A^a$adN Har~aA [ And they said, Go not ye forth to war against the unbelievers in the heat: say, The fire of hell is hotter ]: and so in the same chap. v. 39: (Jel:) and in the same book, iv. 73. (Bd.) You say also, nafaruwA lahumo They went forth to fight them. (TA, from a trad.) And tafaruwA A_ilY AlHarob They hastened to the war, or to war. (Msb.) ― -b10- [Hence,] nafawuA maEahu ; and ↓ A^anofaruwhu , (M, K,) inf. n. A_inofaArN ; (TA;) They aided and succoured them: (M, K:) or the former verb, alone, they, being asked to do so, complied, and went forth to aid. (TA.) ― -b11- nafrabinaA : see 2.

definition: , (T, M, A, Msb,) inf.
sourceDefinition: , (T, M, A, Msb,) inf. n. tanofyrN ; (Msb;) and ↓ Anfr ; (T, K;) and ↓ A$tnfr ; (T, M, A, Msb;) He made (wild animals, T. Msb, or an antelope. K, or a beast of carriage. M,) to take fright, and flee, or run away at random: (K, TA:) or he made a beast of carriage to become impatient, and to retire to a distance: (A:) or he scared away; or made to flee, and go away, or aside, or apart, or to a distance: (so accord. to an explanation of the intrans. v. from which it is derived, in the M:) you say naf~arotuhu and ↓ Aisotanofarotuhu and ↓ A^anofarutuhu : and in like manner, naf~ara Eanohu , and A^anofara Eanohu , [meaning, he scared away, or made to take fright and flee, &c., from him or it: ] (TA:) AlA_inofaAru Eani Al$~aYo'i , and Alt~anofiyru Eanohu , and AlAisotinofaAru , all signify the same, [i. e., the scaring away, &c. from a thing. ] (S.) It is said in a trad. of Zeyneb, the daughter of Mohammad, faA^anofara bihaA Almu$orikuwna baEiyrahaA Hat~aY saqaTato And the polytheists made her camel to take fright and run away at random with her, so that she fell. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence] ba$~irwA walA tunaf~iruwA (assumed tropical:) [ Rejoice people by what ye say. and ] do not encounter them with [ roughness and violence and ] that which will incite them to nufuwr [i. e. flight or aversion ]. (assumed tropical:) Give thou to him a laqab [meaning a nickname or name of reproach ], (S,) or a laqb that is disliked: (K:) as though they held such to be tasofiyrN lilojin~i waAlEayoni Eanohu [ a means of scaring away the jinn, or genii, and the evil eye, from him ]. (S.)

definition: A number of men, from three to ten;
sourceDefinition: A number of men, from three to ten; (S, Msb;) as also ↓ naforN and ↓ naforapN and ↓ nafiyrN : (S:) or to seven: (so in a copy of the Msb, [but probably sbEp is a mistake for tsEp nine: this appears likely from what here follows:]) or a number of men less then ten; (AZ, T, M, K;) as also ↓ nafiyrN ; (K;) and so rahoTN ; (AZ, T;) and some add, excluding women: (TA:) accord. to Fr, (S,) a man's people or tribe consisting of his nearer relations; as also ↓ naforapN ; syn. rahoTN , (S, IAth,) and Ea$iyrapN : (IAth:) [see also naforapN :] accord. to Kr, (M,) all the men or people: (M, K:) accord. to Lth, you say, h`w^ulaA='i Ea$arapu nafarK , i. e. these are ten men: but one does not say, Ei$oruwna nafarFA , nor more than Ea$arap : and Abu-l- 'Abbás says, that nafarN , like qawomN and rahoTN , has a pl. signification, without any proper sing.; and is applied to men, exclusively of women: (T:) it is a quasi-pl. n.: (TA:) and its pl. is A^anofaArN ; (M, K;) occurring in a trad., in the phrase A^aHadN mino A^anofaArinaA , which IAth explains as meaning any one of our people; syn. qawominaA : (TA:) and ↓ nafiyrN , occurring, in the accus. case, in the Kur, xvii. 6, is, accord. to Zj, a pl. [or rather quasipl. n.] of nafarN , like EabiydN and kaliybN . (M.) [See also nafiyrN , below.] Imra-el-Keys says, describing a man as an excellent archer, fahowa laA tanomiY ramiy~atuhu maA lahu laA Eud~a mino nafariho (S,) And he is such that the animal shot by him does not go away after it has been shot and then die. What aileth him? May he be killed, so as not to be numbered among his people. The latter hemistich is a proverb. (Meyd.) The poet here utters an imprecation against the man, but in so doing praises him; as when you say, of a man whose action pleases you, maA lahu qaAtalahu A@ll~`hu and A^axozaAhu A@ll~`hu [q. v.]. (S.) The rel. n. is ↓ nafariY~N . (Sb, M.) -A2- [Accord. to the Msb, it is also a simple subst. from nafara : and app. as signifying especially Aversion. ]

definition: A people hastening to war, or to some other undertaking: an inf.
sourceDefinition: A people hastening to war, or to some other undertaking: an inf. n. used as a subst.: (Msb:) or a people going to execute an affair: (S:) or a people going with one to fight; as also ↓ naforapN [q. v.] and ↓ naforN : (M, K:) each is a noun having a pl. signification: (M:) or the first and last signify a company of men: and the pl. of each is A^anofaArN : (M:) or the first, (S,) or all, (K,) a people, (S,) or company, (K,) preceding in an affair: (S, K:) or the first, those of a man's people who go forth with him to war: or it is a pl. [or quasi-pl.] of nafarN , signifying men assembled to go to the enemy: (Bd, xvii. 6:) or aiders, or assistants. (M.) [See nafarN , in two places.] You say, jaA='ato naforapu baniY fulaAnK , and nafiyruhumo , The company of the sons of such a one, that came forth to execute an affair, arrived. (S, TA.) nafiyru qurayo$K means Those of Kureysh who went forth to Bedr to defend the caravan of Aboo-Sufyán, (M,) which was coming from Syria. (T.) Hence the proverb, fulaAnN laA fiY AlEiyri walaA fiY Aln~afiyri [ Such a one is neither in the caravan nor in the company going forth to fight ]: applied to him who is not regarded as fit for a difficult undertaking: because none held back from the caravan and the fight except him who was crippled by disease and him in whom was no good; (TA:) or the original words of the proverb are lA fiY AlEiyri walaA fiY Aln~afiyri : and these words were first said by Aboo-Sufyán, with reference to the Benoo-Zuhrah, when he found them turning back towards Mekkeh; and, accord. to As, are applied to a man who is held in low and little repute. (Mgh.) [See also Freytag's Arab. Prov., ii. 500.]

sourceDefinition: [and ↓ nafuwrN ] and ↓ musotanofirN signify the same; [i. e., Taking fright, and fleeing, or running away at random: or being, or becoming, impatient, of or at a thing, and retiring to a distance: or fleeing, and going away or aside or apart or to a distance: or the second, being of an intensive form, signifies, as also ↓ yanofuwrN , that does so much or often; or wont or apt to do so: ] (TA:) and naforN is a pl. of naAfirN , (K,) or [rather] a quasi-pl., like as SaHobN is of SaAHibN , and zaworN of zaAy^irN . (T.) humo yatanaAwbuwna Aln~awobapa fiymaA bayonahumo fiY AlmaA'i wagayorihi [ They took turns in the case of a thing that was between them; in the case of water &c. ] (S.) ― -b2- tanaAwabuwA Ealayohi They did it by turns; this person doing it one time: and that, another. definition: What is a day's and a night's journey distant from one: (S, K:) what is a night's journey distant is called Alqarabu : originally in the case of going to water: (S:) or what is three days' journey...
sourceDefinition: What is a day's and a night's journey distant from one: (S, K:) what is a night's journey distant is called Alqarabu : originally in the case of going to water: (S:) or what is three days' journey distant: or what is two leagues ( farosaxaAni ) distant; or three. (TA.) Lebeed says, A_iHodaY baniY jaEofarK kalifotu bihaA lamo tumosi min~iY nawobFA walaA qarabaA [ I have become enamoured of one of the descendants of Jaafar: she has not become a day's and a night's journey (or three days' journey or two eagues, ) distant from me, nor a night's journey distant ]. (S.) Or nwb signifies [in these words of the poet] near, so that he might visit her repeatedly; and qrb and nwb are synonymous: (IAar:) or qrb [is used by him to signify that at such a distance] he might come to her once in three days. (AA.) -A2- nawobN Strength: (K:) as also ↓ nawobpN : ex. A^aSobaHota laA nawobapN laka Thou hast become without strength: and tarakotuhu laA nawobN lahu I left him without strength. (TA.) ― -b2- nawobN Nearness. (ISk, S, K.) -A3- nawobN a pl. (or rather a quasi. pl. n., TA) of naAy^ibN : (RA, K:) [but in what sense I do not find: app., as the act. part. n. of naAba “ it befell, &c. ”]
